### 120.7 The buoyant pressure family - a static pressure given at a patch, carried onto the solved `p_rgh`

BC-11 implements the four buoyant-pressure names of the §120 table. The names
are taken from the user guides of §120 by name only; every equation below is
the hydrostatic decomposition of §20.5 and §9 applied at a boundary face, or
is ours (*DESIGN*). All four are fixed values of the SOLVED pressure - `fr =
1`, `refGrad = 0`, a §4 triple with no new evaluation branch and no kernel:
`prghPressure` and `uniformDensityHydrostaticPressure` ride
`BcKind::FixedValue`, and the two total forms ride `BcKind::TotalPressure`
(14), as `totalPressure` does.

**The solved pressure.** A case gives a STATIC pressure `p` at the patch; the
solvers do not solve for `p`. §20.5 solves for `p_rgh = p - rho (g . x)`, and
the face value has to be written in that variable. There are two forms:

* *absolute* (`ofgpu-vof`, §20): `p` and `p_rgh` in Pa, and `rho_f` is the
  mixture density of the boundary face, `rho = alpha rho_1 + (1 - alpha)
  rho_2` of §20.3 evaluated from the face's `alpha` - the value the solver's
  own `update_properties` writes on that face.
* *kinematic* (`ofgpu-buoyant`, §9): the momentum equation carries `-grad p
  + g (rho/rho_ref - 1)` with `rho/rho_ref = T_ref/T`, and equating it with
  `(-grad p_s + rho g)/rho_ref` gives `grad p = grad p_s/rho_ref - g`, i.e.
  `p = (p_s - rho_ref (g . x))/rho_ref` up to a constant the boundary fixes.
  The solved `p` is `p_rgh` with the REFERENCE density, divided by it. Every
  pressure and density entry of the four conditions is read divided by
  `rho_ref` (the convention of a kinematic case), and `rho_f = 1` in every
  equation below - whatever the face temperature, because the local density
  enters only the buoyancy term.

With `x_f` the face centre, `O` the mesh's local origin (§118.7; `O = 0` in
the f64 build), `U_f` the face velocity and `|U_f|^2 = U_x^2 + U_y^2 + U_z^2`:

```
gh_f    = g . (x_f - O)                                                   (120.7a)
p_rgh,f = p - rho_f gh_f                                    prghPressure  (120.7b)
p_rgh,f = p0 - (1/2) rho_f |U_f|^2 - rho_f gh_f   inflow    prghTotalPressure      (120.7c)
p_rgh,f = p0 - rho_f gh_f                         outflow
p_rgh,f = ph_rgh,f - (1/2) rho_f |U_f|^2          inflow    prghTotalHydrostaticPressure (120.7d)
p_rgh,f = ph_rgh,f                                outflow
p_rgh,f = p_ref + rho_ref g . (x_f - x_ref) - rho_f gh_f   uniformDensityHydrostaticPressure (120.7e)
```

(120.7a) is taken on the STORED coordinate because the solver's own body
force is: `vofBodyForceFluxBoundary` reads `m.b_cf`, which is local under `single`
(§118.7), so a `p_rgh` level written with world coordinates would differ
from the solver's by `rho g . O`. In (120.7e) both `x_f` and `x_ref`
(`pRefPoint`) are world positions - only their difference enters. The
entries: `p` for (120.7b) and `p0` for (120.7c), each a uniform number;
`rhoRef`, `pRefValue` and `pRefPoint` (a vector) for (120.7e). `ph_rgh,f` is
the hydrostatic `p_rgh` of a reference state at rest, on every face of the
patch; this crate solves no such field, so it is an input the caller passes
(below). Inflow is the `totalPressure` test of `field_setup`: `phi_b < 0`
where a boundary flux is given, else `U_f . n_f < 0` - the dynamic term is
the Bernoulli pressure of the fluid coming in, and fluid leaving carries its
kinetic energy out with it.

*Check (the gate's column).* A column at rest with uniform `rho`,
`prghPressure` at its top `z_t` with `p = p_0` and `g = (0, 0, -|g|)`:
(120.7b) gives `p_rgh = p_0 + rho |g| z_t` on the top, the interior at rest
holds it uniform, and `p = p_rgh + rho (g . x) = p_0 + rho |g| (z_t - z)` -
the hydrostatic column `p = p_0 + rho g (h_ref - z)` with `h_ref = z_t`. On
a VERTICAL patch, (120.7e) with `rhoRef = rho` is uniform in `p_rgh` and
leaves the column at rest, where a uniform static `p` through (120.7b) is
not, and drives a flow - the control row of the gate.

**Evaluation** *(DESIGN - ours)*. All arithmetic is f64 from the
`Scalar`-cast inputs and the f64 `geom64` face centres, rounded once into
`Scalar` (§118.2); the operation order is the order the equations are
written in, left to right, `g . d = g_x d_x + g_y d_y + g_z d_z`. The four
are DERIVED conditions in the sense of the `field_setup` module header:
evaluated once, at setup, from the case's initial fields (`rho_f` from the
initial `alpha`, `U_f` from the initial velocity), as `totalPressure` is.
That is exact while the face's phase and velocity do not change - the open
top of a tank in the light phase, a side opening in one fluid. A face whose
`alpha` changes during the run keeps its initial `rho_f`; the per-step
refresh was left to the VOF family unit (BC-21), which did not take it -
it would change existing runs, the user's decision (§120.14).

**Inputs and refusals.** `BcInputs::prgh: Option<PrghInputs>` carries
`g` (the solver's own gravity), `rho_b` (per flattened boundary face, the
absolute form; `None` is the kinematic form), `u_b` (the face velocity for
the two total forms) and `ph_rgh_b` (for (120.7d)). Refused by name, each
message naming the condition and "SPEC-LIT 120.7": any of the four where
`BcInputs::prgh` is `None` (a solver with no `p_rgh` - its pressure is not
the variable these conditions are written in); (120.7c)/(120.7d) without
`u_b`; (120.7d) without `ph_rgh_b`; any of the four on a vector field; a
missing `p`, `p0`, `rhoRef`, `pRefValue` or `pRefPoint`; a `rho` entry
naming any field but `rho`, and a `ph_rgh` entry naming any field but
`ph_rgh` (the density and the hydrostatic field are the solver's own).
`ofgpu-buoyant` passes the kinematic form, `ofgpu-vof` the absolute form
with `rho_b` from `Vof::boundary_density`; both pass `ph_rgh_b = None`, so
(120.7d) is reached through the API only. Every other driver refuses the
four names.

**Gates** (`tests/bc_buoyant_pressure.rs`, both builds; class per docs/17
§5.1, D-F32-1).

`prgh_triples_are_the_closed_forms` - a 4 x 3 x 2 box on [0,2] x [0,1]^2,
`g = (0.5, -1, -9.81)`, a per-face density, velocity, flux sign and `ph_rgh`:
every face of the four names, in the absolute and the kinematic form, is
(120.7b)-(120.7e) in the operation order above bit for bit (class D), `fr`
exactly 1, `refGrad` exactly 0; with no flux the inflow test falls to
`PrghInputs::u_b . n` (4 of the 6 `xMin` faces inflow, no `xMax` face) for
both total forms. `prgh_refusals_are_by_name` - every refusal of the list
above, each message carrying "SPEC-LIT 120.7" (class D). `a_kinematic_
column_open_at_the_top_and_side_stays_at_rest` - `Simple` on a 16 x 1 x 16
box, `T = T_ref` so `b = 0` exactly, `prghPressure p 5` on the top and
(120.7e) with `rhoRef 1` on the side, both of which write 14.81: after 50
outer iterations `max |U|` is 2.4e-15 and `p + g . x` is `5 + 9.81 (1 - z)`
within 1.4e-14 (`single` 4.1e-7 and 8.2e-6, class R); the control - a
uniform static `p 5` on the side - moves at 4.33. `a_stratified_column_open_
at_the_top_is_hydrostatic` - THE gate: `Vof` on a 24 x 1 x 24 box, water
(1000) under air (1) with the interface on a face, `prghPressure p 1000` on
the top: `rho_f` is exactly 1 on the top and 1000 on the floor, `max |U|`
after 20 steps is 1.2e-13 and `p = p_rgh + rho (g . x)` is the two-layer
column `p_0 + rho g (h_ref - z)` (`h_ref` = the top) within 1.1e-12 of 5705.53
(2.0e-16 relative; `single` 5.6e-6 and 2.1e-7 relative, class R); the
control - `fixedValue 1000` of the `p_rgh` LEVEL - is off by 9.81 Pa.
`a_column_open_at_the_side_stays_at_rest` - one fluid at 1000, (120.7e) with
`rhoRef 1000` on a vertical side: `max |U|` 1.4e-16, `p` within 3.0e-11 of
10605.6 (`single` 1.4e-7 and 9.2e-8 relative); the control (a uniform
static `p` through (120.7b)) moves at 0.10. Five tests, five pass in each
build; the two driver knob tests (`ofgpu-vof` on the dam break's
atmosphere, `ofgpu-buoyant` on the plume's outlet) run and change what the
run writes.

Two inputs of the VOF columns are stated because they were measured. Both
start from the hydrostatic `p_rgh` itself (each layer constant formed once
in f64), the hydrostatic initialisation a column at rest is: started from
`p_rgh = 0`, the first pressure solve lifts the column by about 5000 Pa and
leaves the heavy layer's constant 1.4e-8 Pa off (2.3e-12 relative) in f64,
the linear solver's floor and not the condition's. And they step at
`dt = 2.5e-4`. *Finding (f32):* at `dt = 1e-3` the stratified column under
`single` sits at `max |U|` 1.2e-5 to 1.9e-5 from the first step on, above
the class-R bound 1e-5 - the f32 round-off of the face force split
`-grad p_rgh - (g . x) grad rho` at a 1000:1 jump, which reaches the
velocity through `rAU` and therefore scales with `dt`; at 2.5e-4 it is
5.6e-6. The fix is an f64 evaluation of that split under `single` (a §118
numerics change of `vof.cu`), which belongs to the §118 owner.

**`forceSplitDouble`** *(DESIGN - ours; the user's decision of 2026-10-14
to offer the f64 split as a choice)*. `ofgpu-vof -forceSplitDouble`
(`VofControls::force_split_double`) is off by default, and off the `single`
path is the one above, bit for bit. On, under `single`, `Vof::update_force`
forms the internal-face force in f64 from the stored f32 inputs,
`-(g . x)_f deltaCoeffs (rho_N - rho_P) |Sf| + sigma kappa_f |Sf|
snGrad(alpha) - |Sf| deltaCoeffs (p_N - p_P) - c_f` with `c_f` the
non-orthogonal correction of `|Sf| snGrad(p_rgh)` alone, and rounds once
(`vofForceFluxSplit64`, compiled only under `single`), so the gravity and
pressure terms cancel before any f32 rounding; it costs one extra pass over
the faces. The boundary faces (`momForceFluxBoundary`), the face flux `phi`
and `phi_HbyA` keep their f32 split, and a run with the §87 Marangoni model
(`sigma` a field) keeps the f32 path. In the f64 build the setting does
nothing: the split is already double. Its effect on the column is not
measured here; the user ruled out further tests of this item.

* **Rusche, H.** *Computational Fluid Dynamics of Dispersed Two-Phase Flows
  at High Phase Fractions*, PhD thesis, Imperial College London (2002) -
  the modified pressure `p - rho (g . x)` of the two-phase momentum
  equation, and the boundary value it implies for a given static pressure.
* **Batchelor, G. K.** *An Introduction to Fluid Dynamics*, Cambridge
  University Press (1967), §3.5 - Bernoulli's total pressure `p + (1/2) rho
  |U|^2` along a streamline entering through the boundary, and hydrostatic
  equilibrium `grad p = rho g`.

No GPL-licensed source was consulted.

### 120.8 The thermal family - an outer wall, a prescribed heat, a lumped mass and Danckwerts' inlet

BC-12 implements the six thermal names of the §120 table. The names are
taken from the user guides of §120 by name only; the entry keys and every
equation below are ours (*DESIGN*) or the textbook law each cites. All of
them are §4's triple with no new evaluation branch: `turbulentHeatFluxTemperature`
rides `BcKind::FixedFluxTemperature` (§32.2) as it is, and the other three
ride `BcKind::Mixed`, whose triple `crate::energy::Energy` rewrites every
outer iteration from the face's CURRENT conductance - the §98 ambient
triple (S98.1)-(S98.3) carried from the conjugate path onto any fluid wall
the energy equation solves.

**The outer side of a face.** Let `C_b = k_eff,b Delta_b` be the face's
cell-to-face conductance per area (S47.4; `k_eff,b` is `Energy`'s
boundary `k_eff`, molecular plus `rho cp nu_t/Pr_t`), `T_P` the owner
cell's and `T_b` the face's current value. A face loses `H (T_b - T_ref)`
to its outside and receives a prescribed `q_in` (W/m^2, positive INTO the
domain, the §32.2 sign); with `n` wall layers of thickness `t_i` and
conductivity `kappa_i` between the face and an outer surface at `T_o` that
convects at `h` to an ambient `Ta` and radiates grey at `eps` to a surround
at the same `Ta`:

```
R_l    = sum_i t_i/kappa_i                                                   (120.8a)
q_c    = C_b (T_P - T_b)                                                     (120.8b)
T_o*   = T_b - R_l q_c                                                       (120.8c)
b = 4 eps sigma T_o*^3,   a = eps sigma (T_o*^4 - Ta^4) - b T_o*,
H_o = h + b,   T_ref = (h Ta - a)/H_o          (eps = 0: H_o = h, T_ref = Ta)   (120.8d)
H      = H_o/(1 + R_l H_o)                                                   (120.8e)
fr = H/(H + C_b),     refValue = T_ref,     refGrad = q_in/k_eff,b           (120.8f)
```

(120.8a) is the plane wall's series resistance and (120.8e) puts it in
series with the outer film, `(T_b - T_ref)/(R_l + 1/H_o)`; (120.8d) is
(S98.2)-(S98.3)'s tangent of the quartic, taken about the OUTER surface's
temperature. (120.8b) is the heat the last solve conducted from the cell to
the face, which a converged face also passes through the layers, so
(120.8c) is the outer temperature that iterate implies; the first pass, from
a seed with `q_c = 0`, linearises about `T_b`. *Proof of the identity.* §4
gives `T_b = fr T_ref + (1 - fr)(T_P + refGrad/Delta_b)`, and with
`C_b fr = H (1 - fr)` this is `C_b (T_P - T_b) = H (T_b - T_ref) - q_in`:
the heat the cell conducts to the face is the heat the face loses outside
less the heat it is given, **at every iterate**, not at convergence. With
`H = 0`: `fr = 0` and `refGrad = q_in/k_eff,b`, §32.2's fixed flux in
every bit. The face is left untouched while `k_eff,b` or `C_b` is not
positive (before the first `update_k_eff`) or, on a radiating face, while
`T_o*` is not, the convention of `energyFixedFluxTemperature`.

**`externalWallHeatFluxTemperature`.** `mode` is required: `flux` reads `q`
(W/m^2) and is `H = 0`, `q_in = q`; `power` reads `Q` (W) and is `H = 0`,
`q_in = Q/A` with `A` the patch area summed in f64; `coefficient` reads `h`
(> 0, W/(m^2 K)), `Ta` (> 0, K), optionally `thicknessLayers` and
`kappaLayers` (two lists of one length, summed by `cht::layered_resistance`,
§47.9) and `emissivity` in `[0, 1]` (default 0), with `q_in = 0`.
**`turbulentHeatFluxTemperature`** reads `heatSource` (`flux` or `power`)
and `q` (W/m^2, or W spread by area): the flux through the EFFECTIVE
conductivity, which is what §32.2's kernel already writes, so it is that
condition with `refValue = q` or `q/A`.

**`lumpedMassTemperature`.** A mass `m` (kg, `mass`) of specific heat `c_p`
(J/(kg K), `Cp`) behind the patch at one temperature `T_m`, from the
lumped-capacitance balance `m c_p dT_m/dt = -Q` (`Q` the heat the wall
conducts into the domain). It is stepped with the energy equation's OWN ddt
row `a_n T^{n+1} + a_0 T^n + a_00 T^{n-1}` (`timescheme::DdtCoeffs`; Euler,
or `backward` from its Euler first step, §105.16-§105.17), shared out over
the patch by area:

```
H = m c_p a_n / A,   T_ref = -(a_0 T_m^n + a_00 T_m^{n-1})/a_n,   q_in = 0
T_m^{n+1} = sum_f T_b,f |S_f| / A                                            (120.8g)
```

Summed over the patch, (120.8f)'s identity is `m c_p (a_n T_m^{n+1} + a_0
T_m^n + a_00 T_m^{n-1}) = -Q^{n+1}` exactly, with `T_m^{n+1}` the area
mean: the lump's energy balance holds whole and implicit. What is not
lumped is the spread WITHIN a step: a face whose cell is warmer holds a
warmer share, and all faces return to one `T_m` at the next step. On a
patch whose faces see the same cell temperature the two are the same thing.
`T_m^0` is the area mean of the patch's `value`, which is required. The
condition is refused on a steady run (no `a_n`) and by `ofgpu-lowmach` on a
restart (the lump's levels are not in the checkpoint).

**`totalFlowRateAdvectiveDiffusive`.** Danckwerts' inlet condition: the
total heat flow entering - advected plus conducted - is the advected heat of
the incoming stream at `inletValue`. With `phi_conv,b = cp rho_f phi_b`
(`Energy`'s mass flux times `cp`, positive out):

```
H = max(-phi_conv,b, 0)/|S_f|,   T_ref = T_in,   q_in = 0                     (120.8h)
```

so `(-phi_conv,b/|S_f|) T_b + C_b (T_b - T_P) = (-phi_conv,b/|S_f|) T_in` on
an inflow face, the 1-D `u c_in = u c - D dc/dx` of Danckwerts, and an
outflow face is zero-gradient (`fr = 0`, `refGrad = 0`).

**The alphat aliases.** `alphatWallFunction` and `compressible::alphatWallFunction`
set a wall's turbulent thermal diffusivity from its eddy viscosity. This
solver carries no `alphat` field: `k_eff,b` already holds `rho cp
nu_t,b/Pr_t` with `nu_t,b` from `nut`'s own wall function (S26). On a field
named `alphat` the two names are read as `calculated`, with the mapping
printed once (`contract::warn_once`); on any other field they are refused,
naming `alphat`.

**Evaluation** *(DESIGN - ours)*. `Energy::set_thermal_walls` takes the
faces and lumps `field_setup::thermal_walls` reads from `T`'s field, and
holds the per-face `h`, `Ta`, `eps`, `R_l` and `q_in` in f64 buffers in both
builds. The kernel `energyThermalWall` (`cuda/energy.cu`) evaluates
(120.8b)-(120.8f) and (120.8h) in `ofacc` from the widened inputs, in the
order written, with `sigma` the `Scalar` constant widened, and rounds once
per stored value (§118.2); `cht::ambient::ThermalFace::triple` is its host
twin. It runs in `Energy::prepare_coefficients` after the §32.2 rewrite and
again in `correct` right after the convective flux is built, so (120.8h)
reads the flux it is assembled with; both launches sit inside `correct`,
the captured region of `the_energy_correction_replays_bitwise`.
`Energy::advance_lumped_masses` is the one host round trip: once per time
step, after the step is opened and before its first `correct`, it records
`T_m` by (120.8g), rotates the lump's two f64 levels and uploads the step's
`H` and `T_ref`; `correct` refuses a lump whose coefficients were never set.

**Inputs and refusals.** `BcInputs::thermal` is the caller's promise that
`Energy::set_thermal_walls` and `Energy::advance_lumped_masses` are wired;
`ofgpu-lowmach` passes it for `T`. Refused by name, each message naming the
condition and "SPEC-LIT 120.8": the three `Mixed`-kind names where
`BcInputs::thermal` is false (every other setup: a seed with nothing to
rewrite it would freeze the face); a missing or unknown `mode` or
`heatSource`; a missing `q`, `Q`, `h`, `Ta`, `mass`, `Cp`, `value` (lump)
or `inletValue`; `h`, `Ta`, `mass` or `Cp` not finite and positive;
`emissivity` outside `[0, 1]`; layer lists of two lengths or a layer
refused by (S47.11)'s rule; an entry the mode does not read (`h`, `Ta`,
`emissivity` or the layers under `flux`/`power`, `q` or `Q` under
`coefficient`); any of the six on a vector field; and, in `Energy`, a lump
on a steady scheme, a lump face that is not one of the set's faces (a
lump names its faces by boundary-face index, mapped once to their places
in the face list), and a thermal face on an interface (§47.6).

**Gates** (`tests/bc_thermal.rs`, both builds; class per docs/17 §5.1,
D-F32-1; the tolerance is `t` in f64 and `max(t, min(t 2^29, 1e-5))` under
`single`; f64 numbers first, `single` in brackets).

`coefficient_mode_slab_is_the_series_resistance_closed_form` - THE gate,
row 1. A 4 x 1 x 1 slab on [0, 0.1] (`k = 0.05`, xMin `fixedValue 400`),
xMax `mode coefficient; h 10; Ta 300;` with `thicknessLayers (0.01 0.02);
kappaLayers (0.5 2.0);`, steady: the measured `q_m = C_b (T_P - T_b)` is
`q = 100/(0.1/0.05 + 0.03 + 0.1) = 46.948356807511736` within 1.6e-15
[2.7e-7] on xMax and 6.0e-15 [2.4e-6] on xMin, and `T_b = 306.1032863849765`
within 0 [5.1e-8], all held to tol(1e-10), after 2 passes; the control
without the layers is `100/2.1` within 2.9e-15 [3.2e-6]. `a_radiating_outer_
surface_is_the_root_of_the_quartic` - xMin 600, `emissivity 0.8`: `T_b`
lands on the quartic's root 309.59128377473974 within 1.1e-15 [1.8e-8], and
with the two layers on 313.7498487803651 within 1.6e-15 [4.4e-9] (tol(1e-10)),
in 4 [3] tangent passes each (<= 50 asserted). `the_device_triple_is_its_
host_twin` - three passes into the layered radiating case, the kernel's
`fr`, `refValue`, `refGrad` equal `ThermalFace::triple` on the downloaded
state within tol(1e-14) relative, a zero exactly (class R).
`flux_and_power_are_the_fixed_flux_condition` - 20 passes with `q -50`:
`externalWallHeatFluxTemperature mode flux` and `turbulentHeatFluxTemperature
heatSource flux` give `T` on every cell and face bit for bit the
`fixedFluxTemperature` run (class D); `mode power` and `heatSource power`
with `-50 A` deviate by 0 [0] (tol(1e-12)). `a_lumped_mass_decays_
exponentially_at_second_order` - THE gate, row 2: xMin `fixedValue 300`,
xMax `lumpedMassTemperature mass 12; Cp 1000; value uniform 400;`,
`tau = m c_p L/(k A) = 2.4e8 s`, `backward`, one `correct` per step to

(<= 1e-4), 2.52e-4 [2.55e-4] at N = 25, a ratio of 4.06 [3.82] (in [3.5,
4.5], second order); the Euler control at N = 50 is 3.65e-3 [3.65e-3]
(> 1e-3). `danckwerts_inlet_carries_the_advected_heat` - a 16 x 1 x 1
channel on [0, 1], `k = 12`, plug `phi = 0.01 |S_f|`: (a) `inletValue 310`
with xMax `zeroGradient` fills every cell with 310 within 4.7e-15 [7.9e-7]
(tol(1e-10)); (b) `inletValue 301` against xMax `fixedValue 300` holds
`a T_b + C_b (T_b - T_P) = a T_in` at every pass within 6.7e-15 [3.4e-6]
(tol(1e-12)), the converged inlet face sits at 300.616732045547
[300.616882324219] below `T_in` while the `fixedValue 301` control pins

`the_alphat_aliases_read_as_calculated_on_alphat_only` - both names are

### 120.9 The atmospheric family - the Richards & Hoxey surface layer at an inlet, and two wall functions

BC-13 implements the six atmospheric names of the §120 table. The names are
taken from the user guides of §120 by name only; every equation below is
cited, or is ours and marked DESIGN.

**Four inlet profiles** (Richards & Hoxey 1993). `atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity`,
`atmBoundaryLayerInletK`, `atmBoundaryLayerInletEpsilon` and
`atmBoundaryLayerInletOmega` are a `fixedValue` (`BcKind::FixedValue`,
`fr = 1`) whose per-face value the setup computes once, in f64 from the
world face centre (§118.7), and rounds once into `Scalar` - the treatment
§120.5 gives its fixed-value profiles. The neutral surface layer of a
roughness length `z0`, with the height above the ground
`z = max(zDir . x_f - zGround, 0)`:

```
u* = kappa Uref / ln((Zref + z0)/z0)                                 (120.9a)
U  = (u*/kappa) ln((z + z0)/z0) flowDir                              (120.9b)
k  = u*^2 / sqrt(C_mu)                                               (120.9c)
epsilon = u*^3 / (kappa (z + z0))                                    (120.9d)
omega   = epsilon/(C_mu k) = u* / (kappa sqrt(C_mu) (z + z0))        (120.9e)
```

(120.9a)-(120.9d) are Richards & Hoxey's; (120.9e) is (120.9d) through the
k-omega relation `omega = epsilon/(beta* k)` with `beta* = C_mu`
(Wilcox; §6.2). Both logarithms are evaluated as `ln_1p(a/z0)`. The entries:
`flowDir` and `zDir` (required, normalised in f64, a zero vector refused),
`Uref` and `Zref` (required, positive; a time-varying Function1 is refused
by name, as §120.5 refuses one, because no driver runs the timed path for
these names), `z0` (required, positive at every face; `uniform`, a bare
number, or one per face), `zGround` (0 when absent; uniform or per face),
`kappa` (0.41) and `Cmu` (0.09). The entries `d`, `C1` and `C2` are refused
by name: a displacement height and the extended `k` profile of later work
are not in (120.9a)-(120.9e), and dropping them silently would be the
substitution §13.4 forbids. A scalar name on a vector field, and the
velocity name on a scalar field, are refused naming the mismatch.

Richards & Hoxey show that (120.9b)-(120.9d) solve the standard k-epsilon
equations exactly - `k` is uniform, its production equals `epsilon`, and
`nu_t = C_mu k^2/epsilon = kappa u* (z + z0)` - provided

```
sigma_eps = kappa^2 / ((C_2 - C_1) sqrt(C_mu))                       (120.9f)
```

which is 1.1674 for `kappa = 0.41` and the §6.1 constants, against the
standard 1.3. A case that wants the profile kept along a fetch sets it.

**The ground: `nutkAtmRoughWallFunction`** *(DESIGN - ours, after
Hargreaves & Wright 2007)*. Hargreaves & Wright traced the decay of an
inlet profile along an empty fetch to a rough-wall function written in a
sand-grain height rather than in the profile's own `z0`. The wall function
here is written so that a cell sitting on (120.9b)-(120.9c) carries exactly
the shear `u*^2` (BcKind 51, family code 2 of `wfNutWall`, host twin
`wallfunctions::nut_wall_atm_rough`):

```
u* = C_mu^{1/4} sqrt(k_P),
nu_t,w = max(0, u* kappa y / ln(1 + y/z0) - nu)                      (120.9g)
```

With `U_P = (u*/kappa) ln(1 + y/z0)` at the cell's wall distance `y`, the
face shear `(nu + nu_t,w) U_P/y` is `u*^2` for any `y` - the property the
gate measures. `k_P` is floored at `k_min` as `nutk` floors it. `z0` is the
patch's own (required, positive at every face, per face or uniform); it is
NOT a sand-grain height, and `Ks`/`Cs` are not read. The ground's `epsilon`
keeps `epsilonWallFunction` (§6.4); `G` in the wall cell is built from the
`nu_t,w` this writes.

**`nutUBlendedWallFunction`** *(DESIGN - ours)*. The velocity-based family
(§15.1) with the friction velocity a binomial blend of the two asymptotes
(BcKind 52, family code 3, host twins `u_tau_log`, `u_tau_blended`,
`nut_wall_blended`):

```
u_v = sqrt(nu |U|/y)                              (u+ = y+)
u_l: the root of u ln(1 + E y u/nu) = kappa |U|   (u+ = ln(1 + E y+)/kappa)
u_tau = (u_v^n + u_l^n)^{1/n},   nu_t,w = max(0, u_tau^2 y/|U| - nu)  (120.9h)
```

`|U|` is the wall-parallel speed `wfMagUParallel` gives the `nutU` family,
and `n` is the patch entry `n` (4 when absent; positive and finite, or
refused). The log law is written with `ln(1 + E y+)`, not `ln(E y+)`: the two
differ by `1/(kappa E y+)`, under 4e-3 of `u+` from `y+ = 30` on, but only
the first has a root that vanishes with `|U|` (`u_l -> sqrt(kappa/E) u_v`),
so the blend's viscous limit is the sublayer's - `nu_t,w/nu -> (1 +
(kappa/E)^2)^{1/2} - 1 = 8.7e-4` - and not the floor `y+ = 1/E` of the plain
log law. `u_l` is found by Newton from `u_v`, at most 40 steps, stopping
when a step is below `4 eps` of the precision relative: `G(u) = u ln(1 + E y
u/nu) - kappa |U|` is increasing and convex for `u > 0` with `G(0) < 0`, so
after at most one step the iterates fall to the root from above. The blend
is formed as `m (1 + r^n)^{1/n}`, `m = max(u_v, u_l)`, `r = min/max` - the
same number without the overflow `u^n` would risk in `f32`.

**Precision.** Codes 0 and 1 of `wfNutWall` (`nutk`, `nutU` and their
rough forms) keep their arithmetic; only `wallfunctions.cubin` changes, and
no other kernel's SASS moves. The profiles are f64 and rounded once. The
new kernel arithmetic runs in `ofscalar` with `log1p`, `pow` and the
precision's own stopping rule; the twins are held at class R.

**Refusals by name.** A missing or non-positive `z0` (on any of the six), a
missing or non-positive `Uref`/`Zref`/`kappa`/`Cmu`, a zero `flowDir` or
`zDir`, a time-varying `Uref`, the entries `d`, `C1`, `C2`, a non-positive
blend exponent, and the scalar/vector mix-ups. `WallData::build` refuses a
face whose atmospheric family disagrees with its `u_based` flag.

**Gate** (`tests/bc_atmospheric.rs`, both builds; f64 first, `single` in
brackets). `the_inlet_profiles_are_richards_and_hoxey` - a 12-face inlet
graded towards the ground, `Uref 8`, `Zref 20`, `z0 0.05`, `zGround -2`,
`kappa 0.4`, `Cmu 0.085`: the face values of all four names against
(120.9a)-(120.9e) in f64, worst relative 0 [4.8e-8] (tol(1e-14), class R).
`nutk_atm_rough_holds_the_profile_shear` - eight ground faces at `y = 0.05`
with `z0` from 1e-4 to 30 m, `k = u*^2/sqrt(C_mu)` at `u* = 0.5`: the device
`nu_t,w` against `nut_wall_atm_rough` within 1.5e-16 [0] and the wall shear
`(nu + nu_t,w) U(y)/y` against `u*^2` within 2.2e-16 [6.8e-8] (tol(1e-12),
class R). `nutu_blended_meets_its_twin_and_its_limits` - wall-parallel
speeds 1e-6 to 10 m/s (`Re_y` 3.3e-3 to 3.3e4) at `n = 4` and `n = 3`: device
against twin within 0 [4.4e-7] (tol(1e-12), relative to `max(nu_t,w, nu)`);
the viscous limit `nu_t,w/nu = 9.80e-4` (<= 1e-3), the log limit
`u_tau/u_l - 1 = 6.6e-5` (<= 1e-4) with `|G(u_l)|` 0 [1.0e-7] (tol(1e-12)
`kappa |U|`). `atmospheric_refusals_are_by_name` - 12 refusals, each naming
its entry. `a_five_km_fetch_keeps_the_inlet_profile` - THE gate: 50 x 1 x 24
cells over 5000 x 10 x 500 m, the vertical graded 50:1 (first cell 1.59 m),
y empty; xMin and the top carry (120.9b)-(120.9d) (the top's fixed values
hold the shear that drives the layer), xMax `zeroGradient` with `p = 0`,
the ground `noSlip`, `kqRWallFunction`, `epsilonWallFunction` and
`nutkAtmRoughWallFunction z0 0.01`; `Uref 10` at `Zref 10` (`u* =
0.593450`), `nu = 1.5e-5`, k-epsilon with (120.9f), `nut_max_coeff 1e8`
(the default cap `1e5 nu` would bound `epsilon` off a profile whose `nu_t`
reaches 122 m^2/s), the pressure by PCG with DIC. Steady SIMPLE from the
profile stops in 225 iterations at a 25-iteration change of `U.x` below
1e-9 m/s [the 1000-iteration cap, the f32 SIMPLE floor of §118, change
5.7e-6 m/s]. The outlet column against the inlet profile: `U` worst
2.483 % [2.483 %] at `z = 2.53 m` (<= 3 %), `k` worst 8.351 % [8.351 %] at
`z = 2.53 m` (<= 10 %); the ground's `u* = sqrt((nu + nu_t,w) U_P/y)` worst
1.197 % [1.197 %] over all 50 ground faces (<= 3 %) - class P, the same
bands in both builds. 5 of 5 in each build.

Controls, measured once and not kept as tests: the same fetch with the
ground on `nutkWallFunction` (a smooth wall) is off by 58 % (`U`), 65 %
(`k`) and 46 % (`u*`), so the gate sees the wall function; with the
standard `sigma_eps = 1.3` instead of (120.9f), `U` 1.0 % and `u*` 0.7 % but
`k` 12.5 %, outside the band - (120.9f) is what keeps `k`.

Finding (for the §118 owner, F32-13/14/15): under `single`, PBiCGStab with
the diagonal preconditioner on this fetch's pressure system (cells 100 m
x 1.6 m at the ground) does not converge from the first outer iteration
(final residual 38 against an initial 1 after 500 iterations) and the run
is NaN by iteration 8; the f64 build converges with the same controls. PCG
with DIC converges in both builds (171 iterations at the first), which is
why the gate selects it.

* **Richards, P. J., Hoxey, R. P.** Appropriate boundary conditions for
  computational wind engineering models using the k-epsilon turbulence
  model. *J. Wind Eng. Ind. Aerodyn.* 46-47 (1993) 145-153,
  doi:10.1016/0167-6105(93)90124-7 - (120.9a)-(120.9d) and (120.9f).
* **Hargreaves, D. M., Wright, N. G.** On the use of the k-epsilon model in
  commercial CFD software to model the neutral atmospheric boundary layer.
  *J. Wind Eng. Ind. Aerodyn.* 95 (2007) 355-369,
  doi:10.1016/j.jweia.2006.08.002 - the empty-fetch test of horizontal
  homogeneity, and the rough-wall function written in `z0`.

No GPL-licensed source was consulted.

### 120.10 The recycled inflow - an offset plane copied onto an inlet, and a seeded fluctuation

BC-14 implements the three recycled-inflow names of the §120 table. The
names are taken from the user guides of §120 by name only; every equation
below is cited, or is ours and marked DESIGN.

All three are a §4 FIXED VALUE (`BcKind::FixedValue`, `fr = 1`,
`refGrad = 0`) whose `refValue` a refresh kernel rewrites - no new
evaluation branch (§5.2 of the completion plan), and every kernel that asks
whether a face's flux is prescribed sees the fixed value it is.

**`mapped` and `mappedFixedValue`** (one condition, two spellings). The
recycling idea - take the inflow from a plane inside the domain and feed
it back at the inlet, so that a short domain carries a developed profile -
is Lund, Wu & Squires (1998). For each face `f` of the patch, with the
LOCAL f64 face centre `x_f` (§118.7) and the patch entry `offset` `d`:

```
x_s,f = x_f + d,   c(f) = the cell that holds x_s,f                   (120.10a)
psi*_f = psi_c(f)                                                     (120.10b)
```

`c(f)` is found once, at setup, by the parcel walk's point location
(`parcels::locate_cell64`, the half-space test of §66.6 on the f64
`geom64` view), so a point on a shared face goes to the lower-numbered
cell. (120.10b) is the cell value - the sample is not interpolated. With
`setAverage` the samples are rescaled to the area mean `a` (`average`, the
field's rank) *(DESIGN - ours)*:

```
A = SUM_f |S_f|,   m = SUM_f |S_f| psi*_f / A
s = |a|/|m|  if |a| > 0 and |m| >= |a|/2,   s = 1 otherwise
psi_f = s psi*_f + (a - s m)                                          (120.10c)
```

so `SUM_f |S_f| psi_f / A = a` whatever the branch: the factor keeps the
sampled profile's shape where its mean is comparable with the target, and
where it is not (a sample near rest, or a target of zero) the shift alone
moves the mean without amplifying the sample. On a vector field `|.|` is
the magnitude, so the factor is one number and the shift removes the part
of `m` across `a`. On a planar patch with outward normal `n`, (120.10c)
holds the flux:

```
SUM_f psi_f . S_f = A a . n                                           (120.10d)
```

The refresh is `field_ops::update_mapped_scalar`/`_vector`: one
`fldMapped` launch per patch, once per outer iteration before the boundary
evaluation, the sums in `ofacc` (§118.1) in face order and each value
rounded once; without `setAverage` the face value is the cell value, bit
for bit. `Simple::correct_outer` runs it for `U` and `p`;
`BcInputs::mapped` is the caller's promise, and `ofgpu-lowmach` and
`ofgpu-buoyant` give it for both. Without it - every other setup, and every
field outside `Simple` (`T`, `k`, `epsilon`, species) - the two names are
refused by name, because a seed nobody refreshes would freeze the face at
the plane's first sample (§13.4). The setup seeds the face from the
initial cells through the same host twin, `field::mapped::mapped_values`.

Entries: `offset` (required; a constant - a time-varying Function1 is
refused by name), `setAverage` (a switch, false when absent), `average`
(required when `setAverage` is on). This solver reads the sampling from
the field's patch entry, not from a mapped patch in
`constant/polyMesh/boundary`. Refused by name: `sampleMode` other than
`nearestCell`; any `sampleRegion` or `samplePatch` (another region or a
patch-to-patch sample is not built); `interpolationScheme` other than
`cell`; `fieldName` or `field` naming another field; a sample point in no
cell of the mesh.

**`turbulentInlet`** *(DESIGN - ours, on Gillespie's update)*. The face
value is a reference plus a fluctuation with a set RMS and a set memory,
drawn from a counter-based generator so that a run is reproducible and the
device and the host twin draw the same numbers. The unit-variance draw for
step `n`, global boundary face `g` and component `c`:

```
k = seed XOR (n << 32) XOR (3 g + c),   h = SplitMix64(k + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)
u = 2^-53 floor(h / 2^11),   eps = sqrt(3) (2u - 1)                   (120.10e)
```

`SplitMix64` is the finaliser of Steele, Lea & Flood (2014) -
`z = (z XOR z>>30) 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9`, `z = (z XOR z>>27)
0x94D049BB133111EB`, `z XOR z>>31`, in wrapping 64-bit arithmetic - and
`eps` is uniform on `[-sqrt 3, sqrt 3)`, mean 0 and variance 1. With
`s = fluctuationScale` (the field's rank) and the reference `psi_ref`
(`referenceField`, uniform or per face):

```
sigma_f,c = s_c |psi_ref,f|                                           (120.10f)
x^0 = sigma eps^0,   x^n = mu x^(n-1) + sqrt(1 - mu^2) sigma eps^n,
mu = 1 - alpha                                                        (120.10g)
psi_f^n = psi_ref,f + x^n                                             (120.10h)
```

(120.10g) is Gillespie's (1996) exact update of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck
process over a step, `mu = exp(-dt/tau)`, here with `mu` given through
`alpha` rather than through a correlation time: started from a stationary
draw, `x` keeps the RMS `sigma` at every step and its lag-1
autocorrelation is `mu`. `alpha = 1` is white. `|psi_ref,f|` is the vector
magnitude, or the absolute value on a scalar field. The update runs in
f64 in both builds and rounds once; `x^(n-1)` is read back as
`refValue - psi_ref`. Entries: `referenceField` and `fluctuationScale`
(required, `fluctuationScale >= 0`), `alpha` (`0 < alpha <= 1`, 0.1 when
absent), `seed` (a non-negative integer, 0 when absent - this solver's key).

The draw is `field_ops::advance_turbulent_inlet_scalar`/`_vector`: one
`fldTurbulentInlet` launch per patch, once per TIME step, with the step
counter in a device buffer so a captured graph advances it (§81).
`Simple::begin_time_step` runs it for `U`. `BcInputs::turbulent_inlet` is
the caller's promise; no driver gives it today - the steady modes of
`ofgpu-lowmach` and `ofgpu-buoyant` open a time step every outer unit,
which would redraw the fluctuation every iteration - so every driver
refuses the name, as §120.4 records for `advective`; the API carries it.

**Gates** - `tests/bc_mapped.rs`, both builds (f64 [single]), 5 tests.
`mapped_copies_the_sampled_cell` - 4 x 3 x 2 cells over [0,2] x [0,1]^2,
xMin `offset (1.25 0 0)`: every face value is the cell centred at
`x_f + d`, found by a direct search on the centres, bit for bit in both
builds, scalar and vector, for both spellings (class D).
`set_average_holds_the_mean_and_the_flux` - `T = 1 + x + 2y^2 + 0.5z`:
`average 5` takes the factor branch (one ratio over the patch, spread 0
[5.0e-8]), `average 100` the shift branch (spread 0 [5.0e-6]); the area
mean within 1.4e-16 [1.5e-8] of `a` relative (tol(1e-12), class R); the
device against `mapped_values` within 8.9e-16 [0]. `U = (1 + x, y - z,
2z)` with `average (2 0 0)` against a sample mean of `(2.25 0 1)`: each
component's mean within 0 [3.1e-9] of `a` and the inflow (120.10d)
`2.00000000000000` [`2.00000000000000`] against `2 A = 2` (tol(1e-12),
class R). `a_recycled_channel_is_the_cyclic_channel` - THE gate: 16 x 16 x 1
cells over [0,2] x [0,1] x [0,1/16], `nu = 0.01` (Re = 100 on the height).
The cyclic channel is driven by the uniform body force `b = 12 nu U_b/H^2 =
0.12` (the density-ratio form at `T_ref/T = 2`), `p = 0` on one wall. The
recycled channel has xMin `mappedFixedValue offset (1.0625 0 0) setAverage
true average (1 0 0)`, xMax `zeroGradient` with `p = 0`. Steady SIMPLE
stops on a cell change of `U` below 1e-14 in 2037 (cyclic) and 303 (recycled) iterations
[the 4000-iteration cap, the f32 SIMPLE floor of §118]. At the sample
plane, each profile by its own bulk: the worst difference 1.559e-4 [1.557e-4]
of the peak 1.4884 (<= 1 %, class P); the inflow `-SUM phi` within
0 [5.6e-9] of `A` relative (the f64 sum prints `0.062500000000000`) (tol(1e-12), class R).
`turbulent_inlet_rms_is_the_prescribed_scale` - 100 faces, reference
`(2 0 0)`, scale `(0.1 0.2 0.05)`: `alpha 1`, the seed and 99 steps, 1e4
samples a component - `RMS/sigma` 1.00659, 0.99826, 0.99776 and
`mean/sigma` -0.00076, -0.00019, 0.00270 in both builds (RMS within 5 %,
mean within 0.05, class P); the device against `turbulent_advance` over
all 3e4 draws 0 [0]; the same seed draws the same field bit for bit and
another seed does not; `alpha 0.1` over 1000 steps - `RMS/sigma` 0.99402,
1.00313, 1.00159 and lag-1 autocorrelation 0.89835, 0.90040, 0.90024
against `mu = 0.9` (within 0.05); a scalar `T` about 300 at scale 0.02,
`RMS/sigma` 0.99916. `mapped_and_turbulent_inlet_refusals_are_by_name` -
18 refusals, each naming its entry and this section, and the seed of an
accepted `mapped` patch is its sample bit for bit. 5 of 5 in each build.

Control, measured once and not kept as a test: the same recycled channel
with a UNIFORM `fixedValue (1 0 0)` inlet is 2.1e-1 of the peak off the
cyclic profile at the sample plane (at `nu = 0.1`, Re = 10, it was only
7.2e-3 - inside the band - which is why the gate runs at Re = 100: there
the band sees the recycling, not a short entry length).

Finding (for the §118 owner, F32-13/14/15): under `single` neither channel
reaches the 1e-14 change; both run to the 4000 cap. The profiles still
agree to 1.557e-4 of the peak - the f32 SIMPLE floor family of §120.3-§120.6.

* **Lund, T. S., Wu, X., Squires, K. D.** Generation of turbulent inflow

  inflow taken from a plane downstream (the idea; their rescaling of a

* **Gillespie, D. T.** Exact numerical simulation of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck

### 120.11 The inflow database - `timeVaryingMappedFixedValue`, a planar Delaunay in space and linear in time

BC-15 implements the last mapped-inflow name of the §120 table. The name and
the database layout - `constant/boundaryData/<patch>/points` and one folder
per time holding `<field>` - are taken by name and as a file FORMAT only from
the user guides of §120; every equation below is cited, or is ours and marked
DESIGN.

The condition is a §4 FIXED VALUE (`BcKind::FixedValue`, `fr = 1`,
`refGrad = 0`) whose `refValue` a timed apply rewrites after each
`F1Clock::advance` (§120.1) - no new evaluation branch (§5.2 of the
completion plan). Space is settled once at setup on the host; time runs on
the device.

**Space** *(DESIGN - ours, on the cited triangulation)*. With the samples
`p_k` (k = 0..N-1, WORLD f64, §118.7) and a face centre `x_f` (WORLD f64):

```
c = (1/N) SUM_k p_k,   a = argmax_k |p_k - c| (lowest index),   L = |p_a - c|
e1 = (p_a - c)/L,   r_k = (p_k - c) - ((p_k - c).e1) e1,   b = argmax_k |r_k|
collinear if |r_b| <= 1e-9 L, otherwise e2 = r_b/|r_b|
(u, v)(x) = ((x - c).e1/L, (x - c).e2/L)                              (120.11a)
```

The samples' triangulation `T` in `(u, v)` is Delaunay - no sample strictly
inside any triangle's circumcircle (Delaunay 1934):

```
|q_k - z_t| >= r_t  for every triangle t of T and every sample k that is
not a vertex of t, (z_t, r_t) the circumcircle of t                    (120.11b)
```

It is built by Bowyer-Watson insertion (Bowyer 1981; Watson 1981): a super
triangle of half-size 1e3, then for each sample in file order the cavity of
the triangles whose circumcircle holds it strictly (`d^2 < r^2 (1 - 1e-12)`),
grown from the triangle holding the sample through shared edges, then shrunk -
a triangle dropped and the component re-grown - until every cavity edge
`a -> b` has `orient(a, b, p) > 0`, and refilled by the fan from the sample.
Round-off can then leave a triangle not quite Delaunay, never an invalid one.
The super triangles are removed and the boundary completed to the convex
hull: wherever the counter-clockwise boundary turns right at `b`
(`orient(a, b, c) < 0` for boundary edges `a -> b -> c`), the triangle
`(a, c, b)` is added when it holds no sample. The net is checked: every
triangle counter-clockwise and the areas summing to the hull's (Andrew's
monotone chain) within 1e-9, else refused by name. The setup costs `O(N^2)`
for the triangulation and `O(F N)` for the location; none of it runs per step.

```
orient(P, Q, R) = (Q_u - P_u)(R_v - P_v) - (Q_v - P_v)(R_u - P_u)
D = orient(A, B, C) > 0
l_A = orient(x, B, C)/D,  l_B = orient(A, x, C)/D,  l_C = orient(A, B, x)/D
phi_f = l_A phi_A + l_B phi_B + l_C phi_C  (f64, in this order)         (120.11c)
```

for the first triangle with `min(l) >= -1e-10`. A face outside the hull takes
the nearest point of the nearest boundary edge `a b`,
`s = clamp(((x - a).(b - a))/|b - a|^2, 0, 1)`, `phi_f = (1 - s) phi_a +
s phi_b`. Collinear samples are interpolated the same way along `u` between
neighbours, clamped at the ends; one sample is a constant. Barycentric weights
sum to one and reproduce `x`, so (120.11c) is EXACT for a linear field on a
planar patch, which is the gate. `mapMethod nearest` takes the sample nearest
in 3-D (`|p_k - x_f|^2`, the lowest index on a tie).

**Time** (the clamp form of (120.2), §120.1). The time folders are the
sub-folders whose names parse as numbers, `t_0 < ... < t_{K-1}`; slab `k` is
(120.11c) of folder `k`, `V_{k,f,c}` in f64. At the clock's `t`:

```
K = 1 or t <= t_0:  V_0;      t >= t_{K-1}:  V_{K-1}
t_j <= t < t_{j+1}:  V_j + ((t - t_j)/(t_{j+1} - t_j)) (V_{j+1} - V_j)    (120.11d)
```

in double in both builds, rounded ONCE into `Scalar`. The kernels are
`f1TvApplyScalar`/`f1TvApplyVector` in `cuda/function1.cu` (`-fmad=false`),
reading `t` from the device clock so a captured step replays with the time
moving (§81.1 defect (b)); `TvMappedRule::values64` is their host twin, the
same operations in the same order, so the two agree bit for bit. Every
folder's slab is on the card: `K F n_c` doubles.

**Which runs carry it.** As a time-varying Function1 (§120.1): only the
`setup_*_field_timed` entry points, which read the database from
`<case_dir>/constant/boundaryData/<patch>`, seed the triple at `t_start` and
return the patch inside the `TimedBcs` the driver applies after each clock
step. Every other setup path refuses the name, naming the timed entry point,
because a frozen first folder would be the silent substitution §13.4 forbids.
No driver is wired yet (the gap §120.1 records).

Entries: `mapMethod` (`planarInterpolation`, the default, or `nearest`),
`fieldTable` (the file name in each time folder; the field's name when
absent), `perturb` (a number, accepted and unused - (120.11b) does not
perturb the samples), `setAverage` (`false` accepted). A value file may carry
one value of the field's rank before its list - the file's average - which is
read past. Refused by name: `setAverage` on; `offset`; another `mapMethod`;
no case directory; an unreadable `points` or value file; a value count that
is not the point count; two samples at one point (1e-12 in `(u, v)`); two
folders naming one time; no time folder; with two folders or more, a run
`[t_start, t_end]` not inside `[t_0, t_{K-1}]`.

**Gates** - `tests/bc_tvmapped.rs`, both builds (f64 [single]), 4 tests.
`a_linear_field_from_200_scattered_points_is_exact_on_the_faces` - THE gate:
2 x 6 x 5 cells over the unit cube, xMin sampled at its 4 corners and 196
seeded interior points; `T = 1.5 + 3y - 2z`, worst `|phi_f - phi(x_f)|` over
the 30 faces 1.97e-16 [1.97e-16] of `max|T|`; `U = (1 + y/2, 2 - z,
y/4 + 3z/4)` 2.22e-16 [2.22e-16] of `max|U|` (<= 1e-12, class R); the triple
is the slab rounded once, bit for bit.
`the_triangulation_is_delaunay_and_exact_on_linear_data` - on the 200
samples 394 = 2N - 2 - h triangles and no in-circle determinant above 0 [0];
a cocircular 30 x 30 grid gives 2N - 2 - 116 triangles; an 11 x 11 grid on a
tilted plane reproduces a linear field at 50 interior targets to 1.8e-15
[1.8e-15]; collinear samples, the hull clamp and `nearest` give the closed
forms. `time_interpolation_is_exact_at_the_midpoints` - folders 0, 0.5 and 2:
at each folder time the value is the slab bit for bit, at t = 0.25 and 1.25
it is the slabs' midpoint within 0 [1.1e-16] relative (<= 2 eps); on the
device, 16 steps of dt 0.125 to t = 2, every scalar and vector face equals
the host twin bit for bit (class D).
`time_varying_mapped_refusals_are_by_name` - 11 refusals, each naming the
condition and this section. 4 of 4 in each build. The four existing kernels
of `function1.cubin` are SASS-identical in both builds; two are added.

* **Bowyer, A.** Computing Dirichlet tessellations. *Comput. J.* 24 (1981)
  162-166, doi:10.1093/comjnl/24.2.162 - the incremental insertion.
* **Watson, D. F.** Computing the n-dimensional Delaunay tessellation with
  application to Voronoi polytopes. *Comput. J.* 24 (1981) 167-172,
  doi:10.1093/comjnl/24.2.167 - the circumcircle cavity and its refill.
* **Delaunay, B.** Sur la sphere vide. *Bull. Acad. Sci. URSS, Classe Sci.
  Math. Nat.* 6 (1934) 793-800 - the empty-circle property.
* **Andrew, A. M.** Another efficient algorithm for convex hulls in two
  dimensions. *Inf. Process. Lett.* 9 (1979) 216-219,
  doi:10.1016/0020-0190(79)90072-3 - the monotone chain of the net check.

No GPL-licensed source was consulted.

### 120.12 The synthetic LES inflow - a digital filter and divergence-free eddies with a prescribed Reynolds stress

BC-16 implements the two synthetic-inflow names of the §120 table,
`turbulentDigitalFilterInlet` and `turbulentDFSEMInlet`. The names are taken
from the user guides of §120 by name only; every equation below is cited, or
is ours and marked DESIGN.

Both are a §4 FIXED VALUE (`BcKind::FixedValue`, `fr = 1`, `refGrad = 0`) on
a VECTOR field whose `refValue` a kernel rewrites once per TIME step - no new
evaluation branch (§5.2 of the completion plan). On a scalar field both names
are refused as vector conditions. The face value is the mean velocity `UMean`
plus a fluctuation `u'` whose one-point covariance is the prescribed Reynolds
stress `R`. Both draws are counter-based, so a run with the same `seed` draws
the same inflow, and a captured graph advances them (§81): the rule's state
`[n, X]` - the last step drawn and the distance convected - lives on the
device and is moved on by a one-thread kernel after the per-face one.

**The opt-in.** It is `BcInputs::turbulent_inlet`, the one `turbulentInlet`
uses (§120.10): the caller draws once per time step, through
`field_ops::advance_synthetic_inlet_vector(gpu, k, U, dt)`, which
`Simple::begin_time_step` calls with its `dt`. No driver passes the opt-in
today - the steady modes of `ofgpu-lowmach` and `ofgpu-buoyant` call
`begin_time_step` every outer iteration, which would redraw the inflow every
iteration - so every driver refuses both names by name, as BC-14 recorded for
`turbulentInlet`. A transient driver path that passes `turbulent_inlet = true`
makes them usable in a run.

**The draw** *(DESIGN - ours)*. With `mix` the SplitMix64 finaliser of
`z + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15` (Steele, Lea & Flood 2014) and `w_0 = 0x243F6A8885A308D3`:

```
h = mix(seed ^ w_0); h = mix(h ^ t); h = mix(h ^ a); h = mix(h ^ b);
h = mix(h ^ c); h = mix(h ^ d);   u = (h >> 11) / 2^53,
eps(t, a, b, c, d) = sqrt(3) (2u - 1)                                 (120.12a)
```

zero mean and unit variance; the digital filter uses the tag `t = 1`, the
eddies `t = 2`. Signed integers enter as their two's-complement words.

**The patch frame** *(DESIGN - ours)*. With the f64 face centres `x_f`, unit
outward normals `n_f` and areas `|S_f|` (§118.2):

```
nin = -SUM |S_f| n_f / |SUM |S_f| n_f|,   x0 = mean of x_f,
e_y = the global axis (x, y, z order) other than the one most aligned with
      nin, projected on the plane and normalised;  e_z = nin x e_y,
eta_f = e_y . (x_f - x0),   zeta_f = e_z . (x_f - x0)                 (120.12b)
```

and the patch must be planar: every `|nin . (x_f - x0)|` at most `1e-6` of
the patch diagonal in `(eta, zeta)`, or the name is refused. A face normal
to `x` gives `e_y = y`, `e_z = z`.

**The digital filter** (Klein, Sadiki & Janicka 2003). The plane carries a
lattice of `ny x nz` nodes (`planeDivisions`) spanning the face centres'
`(eta, zeta)` range, spacing `Delta_y = (eta_max - eta_min)/(ny - 1)` (zero
when `ny = 1`) and the same in `z`; each face takes its nearest node. Time is
the third lattice direction through Taylor's hypothesis, spacing
`Delta_x = Ubulk dt`. For a length `L` and spacing `Delta`, Klein's filter:

```
n = L/Delta,   N = ceil(2n),   b~_k = exp(-pi k^2 / (2 n^2)),
b_k = b~_k / sqrt(SUM_{j=-N}^{N} b~_j^2),   k = -N..N                 (120.12c)
```

(`n = 0` gives `b_0 = 1`). Component `c` of the filtered field at step `n`,
node `(j, k)`, is the separable sum over a random lattice:

```
u'_c = SUM_a bt_a SUM_b by_b SUM_d bz_d eps(1, n + a, j + b, k + d, c)  (120.12d)
```

each filter of (120.12c) with component `c`'s length in that direction -
`L` is component-major, `(L_ux L_uy L_uz L_vx ... L_wz)`, its direction index
`x` the streamwise `nin`, `y` and `z` the frame's `e_y` and `e_z`; the
components are the global ones. `u'` has zero mean and unit variance per
component (`SUM b^2 = 1` in each direction). The prescribed stress follows
from Lund, Wu & Squires (1998)'s transformation:

```
u = UMean + a u',   a = the lower Cholesky factor of R:
a11 = sqrt(R11), a21 = R21/a11, a22 = sqrt(R22 - a21^2), a31 = R31/a11,
a32 = (R32 - a21 a31)/a22, a33 = sqrt(R33 - a31^2 - a32^2)            (120.12e)
```

so `E[(u - UMean)(u - UMean)^T] = a a^T = R`. A zero pivot whose column is
zero gives a zero column (a stress with a vanishing component); an `R` that
is not positive semi-definite is refused by name. The correlation of `u'_c`
at a lag of `k` lattice cells in one direction is `rho(k) = SUM_j b_j b_{j+k}`,
and by the Poisson sum `SUM_k rho(k) = (SUM_j b_j)^2 = 2n` to within
`exp(-2 pi)` truncation, so the one-sided integral length is

```
Delta (rho(0)/2 + SUM_{k>=1} rho(k)) = n Delta = L                   (120.12f)
```

- the prescribed length, for every component the Cholesky mixing leaves
unmixed (`a_cj = 0` for `j < c`), and a mixture of lengths otherwise. The
first time step's `dt` sets the time filter, so the setup's seed face value
is `UMean`; each launch re-forms the time filter from its own `dt` (a change
of `dt` changes the time correlation from that step on). A filter half-width
above 128 cells, or more than `2^22` taps of one component a face, is refused
by name (at setup for the plane, at the launch for time).

**The divergence-free eddies** (the idea is Poletto, Craft & Revell 2013: a
sum of eddies, each a radial shape times `r x alpha`, divergence-free by
construction, with intensities from the Reynolds stress; the spherical shape,
its constant and the intensity rule below are *DESIGN - ours*). With `N`
eddies of radius `sigma` in a box of volume `V_B`:

```
u'(x) = sqrt(V_B / (N sigma^3)) SUM_k F(|r_k|^2) (r_k x alpha_k),
r_k = (x - x_k)/sigma,   F(q) = (1 - q)^2 for q < 1, 0 otherwise    (120.12g)
```

`F` and `F'` vanish at `q = 1`, so `u'` is C1. Each term is divergence-free:
with `d = r_k`, `div (F(|d|^2) d x alpha) = 2 F'(q) d . (d x alpha)/sigma +
F div(d x alpha) = 0`, both terms zero for any `alpha`:

```
div u' = SUM_k 2 F'(|r_k|^2) r_k . (r_k x alpha_k) / sigma = 0        (120.12h)
```

exactly, because the shape is radial and `sigma` is one number per eddy (an
eddy stretched differently per direction would lose this). With the eddy
centres uniform in a box that holds every face's support ball, independent
`alpha_k` of zero mean and covariance `A`, and
`eps_ijl eps_mjp = delta_lp delta_im - delta_lm delta_ip`:

```
E[u' u'^T] = G (tr A I - A),
G = (1/3) INT F(|r|^2)^2 |r|^2 d^3r = (4 pi/3) INT_0^1 r^4 (1 - r^2)^4 dr
  = (4 pi/3)(128/15015) = 512 pi/45045 = 0.0357082...                 (120.12i)
```

(the sum `1/5 - 4/7 + 6/9 - 4/11 + 1/13 = 128/15015`). Inverting,
`tr R = 2 G tr A`, so

```
A = (tr R/2 I - R) / G,   alpha_k = C eps_k,   C = chol(A)            (120.12j)
```

with `eps_k` three draws of (120.12a). `A` is positive semi-definite exactly
when every principal stress is at most the sum of the other two,
`lambda_i <= lambda_j + lambda_k`; an `R` outside that set - for example the
strongly one-component stress near a wall - is refused by name, naming
(120.12j). The limit is this design's own, derived here; Poletto, Craft &
Revell's abstract says their method reproduces almost all states of
anisotropy, and their own intensity rule is not used.
The box and the convection:

```
s in [-sigma, sigma),  eta in [eta_min - sigma, eta_max + sigma),
zeta in [zeta_min - sigma, zeta_max + sigma),  V_B = 2 sigma W_eta W_zeta;
eddy k:  s0_k = -sigma + 2 sigma u(2, k, 0, 0, 0),  w = s0_k + sigma + X,
g = floor(w / (2 sigma)),  s_k = -sigma + (w - 2 sigma g),
eta_k, zeta_k from u(2, k, g, 1|2, 0),  eps_k from eps(2, k, g, 3..5, 0),
x_k = x0 + s_k nin + eta_k e_y + zeta_k e_z,
X^n = fma(Ubulk, dt, X^(n-1))                                         (120.12k)
```

so an eddy is carried downstream at `Ubulk` and, on leaving at `s = sigma`,
re-enters at `s = -sigma` with a new place across the plane and a new
`alpha`: the streamwise positions stay uniform and the field is stationary.
`nEddy` defaults to `ceil(V_B / sigma^3)` (about four eddies over a point)
and is capped at `2^20`. The setup's seed is (120.12g) at `X = 0`.

**Entries** (this solver's own names; each constant, refused by name when
missing, not finite or of the wrong length). Both: `R` `(xx xy xz yy yz zz)`,
`UMean` (a vector), `Ubulk` (optional, `UMean . nin` when absent; it must be
positive), `seed` (optional, 0). The filter: `L` (nine lengths) and
`planeDivisions` `(ny nz)`. The eddies: `sigma` (positive) and `nEddy`
(optional). Profiles of `R` or `UMean` are not built.

**Precision.** Everything is f64 in both builds - the draw, the filter sums,
the eddy sums and the state - and each face value rounds once into `Scalar`
(§118). The host twins `field::synthetic::df_values` and `dfsem_values` run
in the device kernels' operation order; the device contracts FMAs and its
`exp` is not the host's, so the two agree to round-off.

**Tests** (`tests/bc_synthetic.rs`, both builds; the statistics run on the f64
host twins and are class P, the device rows class R; [brackets] are the
single build).
`digital_filter_reproduces_r_and_l` - a 40 x 40 lattice of unit cells,
400 steps of `Ubulk dt = 1`, `R = (1 0.3 0 0.5 0 0.25)`, lengths `u (2, 1.5,
2.5)`, `v 1.5`, `w (1.5, 2.5, 1.5)`: every `R_ij` within 0.56 % [0.56 %] of
`sqrt(R_ii R_jj)` (band 5 %); the integral lengths of `u` and `w` in time,
`e_y` and `e_z` within 0.78-2.48 % [the same] (band 10 %).
`dfsem_reproduces_r` - a 2 x 2 plane of 32 x 32 faces, `sigma = 0.25`, 191
eddies, 6000 steps of `Ubulk dt = 0.05`, `R = (0.8 0.1 0.05 0.6 0.05 0.5)`:
every `R_ij` within 0.44 % [0.44 %] (band 5 %).
`dfsem_is_divergence_free` - at 1979 points over 20 convected distances,
`|div u'| / max|grad u'|` at most 6.5e-16 [6.5e-16] (bound 1e-10), and the
analytic gradient equals central differences of the velocity to 6.3e-10
[6.3e-10] of `max|grad u'|` (bound 1e-5).
`synthetic_device_matches_host` - an 8 x 8 inlet, 6 steps of `dt = 0.025`:
the filter's device faces equal the twin to 3.3e-16 [0] of `max|u'|`,
the eddies' to 6.9e-16 [0] (<= 1e-12, class R; the single build rounds both to the same f32); the seeds are `UMean`
and the `X = 0` field, bit for bit.
`synthetic_refusals_name_their_reason` - no opt-in, a scalar field, an
unrealisable `R` for the eddies (accepted by the filter), an `R` that is not
positive semi-definite, a missing `L`, a bulk velocity out of the domain.
The correlation-length gate is the filter's: the eddies prescribe a radius,
not a length, and their two-point correlation is what (120.12g) makes of it.

* **Klein, M., Sadiki, A. & Janicka, J.** A digital filter based generation
  of inflow data for spatially developing direct numerical or large eddy
  simulations. *J. Comput. Phys.* 186 (2003) 652-665,
  doi:10.1016/S0021-9991(03)00090-1 - the Gaussian filter (120.12c) and the
  filtered random lattice in space and, through Taylor's hypothesis, time.
* **Lund, T. S., Wu, X. & Squires, K. D.** Generation of turbulent inflow data
  for spatially-developing boundary layer simulations. *J. Comput. Phys.* 140

  (120.12e).
* **Poletto, R., Craft, T. & Revell, A.** A new divergence free synthetic

### 120.13 `cyclicAMI` - a static arbitrary mesh interface, imprinted into a conformal cyclic as the mesh is read (BC-19)

A `cyclicAMI` pair couples two patches that cover the same surface with
faces that do not match. This solver has no interpolation weights; instead
`io::polymesh::read_poly_mesh` imprints every such pair with §120.18's
`mesh::imprint::imprint` before anything else sees the mesh, so the pair
leaves the reader as two conformal patches written face for face, which is
what every cyclic is downstream (§31.1): `PatchKind::Cyclic`, the
`nbr_patch` index, `cyclic_pairing` by position, the §31.1 invariants in
`build_host_mesh`, and every coupled kernel branch, none of them changed.
The field name `cyclicAMI` is `BcKind::Cyclic` (it is in
`IMPLEMENTED_BC_NAMES`, catalogue row implemented). The patch keeps its
type string `cyclicAMI` verbatim. The type names `cyclicAMI`,
`neighbourPatch` and `transform rotational` are taken by name only from the
public user guides of §120; no AMI code was opened.

**The reader.** For each `cyclicAMI` patch `k` whose `neighbourPatch` names
patch `j`: `j` must be `cyclicAMI` and must name `k` back, else the boundary
file is refused by name; a `transform rotational` on either side is refused
by name, because a cyclic pair here maps one side onto the other by a
translation only (§31.1); the patch that comes first in the file is `A`. A
missing or unknown `neighbourPatch` falls to §31.1's own refusal. An imprint
refusal (§120.18: a partial overlap is `cyclicACMI`, a non-planar face, ...)
is reported with the boundary file's path and the pair. Reading the written
imprint again re-imprints a matching pair: no new point, the same face and
patch counts.

**The map handed to the imprint** ((120.18.1) with `R = I`). With `X_P` the
area centroid of patch `P` (each face fanned into triangles about its vertex
mean, each triangle at the mean of its three points with area `|Newell|/2`),
`S_A` the summed area vector of `A` and `n_A = S_A/|S_A|`:

```
t = 0            if |(y - X_A) . n_A| <= tau for every point y of B   (120.13a)
t = X_A - X_B    otherwise
```

with §120.18's `tau`. Two blocks that meet are coplanar and get the identity
exactly, so an in-plane offset stays an offset and is refused by the
coverage rule (120.18.5) as `cyclicACMI`; a periodic pair is translated by
the centroid difference, the translation §31.1's invariant check recovers.
The stated limit: an in-plane offset of a PERIODIC pair is read as part of
its translation.

**A moving mesh.** The imprint is made once, from the points at rest.
`HostMesh::refuse_a_moving_cyclic_ami(who)` refuses any mesh with a
`cyclicAMI` patch by name, naming `who` and the patch, and both moving-mesh
entry points call it first: `MeshMotion::new` (§105.9) and `AleMesh::new`.

**The coupled separation.** `mesh/geometry.rs` measures a coupled face
through both halves, `d = (Cf_own - C_P) + (C_N - Cf_nbr)`, and stores
`Delta = 1/(n . d)` and `k = n - d Delta` (§2.4). The device least-squares
gradient (§3.5, `fvGradScalarLeastSquares`, `boundarySeparation` in
`cuda/fv.cu`) uses for a coupled face

```
d_dev = Sf / (|Sf| Delta) = n (n . d) = d + k / Delta                 (120.13b)
```

the normal projection of `d`, which is `d` itself only where the couple is
orthogonal. On an imprinted 3:2 interface the sub-face pairs are skewed, so
the fit (§3.5, `w = 1/|d|^2`)

```
G = sum_f w d d^T,   b = sum_f w d (psi_N - psi_P),   grad = G^-1 b   (120.13c)
```

with `d_dev` in place of `d` is not exact for a linear field there. This
unit does not change it: the cure (`d = d_dev - k/Delta` in the kernel) moves
the coupled least-squares result of every non-orthogonal cyclic, an existing
path, and is the user's decision (docs/17 §5.3.4).

**The gate (`tests/bc_cyclic_ami.rs`, both builds).** Block A is
`[0,1] x [0,1]` with 8 x 12 cells, block B `[1,2] x [0,1]` with 8 x 8 (the 3:2
interface `amiA`/`amiB` at `x = 1`) or 8 x 12 (a conformal one); the ends
`perA`/`perB` are a second 3:2 `cyclicAMI` pair, translated by 2. Each mesh
is written by `write_poly_mesh_raw` and read back by `read_poly_mesh`. The
channel is laminar, `nu = 0.01`, driven by the body force `0.12` along `x`
(bulk 1, Re 100), `p = 0` on `lowA`, SIMPLE to a cell change below `1e-14`
(4000 at most); the single blocks are §31.1 periodic channels of 16 x 12 and
16 x 8 cells over `[0,2] x [0,1]`. `tol(t)` is `t` in f64 and D-F32-1's
`max(t, min(t 2^29, 1e-5))` under `single`.

| row | claim | class | f64 | single |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pairs | each 3:2 pair 16 + 16 sub-faces on one layer, mutual `nbr_patch`, kind cyclic, type `cyclicAMI`, area 0.1 to `tol(1e-12)`; 160 cells; a second read keeps the counts | D, R | pass | pass |
| refusals | `transform rotational`; a `cyclicAMI` facing a `cyclic`; B lifted 0.1 (`cyclicACMI`, through the reader); a moving mesh at both entry points | D | pass | pass |
| oracle | (120.13c) with `d` over the coupled stencil, `psi = (1.7, -0.9, 0.35) . x + 0.42`, two layers: `max |g - a|/|a| <= 1e-11` | A | 2.4e-15 | 2.4e-15 |
| device LS, off the interface | `<= tol(1e-11)` | R | 2.4e-15 | 9.8e-7 |
| device LS, at the interface | `<= 1e-11` - **MISSED** 5.1e-2; the device equals its (120.13b) twin to `tol(1e-11)` (2.4e-16 / 1.6e-7), which is the cause | R | MISSED | MISSED |
| flux | each pair, `max |phi_A + phi_B| <= tol(1e-14) max |phi_A|` | R | 1.5e-16, 4.2e-15 of max | 0 |
| conformal AMI | both block columns against the 16 x 12 single block, `<= tol(1e-12)` of the peak | R | 3.0e-16 | 2.4e-7 |
| 3:2 channel | each block's middle column (`x = 0.4375`, `1.5625`) against the single block of its own `ny`, `<= 0.5 %` of the peak - **MISSED** 6.7 % and 7.5 % | P | MISSED | MISSED |

The 3:2 channel's bulk is 0.959 and 0.963 against the single blocks' 1.014
(ny 12) and 1.031 (ny 8), whose own departures from Poiseuille
`1.5 (1 - (2y - 1)^2)` are 0.69 % and 1.56 % of the peak. The conformal AMI
pair matching the single block to round-off through the same reader,
imprint, field name and coupling says the miss is the discretisation of a
skewed coupled face, not the wiring: the face value is the linear
interpolation along `d` with no skewness correction, and the gradients its
non-orthogonal correction reads are not exact across it ((120.13b)). Under
`single` every SIMPLE loop stops on the 4000 cap (the f32 SIMPLE floor of
the BC-07 family); the f64 loops stop on the change after 1439 (3:2), 1786
(conformal, ny 12) and 1623 (ny 8) iterations.

### 120.14 The VOF family - a clamped phase fraction, a liquid flow rate, a phase-weighted outlet and a phase-weighted hydrostatic level (BC-21)

BC-21 implements the four VOF names of the §120 table:
`variableHeightFlowRate`, `variableHeightFlowRateInletVelocity`,
`outletPhaseMeanVelocity` and `phaseHydrostaticPressure`. The names, and the
entry keys `lowerBound`, `upperBound`, `flowRate`, `Umean`, `alpha`, `rho`,
`pRefValue`, `pRefPoint` and `phaseFraction`, are taken from the user guides
of §120 by name only; no description, formula or source was read. Every
equation below is ours (*DESIGN*), written on the phase fraction of §20.1,
the mixture density of §20.3 and the `p_rgh` decomposition of §20.5 and
(120.7a). Each is a §4 triple with no new evaluation branch and no kernel:
the phase fraction's clamp and the hydrostatic level ride `BcKind::Mixed`,
the two velocities `BcKind::FixedValue`, and what is new is that the triple
FOLLOWS the liquid - it is rewritten from the current `alpha` once per time
step.

**The face phase fraction.** With `alpha_b,f` the evaluated face value of
the solver's phase fraction, the weight the last three conditions use is

```
a_f = clamp(alpha_b,f, 0, 1)
```

so a round-off excursion of `alpha` out of `[0, 1]` cannot make a weight
negative. `S_f` is the outward face area vector, `|S_f|` its magnitude,
`n_f = S_f/|S_f|` (both f64 from `geom64`, §118.2) and `P` the cell behind
the face.

```
variableHeightFlowRate (on alpha), 0 <= l <= u <= 1:
    alpha_P > u :  fr = 1, refValue = u
    alpha_P < l :  fr = 1, refValue = l                                   (120.14a)
    otherwise   :  fr = 0              (refGrad = 0 throughout)
  => alpha_b,f = clamp(alpha_P, l, u)

variableHeightFlowRateInletVelocity (on U), the liquid rate Q > 0 into the domain:
    D   = sum_f a_f^2 |S_f|
    U_f = -n_f (a_f Q / D)          (U_f = 0 on every face when D = 0)    (120.14b)
  => -sum_f a_f (U_f . S_f) = Q

outletPhaseMeanVelocity (on U), the phase-weighted mean outward velocity Umean:
    A   = sum_f a_f |S_f|,   M = sum_f a_f (U_P . n_f) |S_f|
    U_f = U_P + (Umean - M/A) n_f   (U_f = U_P when A = 0)                (120.14c)
  => sum_f a_f (U_f . n_f) |S_f| / A = Umean

phaseHydrostaticPressure (on p_rgh), the phase density rho, p_ref at x_ref:
    fr = a_f,  refGrad = 0
    refValue = (p_ref + rho g . (x_f - x_ref)) - rho_f g . (x_f - O)     (120.14d)
```

(120.14a) bounds the face value: inside `[l, u]` the face is zero-gradient
and the height of the liquid at the patch follows the interior; outside it
the face is held at the bound crossed. With `fr` exactly 0 or 1, §4's
`fr r + (1 - fr) alpha_P` is the clamp bit for bit. (120.14b) makes the
inflow velocity proportional to the face's liquid fraction - a dry face
takes in nothing, so the gas above a liquid inlet is not pushed in - and
normalises it so the LIQUID flux, the alpha-weighted face flux, is exactly
`Q`; the identity follows from `n_f . S_f = |S_f|`. (120.14c) keeps the
outlet's cell profile and shifts its normal component by one constant, so
the liquid's area-weighted mean outflow velocity is exactly `Umean` - the
outlet takes the liquid at the rate it is given and the free surface finds
the level that carries it. (120.14d) is (120.7e) with `rhoRef = rho`, made
Dirichlet only where the phase is: in it (`a_f = 1`, `rho_f = rho`) the face
holds `p = p_ref + rho g . (x_f - x_ref)`, the phase's own hydrostatic
column, written in the solved `p_rgh` exactly as (120.7e) writes it -
`x_f - x_ref` in world coordinates, `x_f - O` the stored centre the
solver's body force reads (§118.7); out of it (`a_f = 0`) the face is
zero-gradient; a mixed face is weighted between the two. `rho_f` is the
face's mixture density, the value `update_properties` writes from the
face's current `alpha` (§20.3).

**When the triples are written** *(DESIGN - ours)*. `Vof::refresh_vof_family`
rewrites every VOF-family patch once per time step, at the start of
`Vof::step` after the flux-switched fractions and before any boundary value
is evaluated, and first in `Vof::initialise_flux_from_velocity` and
`Vof::initialise` (so the first step's inlet flux is the condition's, and
the pressure-pinning test reads the written `fr`). In order: (120.14a) on
`alpha` from its cells and `alpha`'s faces re-evaluated; then (120.14b) and
(120.14c) on `U` from those faces (and `U`'s cells); then `rho` refreshed
to those faces and (120.14d) on `p_rgh`, after which the pressure reference
is re-decided - a phase-weighted Dirichlet fixes the level only where the
phase is. The refresh runs on the HOST: each field carrying a rule is
downloaded, rewritten on the rule's faces and uploaded; a run with none of
the four names returns at once and is bit for bit what it was. All
arithmetic is f64 from the widened `Scalar` inputs and the f64 `geom64`
face data, sums in face order, each triple entry rounded once into
`Scalar` (§118.2); the operation order is the order written above, `g . d =
g_x d_x + g_y d_y + g_z d_z`. The two rates are constants: `flowRate` and
`Umean` are read through §120.1's Function1 reader, and a time-varying one
is refused, because the refresh runs from the solver's state and no clock.

The liquid flux the alpha equation transports through the inlet is
`phi_b alpha_b` (§20.2's low-order boundary flux), where `phi_b = U_f . S_f`
is the flux the previous step's pressure correction prescribed. It equals
`Q` exactly when the inlet's `alpha_b` does not change from one step to the
next - every face of a (120.14a) inlet held at a bound, or a fixed-value
inlet `alpha` - and with one alpha sub-cycle per step; a free face inside
the bounds moves the transported rate off `Q` by the step's change in
`alpha_b`, the one-step lag every explicit boundary update carries, and
sub-cycles move `alpha_b` within the step. The face flux is deliberately
NOT rewritten before the alpha solve: a boundary flux changed without the
interior flux that balances it would break §20.2's boundedness.

**Inputs and refusals.** `BcInputs::vof_family: Option<&str>` names the
solver's phase-fraction field; `ofgpu-vof` passes it for `alpha`, `U` and
`p_rgh`, and every other setup passes `None`. Refused by name, each message
naming the condition and "SPEC-LIT 120.14": any of the four with
`vof_family = None` (a seed nothing rewrites would freeze a rate or a level
the name promises follows the liquid, §13.4); `variableHeightFlowRate` on
any field but the phase fraction and `phaseHydrostaticPressure` on any
field but `p_rgh`; a velocity name on a scalar field and a scalar name on a
vector field; a missing `lowerBound`, `upperBound`, `flowRate`, `Umean`,
`rho`, `pRefValue` or `pRefPoint`; bounds outside `0 <= l <= u <= 1`; a
time-varying `flowRate` or `Umean`; an `alpha` or `phaseFraction` entry
naming any field but the solver's phase fraction.

Not taken: §120.7 left the per-step refresh of the four buoyant-pressure
names' `rho_f` to this unit. Refreshing them would change what an existing
`prghPressure` run computes wherever the face's `alpha` moves, which is a
numerics change of an existing path (docs/17 §5.3.4) and the user's
decision; they keep their setup-time `rho_f`.

**Gates** (`tests/bc_vof_family.rs`, both builds; class per docs/17 §5.1,
D-F32-1, R rows at `max(t, min(2^29 t, 1e-5))`).

`vof_family_triples_are_the_closed_forms` - a 4 x 3 x 2 box: every rule's
face data is the mesh's (cells, normals, areas, both centres, class D); a
cell `alpha` visiting all three branches of (120.14a) gives its `fr`,
`refValue` and the clamp bit for bit; a face `alpha` with values 1.25 and
-0.125 among them gives (120.14b), (120.14c) and (120.14d) bit for bit
against an oracle in the same order (class D); the inlet carries `Q` = 0.3
to 0 (f64; `single` 1.0e-8) and the outlet's phase mean is 0.25 to 2.2e-16
(`single` 9.1e-9) relative (class R); a dry patch writes 0 and the cell
value. `vof_family_refusals_are_by_name` - every refusal above (class D).
`a_channel_fed_at_a_variable_height_carries_the_liquid_rate` - THE gate:
`Vof` on a 24 x 1 x 12 channel 2 x 1, water (1000) under air (1) to z =
0.5, fed on `xMin` by (120.14b) at `Q = 0.1 x 0.5 x (1/12)` with
(120.14a) at `[0.05, 0.95]` on `alpha`, drained on `xMax` by (120.14c) at
`Umean` 0.1, a slip floor and an open top (`prghPressure p 1000`), 20 steps
of 5e-3 with one sub-cycle: the liquid the alpha equation transports
through the inlet each step is `Q` within 1.0e-15 relative (`single`
2.6e-8), the inlet identity within 1.0e-15 (`single` 4.1e-9), the outlet's
phase mean within 2.8e-16 (`single` 3.4e-8), `alpha_b` on the inlet is the
clamp exactly, and `alpha` stays in `[-5.3e-23, 1 + 1.5e-13]` (`single`
`[-2.8e-14, 1 + 7.2e-6]`), all against 1e-12 (class R).
`a_tank_open_at_a_phase_hydrostatic_side_stays_at_rest` - a 24 x 1 x 24
tank, water under air to z = 0.5, `prghPressure p 1000` on the top and
(120.14d) with `rho 1000`, `pRefValue 1004.905` and `pRefPoint (0 0 0.5)`
on the side `xMax` (the column's level at the interface): wet side faces
are Dirichlet, dry ones zero-gradient; after 20 steps of 2.5e-4 `max |U|`
is 1.2e-13 and `p = p_rgh + rho (g . x)` is the two-layer column within
1.1e-12 of 5705.53 (`single` 4.6e-6 and 7.6e-4, 1.3e-7 relative; class R);
the control - `pRefValue 1000`, 4.905 Pa short - moves at 8.5e-4. Four
tests, four pass in each build; the driver knob test
`phase_hydrostatic_pressure_on_the_atmosphere_changes_what_the_run_writes`
(`ofgpu-vof` on the dam break's dry atmosphere) runs and changes what the
run writes.

* **Hirt, C. W. & Nichols, B. D.** "Volume of fluid (VOF) method for the
  dynamics of free boundaries", *J. Comput. Phys.* 39 (1981) 201-225,
  doi:10.1016/0021-9991(81)90145-5 - the phase fraction whose face value
  weights every condition here.
* **Rusche, H.** *Computational Fluid Dynamics of Dispersed Two-Phase Flows
  at High Phase Fractions*, PhD thesis, Imperial College London (2002) -
  the modified pressure `p - rho (g . x)` the hydrostatic level is written
  in, as in §120.7.
