### 120.15 The species family - a film mass-transfer coefficient through a baffle and to a reservoir (CHR-29)

*DESIGN, with the film law from the literature.* `semiPermeableBaffleMassFraction`
and `specieTransfer` are two §4 triple rewrites on the solved members of a
species set (§19, §86). Their names are taken by name only (§120's rule); the
law they apply is the defining relation of a mass-transfer coefficient (Bird,
Stewart & Lightfoot, §22.1): a flux proportional to a concentration
difference, the coefficient carrying everything between the two values. The
entries are ours: `c`, the film coefficient in m/s (required, finite, `>= 0`;
`c = 0` holds the species back), `neighbourPatch` on a baffle, and `Yinf` on
`specieTransfer` (default 0).

The outward flux of the transported quantity through a face `f` of the patch
is taken between the two cell values adjacent to the baffle, or between the
cell and the reservoir:

```
semiPermeableBaffleMassFraction:  n_f = c (Y_P - Y_N)                      (120.15a)
specieTransfer:                   n_f = c (Y_P - Y_inf)                    (120.15b)
```

per unit area on the constant-density equation of §19. On the mass-weighted
equation of §86 they are `rho_m c (...)`: at a `specieTransfer` face `rho_m =
rho_b`, the face density the assembly already multiplies the diffusivity by;
at a baffle face `rho_m = (rho_b + rho_b,partner)/2`, the same number on the
two sides, so the two sides' film laws are one law. `Y_N` is the value of the
cell behind face `j` of the partner patch: a baffle's two patches pair face
`j` with face `j`, as a cyclic's do, and must have the same size, coincident
face centres (within `1e-6 sqrt(|S_f|)`), the same condition naming each
other, and the same `c` bit for bit, or the flux leaving one side is not the
flux entering the other. Because the driving difference is taken between the
two CELL values, `1/c` is the whole resistance between the two cell centres:
the two half-cells beside the baffle are inside it, not in series with it. A
case that knows a membrane's own coefficient `k_m` and wants the half-cells
in series gives `c = 1/(1/k_m + d_P/D + d_N/D)` itself, `d_P` and `d_N` the two
cell-centre-to-face distances.

The triple that makes the laplacian apply exactly that flux follows from
§4's `snGrad_b = fr Delta_b (psi_ref - psi_P) + (1 - fr) g_ref`:

```
fr = c (rho_m/rho_b) / (Gamma_b Delta_b),   psi_ref = Y_N (or Y_inf),   g_ref = 0   (120.15c)
Gamma_b = nu/Pr + nu_t,b/Pr_t
```

with `rho_m/rho_b = 1` on the constant-density equation and at a
`specieTransfer` face (the factor is then not formed),

and `Gamma_b` formed as `turbGammaBoundary` forms it from the species'
`Pr = nu/D` and `Pr_t = Sc_t`, so `rho_b Gamma_b |S_f| snGrad_b = rho_m c
|S_f| (Y_N - Y_P)` (and without the densities on the constant-density
equation) to round-off. `fr` may exceed 1 when `c > Gamma_b Delta_b`; the matrix
coefficient stays `c |S_f| > 0` and the face value is then the linear
extrapolation that carries that gradient. `c = 0` gives `fr = 0` and `g_ref =
0` exactly: a zero-gradient face whose matrix contribution is exactly zero.
A species with `D = 0` is refused a positive `c` (its half-cell has no
laminar conductance to carry it). Only a plain patch or a wall carries one;
an empty, symmetry or coupled patch is refused by name.

`Species::setup_member` lowers a member's raw field: a field without either
name goes to `setup_scalar_field` unchanged, so a member set up that way is
set up exactly as before; each carrying patch is set up as `zeroGradient`,
its faces are marked `Mixed`, and a rule (patch, face range, partner range,
`c`, `Y_inf`) is kept. `Species::correct_with_density` rewrites every rule's
triple by (120.15c) in one `spcTransferTriple` launch per patch, from the
fields as they stand and the call's `nu_t`, before that species' own solve:
`Y_P` is implicit, `Y_N` is the partner cell's value at the rewrite, the
explicit half of §4's rewrite. The two sides of a baffle therefore carry
equal and opposite fluxes at a steady state and differ by `c |S_f|` (`rho_m c
|S_f|`) times the sum of the two cells' changes over the step in a transient - exact transient
conservation across the baffle would need the baffle as an implicit coupled
entry (§47.3's interface), which this unit does not build. A set without a
rule launches nothing, and the arithmetic of every other species path is the
one it was. `ofgpu-lowmach`'s reacting set (§133.11) sets its members up
through `setup_member`, and writes a baffle's `neighbourPatch` back out.

**The generic reader refuses both names by name.** `BcKind::from_name` has
one arm for the pair, whose note says the condition is lowered only on a
solved member of a species set: on a case without species, or on a field
outside the set (`T`, `U`, the inert remainder), the case is refused naming
the condition, the field and the patch, and `-permissive` substitutes
`zeroGradient`, an impermeable wall. That is why the two rows stay **owned**
by CHR-29 in the table, as CMP-16/17/18's and BC-20's kinds stay owned or
planned while their own lowering path accepts them: `from_name` refuses them
and the species set lowers them.

For the 1-D slab of the gate - `N = 16` cells of `h = 1/16` m, the baffle
between cells 7 and 8, `Y = 1` and `Y = 0` held at the two ends - the profile
is linear in each half, which the finite-volume discretisation reproduces
exactly, and the series resistances from the two end faces to the cell
centres beside the baffle give

```
J = (Y_left - Y_right) / (15 h / D + 1/c)                                  (120.15d)
```

**Gates** (`tests/species_bc.rs`, both builds; class R tolerances are
D-F32-1's `max(t, min(t 2^29, 1e-5))` under `single`):

| test | class | what it holds | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `species_semipermeable_baffle_flux` | R | species A (`c = 1e-4`, `D = 2e-5`) marched to steady state at `dt = 1e7` s: `c (Y_7 - Y_8)`, every interior face's `D (Y_i - Y_i+1)/h` and both end faces' fluxes equal (120.15d)'s `J = 1.758242e-5` to 1e-12 relative; species B (`c = 0`) has `fr = +0` and `g_ref = +0` bit for bit on both baffle faces and relaxes to uniform on each side | 1.657e-14 (f64), 7.653e-6 (f32, tol 1e-5) |

### 120.18 Imprinting a static non-conformal interface - two patches clipped into one conformal pair (BC-18)

`cyclicAMI` is accepted on it since BC-19 (§120.13); this subsection is the
mesh operation §120.13 builds on. `mesh::imprint::imprint(raw, a, b, opts)` takes a
`PolyMeshRaw` and two of its patches, `A` and `B`, whose faces cover the same
surface but do not match, and returns a new `PolyMeshRaw` in which both
patches are replaced by SUB-FACES: every overlapping pair `(a, b)` of an `A`
face and a `B` face gives one sub-face on each side, the sub-face `i` of `A`
and the sub-face `i` of `B` are the same polygon, and every cell that owned
an `A` or `B` face becomes a polyhedron whose faces still close. The operation
is static (it runs once, before the solver, on the host) and all of its
arithmetic is `f64` in both builds: `PolyMeshRaw::points` is `DVec3`
(§118.2), and nothing is rounded to `Scalar`.

**Source.** The clipping is the reentrant polygon clipper of **Sutherland &
Hodgman, "Reentrant polygon clipping", Communications of the ACM 17(1):32-42,
1974, doi:10.1145/360767.360802** (ACM Digital Library, open archive); the
plane frame, the Newell area vector and the edge splitting are elementary
vector geometry. No AMI, imprint or mesh-intersection code was opened.

**The transform.** `B` may sit elsewhere (a cyclic pair): a rigid map takes a
point `y` of `B` into the frame of `A`,

```
x = T(y) = R y + t,     T^-1(x) = R^T (x - t),     R^T R = I   (120.18.1)
```

with `R` checked orthonormal to `1e-12` in every entry of `R^T R - I`; the
identity is the default, for two blocks that meet. A `B` normal maps by `R`.

**Tolerance.** `L` is the diagonal of the bounding box of `A`'s points and
`tau = rel_tol L` (`rel_tol` defaults to `1e-9`). Two points closer than `tau`
are the same point; a point within `tau` of a line or a plane lies on it.

**The plane frame of a face.** For a face with vertices `x_0 .. x_{n-1}`, the
Newell area vector, the centre and the frame are

```
S = 1/2 sum_k x_k x x_{k+1},   e3 = S/|S|,   c = (1/n) sum_k x_k
e1 = unit((x_1 - x_0) - ((x_1 - x_0).e3) e3),   e2 = e3 x e1          (120.18.2)
(s, r) = ((x - c).e1, (x - c).e2),   x = c + s e1 + r e2
```

A face whose vertex lies farther than `tau` from its own plane, or whose loop
in `(s, r)` turns clockwise anywhere (a cross product below `-tau |edge|`), is
refused by name: the clipper needs planar convex faces.

**Pairs.** `(a, b)` is a candidate when the boxes of `a` and `T(b)`, each grown
by `tau`, overlap and every vertex of `T(b)` lies within `tau` of `a`'s plane.
A candidate whose normals agree (`e3_a . R e3_b > 0`) is refused by name:
the two sides face the same way, so the transform is wrong. Non-coplanar
boxes that overlap are not a pair; a faceted curved interface therefore ends
in the coverage refusal below, and that is its stated limit.

**The clip (Sutherland-Hodgman).** In `a`'s frame, `a`'s loop is
counter-clockwise; `T(b)`'s loop runs the other way and is reversed first.
The subject polygon `P` is clipped against each edge `p -> q` of `a` in turn.
With the signed distance

```
d(x) = cross(q - p, x - p) / |q - p|,   cross(u, w) = u_s w_r - u_r w_s     (120.18.3)
```

a point is inside when `d >= -tau`. Each subject edge `S -> E` emits: both
inside, `E`; `S` inside and `E` outside, `I`; `S` outside and `E` inside, `I`
then `E`; both outside, nothing; where

```
I = S + (d_S / (d_S - d_E)) (E - S)                                    (120.18.4)
```

The result, mapped back by (120.18.2), is the sub-face of the pair. It is
dropped when fewer than three distinct points remain after the snap below, or
when `2 |area| <= tau * perimeter` (a contact along an edge or at a corner).

**Snap and weld.** Each sub-face vertex `v` (in `A`'s frame) is matched
twice: `k`, the vertex of `a` within `tau` of `v`, and `m`, the vertex of `b`
with `|v - T(y_m)| <= tau`, either of which may be absent. The `A` side takes
`k` when there is one; else, when there is `m`, one new point `T(y_m)` per
`m`; else a new point at `v`, welded with any earlier such point within
`tau`. The `B` side takes `m` when there is one; else, when there is `k`, one
new point `T^-1(x_k)` per `k`; else one new point `T^-1(v)` per welded `A`-side
point. Matching grids therefore add no point at all. Consecutive repeats in a
loop are removed; collinear vertices are KEPT, because the neighbouring
sub-face or cell face needs them.

**Orientation and pairing.** The `A` sub-face keeps `a`'s orientation (its
area vector along `S_a`); the `B` sub-face of the same pair is the `A` loop
reversed with the same first vertex, `[w_0, w_{n-1}, .., w_1]`, written with
the `B` side's indices, so its area vector, mapped by `R`, is `-S` of the `A`
sub-face: it points out of `B`'s cell, as `S_b` does. The sub-faces of both patches are written in one pair order
(by `A` face, then by `B` face), so face `i` of `A` couples with face `i` of
`B`, as a conformal `cyclic` pairs its faces.

**Coverage.** Each original face must be covered by its sub-faces:

```
| sum_{i : parent(i) = f} |S_i|  -  |S_f| |  <=  1e-8 |S_f|             (120.18.5)
```

for every `f` of `A` and of `B`; otherwise the interface only partly overlaps,
which is `cyclicACMI` and refused (§120), and the refusal names the face and
its covered fraction.

**Splitting the edges of the cells.** An original edge `p q` of an `A` face
that now carries `A`-side points `v` strictly inside it (`|(v - p) x (q - p)|
<= tau |q - p|`, `lambda = (v - p).(q - p)/|q - p|^2` in `(0, 1)`) gets them
inserted, in increasing `lambda`, into every OTHER face of the mesh that has
`p` and `q` consecutive in either direction - the side walls and the internal
faces the edge borders - so each cell stays edge-manifold. The same holds for
`B` with its own points. Patches `A` and `B` that share a point are refused
(the two maps would meet in one face).

**The output.** Internal faces keep their order and owners (with inserted
points); patches keep their order, names, types and kinds; `A` and `B` hold
their sub-faces with the parents' owners; every `start` is recomputed. The
record `Imprinted` carries the mesh, the two patch indices, `parent_a[i]` and
`parent_b[i]` (local face indices of the input patches), and the counts of
new points on each side and of other faces that gained a point.

**Refusals by name.** An unknown patch; the same patch twice; an empty patch;
`R` not orthonormal; patches that share a point; a non-planar or non-convex
face; a coplanar pair facing the same way; a face not covered by (120.18.5).

**The gate (`tests/shared/mesh_imprint_cases.rs`, both builds; all class A or
D - f64 geometry, the same tolerance under `single`).** The meshes are two
one-layer blocks over the unit square, the interface at `z = 0`: `A` is a
3 x 3 grid below, `B` above is a 3 x 3 grid (matching), a 2 x 2 grid (3:2) or
a grid of spacing 0.5 rotated 7 degrees about (0.5, 0.5) and clipped to the
square (12 faces, 28 pairs), and the 3:2 pair again with `B` rotated 90
degrees about the `z` axis through (0.5, 0.5) and moved to `z = 5`, with the
transform that maps it back.

| row | claim | class |
|---|---|---|
| matching | 9 pairs, no new point, each sub-face its parent | D |
| 3:2 counts | 16 pairs; 9 new `A`-side and 16 new `B`-side points; `A` parents split 1/2/4 (corner/edge/centre), every `B` face into 4; 8 `A`-block and 12 `B`-block faces gain one point each | D |
| areas | per parent, the sub-face areas sum to the parent's to `1e-12` relative, both sides, 3:2 and rotated | A |
| pairing | equal sizes; each `B` loop mapped by `T` equals the reversed `A` loop to `1e-12` (bit for bit with the identity); area vectors cancel to `1e-12` | A, D |
| closure | every cell: `|sum_f S_f| <= 1e-12 sum_f |S_f|`, each directed edge once each way, the volume unchanged to `1e-12` relative; `build_host_mesh` accepts the result | A, D |
| transform | the moved 3:2 pair gives the 3:2 counts and pairing | A, D |
| refusals | a 0.1 shift names `cyclicACMI` and a fraction; a 0.01 gap is not covered; the bad requests above | D |

**Measured beside the gate (supervisor probe, not gated).** On the gate
meshes the worst cell closure is 4.2e-17 (3:2) and 1.1e-16 (rotated). On
finer pairs - a 12 x 12 grid against a 1/7 grid turned 13 degrees, 30 x 30
against 1/20 at 7 degrees, 60 x 60 against 1/40 at 3 degrees (396, 2624 and
10264 pairs) - every cell stays edge-manifold, the worst closure is 6.2e-16,
and the cell volumes hold to 2.2e-14 when the fan volume is taken about the
cell's own first point (3.8e-12 about the origin, on a 6e-7 cell: the
measurement's round-off, not the imprint's). The 60 x 60 pair imprints in
0.36 s. The candidate search is all pairs with a box test and the weld and
edge tables are linear scans, so the cost grows with the square of the face
count; binning them is left to the unit that needs larger interfaces.

## 121. Boussinesq buoyancy — `-β(T - T_ref)g` on faces, beside the density-ratio form

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Docs/17 §4.3 allocates §121 to CMP-01. The
§9 density-ratio force stays the default and is unchanged; the Boussinesq form is a
second, opt-in form of the same face body force, for cases whose temperature
differences are small (a liquid, a data hall, a natural-convection cavity).

Sources: **Spiegel, E. A. & Veronis, G. (1960), "On the Boussinesq approximation for
a compressible fluid", *ApJ* 131, 442, doi:10.1086/146849** (open full text at
<https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1960ApJ...131..442S>); **Gray, D. D. & Giorgini, A.
(1976), "The validity of the Boussinesq approximation for liquids and gases",
*Int. J. Heat Mass Transfer* 19(5) 545-551, doi:10.1016/0017-9310(76)90168-X** (both
DOIs checked against Crossref on 2026-10-11). No code was read for this section.

### 121.1 The force

The density is linearised about the reference state, and only the body force sees
the variation:

```
rho/rho_ref = 1 - beta (T - T_ref)                                    (121.1)
b = (rho/rho_ref - 1) g = -beta (T - T_ref) g                         (121.2)
```

`beta` is the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient `-(1/rho)(∂rho/∂T)_p` in 1/K.
For an ideal gas `beta = 1/T_ref`. As in §9 and §5.1 the force enters as a FACE flux
built from the interpolated face temperature, never from a cell value:

```
phib_f = -(beta (T_f - T_ref)) (g · S_f)                              (121.3)
```

evaluated in exactly that order (the bracketed product first, then the dot product),
on the host twin `BuoyancyCoeffs::at` and in the kernels alike. A boundary face whose
flux is prescribed (`momFluxIsPrescribed`: empty, symmetry, or `fr >= 1`) carries
`phib = 0`, as in §9.

### 121.2 Relation to §9

With `beta = 1/T_ref` the two forms differ by exactly the factor `T/T_ref`:

```
b_Boussinesq / b_ratio = [(T_ref - T)/T_ref] / [(T_ref - T)/T] = T/T_ref        (121.4)
```

so (121.2) is the first-order expansion of §9's `T_ref/T - 1` about `T_ref`, and it
overstates a hot plume's force by `T/T_ref` (about 4 at 1173 K against 293 K, the
reason §9 exists). Spiegel & Veronis and Gray & Giorgini state when the linearisation
holds; *DESIGN*: this tree's guard is `beta · max|T - T_ref| ≤ 0.1`, applied when a
case is lowered (CMP-03), not by the force itself.

### 121.3 Design

- `momentum::BuoyancyCoeffs` gains `form: BuoyancyForm` with `DensityRatio` (the
  default) and `Boussinesq { beta }`. Every existing literal names `DensityRatio`, so
  every existing case runs §9's kernels `momBuoyancyFlux` / `momBuoyancyFluxBoundary`
  bit for bit.
- (121.3) runs in its own kernels `momBoussinesqFlux` / `momBoussinesqFluxBoundary` in
  `cuda/momentum.cu`; §9's kernels are not edited, so their SASS does not move.
- No temperature floor: (121.3) has no divide. A NaN temperature propagates instead of
  being replaced by `t_min`. `Momentum::new` refuses a non-finite `beta` by name.
- Case input is CMP-03's, and §121.7 states it: every case format that carries a buoyancy
  block can select the form, with `beta`, under one lowering rule and one validity guard.

### 121.4 The hydrostatic column

On a uniform mesh of spacing `h` in a sealed, stably stratified column, the discrete
balance `|S_f| snGrad(p) = phib_f` (§9, §5.1) holds face by face, so across every
z-face the kinematic pressure jumps by

```
p_{k+1} - p_k = -h g_z beta (T_f - T_ref),    T_f = (T_k + T_{k+1})/2          (121.5)
```

and by zero across every x- and y-face; the fluid stays at rest.

### 121.5 Tests and their precision classes (docs/17 §5.1.4)

| test | assertion | class |
|---|---|---|
| `momentum::tests::boussinesq_over_density_ratio_is_t_over_tref_when_beta_is_one_over_tref` and its twin in `tests/f32_boussinesq.rs` | (121.4) to 4 ulp of the build, at temperatures where `T_ref/T` is exact | D |
| `…boussinesq_is_exactly_zero_at_tref` (and twin) | `b(T_ref) == 0` exactly | D |
| `…boussinesq_hot_cell_accelerates_up` | `b_z > 0` for `T > T_ref` under `g_z < 0`, `b_z < 0` for `T < T_ref` | P |
| `tests/f32_boussinesq.rs::boussinesq_device_flux_is_the_host_formula` | device (121.3) against the host formula, internal and non-prescribed boundary faces, to 16 ulp of the build; prescribed faces exactly 0 | D |
| `simple::tests::boussinesq_hydrostatic_column_jump_is_h_gz_beta_dt` (sealed, f64 lib test) and its twin in `tests/f32_boussinesq.rs` (open top, both builds) | (121.5) to `1e-12` (f64) / `1e-5` (f32) of `max|jump|`; `max|U|` below `1e-9` / `1e-5` m/s | R, `tol32 = max(tol64, min(tol64·2^29, 1e-5))` (D-F32-1) |

**Measured (CMP-01, 2026-10-11, RTX 5070 Ti).** Sealed column, f64: err `3.355e-13`, `max|U|` `4.4e-16` m/s.
Twin, open top: f64 err `8.178e-14`, `max|U|` `1.138e-16` m/s; f32 err `2.646e-6`, `max|U|` `2.951e-9` m/s.
The device flux matches the host formula with the interpolation evaluated as the kernel's fused multiply-add.

*Why the twin's top is open.* The sealed column's pressure is pinned: its matrix is singular, and
`assemble_pressure` removes the source mean in the build's own precision. Under `single` the
float-rounded mean that is left is a component no solver can remove, so the §118.4 refinement works on an
inconsistent system. The run then diverges with NaN residuals at the fifth corrector, with either force form;
§9's own sealed-column tests carry §112.3's ignore for the same reason. That is a finding for the precision
stream, not a property of (121.3). The twin therefore opens the top patch, with U zeroGradient and p fixedValue 0,
so the pressure system is nonsingular in both builds, and (121.5) still holds face by face. Its linear solvers stop
at `1e-14` rather than `1e-12`. With a Dirichlet anchor the stopping residual passes straight into the jumps: at
`1e-12` the f64 twin measured `9.8e-12` of `max|jump|`, falling in proportion to the tolerance.

Gate CMP-B (de Vahl Davis with Boussinesq, CMP-04) is section 121.8.

### 121.6 Buoyancy production of k, ε and ω under Boussinesq (CMP-02)

§17 writes the buoyancy production for any density law, after **Rodi, W. (1987), "Examples of
calculation methods for flow and mixing in stratified fluids", *J. Geophys. Res.* 92(C5)
5305-5328, doi:10.1029/JC092iC05p05305** (DOI checked against Crossref on 2026-10-11):

```
G_b = -(nu_t / Pr_t) g . grad(rho) / rho
```

Under the Boussinesq approximation the density varies only in the body force, so the `rho` that
divides is `rho_ref`, and (121.1) gives `grad(rho)/rho_ref = -beta grad(T)` exactly. Hence

```
G_b = beta (nu_t / Pr_t) g . grad(T)                                  (121.6)
```

evaluated in the order `nu_t · (1/Pr_t) · (g · grad T) · beta`. Against §17's density-ratio form
`(nu_t/Pr_t) g . grad(T) / T` the two differ by exactly

```
G_b,Boussinesq / G_b,ratio = beta T                                   (121.7)
```

which with `beta = 1/T_ref` is the same factor `T/T_ref` that (121.4) gives for the force. The sign
argument of §17 carries over unchanged for `beta > 0`: a stably stratified layer (`grad T` up, `g`
down) has `G_b < 0` and destroys turbulence; the layer above a heat source has `G_b > 0`.

*DESIGN* (CMP-02):

- `turbulence::BuoyancyProduction` gains `form: momentum::BuoyancyForm`, the same enum §121.3 gave
  `BuoyancyCoeffs`, default `DensityRatio`. `models::coupled::ThermalCtx` carries the form from the
  case's `BuoyancyCoeffs` to every model wrapper, beside `g` and `Pr_t`. `T_ref` is still not on it:
  neither (121.6) nor §17's form reads it.
- `DensityRatio` runs §17's kernel `turbBuoyancyProduction` with its launch unchanged, so its SASS and
  every f64 result stay as they were. (121.6) runs in its own kernel
  `turbBuoyancyProductionBoussinesq` in `cuda/turbulence.cu`. It does not read `T`, so it has no
  temperature floor, and `C_3` (constant or Henkes) is computed exactly as §17's kernel computes it.
- How `G_b` enters `k`, `ε` and `ω` (§17's table, the stable-branch switch, SST's per-cell `gamma`) is
  unchanged: the consumers read the `G_b` buffer whichever form wrote it.
- `BuoyancyProduction::validate` refuses a non-finite `beta` by name, as `Momentum::new` does (§121.3).

| test | assertion | class |
|---|---|---|
| `turbulence::tests::boussinesq_gb_equals_ratio_gb_times_t_beta` and its twin in `tests/f32_boussinesq.rs` | (121.7) per cell to 8 ulp of the build; bitwise at `T = 256, beta = 1/256` and `T = 512, beta = 1/512`; `C_3` bitwise equal between the two forms (Henkes and a constant) | D |
| `turbulence::tests::boussinesq_gb_sign_follows_the_stratification` (and twin) | `G_b < 0` for a stable layer, `> 0` above a heat source, each equal to (121.6) evaluated in f64 to 8 ulp of the build | P |
| `turbulence::tests::boussinesq_gb_does_not_read_the_temperature` (and twin) | a NaN or zero temperature field gives the same `G_b` bit for bit as a finite one | D |
| `turbulence::tests::boussinesq_production_refuses_a_non_finite_beta` (and twin) | `validate` refuses NaN and infinite `beta`, naming `beta` | D |

**Landed (CMP-02, 2026-10-11, RTX 5070 Ti).** All four tests and their twins pass in both builds, the
bitwise rows included under `single`. f64 identity: `turbulence.cubin` gains the one new kernel and the SASS of
its 32 existing kernels is unchanged (every other cubin is identical); `ofgpu-validate -sections 10,15`, which
holds §17's `G_b` rows and the coupled-selection run on a buoyant case, is row-identical (85 rows). No case could
select the form then; §121.7 (CMP-03) is where a case selects it.

### 121.7 Case input, the lowering rule and the validity guard (CMP-03)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` The force (121.3) and the production (121.6) are
unchanged; this subsection says how a case reaches them, which drivers run them, and the
guard §121.2 promised.

**Spellings.** The tree reads four case formats that carry a buoyancy block. Each gains the
same two settings, spelled in that format's own idiom:

| format | the form | `beta` [1/K] | read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSONC `case-1` | `physics.buoyancy`: `"densityRatio"` or `"boussinesq"` (required, as before) | `physics.fluid.beta` (optional) | `io::case_json::JsonCase::lower` |
| OpenFOAM dictionary | `buoyancy densityRatio;` or `buoyancy boussinesq;` in `constant/physicalProperties` (or `transportProperties`), absent = `densityRatio` | `beta [0 0 0 -1 0 0 0] 3.4e-3;` in the same file | `momentum::BuoyancyCoeffs::from_case` |
| `*.cht.jsonc` | `buoyancy.model` (optional, absent = `densityRatio`) | `buoyancy.beta` (optional) | `io::case_cht` |
| `*.dc.jsonc` | `air.buoyancy` (optional, absent = `densityRatio`) | `air.beta` (optional) | `io::case_dc` |

**The lowering rule** (`momentum::BuoyancyForm::lower`, one function for all four formats, so
there is one §13.4 contract and not four):

| form | `beta` | result |
|---|---|---|
| `densityRatio` | absent | §9's force, unchanged |
| `densityRatio` | present | refused, naming the `beta` key: nothing reads it (§13.4.1) |
| `boussinesq` | absent | refused, naming the `beta` key. There is no default: `1/T_ref` is the ideal-gas value, a liquid's is an order of magnitude smaller, and the reader is not entitled to pick one |
| `boussinesq` | finite and `> 0` | `BuoyancyForm::Boussinesq { beta }` |
| `boussinesq` | `<= 0`, NaN or infinite | refused, naming the `beta` key |
| any other spelling (dictionary route) | — | refused, naming the key and both spellings |

*DESIGN:* a negative `beta` (water below 4 °C) is refused rather than run, because §121.6's
sign argument for `G_b` assumes `beta > 0`.

**Who runs it.**

- `ofgpu-buoyant` (OpenFOAM dictionary), `ofgpu-cht` (`*.cht.jsonc`) and
  `ofgpu-datacentre` (`*.dc.jsonc`) run the form they are given. Their momentum body force is
  (121.3), and the `G_b` of their turbulence model is (121.6) through `ThermalCtx.form`
  (§121.6).
- `ofgpu-plume` solves no momentum. Its `G_b` takes the case's form, so a Boussinesq case is
  not silently given §17's density-ratio production.
- `ofgpu-lowmach` refuses `boussinesq` by name. §25's formulation carries the full
  variable density `rho = p0/(R_s T)` in its mass and energy balances, and a linearised body
  force would be a second density law that contradicts the first. Under `-permissive` it
  warns and substitutes `densityRatio`, the §13.4 escape hatch.
- *CHT density (DESIGN).* Under Boussinesq the density varies only in the body force
  (§121.1). A conjugate fluid region is therefore run with its density held at `fluid.rho`,
  exactly as §79.6 holds it without a body force: the gas state is pinned at the initial
  temperature and `update_density` is not called. `TRef` and `beta` reach the body force
  only. The density-ratio branch is unchanged in every bit.

**The validity guard.** With `beta` and `T_ref` from the case,

```
delta_B = beta * max_i |T_i - T_ref|                                   (121.8)
```

is taken over the fluid's cell temperatures and boundary-face temperatures (for a conjugate
case, the fluid region's cells and boundary faces only; a solid's temperature is no business
of a body force). It is evaluated in f64 on the host from the field the run starts from: after
the initial values, the boundary conditions and any restart, and before the first iteration.

- `delta_B <= 0.1`: the run proceeds.
- `delta_B > 0.1`, or not a number: the run is refused (`Error::Refused`). The message names
  the `beta` key, `beta`, `max|T - T_ref|`, `delta_B` and the limit `0.1`, and offers
  `densityRatio`. Under `-permissive` the guard warns once and the run continues.
- At the end of the run, the same number on the final field is printed, with a warning line
  when it exceeds `0.1`. It does not refuse, because the result already exists by then.

*Why the start is enough in the common case.* Steady or transient advection-diffusion of `T`
with a bounded convection scheme and no source satisfies a discrete maximum principle, so
`T` stays inside the range of its initial and boundary values, and the initial `delta_B`
bounds every later one. A heat source (a rack, a `fvSources` entry, a CHT solid's power) or
an unbounded scheme can break the bound. The end-of-run line is there for that case.

*The limit (DESIGN).* `0.1` is this tree's single number. Gray & Giorgini (1976) state the
validity of the approximation as bounds on the relative variation of each fluid property.
They do not give one number, so the `0.1` is not theirs. Under the data-centre's humidity
(§54.4) the force reads the virtual temperature `T_v`, but the guard reads `T`. They differ by
about `0.61 q T`, under 2 K at `q = 0.01`.

| test | assertion | class |
|---|---|---|
| `io::case_json::tests::boussinesq_lowers_with_beta` and its twin in `tests/f32_boussinesq.rs` | `physics.buoyancy "boussinesq"` with `physics.fluid.beta 3.4e-3` lowers to `Boussinesq { beta: 3.4e-3 }`, with `g` and `TRef` as stated | D |
| `io::case_json::tests::boussinesq_without_beta_is_refused_by_name` (and twin) | the error names `physics.fluid.beta` and `boussinesq` | D |
| `io::case_json::tests::beta_under_density_ratio_is_refused` (and twin) | the error names `physics.fluid.beta` and `densityRatio` | D |
| `momentum::tests::boussinesq_validity_guard_fires_above_0_1` (and twin) | `delta_B` of 0.099 passes; 0.101 on the hot side and on the cold side is refused, naming the key and `0.1`; a NaN temperature is refused; `densityRatio` is never refused; `-permissive` warns and passes | D |
| `momentum::tests::the_dictionary_route_reads_buoyancy_and_beta` | `from_case` lowers `buoyancy boussinesq; beta ...;`, refuses the three bad rows above and an unknown spelling, and reads a case without either key as `densityRatio` | D |
| `io::case_cht` and `io::case_dc` lowering tests | the same table through `buoyancy.model`/`buoyancy.beta` and `air.buoyancy`/`air.beta` | D |
| `cht::flow::tests::a_boussinesq_cavity_differs_from_and_agrees_with_the_density_ratio_one` | de Vahl Davis at `beta = 1/T_ref`, `Delta T = 0.1 K`: the two runs' fields differ, and their cold-wall Nusselt numbers agree to `1e-3` relative, the `O(beta Delta T)` the two forms differ by | P |
| `ofgpu-buoyant` knob `buoyancy boussinesq` in `every_wired_setting_changes_what_the_run_writes`, and `a_boussinesq_case_past_the_validity_limit_is_refused` | the setting changes what the run writes; the plume at `beta = 1/T_ref` (`delta_B ≈ 3`) is refused before its first iteration | D |
| `ofgpu-datacentre` `the_buoyancy_form_reaches_the_room_run` | the cold-aisle room, 20 iterations, under each form: the rack inlet temperatures differ | D |
| `ofgpu-lowmach` `a_boussinesq_case_is_refused_by_name` | refused naming `boussinesq`, `ofgpu-lowmach` and `densityRatio`; `-permissive` substitutes `densityRatio` | D |

### 121.8 Gate CMP-B de Vahl Davis with Boussinesq (CMP-04)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` The gate is a section of `ofgpu-validate`
(`rust/src/bin/validate.rs`, `check_boussinesq_cavity`; section 61 in run order when it
landed, a number that moves as gates are added) and runs de Vahl Davis's differentially heated square
cavity under the Boussinesq force (121.2) at `beta DeltaT = 0.03` - inside the
validity the approximation is stated for - and asks three things at each Rayleigh
number: the cold wall's mean Nusselt number sits within 2 % of the published one, the
two walls carry the same heat, and the field is centro-symmetric. A control run with
the §9 density-ratio force at the same `DeltaT` is measurably NOT centro-symmetric:
the two forms agree on Nu to `O(beta DeltaT)` and differ in symmetry at that same
order - the ordering the validity guard (121.8) bounds.

**Configuration.** The unit square, `L = H = 1`, `d_z = 1/n`; fluid `rho = cp =
kappa = 1`, `mu = 0.71` (`Pr = 0.71`); hot wall `304.5 K`, cold wall `295.5 K`, so
`DeltaT = 9 K` about `T_ref = 300 K`; `beta = 1/300` /K, the ideal-gas value, so
`beta DeltaT = 0.03`; initial `T = 300 K`; validity `delta_B = beta max|T - T_ref| =
0.015` against the guard's `0.1`. The gravity magnitude follows from Ra's definition,

```
Ra = g beta DeltaT L^3 / (nu alpha),   with nu = 0.71 and alpha = 1
```

so `g = 0.71 Ra / 0.03`, printed into the case document at full f64 precision. The
steady SIMPLE outer loop stops at residual `1e-9`; every other number of the document
is Gate 59-A's, unchanged. Run 4's mesh is graded two-sided, expansion 4, on x and y -
a wall mesh, and still centro-symmetric by construction.

**Measures.** With `Q_wall` the heat flowing INTO the cavity through the wall, and
`k = 1`, `DeltaT = 9`, `d_z = 1/n` on this case:

```
Nu_wall = |Q_wall| / (k DeltaT d_z)                                    (121.9)
w   = |Nu_hot - Nu_cold| / Nu_cold                                     (121.10)
s_T = max_c |(T_c - T_ref) + (T_c' - T_ref)| / DeltaT                  (121.11)
s_U = max_c max(|u_c + u_c'|, |v_c + v_c'|) / max_c max(|u_c|, |v_c|)  (121.12)
s   = max(s_T, s_U)
```

`c'` is the centro-symmetric partner of cell `c`, the cell whose centre is
`(1 - x_c, 1 - y_c)`. The map is built from the cell centres alone - the distinct x
and y coordinates are ranked, the partner of ranks `(i, j)` is `(n - 1 - i, n - 1 - j)`
- and never from the cell index order. If the map is not a bijection of all `n^2`
cells the run is refused, saying so. All four measures are formed in f64 on the host,
under `single` too: the measures see the f32 field through f64 arithmetic.

**Why the Boussinesq cavity is centro-symmetric.** Under (121.2) the map
`(x, y, u, v, T - T_ref) -> (1 - x, 1 - y, -u, -v, -(T - T_ref))` takes every term of
the steady equations to another term of the same equations - advection and the
pressure gradient are odd under it, diffusion is even times odd and stays odd, and
the body force is odd in `T - T_ref` - and it takes the boundary conditions to
themselves, hot to cold at the mirrored wall with the same `DeltaT` about `T_ref`.
The solution therefore comes in centro-symmetric pairs, and a symmetric
discretisation on a symmetric mesh converges to a centro-symmetric field, which is
what (121.11) and (121.12) measure at round-off. Section 9's force `g (T_ref/T - 1)`
has an even part in `T - T_ref`, of relative size `(T - T_ref)/T_ref` - exactly the
part the linearisation drops - so its solution is not centro-symmetric, and the
control run measures how far from it. Gray & Giorgini (1976), in §121's sources,
state the property bounds the linearisation lives inside.

**Runs and rows.** The published mean Nusselt numbers are de Vahl Davis (1983),
*Int. J. Numer. Meth. Fluids* 3 (1983) 249-264, DOI `10.1002/fld.1650030305`
(paywalled), read from the open secondary Qi et al., *Nanoscale Research Letters* 8
(2013) 56, Table 3, DOI `10.1186/1556-276X-8-56` - the same secondary Gate 59-A reads
its Ra = 1e4 number from. Each row's class is docs/17 §5.1.4's; the R-class tolerance
is `1e-6` in the f64 build and `1e-5` under `single`
(`tol32 = max(tol64, min(tol64 * 2^29, 1e-5))`, rule D-F32-1). No row's tolerance,
mesh, `DeltaT` or measure may move to let the row through.

| run | Ra | mesh | grading | form | cap | rows (class, f64 / single tolerance) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1e3 | 40x40 | none | Boussinesq | 2500 | Nu within 2 % of 1.118 (P, 0.02 both builds); `w <= TOL_R` (R, 1e-6 / 1e-5); `s <= TOL_R` (R, 1e-6 / 1e-5) |
| 2 | 1e4 | 60x60 | none | Boussinesq | 3500 | the three rows of run 1 against 2.243 - `devahldavis1983`'s number, marked at Gate 59-A and not re-marked |
| 3 | 1e5 | 80x80 | none | Boussinesq | 5000 | the three rows of run 1 against 4.519 |
| 4 | 1e6 | 120x120 | two-sided, expansion 4 | Boussinesq | 8000 | the three rows of run 1 against 8.800; NOT run under `single` |
| 5 | 1e4 | 60x60 | none | density ratio | 5000 | one require row: `s >= 1e-3` (P, both builds) - the density-ratio form at the same `DeltaT` is NOT centro-symmetric |

Under `single`, run 4 is not run (docs/17 §5.3 rule 4, the 10-minute rule, the
CMP-04 row): in f32 the outer loop does not reach the `1e-9` stopping residual, so
the run would take all 8000 iterations. It reports one `skip` row saying so, by name.

**Measured** - this tree, `ofgpu-validate -sections 61`, NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti, f64
build, every number the run printed:

| run | Nu_cold | against published | iterations | w | s_T | s_U |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.11865 | +0.06 % | 1683 | 1.9e-13 | 2.5e-13 | 2.4e-13 |
| 2 | 2.25053 | +0.34 % | 2406 | 8.8e-12 | 3.6e-12 | 3.6e-12 |
| 3 | 4.54582 | +0.59 % | 3452 | 6.3e-12 | 3.1e-12 | 3.6e-12 |
| 4 | 8.83870 | +0.44 % | 6059 | 1.2e-14 | 2.0e-13 | 1.9e-13 |
| 5 | 2.25064 | - | 3509 | 6.6e-7 | 2.98e-3 | 8.7e-3 |

All thirteen f64 rows hold - four Nu rows, four `w` rows, four `s` rows and the
control's require row - and the control's `s` sits five orders above the Boussinesq
runs', which is the gate's second claim measured, not assumed.

**Measured under `single`** - the same source built with `--features single`, same section:

| run | Nu_cold | Nu_hot | against published | iterations | w | s_T | s_U |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.12213 | 1.11645 | +0.37 % | 2500, not converged | 5.07e-3 | 1.64e-3 | 1.48e-3 |
| 2 | 2.24888 | 2.25151 | +0.26 % | 3500, not converged | 1.17e-3 | 7.53e-4 | 8.61e-4 |
| 3 | 4.54798 | 4.54167 | +0.64 % | 5000, not converged | 1.39e-3 | 7.46e-4 | 1.06e-3 |
| 4 | - | - | - | `skip` row, not run | - | - | - |
| 5 | 2.24889 | 2.25138 | - | 5000, not converged | 1.11e-3 | 3.68e-3 | 7.94e-3 |

The three Nu rows sit inside the 2 % band. The six R-class rows - `w` and `s` of runs
1, 2 and 3 - FAIL, at about `1e-3` against their `1e-5` tolerance. This is a recorded
f32 finding for the precision stream (§118), and no tolerance is moved for it. What was
measured: in f32 the steady SIMPLE outer loop does not reach the `1e-9` stopping
residual (every run takes its full cap and reports `converged false`; a probe of run 1
measured the same `w` and `s` at 1000 and at 3000 iterations, so more iterations do not
help), and the field it stays on carries a wall-to-wall heat imbalance and a
centro-symmetry defect of order `1e-3`. The cause was not isolated here. The control's
require row holds under `single`, but there it does not separate the two forms: the
Boussinesq runs' own `s` is of the same order as the control's. The claim that the
density-ratio form is the asymmetric one therefore rests on the f64 rows. Run 4 is
skipped under `single` by the 10-minute rule, as the table above states.

## 122. The compressible gas — the perfect-gas state, the gauge pressure about `p_op`, Sutherland, and the f32 design

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Docs/17 §4.3 allocates §122-§127 to the
compressible formulation of tranche 17. CMP-05 wrote all six sections as contracts.
CMP-06 to CMP-29 implement them, and each of those units amends its own section in
place when it lands (a "Landed" paragraph with what it measured). No code was read
for these sections. In particular no OpenFOAM solver or boundary-condition source
(`rhoCentralFoam`, `rhoPimpleFoam`, `rhoSimpleFoam`, `sonicFoam`, `waveTransmissive`,
`totalTemperature`) and no SU2 file (LGPL) was read. Boundary-condition and dictionary
NAMES follow the public user guides by name only (§120). In these six sections an
equation label and a subsection can share a number (`(122.1)` and §122.1), so code
cites a subsection as `§12N.M` and an equation as `(12N.M)`, never the bare `S12N.M`
form that §80.4's ratchet counts as ambiguous.

**What the solver is.** `ofgpu-compressible` is one pressure-based, all-speed,
segregated `(U, p, T)` solver in a self-contained module `rust/src/compressible/`
(`mod.rs`, `thermo.rs`, `momentum.rs`, `pressure.rs`, `energy.rs`, `bc.rs`, `lts.rs`,
`exact.rs` with `exact/riemann.rs`, `gatemesh.rs`, `tests.rs`), with its kernels in a
new `rust/cuda/compressible.cu`, on the `vof.rs` precedent. It reuses the `fv`
operators, the ρ-weighted ddt kernels (`fvDdtEulerRho`, `fvDdtBdf2Rho` in
`cuda/fv.cu`), the §4 triple, the §7 limiters and the §8 Krylov solvers, and it edits
none of `crate::momentum`, `crate::simple` or `crate::energy`, so §25, §26 and §59
stay bitwise. *DESIGN* (docs/17 COMP decision 1): pressure-based rather than
density-based, because every boundary condition, scheme, solver, writer, reader,
turbulence model and the studio is keyed to a segregated `(U, p, T)` solver, and the
pressure-based route has an exact incompressible limit ((124.6)). A density-based
HLLC module is a contingency that needs the user (docs/17 §2, COMP §5 risk 2).

**A note on what "read" means in §122-§127.** As in §128: each source is marked
**read** (and where) or *not read*. A DOI marked *not read* was checked on Crossref
(title, authors, journal, volume and pages agree). Every equation below is either
stated from a source marked **read**, or derived in the text from such equations and
marked as derived. Numbers are not recalled: every numeric value below was read from
a source or computed by the CMP-05 oracle (an independent f64 Python evaluation of the
equations as written here, kept outside the tree), and says which.

* **Blazek, J.** (2015), *Computational Fluid Dynamics: Principles and Applications*,
  3rd ed., Elsevier, DOI 10.1016/C2013-0-19038-1. *Not read here.*
* **Ghia, U., Ghia, K.N. & Shin, C.T.** (1982), *JCP* 48:387-411, DOI
  10.1016/0021-9991(82)90058-4: the existing `reference/ghia1982` key.
* **Gordon, W.J. & Hall, C.A.** (1973), "Construction of curvilinear co-ordinate
  systems and applications to mesh generation", *IJNME* 7:461-477, DOI
  10.1002/nme.1620070405 (transfinite interpolation, for CMP-26). *Not read.*
* **Cook, P.H., McDonald, M.A. & Firmin, M.C.P.** (1979), "Aerofoil RAE 2822 -
  pressure distributions, and boundary layer and wake measurements", AGARD-AR-138,
  through the NPARC Alliance validation archive
  `www.grc.nasa.gov/WWW/wind/valid/raetaf/raetaf.html` (**read** 2026-10-07 for its
  case and file list, §127.5).

### 122.1 The state

The gas is thermally and calorically perfect. The pressure unknown `p` is a GAUGE
pressure about a host constant `p_op` (§122.2):

```
p_abs = p + p_op                                                   [Pa]          (122.1)
R_s   = R / W ,   R = 8.314462618 J/(mol K)                         [J/(kg K)]    (122.2)
psi   = 1 / (R_s T) ,   rho = psi p_abs                                           (122.3)
c     = sqrt(gamma R_s T) ,   M = |u| / c                                         (122.4)
c_p   = gamma R_s / (gamma - 1) ,   c_v = c_p - R_s ,   h = c_p T                 (122.5)
```

(122.3) is the perfect-gas law. (122.4) is derived: `c^2 = (d p/d rho)` at constant
entropy, which with NACA 1135 (34), `p/rho^gamma = constant`, is `gamma p/rho`, and
`gamma R_s T` by (122.3). `psi = d rho/d p` at constant `T` exactly, which §124 uses.
`T` is absolute, in kelvin, never an offset. (122.5) fixes the enthalpy datum at
`h(0 K) = 0`, the datum under which NACA 1135 (43) is equivalent to
`c_p T_0 = c_p T + |u|^2/2`.

*DESIGN* - **the gas is `(gamma, W)`, and `c_p` follows from them.** A case states
`gamma` and `W`. A stated `c_p` must equal (122.5) within `1e-6` relative, or the case
is refused by name (`physics.compressible.cp`, with the stated and the derived value;
§13.4: `-permissive` warns and uses the derived one). An inconsistent `c_p` would make
the energy equation's `h_0 = c_p T + K` and the isentropic boundary relations of §126,
which use `gamma`, disagree about the same total state. The compressible module
therefore does NOT take `crate::energy::GasProperties::default()`'s `cp = 1006`,
which differs from (122.5) at `gamma = 1.4`, `W = 0.0289647` by 0.13 %. Its own
default is air: `gamma = 1.4`, `W = 0.0289647`, so `R_s = 287.0550227690948` and
`c_p = 1004.692579691832` J/(kg K) (oracle, from (122.2) and (122.5)).

**Viscosity and conduction.** Either a constant `mu`, or Sutherland's law as the U.S.
Standard Atmosphere 1976 writes it (eq. (51)), with its constants for air:

```
mu(T)  = A_s T^(3/2) / (T + T_s) ,   A_s = 1.458e-6 kg/(m s K^(1/2)) ,  T_s = 110.4 K   (122.6)
kappa  = mu c_p / Pr                                                                  (122.7)
mu_eff = mu + mu_t ,   kappa_eff = kappa + c_p mu_t / Pr_t                             (122.8)
```

`Pr` defaults to 0.71 and `Pr_t` to 0.85, the crate's existing `GasProperties`
defaults. (122.8) is §26's `k_eff = k + rho c_p nu_t/Pr_t` with `mu_t = rho nu_t`.
The oracle gives `mu(273.15) = 1.716079266245527e-05` and
`mu(300) = 1.8460015185931457e-05` Pa s. `c_p(T)` from §100 is a coefficient change
and is out of scope: v1 has constant `c_p`, as §26 does.

### 122.2 The gauge pressure, and why it is the f32 design

*DESIGN* (docs/17 COMP decision 3, and docs/17 §5.1.5: "pressure-like unknowns are
deviations"). Every equation the Krylov solver sees, and the momentum gradient, uses
`p` alone. `p_op` is a host `f64` constant in both builds. It reaches a kernel only
inside `p + p_op` in (122.3) and in the boundary formulas of §126. In f32 the spacing
of floats at 1e5 is `7.8125e-3` Pa, and at 300 K it is `3.0518e-5` K (oracle). A
transonic pressure difference of about 1e4 Pa and the 7e2 Pa of `M = 0.1` are
resolved with five or more significant digits as gauge values, and so is the 1 Pa
perturbation CMP-08 tests. Formed as an absolute pressure, the same 1 Pa would carry
fewer than three significant digits. The oracle, in f32 with `T = 300 K`, `p_op = 1e5` and the
operation order `psi * (p + p_op)`, gives
`rho(p = 1) - rho(p = 0) = 1.156330e-05` against `psi * 1 = 1.161218e-05`: a 0.421 %
error, inside CMP-08's 1 % bar (0.410 % at 288.15 K and 0.014 % at 273.15 K).

`p_op` is stated by the case (`pOperating` / `physics.compressible.pOperating`,
CMP-14), with no default: a compressible case that omits it is refused by name. A
written `p` field is the gauge `p`. CMP-15 decides whether `p_abs` is written as well;
it is not (§125.8).

### 122.3 Floors, bounds and what is never clipped

* `cuda/compressible.cu` defines no floor. No `OFGPU_CMP_TINY` exists, and each kernel's header says "no floor and no clip". The one host threshold its kernels receive, §126.11's direction threshold `tmin = 1e-6`, is formed in f64 on the host and is not a floor. §112.1's table carries the row (CMP-28), and `compressible::tests::the_compressible_kernels_carry_no_double_only_literal` holds it. A host floor that a later unit adds uses `SCALAR_FLOOR` (§112.1).
* **Bounds are counted, never clipped.** After each solve of an outer iteration the
  driver counts the cells with `T <= 0`, `p_abs <= 0` or `rho <= 0`, and records the
  first such cell and its value. A nonzero count is printed on the iteration line. The
  run then stops at the end of that outer iteration with `Error::Refused` naming the
  field, the cell and the value; `-permissive` does not lift it, because the gas law
  has no state there (CMP-12's `bounds_counter_fires_and_names_the_cell`).
* The Mach number is (122.4) per cell; `M_max` and `M_mean` are reduced as (93.7) and
  printed on every iteration line, as §93.5 does for `ofgpu-lowmach`. The low-Mach
  solver's `M > 0.3` refusal (§93.6) now names `ofgpu-compressible` (CMP-15, message
  only).

### 122.4 Scope

v1 is single-GPU (decomposition refused by name; docs/17 COMP decision 14), laminar or
Spalart-Allmaras (§127.1), with constant `c_p`, no sources, no mesh motion and no
radiation. Everything else is refused by name in `ofgpu-compressible` (CMP-15; the list
is in §125.8).

### 122.5 The device twins of the gas state (CMP-08)

`cuda/compressible.cu` evaluates (122.3), (122.4), (122.6) and (122.7) elementwise, one
thread per cell. `src/compressible/thermo.rs` holds the gas (`PerfectGas`), the host
twins and the launchers. This subsection adds no physics. It fixes the ORDER of the
operations, because the gate between the device and the host is counted in
representable numbers, and it is the same count in both builds.

**The constants are formed once in f64 and rounded once.** `R_s` and `c_p` are (122.2)
and (122.5) in f64 in both builds, with `c_p` formed as `gamma R_s / (gamma - 1)` in
that order. A kernel never sees `gamma`, `W` or `Pr`. It receives the numbers of
(122.9), each formed in f64 and rounded to the working precision (`fl`), and the host
twin uses the same rounded numbers:

```
rs  = fl(R_s) ,  pop = fl(p_op) ,  grs = fl(gamma R_s) ,  cpr = fl(c_p / Pr) ,
as  = fl(A_s) ,  ts  = fl(T_s) ,   mu0 = fl(mu)  (constant viscosity)             (122.9)
psi = 1 / (rs T) ,   rho = psi (p + pop)                                           (122.10)
mu  = (as (T sqrt(T))) / (T + ts)   (Sutherland) ,   mu = mu0   (constant) ,
kappa = mu cpr                                                                     (122.11)
c   = sqrt(grs T) ,   M = sqrt(u_x u_x + u_y u_y + u_z u_z) / c                    (122.12)
p   = rho / psi - pop                                  (host only, the inverse)    (122.13)
```

Every operation in (122.10)-(122.13) is in the working precision, in the order the
brackets show, left to right where there are none. (122.10) is (122.3) with (122.1),
(122.11) is (122.6) and (122.7), and (122.12) is (122.4). `T^(3/2)` is written
`T sqrt(T)`: one correctly rounded square root and one product, where `pow` would
differ in its last bit between the host's library and the device's. `p + pop` is one
sum in the working precision, which is the operation §122.2's oracle measured.

**No floor and no clip.** §122.3 counts a state outside the gas law and never clips
it, so these kernels have no guard: `T = 0` gives an infinite `psi`, and `T < 0` a NaN
`c`. CMP-12's counter is what reports them. `cuda/compressible.cu` therefore defines
no `OFGPU_CMP_TINY` yet. The first kernel that divides by something a floor must
protect defines it, with §122.3's two values.

**Contraction.** `compressible.cu` is compiled with nvcc's default contraction (it is
not in `build.rs`'s `FMAD_OFF_UNITS`). The only product that feeds a sum is the sum of
squares in (122.12), so only `M` can differ from the host through a fused
multiply-add. That is §67.11's stance: the device is the reference and the host is a
check, and the gate is four units in the last place rather than bitwise.

**The gates.** `ulp distance` is the number of representable values between two
finite numbers of one sign, which is the difference of their bit patterns read as
integers. The answer keys are from the CMP-08 oracle: an independent NumPy evaluation
of (122.9)-(122.13) in `float64` and in `float32`, kept outside the tree. It
reproduces §122.1's two viscosities and §122.2's three f32 errors.

| gate (the lib tests are `compressible::thermo::tests::*`, the f64 build; the same four names in `tests/compressible_thermo.rs` run in both builds) | bar | class |
|---|---|---|
| `gpu_matches_host_to_4ulp` | 4096 random states (`T` in [200, 2000] K, gauge `p` in [-5e4, 5e5] Pa about `p_op = 101325`, each velocity component in [-800, 800] m/s) and one state at rest, for Sutherland air and for a constant viscosity: `psi`, `rho`, `mu`, `kappa`, `c` and `M` from the device lie within 4 ulp of the host twin, and `M = 0` exactly at rest | D |
| `sutherland_air_at_273_15_is_1_716e_5` | `|mu(273.15) - 1.716e-5| < 5e-9` Pa s, the four digits White and the Standard Atmosphere print (P). `mu(273.15) = 1.716079266245527e-05`, `mu(300) = 1.8460015185931457e-05` Pa s and `kappa(300) = 0.026122028560991366` W/(m K) to `1e-14` relative (R). A constant viscosity returns its number at every `T` (D) | P, R, D |
| `ideal_gas_round_trip` | `R_s = 287.0550227690948` and `c_p = 1004.692579691832` J/(kg K) to `1e-15` relative, f64 in both builds (A). `rho(p = 0, 288.15 K, p_op = 101325) = 1.2249908312368587` kg/m3, `c(288.15) = 340.29526405061904` and `c(300) = 347.2219888817812` m/s to `1e-14` relative (R). Over the 4096 states, `p -> rho -> p` through (122.10) and (122.13) returns `p` within 4 ulp of `p_abs` (D). A stated `c_p` off (122.5) by more than `1e-6` relative is refused by name (§122.1) | A, R, D |
| `f32_gauge_pressure_resolves_1pa` | with `p_op = 1e5` and `T` = 300, 288.15 and 273.15 K, on the device and on the host twin: `rho(p = 1) > rho(p = 0)` and `|(rho(1) - rho(0))/psi - 1| <= 0.01` (P). Control, `single` only: at 300 K the error is above `1e-3` (the oracle gives 4.209e-3), so the row is known to measure f32 arithmetic | P |
| `the_compressible_thermo_update_replays_bitwise` (lib) | §81.7's row for `src/compressible/thermo.rs`: the three kernels capture into one graph and replay bitwise | D |

R rows take `tol32 = max(tol64, min(tol64·2^29, 1e-5))` (D-F32-1), which is `5.4e-6`
for `1e-14`. No row carries a tolerance of its own for f32.

**Landed (CMP-08).** Measured on the RTX 5070 Ti, in both builds. Over the 4097 states
and both gases the device's `psi`, `rho`, `mu`, `kappa` and `c` equal the host twin bit
for bit (0 ulp), and `M` differs by at most 2 ulp, which is the fused sum of squares
the paragraph on contraction names. The round trip returns `p` within 1.5 ulp of
`p_abs` (oracle; the test holds it to 4). The 1 Pa row measures, device and host
alike: in f64 `5.7e-12`, `1.5e-12` and `1.9e-12` at 300, 288.15 and 273.15 K; under
`single` `4.2089e-3`, `4.1011e-3` and `1.3870e-4`, which are §122.2's oracle values
(0.421 %, 0.410 %, 0.014 %), so the control (above `1e-3` at 300 K) holds. The replay
gate captures 5 kernel nodes (the three kernels and the two field operations that
feed `M` back into `T`) and replays three times bitwise over 7 buffers and 1792
values. The 46 cubins that existed before are unchanged in SASS in both builds.

### 122.6 The case input (CMP-14)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` The dictionary keyword NAMES and the unit of
`molWeight` are from the OpenFOAM *User Guide* v12, "Thermophysical models",
<https://doc.cfd.direct/openfoam/user-guide-v12/thermophysical> (DOCUMENTATION,
**read** 2026-10-14). No OpenFOAM source file was opened.

A compressible case states the gas of §122.1 in one of two ways, and both end in the
same `compressible::thermo::PerfectGas`, validated by `PerfectGas::validate`.

**JSONC** (`src/io/case_json.rs`): `physics.compressible { gamma, W, cp, Pr,
viscosity, pOperating }`. `gamma` and `W` (kg/mol) are required. `cp` is optional
and is only checked: §122.1's `1e-6` relative rule refuses a disagreeing value by name
(`physics.compressible.cp`), and `-permissive` warns and keeps the derived `c_p`.
`Pr` defaults to 0.71. `viscosity` is `{ "model": "sutherland", "As", "Ts" }`, which
is (122.6), or `{ "model": "const", "mu" }`. `pOperating` is §122.2's `p_op` in Pa,
with no default. `Pr_t` is §122.1's 0.85, and neither route has a key for it. Every
object is `deny_unknown_fields`, so an unknown key is refused with its JSON path. Two
patch kinds read a `freestream { U, p, T }`: `p` is gauge in the datum of the `p`
field (§122.2) and `T` is in kelvin.

* `supersonicInlet` (§126.2) lowers `U`, `p` and `T` to `fixedValue` at that state.
* `farfield` (§126.6) lowers all three to `characteristicFarfield`, with the free stream
  as each field's `value`. CMP-18 implements the kind (§126.10).

Both kinds are refused in a case without `physics.compressible`, without a
`freestream`, or with a `U`, `p` or `T` entry of their own, because the preset decides
all three. They are also refused when the free stream has no gas-law state: `T <= 0`,
`p + p_op <= 0` or a non-finite value (§122.3). A `freestream` on any other kind is
refused, and so is a compressible case without `initial.T`.

**OpenFOAM** (`src/io/thermo_dict.rs`, `constant/thermophysicalProperties`): one
`thermoType` with `type` `hePsiThermo` or `heRhoThermo`, `mixture pureMixture`,
`transport` `sutherland` or `const`, `thermo hConst`, `equationOfState perfectGas`,
`specie specie` and `energy` `sensibleEnthalpy` or `sensibleInternalEnergy`. Every
one of the seven is required, and any other model is refused with the menu. The
`mixture` block holds `specie { molWeight; nMoles }`, `thermodynamics { Cp; Hf }` and
`transport { As; Ts; Pr }` (sutherland) or `transport { mu; Pr }` (const). The file
also has a top-level `pOperating`, which is required. Any other key, at any of these
levels, is refused by name with the keys that are read, through §13.4's `unsupported`.
The dictionary states `molWeight` in g/mol and `Cp` rather than `gamma`, so the gas
follows from (122.2) and (122.5) solved for `gamma` (derived):

```
W = molWeight / 1000 ,   gamma = c_p / (c_p - R_s) ,   R_s = R / W                   (122.14)
```

`c_p <= R_s` has no `gamma` above 1 and is refused by name. With constant `c_p`, the
two `energy` forms describe the same state; the form is kept for CMP-15's driver.
`Hf` must be 0, because (122.5) fixes `h(0 K) = 0` and a formation enthalpy matters
only to a reacting mixture. `nMoles` must be 1. `Pr` is read under both transport
models and defaults to 0.71 when absent. The User Guide lists no `Pr` for
`sutherland`, but this solver's conductivity is (122.7) under both models, so it needs
one. The oracle gives `molWeight 28.9647` with `Cp 1004.692579691832` as `W = 0.0289647`,
`R_s = 287.0550227690948` and `gamma = 1.4000000000000001`, which is §122.1's air to
one ulp. `ThermoDict::to_text` writes the subset back in Rust's shortest round-trip
form, so a read, a write and a second read agree bit for bit
(`thermophysical_subset_round_trips`).

**Landed (CMP-14).** Tests: `io::thermo_dict::tests::{thermophysical_subset_round_trips,
unknown_thermo_key_is_refused_by_name}`, `io::case_json::tests::jsonc_compressible_lowers`,
and the schema sync test `the_shipped_schema_is_the_generated_one` on the regenerated
`docs/schema/case-1.json`. No driver reads either route yet: `ofgpu-compressible`
(CMP-15) is the first.

## 123. Momentum in conservative form — the mass flux, the full Newtonian stress, and Rhie-Chow with a density

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` CMP-09 implements this section in
`src/compressible/momentum.rs` and `cuda/compressible.cu`.

### 123.1 The equation

```
d(rho u)/dt + div(mdot u) = -grad p + div(tau) + rho g                                    (123.1)
tau = mu_eff ( grad u + (grad u)^T - (2/3)(div u) I )                                     (123.2)
```

This is the Navier-Stokes momentum equation for a Newtonian fluid with Stokes's
hypothesis; `mdot` is `rho u` as a face mass flux. `g` is on only when the case states
gravity; `rho g` then enters on faces, as §5.1 requires of every body force.

### 123.2 The discretisation

`mdot_f` is a face MASS flux, in kg/s, distinct from §1's volumetric `phi_f`. With §1's
index convention, `(grad u)_ij = d u_j/d x_i`, the face stress flux of component `i` is
`(tau . Sf)_i = mu_eff,f ( Sf . grad u_i  +  ((grad u) . Sf)_i  -  (2/3) tr(grad u) Sf_i )`
(derived from (123.2)). The first term is implicit, the other two are explicit
(deferred) from the latest `u`:

```
implicit:  ddt_rho(u)  +  sum_f mdot_f u_f  -  sum_f mu_eff,f |Sf| snGrad(u)                (123.3)
explicit:  b_P += sum_f mu_eff,f [ (grad u)_f . Sf  -  (2/3) tr(grad u)_f Sf ]               (123.4)
ddt_rho(u) = (rho_P u_P - rho_P^o u_P^o) V_P / dt                                  (Euler)
           = (3 rho_P u_P - 4 rho_P^o u_P^o + rho_P^oo u_P^oo) V_P / (2 dt)          (backward)
```

`u_f` uses §7's limited weights on `mdot_f`; `snGrad` is §12's, with its
non-orthogonal correction. The ρ-weighted ddt is `fvDdtEulerRho` / `fvDdtBdf2Rho`
unchanged. `rho_P` is the density of the current outer iterate, `rho_P^o` the density
of the last step (refreshed once per step, §125.3). LTS (§125.4) uses Euler with the
per-cell `dt_P`.

**Rhie-Chow with a density** (§5.1, written for the ρ-weighted matrix):

```
A_P u_P = H_P - V_P (grad p)_P + V_P rho_P g ,   rAU_P = 1/A_P   [m^3 s/kg] ,   HbyA = rAU H   (123.5)
phi_HbyA,f  = HbyA_f . Sf                                                [m^3/s]              (123.6)
mdot_f      = rho~_f phi_HbyA,f  -  rho_f rAU_f ( |Sf| snGrad(p) - rho_f g . Sf )   [kg/s]    (123.7)
u_P         = HbyA_P - rAU_P ( (grad p)_P - rho_P g )                                         (123.8)
```

`rho_f` (in the pressure part and in the body force) is the linear interpolate
`w rho_P + (1 - w) rho_N`. `rho~_f` (in the convective part) is the retarded density
of (124.3). (123.6)-(123.8) are §5.1's structure with `rho` written where the
incompressible solver has a constant; the split of `rho_f` from `rho~_f` is the all-speed
coupling of §124 (derived there). *DESIGN*: the body force sits beside the pressure
gradient with the same weight `rho_f rAU_f`, so a hydrostatic state
(`snGrad(p) = rho_f g . n`) carries zero mass flux on every face, the property §5.1's face
treatment of body forces exists for. Every `rAU`, `HbyA` and `phi_HbyA` is formed exactly
once per corrector, on the §14 schedule.

**What CMP-09 must make true.** `uniform_flow_is_a_fixed_point_to_round_off` (uniform
`rho, u, p, T`: the momentum residual is zero to round-off; class R, docs/17 §5.1.4);
`rho_one_matrix_equals_incompressible_matrix_times_rho` (with `rho = 1` everywhere,
`mu = nu` and `mdot = phi`, the matrix and source equal the kinematic assembly's
BITWISE in f64; class D); `explicit_transpose_stress_vanishes_for_solenoidal_linear_u`
((123.4) is zero for `u = (a y, b x, 0)`; class R); `couette_shear_stress_exact`
(linear `u(y)`: the wall shear stress `mu U/h` to round-off; class R).

### 123.3 The assembly as built (CMP-09)

`src/compressible/momentum.rs` holds `RhoMomentum`, and `cuda/compressible.cu` gains
six kernels. This subsection adds no physics: it fixes what each call forms, in which
order, and from which existing kernel, because one of its gates is bitwise. The
precedent is `src/vof.rs`, which assembles its own ρ-weighted momentum from the same
operators. Everything §3, §7, §12 and §5.1 already compute is CALLED, not re-derived:
the scalar operators of `src/fv.rs`, the time term `timescheme::Ddt::add_rho`
(§86.3), and the Rhie-Chow kernels of `cuda/momentum.cu`, which take their face force
as an argument and do not know whose it is.

**The inputs.** `u` (three time levels and its §4 triple), the face mass flux `mdot`
[kg/s], `rho` as a field with its two old levels and its boundary values, the
effective viscosity `mu_eff` of (122.8) as a field with boundary values, and the gauge
`p`. The module never evaluates the gas law.

**The viscous coefficient and the explicit stress** (`set_viscosity`):

```
mu_f = w mu_P + (1 - w) mu_N    (internal) ,   mu_f = mu_b    (boundary) ,   G_f = mu_f |Sf|     (123.9)
T_P  = (grad u)_P ,   T_ij = d u_j / d x_i                     (§1's convention, §12's scheme)
T_f  = w T_P + (1 - w) T_N      (internal and coupled) ,   T_f = T_P      (any other boundary face)
q_f,i = mu_f ( sum_j T_f,ij Sf_j  -  (2/3) (T_f,xx + T_f,yy + T_f,zz) Sf_i )                     (123.10)
E_P  = sum_{f owned by P} q_f  -  sum_{f whose neighbour is P} q_f  +  sum_{boundary f of P} q_f   [N]   (123.11)
```

(123.10) and (123.11) are (123.4), written per face and per cell. An `empty` face
carries no `q`. `E_P` is an integrated force, so it enters the source as it is, with no
volume factor. With `full_stress = false` neither the gradient nor `E` is formed and
nothing is added: that is the laplacian-only operator, and it is what the bitwise gate
below compares with the kinematic assembly, whose own explicit stress term
(`momStressCorrection`) is a different expression.

**One component's system** (`assemble_only`, `solve`), in the order
`momentum::Momentum::assemble_component` uses, so that equal inputs give equal bits:
the component view of `u`; `Ddt::add_rho` with `rho, rho^o, rho^oo`; `fvm_div_gauss`
on `mdot` with §7's weights (sensor `|u|`, as `momentum::Momentum` takes it); the deferred half of a
higher-order scheme (§11.1); `fvm_laplacian` with `-G_f`; §12.3's explicit
non-orthogonal correction; `source_P += E_P,c` when `full_stress`; `ldu_ops::relax`
by `u_relax` (always, also at 1, where it only enforces dominance); the boundary fold.
There is NO bounded-convection correction: in conservative form `sum_f mdot_f` is the
other half of `d(rho u)/dt` (§86.4), not a spurious source. The pressure gradient and
the body force are held back as `force` until the solve, as §5.1 requires of `H`.
`localEuler` and `CrankNicolson` are refused by name here; §125.4's per-cell step is
CMP-13's.

**The force** (`set_force`), formed on faces and reconstructed, as §5.1 does:

```
phig_f = rho_f (g . Sf) ,   rho_f = w rho_P + (1 - w) rho_N  (boundary: rho_b)                  (123.12)
F_f    = phig_f - |Sf| snGrad(p)_f          (0 on a face whose flux the velocity prescribes)
force_P = reconstruct(F)_P   [N/m^3] ,   source_c = su_c + V_P force_P,c                        (123.13)
```

`phig` is zero on a prescribed-flux boundary face and is not formed at all when
`g = 0`. (123.12) is evaluated by §121's kernel pair with `beta = -1` and
`T_ref = 0`, for which (121.3) is `rho_f (g . Sf)` with no rounding added: the
subtraction of zero and the two sign changes are exact.

**The residual** (`residual`), per component `c`, with `A` and `su` as assembled:

```
r_P,c = ( su_P,c + V_P force_P,c ) - (A u_c)_P                                                  (123.14)
```

**Rhie-Chow** (`rhie_chow`): `rAU = V/diag` (`momRau`, zero where the diagonal is
zero), `HbyA` (`momHbyA`), `rAU_f` (`momFaceInterp`) and `phi_HbyA` of (123.6)
(`momPhiHbyA` with a zero body-force flux: the gravity part of (123.7) belongs to the
pressure equation, §124). Then the convective half of (123.7) with the retarded
density of the current iterate:

```
mdot_HbyA,f = rho~_f phi_HbyA,f ,   rho~_f = rho_P if phi_HbyA,f >= 0 else rho_N     (internal, coupled)
              boundary: rho~_f = rho_P if phi_HbyA,f >= 0 (outflow) else rho_b ;  0 on `empty`   (123.15)
```

**The viscous traction on a boundary face** (`boundary_traction`), the force the fluid's
viscous stress exerts through the face, per (123.2):

```
t_b = mu_b ( |Sf| (u_b - u_P) delta_b  +  T_P . Sf  -  (2/3) tr(T_P) Sf )   [N] ,
      (T_P . Sf)_i = sum_j T_P,ij Sf_j ;   0 on `empty` and coupled faces                       (123.16)
```

`delta_b` is the mesh's boundary `deltaCoeff` and `u_b` the evaluated boundary value.
With `full_stress = false` only the first term is formed.

**Contraction, and what the bitwise gate can claim.** `timescheme.cu` is compiled
with contraction. `tsDdtGeneral` writes `diag += (sign V) a_N`, one fused operation;
`tsDdtGeneralRho` writes `diag += ((sign V) a_N) rho`, whose product `(sign V) a_N` is
rounded before the fused step. With `rho = 1` the two agree bit for bit when
`(sign V) a_N` is exact, which it is when `a_N` is a power of two (Euler with
`dt = 2^-k`), and can differ in the last place otherwise. The gate therefore claims
BITWISE equality for the steady operator on any mesh and for Euler at `dt = 2^-10`,
and holds the cases where `a_N` is not a power of two (Euler at `dt = 1e-3`, and
backward at `dt = 2^-10`, whose `a_N` is `1.5·2^10`) to class R. This is a property of
the two existing kernels, stated here; neither is changed. The backward leg is not at
`dt = 1e-3`, because the KINEMATIC side cannot run it in the f32 build:
`timescheme::fvm_ddt` refuses coefficients whose sum exceeds `1e-12` of their scale
(`DdtCoeffs::is_consistent`), and three rounded f32 coefficients sum to `3.05e-5`
against a bar of `2.0e-9` at `dt = 1e-3`. `fvm_ddt_rho`, which this module calls, has
no such guard and runs backward at `dt = 1e-3` in both builds (the fixed-point row
above does). The guard's f64 constant is a finding for §118's stream, not changed here.

**Answer keys** (derived). For uniform `mu`, (123.4) is
`div( mu (grad u)^T - (2/3) mu (div u) I ) = (mu/3) grad(div u)`. For
`u = (a y, b x, 0)` it is zero. For `u = (c x y, 0, 0)`, `div u = c y` and the force
on a cell is `(0, mu c V_P / 3, 0)`: on a uniform hexahedral mesh the Green-Gauss
gradient of a bilinear field is exact, so the discrete `E_P` equals it to round-off in
every cell that owns no boundary face. Reversing the index order in (123.10) gives
`(0, -2 mu c V_P/3, 0)`, and dropping the `2/3` term gives `(0, mu c V_P, 0)`, so
the row separates all three. For plane Couette flow `u = (U y/h, 0, 0)`,
`T_yx = U/h` alone: the traction (123.16) is `(±mu U |Sf|/h, 0, 0)` on the walls
`y = h` and `y = 0`, and `(0, ±mu U |Sf|/h, 0)` on the faces `x = max` and `x = min`
(the complementary shear `tau_yx = tau_xy`, carried by the explicit term alone).

| gate (lib: `compressible::momentum::tests::*`, f64 build; the same names in `tests/compressible_momentum.rs` run in both builds from one shared source) | bar | class |
|---|---|---|
| `uniform_flow_is_a_fixed_point_to_round_off` | uniform `rho = 1.177`, `u = (37.5, -12.25, 4)`, `p = 250`, `mu = 1.846e-5` on a 6x5x4 box graded 3:1 in y, for steadyState, Euler and backward (`dt = 1e-3`) and for upwind and linear: `|r_P,c| <= 1e-13 |diag_P| max|u_c|` in every cell (the magnitude: with `linear` a cell beside a Dirichlet outflow face has a negative diagonal); `|force_P,c| V_P <= 1e-13 |p| S_P`, with `S_P` the summed face area of the cell (the face difference of a uniform `p` is exactly zero, but §12.3's explicit correction multiplies a Green-Gauss gradient that is zero only to round-off by correction vectors that are zero only to round-off on a graded mesh, so the force is of order `1e-30`, not zero); `HbyA = u`, `phi_HbyA = u . the result, which is zero.

**Landed (CMP-09).** Measured on the RTX 5070 Ti, in both builds; each number is the

of its bar (at most `1.4e-28` N/m3 in f64 and `3.7e-20` in `single`), and the control `1.0895 |diag_P|` in both. The

and E also came out at 0 ulp in `diag` and in `source` in both builds: this compiler
does not separate the two time kernels, and the row still claims only class R there.
The stress row: `1.5e-3` and `5.7e-3` for the rotation, `1.5e-3` and `4.3e-3` for the

(`tests/compressible_thermo.rs` 4 of 4). Every other cubin is unchanged in SASS under
