## 124. The all-speed pressure equation — continuity with the gas law, the retarded density, and the incompressible limit

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` CMP-10 implements this section in
`src/compressible/pressure.rs` and `cuda/compressible.cu`.

### 124.1 The derivation

The equation is derived here from continuity, (122.3) and §123.2. That pressure-based
all-speed methods take this form is the literature's: Karki & Patankar (1989),
Demirdžić, Lilek & Perić (1993), Issa, Gosman & Watkins (1986), Moukalled et al. ch. 16
(*not read*). Discrete continuity in cell P, with the same time scheme as momentum (the
ρ-ddt of the continuity equation and of (123.3) must be the same, or mass is not
conserved in the momentum's ddt):

```
ddt(rho)_P + sum_f mdot_f = 0 ,   ddt(rho)_P = (rho_P - rho_P^o) V_P / dt                   (124.1)
```

(backward: `(3 rho_P - 4 rho_P^o + rho_P^oo) V_P / (2 dt)`). Linearise the density
about the current iterate `*` at frozen `T` (so frozen `psi`):

```
rho_P  = rho_P*  + psi_P  (p_P - p_P*)                                                       (124.2)
rho~_f = rho~_f* + psi~_f (p~_f - p~_f*)                                                     (124.3)
```

For the perfect gas (124.2) is exact, not a linearisation: with
`rho* = psi (p* + p_op)` it is `rho_P = psi_P (p_P + p_op)`, (122.3) itself. `~` marks
the **retarded** (upwind-biased) face value: `psi~_f`, `p~_f` and `rho~_f*` are those of
the cell upwind of `phi_HbyA,f` (default), or a §7-limited face value of them (option
`limitedRetarded`, the limiter named as §7 names it). The retarded density is the
shock-capturing mechanism of the pressure-based route: Hafez, South & Murman (1979)
introduced the upwinded ("artificially compressible") density for transonic flow
(*not read*). Substituting (124.2), (124.3) and (123.7) in (124.1):

```
psi_P V_P/dt p_P  +  sum_f psi~_f phi_HbyA,f p~_f  -  sum_f rho_f rAU_f |Sf| snGrad(p)
     =  -(rho_P* - psi_P p_P*) V_P/dt  +  rho_P^o V_P/dt  -  sum_f (rho~_f* - psi~_f p~_f*) phi_HbyA,f   (124.4)
```

(Euler shown, without gravity. Backward scales the `psi_P` term and the
`(rho_P* - psi_P p_P*)` term by 3/2, and `rho_P^o V_P/dt` on the right becomes
`(4 rho_P^o - rho_P^oo) V_P/(2 dt)`. With gravity the right-hand side gains
`- sum_f rho_f rAU_f rho_f (g . Sf)`, from (123.7).) For the perfect gas
`rho* - psi p* = psi p_op`, so the right-hand side is
`-psi_P p_op V_P/dt + rho_P^o V_P/dt - sum_f psi~_f p_op phi_HbyA,f`: plan docs/17 COMP
§2.2 item 3, recovered. The unknown is `p`, gauge, alone.

**The matrix.** The first term is a diagonal; the second is a convection operator on
`p` with face "velocity" `psi~_f phi_HbyA,f` (upwind: owner/neighbour coefficient by the
sign of `phi_HbyA,f`); the third is §5.1's Laplacian with `rho_f rAU_f`. It is
asymmetric, so it is solved by PBiCGStab with DILU (§8.1, §8.3). Non-orthogonal
correctors follow §5.2. Boundary faces carry `p`'s §4 triple in both the convective and
the Laplacian part.

### 124.2 After the solve

```
mdot_f = (123.7) with the new p and rho~_f from (124.3) at the new p                          (124.5)
u_P    = (123.8) ,     rho_P = psi_P (p_P + p_op)
```

`mdot_f` is formed from the matrix's own face coefficients and the new `p`, as §5.1
forms `phi`, so (124.1) holds to the linear solver's tolerance with `rho_P` from the
gas law; CMP-10's `mass_imbalance_after_correction_below_solver_tol` checks it (class A).
`p` is relaxed by `alpha_p` in steady SIMPLE only (§5.2), never on a final transient
corrector (§14).

### 124.3 The incompressible limit

With `psi = 0`, `rho* = rho^o = rho` held and no gravity, (124.4) becomes

```
sum_f rho_f rAU_f |Sf| snGrad(p) = sum_f rho~_f phi_HbyA,f                                    (124.6)
```

For uniform `rho` this is §5.1's `laplacian(rAU_f, p) = div(phi_HbyA)` for the kinematic
pressure `p/rho`, multiplied by `rho`: the ρ-weighted `A_P` is `rho` times the kinematic
one, so `rho_f rAU_f` is the kinematic `rAU_f` and `HbyA` is the kinematic `HbyA`
(derived). CMP-10's `psi_zero_reduces_to_incompressible_to_round_off` holds the
assembled system to that, to round-off (class R). Gate CMP-AC/LM (§127.6)
holds the whole solver to Ghia at `M = 0.05`.

### 124.4 The assembly as built (CMP-10)

`src/compressible/pressure.rs` holds `RhoPressure`, and `cuda/compressible.cu` gains
seven kernels. Like §123.3, this subsection adds no physics. It fixes the sign, the
order and the face values, because two of the gates below compare this system with
another one. Everything §3, §5.1, §7 and §12 already compute is CALLED: the scalar
operators of `src/fv.rs`, the face-flux sum of `cuda/simple.cu` (`smpFaceFluxSum`),
the product and velocity-correction kernels of `cuda/momentum.cu` (`momMul`,
`momCorrectVelocity`), and the face fields `RhoMomentum` (§123.3) leaves behind
(`rAU`, `HbyA`, `rAU_f`, `phi_HbyA`, `phig`, `force`).

**The sign.** The system assembled is (124.4) multiplied by `-1`. Its Laplacian then
enters as `fvm_laplacian(.., +1)`, exactly as in §5.1's incompressible pressure
equation (`Simple::assemble_pressure`), and the limit (124.6) is that equation's
matrix with its source scaled by `rho`:

```
A p = b
A p = laplacian(rho_f rAU_f, p) - sum_f psiPhi_f p~_f - a_n V_P psi_P p_P                      (124.7)
b   = sum_f s_f + V_P ( a_n (rho_P* - psi_P p_P*) + a_0 rho_P^o + a_00 rho_P^oo )
psiPhi_f = psi~_f phi_HbyA,f
s0_f     = (rho~_f* - psi~_f p~_f*) phi_HbyA,f ,   s_f = s0_f + rho_f rAU_f phig_f               (124.8)
```

`sum_f` runs over the cell's faces with the outward sign (owner `+`, neighbour `-`,
boundary `+`). `(a_n, a_0, a_00)` are the coefficients of the momentum equation's own
time term (`RhoMomentum::ddt`, §13.3), so continuity and momentum share one ddt, as
(124.1) requires. `steadyState` writes no time term. (124.7)-(124.8) are (124.4) with
the gravity term of §124.1 and the backward form folded into the three coefficients.

**Face values.** One set of weights serves the convective operator and every
retarded value: `w_f` on internal faces and `bw_b` on boundary faces. With
`Retarded::Upwind` (the default) they are §3.1's upwind weights on `phi_HbyA`. With
`Retarded::Limited(l)` they are the weights of the §7 limiter `l` on `phi_HbyA`, with
`p` as the sensor and its Gauss gradient forming `r`. This is §124.1's option
`limitedRetarded`. For each cell quantity `x` in `{psi, rho*, p*}`:

```
internal face:                      x~_f = w_f x_P + (1 - w_f) x_N
cyclic face with a cell across it:  x~_b = bw_b x_P + (1 - bw_b) x_nbr
any other boundary face:            psi~_b  = psi_P  if phi_HbyA,b >= 0, else psi_b
                                    rho~*_b = rho*_P if phi_HbyA,b >= 0, else rho*_b
                                    p~*_b   = p*_b
empty face:                         psiPhi_b = s0_b = s_b = 0                                     (124.9)
```

On a non-coupled boundary face `p~` is the value of `p`'s §4 triple, which is how
`fvm_div_gauss` evaluates it (§124.1: "boundary faces carry `p`'s §4 triple in both
the convective and the Laplacian part"). `psi~_b` and `rho~*_b` follow (123.15). With
upwind weights, (124.9) is (123.15)'s selection exactly, because `1 x_P + 0 x_N = x_P`.
`rho_f` in `rho_f rAU_f` is `fv::interpolate_linear` of `rho*`: linear on internal
faces, `rho*_b` on the boundary. `rAU_f` is `RhoMomentum`'s `rauf`. The Laplacian
coefficient is the product `(rho_f rAU_f) |Sf|`, formed in that order. `phig_f` is
(123.12), which is zero when `g = 0` and on a prescribed-flux face.

**The order** (`assemble_only`, and each non-orthogonal corrector of `solve`):
1. zero the matrix;
2. add the time term;
3. add `fvm_div_gauss(psiPhi, w, bw, p, -1)`;
4. add `fvm_laplacian((rho_f rAU_f) |Sf|, p, +1)`;
5. when §12.3's scheme applies, add `fvm_laplacian_non_orth_correction` with the Gauss `grad p` of the current `p`;
6. add `source += sum_f ±s_f` (`smpFaceFluxSum`, accumulating);
7. fold in the boundary contributions.

`solve` forms `p*` (cell and boundary values), the weights, `psiPhi`, `s0`, `s` and
`rho_f rAU_f` ONCE, at its start, from the `p`, `rho*` and `psi` it is handed. The
linearisation point does not move during the non-orthogonal correctors.

No reference level is fixed and nothing is pinned. With `psi > 0` a transient system
has its time diagonal, and a steady one needs a face where `p` is a Dirichlet value.
A closed steady box at `psi = 0` is singular, and refusing it is the outer loop's
job (CMP-12).

The linear solver is PBiCGStab (§8.1). `PCG` and `DIC` are refused by name, because
the matrix is asymmetric. `GAMG` is refused by name too, because only the
incompressible pressure equation has the AMGX backend (§8.3).

**After the solve** (`correct`). `p` is evaluated on its boundary first. Then:

```
lap_f  = (rho_f rAU_f |Sf|) snGrad(p)_f      fv::sn_grad_flux, plus §12.3's correction when it applies
mdot_f = s0_f + psiPhi_f p~_f - lap_f + rho_f rAU_f phig_f                                       (124.10)
u_P    = HbyA_P + rAU_P force_P              force: RhoMomentum::set_force at the new p and rho*
rho_P  = rho_P* + psi_P (p_P - p_P*) ,   rho_b = rho_b* + psi_b (p_b - p_b*)                       (124.11)
```

(124.10) is (124.5) written with the face values of (124.9). Its diffusive part comes
from the matrix's own coefficient `rho_f rAU_f |Sf|` through `sn_grad_flux`, which
multiplies in `fvm_laplacian`'s order. So on an orthogonal mesh
`ddt(rho)_P V_P + sum_f mdot_f` equals the linear system's residual `b - A p` to
round-off, and the solver's tolerance bounds it. On a non-orthogonal mesh the last
corrector's explicit term was formed with the previous `p`, which is the usual lag of
deferred correction.

(124.11) is (124.2) itself, at frozen `psi`. When the caller hands in
`rho* = psi (p* + p_op)` (`thermo::gas_state`, §125.3 step 4), it is the gas law
(122.3) to round-off. At `psi = 0` it holds `rho`, which (124.6) needs. *DESIGN*:
writing (124.11) instead of re-evaluating `psi (p + p_op)` has two effects. The
module needs neither `p_op` nor `T`, just as §123.3 kept the momentum equation free
of the gas law. Continuity also stays at the matrix's balance.

`u` is corrected with the CELL `rAU`, as `momCorrectVelocity` does for §5.1. `p` is
not relaxed here; that is step 6 of §125.3's loop.

**Classes.** §124.2 named the imbalance row class A. It is class R. `mdot` and `rho`
are stored in the build's precision, so under `single` the identity holds only to
f32 round-off. No evaluation in f64 can recover what the store already rounded.

| gate (lib: `compressible::pressure::tests::*`, f64 build; the same names in `tests/compressible_pressure.rs` run in both builds from one shared source) | bar | class |
|---|---|---|

## 125. Energy, the outer loop, and the local time step

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` CMP-11 implements §125.1-§125.2 in
`src/compressible/energy.rs` (as built: §125.5), CMP-12 §125.3 in `src/compressible/mod.rs`
(as built: §125.6), and CMP-13 §125.4 in `src/compressible/lts.rs` (as built: §125.7).

### 125.1 The energy equation, solved for `T`

The total-energy conservation law, with `E = h - p/rho + K`, `K = |u|^2/2` and the
total enthalpy `H = h + K` (Carlson's eq. (36) writes `H_t` this way for the perfect
gas, **read**; NASA Glenn's *Navier-Stokes Equations* page,
`www.grc.nasa.gov/www/k-12/airplane/nseqs.html`, states the conservative total-energy
equation, **read**, as an image):

```
d(rho E)/dt + div(rho u H) = div(kappa_eff grad T) + div(tau . u) + rho g . u
```

Expanding `d(rho E)/dt = d(rho h)/dt - dp/dt + d(rho K)/dt` and putting `h = c_p T`
(122.5) gives the form solved (derived):

```
d(rho c_p T)/dt + div(mdot c_p T) - div(kappa_eff grad T)
      =  dp/dt  -  [ d(rho K)/dt + div(mdot K) ]  +  div(tau . u)  +  rho g . u            (125.1)
```

`dp/dt` is the gauge `p`'s, because `p_op` is constant. Discretely: the left side is
implicit in `T` (`fvDdtEulerRho`/`fvDdtBdf2Rho` with weight `rho c_p`, `fvm_div_gauss`
on `mdot c_p`, `fvm_laplacian(kappa_eff)`). The right side is explicit from the latest
`p`, `u` and `mdot`: `dp/dt = (p_P - p_P^o)/dt` (backward: its BDF2 form); the `K` terms
are `(rho_P K_P - rho_P^o K_P^o) V_P/dt + sum_f mdot_f K_f`; the viscous work is
`sum_f (tau_f . u_f) . Sf` with `tau_f` from (123.2) and `u_f` linear; the gravity work
is on only with gravity. A steady SIMPLE run has no ddt terms at all, so `dp/dt` and
`d(rho K)/dt` are absent there; an LTS run (§125.4) keeps them with its `dt_P`.

*DESIGN* - **`K_f` uses the face weights of `T_f`.** Then `sum_f mdot_f (c_p T_f + K_f)`
is a sum of face fluxes of `h_0 = c_p T + K`, so in steady, inviscid, adiabatic flow the
discrete energy equation conserves `h_0` along a stream tube to the solver's tolerance.
That is what places a captured shock's jump where (127.2) puts it (Moukalled ch. 16 and
Ferziger & Perić ch. 11 make this argument; *not read*). CMP-11's
`h0_conserved_along_inviscid_duct_to_1e-6` holds it (class A).

The viscous work is a switch (`viscousWork`, default on when `mu > 0`). CMP-11's
tests: `uniform_flow_preserves_t` (class R), `slab_conduction_linear_exact` (class R),
`viscous_work_matches_couette_exact` ((127.12); class P),
`h0_conserved_along_inviscid_duct_to_1e-6` (class A).

### 125.2 What is NOT in (125.1)

There is no `p0(t)` and no low-Mach divergence constraint (§25.1); this is the fully
compressible equation. There is no radiation and no source (§122.4).

### 125.3 The outer loop

One loop with two switches, as §14 asks (PIMPLE transient; SIMPLE steady; LTS steady,
§125.4):

```
per time step (or pseudo step):
    refresh old levels ONCE:  rho^o <- rho, u^o <- u, T^o <- T, p^o <- p, K^o <- K
                              (backward also rotates ^oo)
    for outer in 1..nOuterCorrectors:
        final = (outer == nOuterCorrectors)
        1. psi, mu, kappa from T                   (122.3), (122.6)-(122.8)
        2. momentum predictor                      (123.3)-(123.4), relaxed by alpha_U unless final
        3. energy                                  (125.1), relaxed by alpha_T unless final
        4. psi from the new T
        5. for corr in 1..nCorrectors:             (§14: H RE-EVALUATED each corrector)
               rAU, HbyA, phi_HbyA                 (123.5)-(123.6)
               for nc in 0..nNonOrthCorr:  solve (124.4)
               correct mdot, u, rho                (124.5)
        6. relax p by alpha_p (steady SIMPLE only, never on a final transient corrector)
        7. turbulence (SA, §127.1) on the new mdot
        8. bounds count (§122.3); residuals; stop on residualControl (§14, initial residuals)
```

*DESIGN* - the old levels are refreshed once per step, at its start, never inside the
outer loop (the split `ofgpu-lowmach`'s `Energy` lacks, `lowmach.rs`'s note on its own
loop). CMP-12's `one_step_twice_equals_two_steps_state` holds it (two calls of one step
equal one call of two steps, bitwise in f64; class D). Each outer iteration reports the
mass imbalance `sum_P |ddt(rho)_P + sum_f mdot_f| / sum_P rho_P V_P/dt` and the `h_0`
residual (the initial residual of (125.1)). `quiescent_box_stays_at_rest` (class R)
completes CMP-12's tests.

### 125.4 The local time step for steady runs

```
dt_P = CFL * V_P^(1/3) / ( |u_P| + c_P )                                                  (125.2)
```

*DESIGN*: (125.2) is the acoustic Courant condition (Courant, Friedrichs & Lewy 1928,
*not read*) with the cell's length scale `V^(1/3)`. Blazek (2015) ch. 6 gives a
multi-dimensional spectral-radius form (*not read*); (125.2) is the simple one. Each
cell's ddt terms in (123.3), (124.1) and (125.1) use its own `dt_P` with the Euler
scheme; old levels are refreshed once per pseudo step. At a converged fixed point
every ddt difference is zero, so the fixed point does not depend on `CFL`. CMP-13's
`steady_fixed_point_independent_of_cfl` holds two CFLs to the same field within `1e-8`
in f64 (class P; the same bar in f32 is reported as its own row if missed, §5.1.4) and
`dt_field_matches_host_formula` holds (125.2) to its host twin (class R).
*As built* (§125.7): the fixed-point row is MISSED. `rAU` (123.5) carries the time term's
diagonal, so the Rhie-Chow flux keeps `CFL` at the fixed point.

### 125.5 The assembly as built (CMP-11)

`src/compressible/energy.rs` holds `RhoEnergy`, and `cuda/compressible.cu` gains three
kernels. Like §123.3 and §124.4, this subsection adds no physics: it fixes the scaling,
the order and the face values of (125.1). Everything §3, §7, §12 and §86.3 already
compute is CALLED: the scalar operators of `src/fv.rs`, the time term
`timescheme::Ddt::add_rho`, the face product of `cuda/momentum.cu` (`momMul`) and the
face-flux sum of `cuda/simple.cu` (`smpFaceFluxSum`).

**The scaling.** *DESIGN*: `c_p` is constant (`hConst`, §122.1), so the system
assembled is (125.1) divided by `c_p`. The time term is `Ddt::add_rho` with weight `rho`
on `T`'s old levels, the convection is `fvm_div_gauss` on `mdot`, the laplacian's
coefficient is `kappa_f |Sf| / c_p`, and every explicit term carries
`rcp = fl(1/c_p)`, formed in f64 and rounded once. The solution is (125.1)'s; only the
rounding of the scaling differs. The system is

```
A T = b
A T = ddt_rho(T) + sum_f mdot_f T~_f - sum_f rcp kappa_f |Sf| snGrad(T)                      (125.3)
b   = sum_f ±e_f + rcp V_P [ (a_n p_P + a_0 p_P^o + a_00 p_P^oo)
                             - (a_n rho_P K_P + a_0 rho_P^o K_P^o + a_00 rho_P^oo K_P^oo)
                             + rho_P g . u_P ]
e_f = rcp ( W_f - mdot_f K~_f ) ,   K = |u|^2 / 2 ,   W_f = u_f . (tau_f . Sf)                     (125.4)
(tau_f . Sf)_i = mu_f ( sum_j (T_f,ij + T_f,ji) Sf_j - (2/3) tr(T_f) Sf_i ) ,   T_ij = d u_j/d x_i  (grad u)
```

`(a_n, a_0, a_00)` are this equation's own time coefficients (`DdtCoeffs`), so `dp/dt`,
`d(rho K)/dt` and `d(rho T)/dt` are one scheme. `K^o` and `K^oo` are `|u^o|^2/2` and
`|u^oo|^2/2`, formed from `u`'s old levels. `(tau . Sf)` is (123.2) contracted with
`Sf` in §123.2's three terms. `sum_f` runs over the cell's faces with the outward sign
(owner `+`, neighbour `-`, boundary `+`).

**Face values.** One set of weights serves `T~_f` and `K~_f`: §7's weights of the
scheme on `mdot`, with `T` as the sensor (§125.1's DESIGN). A deferred-correction scheme
(`linearUpwind`, `linearUpwindBlended`, `cubic`) has no weight for its face value, so it
is refused by name. `u_f`, `mu_f` and the face tensor `T_f` of `grad u` (§123.3's `T`,
not the temperature) are linear on the mesh weights:

```
internal face:                      K~_f = w_f K_P + (1 - w_f) K_N ,   T_f = l_f T_P + (1 - l_f) T_N ,   u_f likewise
cyclic face with a cell across it:  the same with bw_b (K) and the mesh's b_weights (T_f, u_f)
any other boundary face:            K~_b = |u_b|^2/2 ,   u_f = u_b ,   T_f = T_P                     (123.10)
empty face:                         e_b = 0
```

`u_b` is the value of `u`'s §4 triple, as `T~_b` is the value of `T`'s, so a boundary
face's flux is `mdot_b (T_b + K_b/c_p)` from the two triples.

**The order** (`assemble_only`, and `solve` before its one linear solve):
1. the weights, `rcp kappa_f |Sf|`, and, with `viscousWork`, `mu_f` and `grad u`; then `e_f`;
2. zero the matrix;
3. `Ddt::add_rho(rho, rho^o, rho^oo; T^o, T^oo, +1)`;
4. `fvm_div_gauss(mdot, w, bw, T, +1)`;
5. `fvm_laplacian(rcp kappa_f |Sf|, T, -1)`, and §12.3's correction with the Gauss `grad T`;
6. `source += sum_f ±e_f` (`smpFaceFluxSum`, accumulating);
7. the cell source, launched when the time coefficients are not all zero or `g != 0`;
8. `ldu_ops::relax` by `alpha_T`, always (at 1 it only enforces dominance);
9. the boundary fold.

`solve` then solves for `T` and evaluates its boundary values. The solve's initial
residual is the `h_0` residual of §125.3 step 8. `set_t_relax` sets `alpha_T` for a final
corrector. Refused by name: `localEuler` and `CrankNicolson` (as §123.3 refuses them),
`PCG`, `DIC` and `GAMG` (the convection makes the matrix asymmetric), `alpha_T` outside
`(0, 1]`, and a `c_p` that is not positive and finite.

  with van Leer; the upwind `h0` drift is `1.2e-14` and `7.8e-8`; `T` falls 110.09 K.

  bitwise over 4 buffers and 174 values.

*Finding (single).* A first form of the Couette row let the x boundary faces carry the
channel's through-flow. Each cell's two x faces then carry K fluxes `4e4` times its viscous
work, which cancel exactly only in exact arithmetic. Under `single` the rounding of that
cancellation moved the worst cell to `3.5e-3` of the rise, inside the bar but six times the
f64 error, and f64 was unchanged. The row now states the one-dimensional channel. A case
whose energy balance is a small difference of large convected `K` fluxes carries that
rounding in `single`.

Every cubin but `compressible.cubin` is unchanged in SASS in both builds, apart from
`solidblock.cubin` in f64, which flipped between its two known hashes on a rebuild with
no edit to it (nvcc's nondeterminism, as CMP-08 recorded). CMP-08's, CMP-09's and
CMP-10's integration tests are unchanged (4, 5 and 4 passed in both builds).

### 125.6 The outer loop as built (CMP-12)

`src/compressible/mod.rs` holds `Compressible`, the loop of §125.3 over CMP-08's gas law,
CMP-09's momentum, CMP-10's pressure and CMP-11's energy equations. It adds no kernel:
`cuda/compressible.cu` is unchanged, and the only arithmetic of its own is step 6's
relaxation through `simple.cu`'s `smpRelaxField`. `CompressibleState` holds `u`, the gauge
`p` and `T` with the caller's boundary conditions, and `rho`, `psi`, `mu`, `kappa` and
`mdot`. The boundary values of `rho`, `psi`, `mu` and `kappa` are formed elementwise from
`p`'s and `T`'s evaluated boundary values. Their own boundary conditions are never
evaluated.

*DESIGN* - the choices §125.3 leaves open:

* **Steady or transient** is the momentum equation's ddt scheme: `steadyState` is SIMPLE,
  `Euler` or `backward` is PIMPLE. The energy equation must name the same scheme, `delta_t`
  and `g`, or `Compressible::new` refuses by name. `c_p` is never an input (§122.1), so
  the loop writes `PerfectGas::cp` into the energy controls.
* **"Final"** exists only in a transient run: on the last outer iteration `alpha_U` and
  `alpha_T` are 1 (`RhoMomentum::set_u_relax`, `RhoEnergy::set_t_relax`), and `p` is not
  relaxed. A steady run relaxes all three on every iteration.
* **The old levels.** At the top of every step, `advance_time_levels` rotates `rho`, `u`,
  `T` and `p`, and `K^o` follows because the energy source forms it from `u^o`. Both
  equations' `TimeState::advance` runs at every step but the first, so a first backward
  step is Euler (§13.3). `initialise` seeds both old levels from the initial fields. It
  evaluates the boundaries of `u`, `p` and `T`, forms `mu`, `kappa`, `psi` and `rho`, and
  sets `mdot = rho_f (u_f . Sf)` with a linear `rho_f`.
* **Steps 1 and 4.** Step 1 is `transport` (`mu`, `kappa`). Step 4 is `gas_state`, which
  gives `psi` AND `rho* = psi (p* + p_op)`, the consistent `rho*` that CMP-10's corrector
  needs. The corrector leaves `rho = psi (p + p_op)` to round-off, so a second corrector
  starts from a consistent `rho*` too.
* **Step 6.** `p` is relaxed against its value before the correctors, in a steady run and
  on a transient run's non-final outer iterations. Then `p`'s boundary is evaluated and
  `gas_state` restores the gas law. Every outer iteration therefore ends with
  `rho = psi (p + p_op)`.
* **Step 7 is absent.** The gas is laminar until CMP-14's SA lands.
* **Step 8.** The mass imbalance is formed in f64 on the host after the correctors, on the
  momentum equation's time coefficients. A steady run has no `ddt(rho)` and divides by its
  `delta_t`. The `h_0` residual is the energy solve's initial residual. The bounds count
  tests `!(x > 0)`, so a NaN counts. Its order is `T`, then `p_abs = p + p_op`, then
  `rho`, each by cell index, and the first violation found is the one named. `M_max` and
  `M_mean` are (93.7). `OuterReport::line` prints all of these, and `BOUNDS n` when `n` is
  nonzero. `residualControl` (`u`, `p` on the first corrector, `T`) stops only a steady
  `run`. A transient step reports it and stops nothing.
* **Capture.** The registry row is `Refused`: step 8 reads `T`, `p`, `rho`, `u` and
  `mdot` back after every outer iteration and stops on what it reads. Each of the four
  equations is gated on its own.

*Tree over plan.* The row names `mod.rs` and `tests.rs`. The final-corrector rule also
needs `RhoMomentum::set_u_relax`, which is additive, and the module root needs its
capture-registry row.

### 125.7 The local time step as built (CMP-13)

`src/compressible/lts.rs` holds (125.2) and the per-cell time terms, and
`cuda/compressible.cu` gains four kernels after CMP-08's to CMP-11's nineteen, which are
untouched. `cmpLtsRDeltaT` forms the reciprocal step `r_P = (|u_P| + c_P) / (CFL V_P^(1/3))`
with `c_P = sqrt(grs T_P)` as (122.12) forms it. `cmpDdtRhoLocal`, `cmpPressureDdtLocal` and
`cmpEnergySourceLocal` are `tsDdtGeneralRho`, `cmpPressureDdt` and `cmpEnergySource` with the
Euler coefficients `a_n = r_P`, `a_0 = -r_P`, `a_00 = 0` taken per cell, in the same expression
order. They carry no floor and no clip (§122.5).

*DESIGN* - the choices §125.4 leaves open:

* **Selection.** A run names `localEuler` for the momentum AND the energy equation (one
  scheme for both, as §125.6 already requires). `Compressible::new` then builds both
  equations on `Euler` and attaches a `LocalStep` to each (`attach_local_step`). The
  pressure equation reads the momentum equation's, because (124.1) shares its ddt. The run
  is steady: every outer iteration is relaxed, and `residualControl` stops it. `CFL` is
  `CompressibleControls::lts.cfl`, finite and above 0, or `Compressible::new` refuses it by
  name. The default is 1, the acoustic Courant limit of an explicit scheme. A lone
  `RhoMomentum` or `RhoEnergy` still refuses `localEuler` by name.
* **When `r` is formed.** Once per pseudo step, at its top, right after the old levels
  rotate. It is formed from the cell `u` and `T` the step starts from, so every outer
  iteration and every corrector of the step uses one step field. The energy equation's
  field is a device copy of the momentum equation's.
* **The mass imbalance** of §125.6 step 8 takes `a_n = r_P`, `a_0 = -r_P` per cell, and its
  denominator is `sum_P rho_P V_P r_P`.
* **Capture.** The registry row is `Via` the module root, which is `Refused`. The step is
  formed inside `Compressible::step`, and the three time-term kernels run only in equations
  that `Compressible::new` attached it to. The equations' own capture gates run their scalar
  coefficients.

*Tree over plan.* The row names `lts.rs` and `compressible.cu`. The equations also need an
optional attached step: `RhoMomentum::attach_local_step` and `RhoEnergy::attach_local_step`
(additive), one branch in each time term, and the module root's wiring.

**The fixed-point row is MISSED** (an open finding for the user). §125.4 argues that every
ddt difference is zero at a converged fixed point, so the fixed point does not depend on
`CFL`. The argument misses one term. `rAU = V/a_P` (123.5) carries the time term's diagonal
`V_P r_P rho_P`, and the Rhie-Chow flux of (123.6)-(123.7) carries `rAU` at the fixed point,
where the ddt differences themselves vanish. So the fixed point moves with `CFL`, just as
steady SIMPLE's moves with `alpha_U`, whose relaxed diagonal enters `rAU` the same way. A
cure would change the Rhie-Chow numerics (a time-step-independent `rAU` or a ddt
correction), so it is the user's decision (docs/17 §5.3.4).

CMP-13's gate table (`tests/shared/compressible_lts_cases.rs`, included by
`src/compressible/lts.rs` and by `tests/compressible_lts.rs`, so it runs in both builds):

| test | class | what |
|---|---|---|
| `dt_field_matches_host_formula` | R | One pseudo step of the graded 5x4x3 channel at `CFL` 0.7. The momentum equation's `r_P` equals `1/host_delta_t` in f64 on the device's own inputs within `tol_r(1e-12)` relative, cell by cell. The energy equation's copy has the same bits. Control: `r` varies by more than 1.2 across the box |
| `uniform_step_equals_euler` | R | A uniform 4^3 closed box at 300 K, with one cell 2e4 Pa up and gravity on, so `r_P = c/(CFL h)` is one value. One `localEuler` pseudo step (two outer iterations, relaxation 1) equals one Euler step at `dt = CFL h/c` within the quiescent box's bars (§125.6). Controls: `u` moves by more than 100 bars, and Euler at `2 dt` misses by more than 100 |
| `steady_fixed_point_independent_of_cfl` | P | The steady channel, 1500 pseudo steps at `CFL` 2, 20 and 1e6 and steady SIMPLE at `alpha_U` 0.9 and 0.7, each at its initial-residual floor in f64. Records the miss: `CFL` 2 against 20 is above `1e-8`. Records the cause: SIMPLE's two `alpha_U` differ by more than `1e-8`, the distance to SIMPLE falls as `CFL` grows, and at `CFL` 1e6 `u` and `T` are SIMPLE's within `1e-8`. Under `single` every row is reported (§5.1.4). Control: five pseudo steps in, the two CFLs are `4.3e-3` apart |
| `lts_refusals_name_the_setting` | D | `cfl` 0, -1, NaN and infinity. `localEuler` on the momentum equation alone (`ddtSchemes differ`). A lone `RhoMomentum` on `localEuler` |

Each difference is taken over the field's largest magnitude: `max_P |a_P - b_P| / max_P |a_P|`
(`u` in the Euclidean norm, gauge `p`, `T` in K).

### 125.8 The driver as built (CMP-15)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` `rust/src/bin/compressible.rs` is `ofgpu-compressible`
(a `[[bin]]` of its own). It reads a case in either format, refuses by name what §122.4
leaves out, builds `Compressible` (§125.6) and calls `step` once per time step or SIMPLE
iteration. It adds no numerics. The case's settings reach the controls through one
function, `driver_controls`, which both `run` and the pair test call (§13.4.1).

**The run mode is the case's.** `ddtSchemes default` (JSONC `numerics.ddt`) `steadyState`
or `localEuler` makes a steady run, and `Euler` or `backward` a transient one at the
case's `deltaT`. The number of steps is the case's `endTime/deltaT`
(`TurbulenceControls::n_outer_iterations`, as both readers lower it), and `-iters N`
overrides it. A steady run stops early when `residualControl` (`U`, `p`, `T`; OpenFOAM
`SIMPLE/residualControl` only, because JSONC has no such key; the energy bar may be
spelled `T`, `h` or `e`) is met on the initial residuals (§125.6). A bar the case does not
name is 0 and is never met, and the banner says that the run will take every iteration.

**What is read, and from where** (both formats through `common::CaseNumerics`):

| control | setting |
|---|---|
| `momentum.div_scheme`, `grad_scheme`, `sn_grad` | `div(phi,U)`, `grad(U)`, `laplacianSchemes`/`snGradSchemes` `default` |
| `energy.div_scheme`, `grad_scheme`, `sn_grad` | `div(phi,T)`, `grad(T)`, the same `default` |
| `pressure.retarded` | `div(phid,p)`: `Gauss upwind` (and its absence) is `Retarded::Upwind`; a §7 limited scheme is `Retarded::Limited`, §124.1's `limitedRetarded`; any other scheme is refused by name |
| `u_solver`, `p_solver`, `t_solver` | `solvers/U`, `solvers/p`, `solvers/T` (JSONC `numerics.solvers`) |
| `u_relax`, `t_relax`, `p_relax` | `relaxationFactors` `U`, `T` (equations) and `p` (fields); JSONC `numerics.relaxation` |
| `n_outer`, `n_corr`, `pressure.n_non_orth_corr` | `nOuterCorrectors`, `nCorrectors`, `nNonOrthogonalCorrectors` |
| `lts.cfl` | `maxCo` (§125.7) |
| `momentum.g`, `energy.g` | `constant/g` (JSONC `physics.gravity`) |
| `gas` | `constant/thermophysicalProperties` or `physics.compressible` (§122.6) |

`viscousWork` stays on, the §125.1 default when `mu > 0`; no case key exists for it yet. A
`bounded` prefix on `div(phi,U)` or `div(phi,T)` is refused by name: both equations are
conservative on the mass flux, and `div(mdot)` is `-ddt(rho)` there, not a convergence
error. Under `-permissive` the scheme runs without the prefix and says so.

**Refused by name** (§122.4): `-np` and `-parallel`, an mpiexec environment (`PMI_RANK`,
`PMI_SIZE`) and a `processor*` directory (decomposition); the JSONC `motion` block and a
`constant/dynamicMeshDict` other than `staticFvMesh` (motion); JSONC `sources` and the files
`fvOptions`, `fvModels` and `fvConstraints` under `constant/` or `system/` (sources); every
turbulence model but laminar; `physics.buoyancy` `boussinesq` (this solver carries the full
density); a non-Newtonian rheology; a case with no gas. *As built* (CMP-25): Spalart-Allmaras
runs here in its conservative form (§127.1), on the OpenFOAM route and with the coupling of
§127.1.2; a JSONC case naming it is refused with a message that names `physics.turbulence`,
`SpalartAllmaras` and `nuTilda`, because the JSONC format has no nuTilda initial field to state
the model's unknown with. A boundary
condition on `U`, `p` or `T` must be one of `fixedValue`, `zeroGradient`, `fixedGradient`,
`mixed`, `noSlip`, `slip`, `symmetry`, `symmetryPlane` and `empty`, the types whose §4 triple
as set up is the whole condition (§126.7). Every other type is refused with the field, the
patch and the type. CMP-16's inlets (`totalPressure` with `gamma`, `totalTemperature`,
`flowRateInletVelocity` with `massFlowRate`) are lowered before this check (§126.8), and so
are CMP-17's `waveTransmissive` (§126.9) and CMP-18's `characteristicFarfield` (§126.10).
Every other type is refused with a message saying that this driver rewrites no boundary
between iterations but §126.8-§126.10's conditions.
`output.restart` is refused through `OutputPlan::refuse_restart`, because no checkpoint of
the compressible state exists.

**What is written.** `p` (the gauge `p` of §122.2), `U`, `T`, `rho` and `Mach` go through
the one pipeline of §44, from the case's `output` block or from `-output`, `-writeInterval`
(transient) and `-writeEvery` (steady). The writers are `foam`, `vtu`, `nvdb`, `vdb` and
`usda`. `rho` is the solver's cell and boundary density. `Mach` is (122.12) on the host,
from the written `u` and `T`, per cell and per boundary face. Both carry `calculated` on
every patch but a constraint patch. *DESIGN* (§122.2 left it to CMP-15): `p_abs` is not
written. `pOperating` is a constant of the case, so `p_abs = p + p_op` is recovered exactly
from the written `p`, and a second pressure field would be a second statement of one
unknown.

**The low-Mach refusal.** `ofgpu-lowmach`'s `M > 0.3` refusal and its `-permissive`
warning (`energy::refuse_above_low_mach`, §93.6) and its banner line now name
`ofgpu-compressible` (message only).

**Tests** (`cargo test --release --bin ofgpu-compressible`, module `compressible`):

| test | class | what it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `every_knob_changes_the_run` | D | The 50-cell tube below, three steps. Each of 20 settings changes the written bytes: `div(phi,U)`, `div(phi,T)`, `div(phid,p)`, `grad` (with a limited scheme that reads it), `relaxation` `U`, `T` and `p` (with two outer correctors, so a non-final iteration is relaxed), `correctors`, `outerCorrectors`, the `p`, `U` and `T` solver tolerances, `ddt` Euler to backward, `deltaT`, `gamma`, `W`, `Pr`, the Sutherland `As`, `pOperating` and `gravity`. `nonOrthogonalCorrectors` is §13.4.1's one admissible exception (the tube is orthogonal, so the correction it repeats is zero) and is asserted on the controls |
| `the_orthogonal_settings_reach_the_controls` | D | `nonOrthogonalCorrectors 2` reaches `pressure.n_non_orth_corr`; `-iters 7` overrides the case's 3 steps. On the OpenFOAM cavity made steady with `localEuler`, `SIMPLE/residualControl { p 1e-3; U 1e-4; h 1e-5; }` reaches the three bars and `maxCo 5` reaches `lts.cfl` (a steady run's stop and its pseudo step are not shown by three transient steps) |
| `refusals_name_the_setting` | D | 11 JSONC refusals (SA naming nuTilda, kOmegaSST, `sources`, `motion`, `boussinesq`, `div(phid,p) Gauss linear`, `bounded`, an `inletOutlet` `U`, no `physics.compressible`, `-np`, `-writeEvery` on a transient run) and 5 OpenFOAM ones (`processor0`, `dynamicMeshDict`, `system/fvOptions`, `simulationType RAS`, no `thermophysicalProperties`); each message names its setting |
| `a_fifty_cell_tube_runs_in_under_thirty_seconds` | P | The smoke run: 1 m tube, 50 x 1 x 1 cells, air at 300 K and 50 m/s, a 320 K inlet, a fixed `p = 0` outlet, symmetry sides, Euler at `1e-5` s for 30 steps. It runs in under 30 s with no bounds violation, `M_max` in (0.14, 0.15) (50/347.2 = 0.144), and the five fields written |
| `an_openfoam_case_runs_and_writes_the_five_fields` | P | A blockgen 8 x 8 x 1 cavity with `thermophysicalProperties` (§122.6's air), laminar, Euler at `1e-3` s for 5 steps, writes the five fields |

The driver is a binary, and the tests are bin tests of the f64 build (the single lib test
crate does not compile, §112.3). The single build compiles the binary
(`cargo build --release --features single --bin ofgpu-compressible`). Its rows are class D
and P: they ask for a bit difference, a finite run and a refusal text, so no f32 tolerance
is involved.

*Landed* (f64): `every_knob_changes_the_run` found no inert setting (20 of 20).
The smoke run took `0.22` s for its 30 steps (bar 30 s), and `M_max` was `0.1440`. The
single-precision binary runs the same tube in `0.31` s with `M_max` `0.1440` (reported, not a
test row).

#### 125.8.1 A non-uniform start in a JSONC case: `initial.regions` (CMP-28)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` A JSONC `initial` block states one uniform value per field, so a shock tube's two states could not be written as a case (docs/17-review-later.md, CMP-29's row). `initial.regions` is a list of boxes. Each box states any of `U`, `p` and `T`, and those values replace the uniform ones in the cells whose centre lies in the box. The rule is ORIGINAL, this tree's choice:

```
S_r = { c : min_r,k <= x_c,k <= max_r,k for k = 1, 2, 3 },   x_c = origin + c_c, widened to f64      (125.5)
phi_c := phi_r  for every c in S_r and every phi in {U, p, T} that region r states, r = 0, 1, ... in file order   (125.6)
```

The box is closed, so a centre on a face of it is inside. A later region overrides an earlier one where they overlap. The values reach the fields `as Scalar`, the same conversion every stated value takes. The selection is made on the host, in f64 in both builds, before any GPU work.

`JsonCase::lower` refuses a region, by its JSON path, when it states none of `U`, `p` and `T` (`initial.regions[i]`); when a box bound is not finite or `min > max` (`initial.regions[i].box`); when it states `T` while the case has no `initial.T`, or a `T <= 0` (`initial.regions[i].T`). It refuses any region on a case without `physics.compressible`, because only `ofgpu-compressible` applies them. `LoweredCase::apply_initial_regions` refuses a box that selects no cell of the mesh. The driver prints one line per region: `initial.regions[i]: N cells (SPEC-LIT 125.8.1)`.

**`cases/sodShockTube.jsonc`** states Sod's problem (Sod 1978, doi:10.1016/0021-9991(78)90023-2) as Gate CMP-SOD sets it up (§127.6.1): 200 cells, air with `mu = 0`, `p_op = p_L = 1e5` Pa, the left state `p = 0`, `T = 348.36526821702523` K, and one region `x >= 0.5` with `p = -90000`, `T = 278.69221457362016` K, both ends closed walls. It runs to `t = 0.2 L/sqrt(p_L/rho_L) = 6.324555320336759e-4` s in 176 steps, with the gate's PIMPLE leg (5 outer iterations, `p` unrelaxed, van Leer on the three convections). That leg meets the gate's bars; the gate's own PISO row misses them. The case is not a gate, and no test checks its numbers against the exact solution.

| test | class | what it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `io::case_json::tests::initial_regions_lower_in_order_and_refuse_by_name` | D | two regions lower in file order with their stated values; the five refusals, each by its path |
| `io::case_json::tests::initial_regions_apply_by_cell_centre` | D | 10 cells: `x >= 0.5` selects 5 cells and `x >= 0.75` 3, the later region wins on `p` and `U` and keeps the earlier `T`; a box off the mesh is refused; no regions touches nothing |
| `the_shipped_sod_case_states_the_gate_pimple_controls` (bin) | D | `driver_controls` of the shipped case is Gate CMP-SOD's PIMPLE leg, setting by setting |
| `the_shipped_sod_case_runs` (bin) | P | the shipped case runs 176 steps with no bound, writes the five fields, and its final `p` is not uniform |

**Measured** (2026-10-18, this tree, the RTX 5070 Ti shared with two other jobs): `ofgpu-compressible cases/sodShockTube.jsonc` prints `initial.regions[0]: 100 cells` and runs 176 steps with no bound, in 25.3 s (f64; final `M_max` 0.9918) and 39.3 s (f32; final `M_max` 0.9930).

#### 125.8.2 The nozzle recipe: `cases/nozzle` (CMP-28)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` A JSONC mesh is a box, so Gate CMP-NOZ's duct (§127.5.2) ships as an OpenFOAM case directory. Its `constant/polyMesh` is what `write_poly_mesh_raw` writes for `nozzle_duct(&DuctSpec::default())`: 200 cells, patches `inlet`, `outlet`, `walls` and `frontAndBack`. The test `the_shipped_nozzle_case_is_the_generated_one` pins it to that builder, and with `OFGPU_WRITE_NOZZLE_CASE=1` the same test rewrites it. The case is the gate's subsonic regime: air with `mu = 0` and `p_op = 1e5` Pa, a `totalPressure` inlet (`p0 = 0` gauge, so `p_t1 = p_op`) with `totalTemperature` `T0 = 300` K, a fixed outlet `p = -5000` Pa (`p_b/p_t1 = 0.95`), and `symmetry` walls. It starts at rest at `T = 300` K, with a gauge `p` of `-25 (2i + 1)/2` Pa in cell `i`: the gate's linear start, taken at each cell's axial midpoint (ORIGINAL). It runs the gate's controls: `localEuler` at `maxCo 1`, one outer corrector, van Leer on the three convections, relaxation `p` 0.3, `U` 0.7 and `T` 0.7, and 15000 iterations. `cases/nozzle/README.md` is the recipe. The gate MISSES its `M(x)` bar on this duct (§127.6.5), and the case reproduces that run; it does not claim a pass.

| test | class | what it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `the_shipped_nozzle_case_is_the_generated_one` (bin) | D | the five polyMesh files and `0/p`'s internal list are the generated ones |
| `the_shipped_nozzle_case_states_the_gate_controls` (bin) | D | `driver_controls` of the case is Gate CMP-NOZ's, setting by setting |
| `the_shipped_nozzle_recipe_runs` (bin) | P | `-iters 200` runs 200 iterations with no bound |

**Measured** (2026-10-18, the shared RTX 5070 Ti): as written, f64, 15000 iterations in 463 s, no bound, final `M_max` 0.6736 and `M_mean` 0.4503. The single build's `-iters 200` smoke ran in 10.2 s with no bound. Its 15000-iteration run was not made under the 10-minute rule. All 19 of `ofgpu-compressible`'s tests pass in f64. Under `single`, 18 pass, and the one failure is the pre-existing `every_knob_changes_the_run` of §112.3.

## 126. The compressible boundary conditions — each a §4 triple rewrite

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` CMP-16 implements §126.1-§126.3 (as built in
§126.8), CMP-17 §126.4-§126.5 (as built in §126.9) and CMP-18 §126.6 (as built in §126.10), in `src/compressible/bc.rs` and `cuda/compressible.cu`; BC-20 adds the free-stream family there (§126.11).
docs/17 §5.2.3 gives COMP these kinds. Each registers its name in §120's catalogue when
it lands. Every one is a kernel that rewrites the §4 triple
`psi_b = fr psi_ref + (1 - fr)(psi_P + g_ref/Delta_b)` on its faces once per outer
iteration, from the latest interior state: the assembly gains no branch.

`n` is the unit OUTWARD normal (`Sf/|Sf|` on a boundary face). A face is an inflow face
when `u_b . n < 0`, the convention of Carlson's Table 1. `u_n,P = u_P . n` and
`c_P = sqrt(gamma R_s T_P)` are the owner cell's.

### 126.1 Total pressure and total temperature (`totalPressure` with `gamma`, `totalTemperature`)

On an inflow face, from the boundary velocity `u_b` (which `U`'s own condition supplies,
normally extrapolated):

```
T_b = T_0 - |u_b|^2 / (2 c_p)                                                              (126.1)
p_b = (p_0 + p_op) (T_b / T_0)^(gamma/(gamma-1)) - p_op                                   (126.2)
    = p_0 + (p_0 + p_op) expm1( gamma/(gamma-1) * log1p( -|u_b|^2 / (2 c_p T_0) ) )        (126.3)
```

(126.1) is Carlson's eq. (48) and NACA 1135 (43) (`c_p T_0 = c_p T + |u|^2/2` with
(122.5)); (126.2) is NACA 1135 (35) and (44) with `T_b/T_0` in place of
`(1 + (gamma-1)/2 M^2)^-1`; the oracle holds (126.1)-(126.2) to NACA (43)-(44) to
`5.6e-16`. (126.3) is (126.2) rewritten (derived) so that the gauge `p_b` is formed
without the cancellation of `(...) - p_op`: it is the form the kernel evaluates in both
builds. `p_0` is the case's total pressure in the gauge of the `p` field (so the
absolute total pressure is `p_0 + p_op`), and `T_0` its total temperature. The triples
are `fr = 1` with `psi_ref = p_b` (on `p`) and `psi_ref = T_b` (on `T`). On an outflow
face both are zero-gradient (`fr = 0, g = 0`). `totalPressure` WITHOUT `gamma` stays
the incompressible condition of `field_setup.rs`, bitwise unchanged.

*DESIGN* - the explicit form (126.1)-(126.2) rather than Carlson §2.7's characteristic
form ((36)-(47), which extrapolates `R+` and solves a quadratic for `c_b`): the
pressure-based solver takes its inflow velocity from the momentum equation, and the
explicit form is exact for any `u_b`. CMP-16's
`total_conditions_satisfy_isentropic_relation_to_round_off` (class R) and
`outflow_face_is_zero_gradient` (class D) test it.

### 126.2 Supersonic inflow (the JSONC preset `supersonicInlet`)

`p`, `U` and `T` are all `fixedValue` (`fr = 1`) at the stated state: Carlson §2.9,
eq. (57), "all" specified for supersonic inflow (Table 1, case 3).

### 126.3 Compressible mass-flow inlet

```
u_b = - ( mdot_set / sum_{f in patch} rho_f |Sf| ) n_f ,   rho_f = psi_f (p_b,f + p_op)      (126.4)
```

`fr = 1` on `U` with `psi_ref = u_b`. Then `sum_f rho_f u_b . Sf = -mdot_set` exactly up
to round-off (derived; the inflow sign is the outward normal's). `T` comes from its own
condition: `fixedValue`, or `totalTemperature` through (126.1), Carlson's eq. (48)
adiabatic statement. `p` is zero-gradient. CMP-16's `mass_flow_inlet_delivers_mdot_to_1e-10`
(class A) tests it.

### 126.4 Static-pressure outlet with the supersonic switch

```
p_b = p_set                      if  u_n,P / c_P < 1        (fr = 1)
    = extrapolated  (fr = 0, g = 0)   otherwise                                          (126.5)
```

Carlson §2.4 eq. (25), applied per face with the owner's normal Mach number. `U` and `T`
are zero-gradient (Carlson §2.4 "extrapolate U, T"). The switch is evaluated per face
each outer iteration.

### 126.5 The non-reflecting outlet (`waveTransmissive`, with `lInf` and `fieldInf`)

The outgoing-wave condition on a field `phi` is advective with a linear relaxation
toward a far value `phi_inf` over a length `L` (`lInf`):

```
d phi/dt + w d phi/dn = K (phi_inf - phi)                                                  (126.6)
w = u_n,P + c_P   (on p) ,     w = u_n,P   (on any other field)
K = sigma c_P (1 - M_n^2) / L ,   M_n = u_n,P / c_P ;    K = 0 when lInf is not stated
```

Discretised implicitly in time on the face, with `d phi/dn = (phi_b - phi_P)/Delta_b`
and `alpha = w dt / Delta_b`:

```
(phi_b - phi_b^o)/dt + w (phi_b - phi_P)/Delta_b = K (phi_inf - phi_b)
  =>  phi_b = fr ref + (1 - fr) phi_P ,
      fr  = (1 + K dt) / (1 + alpha + K dt) ,   ref = (phi_b^o + K dt phi_inf) / (1 + K dt)    (126.7)
```

(126.7) is (126.6)'s update exactly (derived), and it is the §4 triple with
`psi_ref = ref`, `g_ref = 0`: the oracle holds the two to `4.4e-16` on 1000 random
states. `phi_b^o` is the face value of the last step (refreshed once per step, §125.3);
under LTS `dt` is the owner's `dt_P`. (126.6) needs a time step, so a steady SIMPLE run
without LTS refuses `waveTransmissive` by name. The form is Orlanski's (1976) advective outlet
with the acoustic speed added for `p`, and the relaxation term is the partially
reflecting treatment of Rudy & Strikwerda (1980) and Poinsot & Lele (1992) (all *not
read*). docs/17 §5.2.3 gives BC-09 the generic `advective` kernel with the wave speed
as a face-field input; CMP-17 calls it with (126.6)'s `w`, and if BC-09 has not landed
when CMP-17 runs, CMP-17 writes the kernel to BC-09's contract.

**`sigma` has no recalled default.** The plan quotes about 0.27 from Rudy & Strikwerda
(1980); that paper is not read here. CMP-17 reads it and records the value with its
page in this subsection, or, failing that, `sigma` is a required entry when `lInf` is
stated. CMP-17 did not read it, so `sigma` is required (§126.9). The reflection coefficient Selle et al. (2004) derive for this condition is not
used by any gate: Gate CMP-NR measures the reflection directly (§127.6).

### 126.6 The characteristic far-field (`characteristicFarfield`; JSONC `farfield`)

Carlson §2.2, eqs. (8)-(17), with `i` the interior (owner) state and `o` the stated
free stream, in absolute pressure, with `U_i = u_i . n`, `U_o = u_o . n`,
`c^2 = gamma p_abs/rho`:

```
R+ = U_i + 2 c_i/(gamma - 1) ,          R- = U_o - 2 c_o/(gamma - 1)                         (126.8)
if U_i > 0 and |U_i|/c_i >= 1:  R- = U_i - 2 c_i/(gamma - 1)      (supersonic outflow)       (126.9)
if U_i < 0 and |U_i|/c_i >= 1:  R+ = U_o + 2 c_o/(gamma - 1)      (supersonic inflow)
U_b = (R+ + R-)/2 ,        c_b = (gamma - 1)(R+ - R-)/4                                       (126.10)
u_b = u_i + (U_b - U_i) n ,   s_b = p_abs,i / rho_i^gamma        if U_b > 0  (outflow)
u_b = u_o + (U_b - U_o) n ,   s_b = p_abs,o / rho_o^gamma        if U_b <= 0 (inflow)         (126.11)
rho_b = ( c_b^2 / (gamma s_b) )^(1/(gamma-1)) ,  p_abs,b = rho_b c_b^2 / gamma ,  T_b = p_abs,b / (rho_b R_s)   (126.12)
```

(126.8)-(126.12) are Carlson's (8), (12), (13), (14), (15), (16) and (17), with his
entropy `c^2/(gamma rho^(gamma-1))` written as `p/rho^gamma` (the same quantity, by
(122.4)). Supersonic branches follow Carlson's text: in supersonic outflow no incoming
characteristic exists and every quantity comes from the interior; in supersonic inflow
every quantity comes from the free stream. The triples are `fr = 1` on `p`
(`psi_ref = p_abs,b - p_op`), `U` (`u_b`) and `T` (`T_b`), refreshed each outer
iteration. CMP-18's tests: `freestream_preserved_m0_5_and_m1_5` (interior state equal
to the free stream at normal Mach `+-0.5` and `+-1.5`: the face state equals it to
`1e-10` relative in f64 and `1e-5` in f32; class R), `branch_selection_by_un_and_c`
(class D), `invariants_exact_on_host_twin` (class R). The oracle reproduces the free
stream to the last digit printed (15) on all four branches.

### 126.7 Walls and symmetry

Unchanged: `noSlip` (with adiabatic `zeroGradient` or isothermal `fixedValue` on `T`),
`slip`/`symmetryPlane` (§120's aliases) and `empty` carry no compressible algebra. A
slip wall makes the quasi-1-D duct and the Ringleb walls of §127.3.

### 126.8 The inlets as built (CMP-16)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` `rust/src/compressible/bc.rs` and three
kernels of `cuda/compressible.cu` (`cmpBcTotalTemperature`, `cmpBcTotalPressure`,
`cmpBcMassFlowInlet`) implement §126.1 and §126.3 exactly as written there: (126.1) on
`T`, (126.3) on `p`, (126.4) on `U`. §126.2's preset needs no kernel: CMP-14 already
lowers a JSONC `supersonicInlet` rule to `fixedValue` on `U`, `p` and `T` (§122.6).

**Names.** On the OpenFOAM route (`0/p`, `0/T`, `0/U`) the three conditions are
`totalPressure` with `p0` and `gamma` on `p`, `totalTemperature` with `T0` (and an
optional `gamma`) on `T`, and `flowRateInletVelocity` with `massFlowRate` on `U`. JSONC has
no spelling for them yet, because a new JSONC kind needs the schema and the gui pick-lists
too. `bc::lower` reads every value in f64 in both builds and refuses by name: a
`totalPressure` without `gamma` (that is the kinematic `p0 - |U|^2/2` condition of
`field_setup.rs`, which a gas does not obey), a stated `gamma` that differs from the gas's
by more than `1e-12` relative (the gas law carries one ratio), a missing `p0`, `T0` or
`massFlowRate`, `p0 + p_op <= 0`, `T0 <= 0`, `massFlowRate <= 0`, a
`volumetricFlowRate`, a kind on the wrong field, and a mass-flow inlet whose `p` is not
`zeroGradient` (§126.3).

**Lowering, not a new setup arm.** `bc::lower` hands the shared setup of `field_setup.rs` the
three fields with each of these entries replaced by a `fixedValue` placeholder (at `p_0`,
`T_0` or zero velocity), and returns one `BcRule` per mesh patch (its face range and its
value). `Compressible::set_boundary_rules` attaches them. `field.rs` and `field_setup.rs` are
not touched, so the incompressible `totalPressure` of every other driver is bitwise what it
was. §120's catalogue keeps `totalTemperature` as owned by CMP-16, because the catalogue
describes `BcKind::from_name`, and the shared setup still refuses it (it has no gas law).
The driver writes the fields with the types as read.

**When.** `Compressible::initialise` applies the rules once after its first gas state and
then re-forms `mu` and `kappa`. `Compressible::step` applies them at the top of every
outer iteration (step 0 of §125.6's loop), from the latest state, in this order:

1. The mass-flow inlets, from `psi_b` and `p_b`, then `U`'s face values.
2. The total temperatures, from `u_b`, then `T`'s face values.
3. The total pressures, from `u_b` (and `T_b`), then `p`'s face values.
4. `psi` and `rho` on the boundary faces only, by (122.10). The cells are not touched.

A run with no rule launches none of this, so it is bitwise the CMP-15 driver.

**`T_0` of `totalPressure`.** It is the same patch's `totalTemperature` `T0` when `T` carries
one. Otherwise each face takes `T_0 = T_b + |u_b|^2 / (2 c_p)`, which is (126.1) solved for
`T_0` at the face (NACA 1135 (43), derived). Either way (126.3) holds with the face Mach
number `M^2 = |u_b|^2 / (gamma R_s T_b)`.

**Constants and order.** The host forms `cp2 = fl(2 c_p)`, `ge = fl(gamma/(gamma-1))` and
`pt = fl(p_0 + p_op)` in f64 and rounds each once. The kinetic term is `q / cp2`, a division
by the doubled `c_p`, not a product with a rounded reciprocal. (126.4)'s sum
`A = sum_f rho_f |Sf|` is accumulated in `ofacc` by one block of 256 threads, with a
fixed-order tree in shared memory, so it is deterministic. `rho_f = psi_f (p_f + p_op)` is
formed in the order `cmpGasState` forms `rho`, so it is the `rho` the boundary carries.
Then `u_b = -(mdot/A) Sf/|Sf|`. There is no floor and no clip: `|u_b|^2 >= 2 c_p T_0` has no
isentropic state, and the kernels write what (126.1) and (126.3) give there (§122.3).

**The gate** (`tests/shared/compressible_bc_cases.rs`, included by the lib tests of
`compressible::bc` and by `tests/compressible_bc.rs`, so both builds run it):

| test | class | row | measured (f64; f32) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `total_conditions_satisfy_isentropic_relation_to_round_off` | R, `tol_r(1e-13)` | inflow faces at M 0.1, 0.5, 0.9; `T_b` and `p_b + p_op` against NACA 1135 (43)-(44), once with `totalTemperature`, once with a fixed `T` | `e_T` 0, `e_p` <= 1.43e-16; `e_T` <= 8.0e-9, `e_p` <= 2.5e-8 |
| `outflow_face_is_zero_gradient` | D | `u_b . Sf > 0`: `fr = 0` and `refGrad = 0` bitwise, and the face value is the owner cell's, bitwise, on `p` and `T` | bitwise in both |
| `mass_flow_inlet_delivers_mdot_to_1e_10` | A, 1e-10 (f32: `tol_r(1e-10)`) | a graded 6-face patch with a non-uniform `T`: `sum_f rho_f u_b . Sf = -mdot`, and `u_b` is normal to the face | rel. err 0; 1.5e-8 |
| `a_total_pressure_tube_runs` | P | 50-cell tube, `p0 = 2000` Pa and `T0 = 300` K against a fixed `p = 0` outlet, 10 Euler steps: no bounds violation, finite, and the inflow accelerates from 10 m/s | `u_b` 14.54 m/s, `M_max` 0.042 in both |
| `inlet_refusals_name_the_setting` | D | the refusals above name the field, the patch and the entry | - |

The plan names the third test `mass_flow_inlet_delivers_mdot_to_1e-10`, which is not a
Rust identifier, so it is spelled `..._1e_10`. Its f32 row takes D-F32-1's `tol32`: the
sum equals `-mdot` up to round-off by construction (§126.3), so it is an R-class row in
f32. The driver adds `an_openfoam_case_with_the_compressible_inlets_runs` (the
OpenFOAM route reads both kinds and runs) and a refusal row for `totalPressure` without
`gamma`.

### 126.9 The outlets as built (CMP-17)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` `rust/src/compressible/bc.rs` (`OutletRule`,
`CompressibleOutlets`) and two kernels appended to `cuda/compressible.cu`
(`cmpBcSupersonicSwitch`, `cmpBcWaveSpeed`) implement §126.4 and §126.5. The Robin rewrite
of (126.7) is BC-09's own kernel (`fldAdvectiveRobinScalar`, (120.4d) of SPEC-LIT 120.4),
called through `field_ops::advective_robin_scalar` with (126.6)'s `w` and `K` as its
face-field inputs, as docs/17 §5.2.3 planned. `field.rs` is not edited and no `BcKind` is
added: the outlets carry their own kind mask (`BcKind::Advective` on their faces, -1
elsewhere), which is the buffer the kernel matches.

**Names.** On the OpenFOAM route, `waveTransmissive` on `p` or `T` with the optional entries
`lInf`, `fieldInf`, `sigma` and `gamma`. `sigma` is this solver's own entry: Rudy &
Strikwerda (1980) is not read, so §126.5's fallback holds and `sigma` is REQUIRED when
`lInf` is stated, with no default. `bc::lower` reads every value in f64 and refuses by
name: `lInf <= 0`; `lInf` without `sigma` or without `fieldInf`; `sigma <= 0`; `sigma` or
`fieldInf` without `lInf` (read by nothing, since `K = 0` then); a stated `gamma` that is
not the gas's (§126.8's rule); a `phi`, `rho` or `psi` entry naming another field than
`phi`, `rho` and `thermo:psi` (or `psi`), since (126.6) is formed from the solver's own
state; and `waveTransmissive` on `U`, which is not built (a non-reflecting outlet takes
`U` zero-gradient). `Compressible::set_outlet_rules` refuses it under `steadyState` (no
time step) and `CrankNicolson` ((120.4c) is defined for Euler and backward only).
`advective` stays refused in `ofgpu-compressible`, with a message naming
`waveTransmissive`. §120's catalogue keeps `waveTransmissive` as owned by CMP-17, for the
reason §126.8 gives for `totalTemperature`: the catalogue describes `BcKind::from_name`.

**The supersonic switch** is attached to every `fixedValue` `p` patch as read (§126.4 does
not name a type; the static-pressure outlet is the fixed `p`). `cmpBcSupersonicSwitch`
writes `fr = 1` where `u_n,P / c_P < 1` and `fr = 0` otherwise, and `refGrad = 0`; it
leaves `refValue` (the stated `p`) as set up. A subsonic face therefore carries the triple
it had, and a supersonic inflow face (`u_n < 0`) stays fixed. `u_n,P = (u_P . Sf)/|Sf|`
and `c_P = sqrt(fl(gamma R_s) T_P)` are the owner cell's.

**`waveTransmissive`.** It is built as a `zeroGradient` placeholder, so `phi_b^o` starts
at the owner's value. `cmpBcWaveSpeed` forms, per face,

```
w = max(u_n,P + c_P, 0)   on p ,     w = max(u_n,P, 0)   on T
K = max(sigma_by_l c_P (1 - M_n^2), 0) ,   M_n = u_n,P / c_P ,   sigma_by_l = fl(sigma / lInf)
```

Both clips are *DESIGN*, ours, and the only ones. `w >= 0` is (120.4b)'s rule: a back-flow
`T` face holds its time extrapolation (`fr = 1`). `K >= 0` holds because at `M_n >= 1`
there is no incoming characteristic to relax. Without `lInf`, `sigma_by_l = 0` and
`K = 0`. Time:

* Under `Euler` or `backward`, `w` and `K` are used as formed, with the run's own
  `(a_n, a_0, a_00)` (`Ddt::face_coeffs`). That is (120.4d), which is (126.7) under Euler.
* Under `localEuler`, `cmpBcWaveSpeed` divides `w` and `K` by the owner's `r_P = 1/dt_P`,
  and the Robin kernel takes `(1, -1, 0)`. Then `d = 1 + K dt_P` and
  `fr = d/(d + w dt_P Delta_b)`, which is (126.7) with §126.5's "under LTS `dt` is the
  owner's `dt_P`".

`phi_b^o` and `phi_b^oo` are set to the face values in `Compressible::initialise`, and
rotated (`oo <- o`, `o <- phi_b`) once at the top of every step. The rewrite runs at the
top of every outer iteration, after the inlets and the switches. The order is `p`'s
faces, then `T`'s, each followed by its §4 evaluation, and then `psi` and `rho` on the
boundary faces (§126.8 step 4). The start of a run applies the switches only, because it
has no step yet.

**The gate** (`tests/shared/compressible_bc_cases.rs`, both builds as in §126.8):

| test | class | row | measured (f64; f32) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `robin_form_matches_advective_update_exactly` | R, `tol_r(1e-13)` | 4 faces at `M_n` 0.3, 0.8, 1.2 (`K` clipped) and -0.4 (`w` clipped on `T`), `p` and `T` with `lInf`, Euler and LTS, the cells moved off `phi_b^o`. The device `fr`, `refValue` against (126.7), and the face value against the face update `(phi_b - phi_b^o)/dt + w Delta_b (phi_b - phi_P) = K (phi_inf - phi_b)` solved directly | <= 3.8e-16; <= 8.6e-8 |
| `supersonic_switch_by_owner_mach` | D | `M_n` 0.5, 0.999, 1.5 and -1.5. `fr` 1, 1, 0, 1 bitwise, `refValue` kept, and `p_b` the owner's on the supersonic face | bitwise in both |
| `subsonic_fixed_p_outlet_is_bitwise_unchanged` | D | 40-cell tube, 10 Euler steps, with and without the switch attached: `p`, `p_b`, `T`, `rho`, `rho_b`, `u_x` | 0 differing values in both |
| `gate_cmp_nr_acoustic_pulse` | P | Gate CMP-NR, below | below |
| `outlet_refusals_name_the_setting` | D | the refusals above | - |

The driver adds `an_openfoam_case_with_a_wave_transmissive_outlet_runs`: the OpenFOAM route
reads `waveTransmissive` on `p` and runs.

**Gate CMP-NR as measured.** The tube is 200 cells of 5 mm, closed on the left, with air at
300 K and `p_op = 1e5` Pa. The pulse is `p' = A exp(-((x - x0)/W)^2)` with `A = 1e-3 p`,
`W = 10` cells (an e-folding width of 20 cells) and `x0` 40 cells from the outlet. It is
initialised as a simple wave (`u' = p'/(rho_0 c_0)`, isentropic `T'`). The run uses Euler,
acoustic CFL 0.2, one outer iteration and 3 correctors. The outlet is
`waveTransmissive` with `lInf 1`, `sigma 0.25` and `fieldInf 0`.

**Reflection** is the largest `|p'_run - p'_ref|` at the probe (cell 190, 10 cells from the
outlet) over 400 steps, divided by the largest `|p'_ref|`. Here `ref` is the same run in a
400-cell tube, whose outlet nothing can come back from within the window. *DESIGN*, ours.
The characteristic split `max|p-|/max|p+|` with `p+- = (p' +- rho_0 c_0 u')/2` is printed
only: in the reference run, where nothing is reflected, it already reads 0.089, because
the discrete wave's `u'/p'` is not `1/(rho_0 c_0)`.

**The long-time mean** is the outlet face's `p` averaged over the last tenth of 16 000
steps (46.1 ms = 4/K with `K = sigma c / lInf`), against `fieldInf`, relative to `A`.

| row | bar | f64 | f32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| reflection, `waveTransmissive` | <= 0.05 | **0.1821, MISSED** | **0.1828, MISSED** |
| reflection, fixed `p` (control) | >= 0.9 | 0.9776 | 0.9778 |
| long-time outlet mean | <= 1e-3 of `A` | 2.57e-4 | **1.102e-3, MISSED** |

**The miss.** It is asserted as MISSED (user rule of 2026-10-14) and recorded for review. The
measurements give two parts:

1. The pulse crosses the tube at 1.186 `c_0`, about `sqrt(gamma) c_0`, in both the
   200-cell and the 400-cell tubes. The speed was measured from the peak's arrival at the
   probe, and in a separate two-probe run at CFL 0.2 and 0.05 (1.1878 and 1.1862 `c_0`, so
   it does not depend on `dt`). So the CMP-09..CMP-13 solver carries sound about
   `sqrt(gamma)` too fast, and (126.6)'s `w = u_n + c_P` with the true `c` is slower than
   the solver's own wave. The outlet then reflects an inverted copy of the pulse.
   CMP-20's Gate CMP-AC ("speed within 1 % of (122.4)'s `c`") is the gate that owns this
   speed.
2. A diagnostic build that formed `w` with `fl(gamma^2 R_s)` brought the reflection down to
   0.119 (0.122 with `lInf`), not to 0.05. The rest grows as `dt` falls: 0.117, 0.140,
   0.179 and 0.261 at CFL 1.0, 0.5, 0.2 and 0.05 with `K = 0` and the true `c`. The
   half-cell advective closure (126.7), coupled to the segregated pressure equation by
   its Robin coefficient alone, is therefore not the scheme's own non-reflecting
   relation.

`K` is not the cause (0.1792 with `K = 0`), and more outer iterations or correctors do not
help (0.2288 with 3 outer iterations, 0.1821 with 6 correctors). Each cure changes
numerics, either the solver's acoustic speed (the energy-pressure coupling of §124/§125)
or the outlet's closure (a characteristic condition on `U` as well), and is the user's
decision.

The f32 long-time row misses on its own (§112.3's rule: its own row, both values). The f64
outlet mean decays like `exp(-t/tau)`, halving about every 2000 steps, down to 5.5e-3 Pa at
step 20 000. Under single it stops decaying at step 14 000 and wanders between -0.07 and
+0.16 Pa (to 24 000 steps, sampled every 2000). That is a few f32 ulps of the absolute
state about `p_op = 1e5` Pa: an f32 floor, for §112's owner, not a property of the outlet.

### 126.10 The far-field as built (CMP-18)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` `rust/src/compressible/bc.rs` (`FarfieldRule`,
`CompressibleFarfields`, the host twin `farfield_face`) and one kernel appended to
`cuda/compressible.cu` (`cmpBcFarfield`) implement §126.6 exactly as written there:
(126.8)-(126.12), Carlson (2011) §2.2 eqs. (8)-(17). `field.rs` is not edited and no
`BcKind` is added. §120's catalogue keeps `characteristicFarfield` and `farfield` as owned
by CMP-18, for the reason §126.8 gives for `totalTemperature`: the catalogue describes
`BcKind::from_name`, and the shared setup still refuses both.

**Names.** `characteristicFarfield` on `U`, `p` and `T` of the same patch, each with one
uniform `value`: the free stream's `u_o`, gauge `p_o` (in the datum of `p`) and `T_o`. The
JSONC kind `farfield` lowers to exactly that (§122.6), and `bc::lower` also accepts the
spelling `farfield` in a field file. `bc::lower` refuses by name: the kind on one or two of
the three fields only (one free stream decides all three), a missing or non-uniform
`value`, `T_o <= 0`, `p_o + p_op <= 0` (§122.3), and a stated `gamma` that is not the gas's
(§126.8's rule). Each entry is built as a `fixedValue` placeholder at its free-stream value,
so the faces hold the free stream until the first rewrite. The supersonic switch of §126.9
is not attached: it is attached to a `fixedValue` `p` as read, and this one is not.

**The kernel.** One thread per face of one patch, from the OWNER cell `P`:

```
n = Sf/|Sf| ,  U_i = u_P . n ,  c_i = sqrt(fl(gamma R_s) T_P) ,  U_o = u_o . n
rho_i = (p_P + p_op) / (fl(R_s) T_P)                                    (122.10)'s state
```

then (126.8)-(126.12) in that order, with `fl(2/(gamma-1))`, `fl(1/(gamma-1))`,
`fl(gamma - 1)`, `fl(gamma)`, `fl(R_s)` and `fl(p_op)` formed on the host in f64 and
rounded once, and `c_o = fl(sqrt(gamma R_s T_o))` and `s_o = fl(p_abs,o / rho_o^gamma)`
formed there per patch. (126.9)'s test is `|U_i|/c_i >= 1`, written as a division, as
§126.9's switch writes it. `c_b = (gamma - 1)(R+ - R-) * 0.25`, and the gauge `p` is
`rho_b c_b^2/gamma - p_op`. It writes `fr = 1` and `refGrad = 0` on all three fields and
`refValue = u_b`, `p_abs,b - p_op` and `T_b`, reading only cells, so every face sees the
state of the same moment. There is no floor and no clip: `c_b <= 0` (an expansion the two
invariants cannot carry) is written as the formulas give it, and §122.3's counter sees the
state that follows. `farfield_face` is the f64 host twin in the kernel's operation order;
it also names the face's branch.

**When.** `Compressible::set_farfield_rules` attaches the rules. The rewrite runs once in
`Compressible::initialise` and at the top of every outer iteration, after the inlets of
§126.8 and before the outlets of §126.9; then `U`'s, `p`'s and `T`'s face values, and `psi`
and `rho` on the boundary faces (§126.8 step 4). It needs no time step, so steady runs
take it. A run with no far-field launches none of this.

**The gate** (`tests/shared/compressible_bc_cases.rs`, both builds as in §126.8):

| test | class | row | measured (f64; f32) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `freestream_preserved_m0_5_and_m1_5` | R, `tol_r(1e-10)` (1e-10; 1e-5) | interior equal to the free stream (`u = (M c, 0.2 c, 0)`, `p` 2000 Pa gauge, 300 K) on a far-field at both ends, `M` 0.5 and 1.5, so normal Mach +-0.5 and +-1.5, all four branches. `u_b` against `u_o` relative to `\|u_o\|`, `p_b` relative to `p_o + p_op`, `T_b` relative | `e_u` 2.2e-16, `e_p` 2.9e-16, `e_T` 1.9e-16; 1.6e-7, 1.5e-7, 1.0e-7 |
| `branch_selection_by_un_and_c` | D | rows at `M_n` +-0.5 and +-1.5 against a free stream entering at 0.1 `c`. Changing the free stream's tangential `u` and `p` at fixed `T` leaves the two outflow branches bitwise unchanged; changing the interior's leaves the two inflow branches; the whole free stream leaves supersonic outflow only; the whole interior (in-branch) leaves supersonic inflow only. Every other face changes. `fr = 1` and `refGrad = 0` bitwise, and the face value is `refValue` bitwise | bitwise in both |
| `invariants_exact_on_host_twin` | R, `tol_r(1e-13)` | varied interior (`M_n` 0.4, 1.3, -0.7, -1.2; 305 to 312.5 K; tangential `u`) against a free stream at 310 K entering at 0.2 `c_o`: the device state against `farfield_face` (velocity relative to `c_o`), and on the device face `R+`, `R-` against the sides (126.8)-(126.9) take them from, the entropy and the tangential velocity against the side (126.11) takes them from | twin 4.3e-16, invariants 3.4e-16; 6.2e-7, 1.7e-7 |
| `a_farfield_tube_runs` | P | 50-cell tube, far-field at both ends (free stream M 0.3 along x, 300 K), 305 K interior, 10 Euler steps: finite and no bounds violation | `M_max` 0.3054 in both |
| `farfield_refusals_name_the_setting` | D | the refusals above; `farfield` lowers to the same rule | - |

The f32 rows of the first and third tests are R-class rows under D-F32-1: `tol_r(1e-10)`
and `tol_r(1e-13)` are both `1e-5` in f32, the plan's figure for the first. The driver adds
`a_jsonc_farfield_tube_runs`: the JSONC route lowers `farfield` with its `freestream`, runs
the tube with no bounds violation, and writes `p` with the type `characteristicFarfield`.

### 126.11 The free-stream family as built (BC-20)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` docs/17 BC-20, reduced by docs/17 §5.2.3 item 3:
`inletOutletTotalTemperature`, `supersonicFreestream`, `freestreamPressure` with its
supersonic switch, and `fixedPressureCompressibleDensity`, built on `src/compressible/bc.rs`
(`FreestreamRule`, `CompressibleFreestreams`, `check_rho` and the host twins
`supersonic_freestream_face`, `freestream_fraction`, `prandtl_meyer`) and two kernels appended
to `cuda/compressible.cu` (`cmpBcSupersonicFreestream`, `cmpBcFreestreamPressure`). BC-20's
acoustic-pulse row is dropped as a duplicate of Gate CMP-NR (§126.9); each remaining name has
a closed-form gate. `field.rs` is not edited and no `BcKind` is added: §120's catalogue keeps
the three new names as planned by BC-20 and `freestreamPressure` as implemented and extended
by BC-20, for the reason §126.8 gives for `totalTemperature` (the catalogue describes
`BcKind::from_name`, and the shared setup is unchanged). Only `ofgpu-compressible` lowers
them. The names follow the public user guides by name only; the equations below are NACA
Report 1135's and this tree's DESIGN.

**`inletOutletTotalTemperature`** on `T`, with `T0` (and an optional `gamma`, held to the
gas's): (126.1) on an inflow face, zero gradient on an outflow face. That is exactly what
§126.8's `totalTemperature` rule already does, so `bc::lower` returns the same
`RuleKind::TotalTemperature` rule and `cmpBcTotalTemperature` runs it; the two names give
bitwise the same triples.

**`freestreamPressure`** on `p`, with `freestreamValue` (gauge, in the datum of `p`) and an
optional `supersonic` switch (`true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`; absent is `false`).
The public description of the name (docs/01-model-catalog.md) is a blend "between zero
gradient for normal inlet and fixed value for normal outlet flow" by the velocity
orientation. *DESIGN* - the blend is linear in the direction cosine of the face velocity:

```
cos = (u_b . Sf) / (|u_b| |Sf|), clamped to [-1, 1];  cos = 0 when |u_b| = 0
fr  = 1/2 + cos/2   (subsonic, the default)
fr  = 1/2 - cos/2   (supersonic true)                                                      (126.13)
refValue = freestreamValue,  refGrad = 0
```

with `u_b` the face value of `U` (its own condition). The subsonic form fixes `p` where the
flow leaves and extrapolates it where the flow enters, the one outgoing characteristic of a
subsonic inflow; the supersonic form is the reverse, Carlson (2011) Table 1's "all"
specified at a supersonic inflow and none at a supersonic outflow. The generic
`freestreamPressure` of the other drivers (an `inletOutlet`, §120's table) is unchanged.

**`supersonicFreestream`** on `U`, with `UInf` (a uniform vector), `pInf` (gauge, in the
datum of `p`), `TInf` and an optional `gamma` (held to the gas's). *DESIGN* on NACA Report
1135's isentropic relations (43)-(44) and its Prandtl-Meyer function (171): the stated
stream is turned through the simple wave that takes it from `pInf` to the face pressure.
With `M_inf^2 = |u_inf|^2/(gamma R_s T_inf)`, `T_0 = T_inf (1 + (gamma-1)/2 M_inf^2)` (43)
and `p_0 = (p_inf + p_op)(T_0/T_inf)^(gamma/(gamma-1))` (44), on a face whose OWNER velocity
enters (`u_P . n < 0`):

```
M_b^2 = 2/(gamma-1) expm1( (gamma-1)/gamma log( p_0 / (p_b + p_op) ) ),  raised to 1 below 1   (126.14)
nu(M) = sqrt((gamma+1)/(gamma-1)) atan sqrt( (gamma-1)/(gamma+1) (M^2-1) ) - atan sqrt(M^2-1)  (126.15)
delta = nu(M_b) - nu(M_inf),  T_b = T_0/(1 + (gamma-1)/2 M_b^2),  |u_b| = M_b sqrt(gamma R_s T_b)
e = u_inf/|u_inf|,  t = n - (n . e) e
u_b = |u_b| (cos delta  e - sin delta  t/|t|)   if |t| > 1e-6,   u_b = |u_b| e   otherwise      (126.16)
```

`fr = 1`, `refValue = u_b`, `refGrad = 0`. (126.14) is (44) solved for `M` and written with
`expm1` so that `p_b = p_inf` returns `M_inf` without cancellation; (126.15) is NACA (171).
`p_b` is `p`'s face value (its own condition, normally zero gradient or `freestreamPressure`
with `supersonic`). An expansion (`p_b < p_inf`, `delta > 0`) turns the entering stream
toward `-n`, into the domain, and a compression away from it: the sense of a simple wave
whose lower pressure lies inside. A face whose owner velocity leaves (`u_P . n >= 0`) is
vented: zero gradient. The limits, recorded: `M_b` is raised to 1 when `p_b` is at or above
the free stream's total pressure (no Prandtl-Meyer wave is subsonic); a stream within about
1e-6 rad of the face normal has no turning plane and keeps its direction; `delta` is not
limited, so a turn past the face plane is written as the formulas give it; a non-positive
`p_b + p_op` gives a NaN that §122.3's counter sees. A free stream below Mach 1 is refused by
name (it takes `characteristicFarfield`, §126.10).

**`fixedPressureCompressibleDensity`** on `rho`: the density at the patch from the equation
of state at the patch pressure, which is (122.10) at the face, `rho_b = (p_b + p_op)/(R_s
T_b)`. `ofgpu-compressible` does not solve `rho`; it forms it on EVERY boundary face from
`p`'s and `T`'s face values at each gas-state update, so the condition is what every face
already does. The driver reads a `rho` file when the OpenFOAM case has one, and
`bc::check_rho` accepts `fixedPressureCompressibleDensity`, `calculated` and the constraint
types (`empty`, `symmetry`, `symmetryPlane`, `wedge`, `cyclic`, `cyclicAMI`); any other type
would state a second density and is refused by name. The written `rho` keeps §44's
`calculated` types.

**When.** `Compressible::set_freestream_rules` attaches the rules. The rewrite runs once in
`Compressible::initialise` and at the top of every outer iteration, FIRST (before §126.8's
inlets, so an inlet `T` on the same patch reads the new `u_b`): the `supersonicFreestream`
faces, then `U`'s face values, then the `freestreamPressure` faces from those `u_b`, then
`p`'s face values; `psi` and `rho` on the boundary faces follow with the other rules. A
`supersonicFreestream` reads `p`'s face value of the previous evaluation. All host constants
(`e`, `T_0`, `p_0`, `nu(M_inf)`, `2/(gamma-1)`, `(gamma-1)/gamma`, `(gamma-1)/2`,
`gamma R_s`, `sqrt((gamma+1)/(gamma-1))`, `(gamma-1)/(gamma+1)`, `p_op`, `1e-6`) are formed
in f64 and rounded once. No time step is needed, so steady runs take them.

**The gate** (`tests/shared/compressible_bc_cases.rs`, both builds as in §126.8):

| test | class | row | measured (f64; f32) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inlet_outlet_total_temperature_is_total_temperature` | D, R `tol_r(1e-12)` | rows entering at M 0.3, 0.8 and 0.5 (tangential part) and one leaving: `T`'s `fr`, `refValue`, `refGrad` and face values bitwise those of `totalTemperature`; an inflow face against NACA (43); the leaving face the cell's | bitwise; `e_T` 1.9e-16; 2.9e-8 |
| `freestream_pressure_blends_by_direction` | D, R `tol_r(1e-14)` | face velocity out, in, at 60 degrees and zero, both switch positions: `fr` of (126.13) (bitwise on the aligned and zero rows), `refValue` = `freestreamValue` bitwise, the face value the blend, the host twin | 0; 2.9e-9 |
| `supersonic_freestream_matches_prandtl_meyer` | R `tol_r(1e-12)`, twin `tol_r(1e-13)`, D | M 2 at 10 degrees, face pressure 1.0, 0.8 and 1.15 of `p_inf` and one leaving row: the free stream returned at `p_inf`; `M_b` from `\|u_b\|` and (126.1) gives the face pressure by NACA (44); the turn is `nu(M_b) - nu(M_inf)` by NACA (171) (3.861 and -2.514 degrees), toward `-n` on the expansion, in the stream's plane; the leaving face vented bitwise | worst 2.8e-15, twin 2.3e-16; 4.3e-7, 1.3e-7 |
| `fixed_pressure_compressible_density_is_the_gas_law` | R `tol_r(1e-12)` | every boundary face after `initialise`, a fixed `p` (3000 Pa) and `T` (320 K) at one end: `rho_b` against (122.10); `check_rho` accepts the name, `calculated` and `empty` | 1.9e-16; 4.5e-8 |
| `a_supersonic_freestream_tube_runs` | P | 50-cell tube carrying M 2: `supersonicFreestream`, `freestreamPressure` (supersonic) and `inletOutletTotalTemperature` on both ends, 10 Euler steps: finite, no bounds violation | `M_max` 2.0000 in both |
| `bc20_refusals_name_the_setting` | D | a missing or malformed `UInf`, `pInf`, `TInf`, `freestreamValue`, `T0`; `TInf <= 0`; an absolute `pInf` or `freestreamValue <= 0`; a subsonic `UInf`; another `gamma`; a `supersonic` that is not a switch; each name on the wrong field; a `fixedValue` `rho` | - |

The f32 rows are R-class rows under D-F32-1: `tol_r(1e-12)`, `tol_r(1e-13)` and
`tol_r(1e-14)` are `1e-5`, `1e-5` and `5.4e-6` in f32.
