### 132.9 The device kernels as built (CHR-07a, `cuda/chem.cu`, `src/chem/device.rs`)

Two kernels, one thread per cell, compute in `typedef double ofchem` in both
builds (§132.6):

* **`chemProductionRates`** evaluates (130.1) from `(T, p, Y)` through
  (128.9)'s concentrations, which is `production_rates_tpy` of §130.7. `T`,
  `p`, `Y` and `omega` cross as `ofscalar`; the sums run in `ofchem` and
  `omega` is rounded once on the way out.
* **`chemReactorJacobian`** evaluates the reactor right-hand side
  (132.7)-(132.9) with R8's clip `Y⁺_k = max(Y_k, 0)`, which is
  `ConstPressureReactor::rhs` of §132.8, and then §132.3's one-sided
  difference column by column, `δ_j = 2^-26 max(abs(y_j), atol_j)`, which is
  `fd_jacobian` of §132.7 (`2^-26` is `sqrt(eps_64)` exactly). The state
  `y = (Y_1..Y_K, T)`, `p`, `atol`, `f0` and `J` are `ofchem` in both builds:
  they are internal to the chemistry step that CHR-07b integrates in double.

**Design choices of this unit (ORIGINAL; SAND89-8009 gives only the
equations).**

* **D1, one for one.** Every choice of §130.7 is made as the host twin makes
  it, in the host twin's order: the forward term directly with `pow`, the
  reverse term as one `exp` of the log sum (130.16)/(130.17) with `sgn(A)` as
  `copysign(1, A)`, the order-0 skip on both sides, `q_f = q_r = 0` exactly at
  `Pr = 0`, `Pr/(1+Pr) = 1` at an infinite `Pr`, `ln K_c` summed over the
  products and then the reactants (130.6), and (130.1) accumulated reaction
  by reaction, reactants then products. The third-body sum (130.3) runs over
  every species in index order with `alpha = 1` where none is listed, as
  `third_body_concentration` does. `G/RT` is evaluated only for the species
  of reversible reactions without `REV`.
* **D2, the flat mechanism.** The mechanism is uploaded once as two arrays,
  one of `double` and one of `int`, whose layout is stated in
  `src/chem/device.rs` and in the header of `cuda/chem.cu` with the same field
  list: the species records (molar mass, range, both NASA-7 sets), `R` and
  `p_ref` taken from the host so that no constant is spelled twice, one record
  per reaction (kind, reverse kind, Arrhenius sets, fall-off parameters), the
  order and stoichiometry lists, and one dense efficiency row per third-body
  reaction.
* **D3, refusals per cell.** A kernel cannot return §130.7's `Error::Config`,
  so each cell writes a status, in the host twin's order of checks:
  `1` a pressure not finite or not above 0, `2` a temperature not finite or
  not above 0, `3` a mass fraction negative or not finite (production rates
  only; the reactor clips), `4` no species present (`Σ Y/W` not above 0),
  `5` a `T` outside the thermo range of a species whose record is needed.
  A refused cell writes NaN to all its outputs, so it cannot be used
  silently. The Jacobian's status is the first refusal met at `y` or at any
  perturbed column.
* **D4, contraction.** `chem.cu` is compiled with nvcc's default
  `-fmad=true`. The gate is 1e-12 against the host, not bitwise, so it is not
  a `FMAD_OFF_UNITS` member (§82.4's exception is for bitwise gates).

**The measure.** `omega_k` is a sum of terms of both signs, so the error is
taken against the gross rate of the species,

```
G_k = Σ_i Σ_(entries of k in reaction i) ν (|q_f,i| + |q_r,i|),    e_k = |omega_dev,k - omega_host,k| / G_k
```

with the reactant and product entries both counted. A species with `G_k = 0`
must come back exactly 0. This is the denominator §130.6's mass identity
uses. For the Jacobian, each of the two evaluations in a column is within the
right-hand-side bound at the state it ran on, so the derived bound is

```
abs(J_dev,ij - J_host,ij) δ_j <= 1e-12 ( F_i(y) + F_i(y + δ_j e_j) ),
F_i = W_i G_i / rho (i <= K),     F_T = Σ_k abs(H_k) G_k / (rho cp)
```

and `f0` is held to `1e-12 F_i(y)`; a zero bound means exact equality. The
perturbed state's scale is needed, not only `F_i(y)`: at a state where a
species is exactly 0, a reaction with a FORD order on it has `G = 0` at `y`
and a genuine nonzero quotient after the perturbation (`J ≈ -0.93` in the
fixture's CH4 row at the zeroed-O2 states, on the host and the device alike).

| row | measure | tolerance | class | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chem_device_omega_matches_host` | 4096 random states of §130.7's generator on the 14-reaction fixture, `max e_k` | 1e-12 (f64 build); f32 build: inputs rounded to f32 and the host evaluated at the rounded inputs, 1e-6 (the plan's band, inside the class rule's 1e-5) | P; R in f32 | f64 build `1.68e-14` (cell 737, O2); f32 build `5.89e-8` |
| `chem_device_omega_matches_host_gri30` | the same on GRI-Mech 3.0 when its paths are set (§129.6) | the same | P; R in f32 | with the user's GRI-Mech 3.0 copy: f64 build `5.67e-14`; f32 build `5.92e-8` |
| `chem_device_jacobian_matches_host` | 4096 random states, `f0` and `J` against `rhs` and `fd_jacobian` | the bounds above, both builds (inputs are double in both) | P | worst `f0` at `1.70e-2` of its bound, worst `J` at `1.42e-2` of its bound, both builds |
| `chem_device_refuses_by_status` | statuses 1-5 and the NaN outputs; a clipped negative `Y` is not refused by the reactor | exact | D | — |
| `chem_device_replays_under_capture` | both kernels inside §81.5's protocol, the rates feeding the next iteration's `T` | bitwise | D | 4 kernel nodes, 3 replays bitwise over 6 buffers / 9280 values |

### 132.10 The device integrator as built (CHR-07b, `cuda/chem.cu`, `src/chem/device.rs`)

One kernel, **`chemIntegrate`**, runs one thread per cell over one flow step
`dt`. Each thread is `ConstPressureReactor::advance` of §132.8, that is
§132.7's `integrate_observed` with `ros_step`, `lu_factor`, `lu_solve`,
`fd_jacobian` and `error_norm`, under advance's observer. It computes in
`typedef double ofchem` in both builds (§132.6, §118.10). The right-hand
side is §132.9's `chemRhs`, and its arithmetic is unchanged.
`integrate_fields` is the ofscalar crossing. `chemPackState` widens
`(T, p, Y)` exactly into a double state, `chemIntegrate` runs on it, and
`chemUnpackState` rounds the state once on the way out. In the f64 build it
is bitwise `integrate`.

**Design choices of this unit (ORIGINAL; Sandu et al. and SAND89-8009 give
only the method and the equations).**

* **D5, one for one.** R1-R4 and R10 are made as the host twin makes them,
  in its order:
  * the pivoted LU, first on a tie, with the update skipped when the
    multiplier is exactly 0;
  * `lu = (-γ h) J + I`;
  * the stage sums that skip an exactly-zero `α_ij` or `γ_ij`;
  * `y_{n+1}` and `Est` in one loop over the stages;
  * (132.5) over `m = K + 1` components;
  * the factor `min(fac_max, max(0.1, 0.9 / Err^(1/(p̂+1))))`;
  * `J` once per accepted point, with `δ_j = 2^-26 max(|y_j|, atol_j)`;
  * the shortened last step;
  * the non-finite rejection that divides `h` by 10;
  * the clip of `Y_k` in `[-atol_y, 0)` to 0 after each accepted step.

  `h_min` is 0, as advance sets it. R11's ignition delay is host-only. The
  coefficient set and the tolerances reach the kernel as one double control
  array, which `DeviceReactor::new` builds from `ReactorOptions` and the
  set's own `Coefficients`, so no constant is spelled twice. Its field list
  is stated in `src/chem/device.rs` and in `chem.cu`'s header.
* **D6, the step memory.** `h[c]` goes in as the cell's first trial step
  (advance's `h0`, clamped as R3 clamps it) and comes out as
  `RosStats::h_next`, the step the controller proposed after the last
  accepted step. A caller can carry it to the next flow step. The counts
  `accepted`, `rejected` and `clipped` come out per cell.
* **D7, refusals per cell**, extending §132.9 D3. Before the run the checks
  are, in advance's order:
  * `1`, the pressure (R7);
  * `3`, a mass fraction negative or not finite (R9);
  * `2`, the temperature;
  * `9`, an `h[c]` that is not finite or not above 0 (R5's `h0`).

  During the run:
  * any `chemRhs` refusal (2, 4, 5) at `y`, at a perturbed column or at a
    stage argument ends the cell, as the host's error ends advance;
  * `6`, a singular `I - γhJ`;
  * `7`, more step attempts than `max_steps`;
  * `8`, a `Y_k < -atol_y` after an accepted step (R10).

  A refused cell writes NaN to its whole state column and to `h[c]`. On the
  host side, `DeviceReactor::new` refuses each of the following, naming it:
  `rtol`, `atol_y`, `atol_t`, `h_max` (`+inf` allowed) and `max_steps`
  (1 to `i32::MAX`). `integrate` refuses a `dt` that is not finite or is
  below 0. `dt = 0` launches nothing.
* **D8, contraction.** The integrator's own multiplies, adds, subtracts and
  divides (the LU, the solves, the stage sums, the error norm and the step
  arithmetic) use the round-to-nearest intrinsics. nvcc therefore does not
  fuse them, and they are evaluated as the host evaluates them. `chemRhs`
  keeps D4's default contraction, so the results of §132.9 do not move.
  This did not change the step-sequence statistics below (622 against 620
  differing cells), and it is kept because it removes one source of
  difference at no cost to the gate.
* **D9, the scratch.** The per-cell vectors live in SoA device scratch with
  stride `n`, sized at setup (`IntegrateWork`): ten vectors of `m`, `J`, the
  LU factors and the pivots. The launch allocates nothing and does not sync,
  so it can be captured.

**The flow step of the gate, and why it is 1e-6 s.** A one-sided FD
Jacobian with `δ_j = 2^-26 |y_j|` divides a right-hand-side difference by
`δ_j`. A device-host difference at §132.9's measured level (1.7e-14 of the
gross rate) therefore moves `J`, and through it `Err`, enough to flip
accept/reject decisions near `Err = 1`. Once the step sequences differ, the
two end states differ by an integration error, not by round-off.

The supervisor probed this outside the tree. It ran the host twin against
itself, with its right-hand side scaled by `1 ± 1e-14` (a fixed hash sign
per call and component), on the same generator:

| dt | cells | step sequences changed | worst dY | worst dT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1e-4 s | 256 | 231 | `1.34e-11` | `1.35e-8` K (33 cells above 1e-9 K) |
| 1e-6 s | 512 | 414 | `2.47e-12` | `2.98e-10` K |

With a one-ulp scaling at 1e-4 s, the worst dT is `3.9e-10` K. The plan's
`T 1e-9 K` row is therefore below the problem's own round-off conditioning
when ignition falls inside the step, and no twin that is not bitwise could
meet it there. The device itself, measured at 1e-4 s on 4096 cells, gave worst dY `1.75e-11`,
worst dT `5.95e-8` K, and 620 of 4096 cells with a different step count.

The gate runs at **`dt = 1e-6` s**. That is the flow step at which CHR-09's
Lie split calls this integrator, and the tolerances are unchanged. This was
decided by recommendation. A gate across ignition inside one step needs a
derived bound, and that is the user's decision (docs/17 §11). The user
accepted on 2026-10-14 that the device-host `T` gate runs at `dt = 1e-6` s.

**The test population.** SplitMix64 seed 20261013, per cell `c`, with the
draws in this order: `φ = 0.6 + 0.8u`, `T0 = 1000 + 1000u`,
`p = 10^(4+2u)` Pa, `r = 10^(-6+3u)`. Even cells are H2-air
(`2φ : 1 : 3.76`) and odd cells are CH4-air (`φ : 2 : 7.52`), with H, O and
OH at `r` moles each, except every tenth cell, where they are exactly 0.
`Y` comes from the TM-4513 molar masses. Every cell starts with
`h = 1e-10` s and uses the default `ReactorOptions` (RODAS3, `rtol` 1e-8,
`atol_y` 1e-14, `atol_t` 1e-8 K). The mechanism is §132.8's 15-reaction
reactor fixture, whose rates are placeholders, and GRI-Mech 3.0 when its
paths are set (§129.6). JL4 is not in the tree (§129.6).

| row | measure | tolerance | class | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chem_device_integrate_matches_host` | 4096 cells, one `dt = 1e-6` s, f64 state API, device against `advance` | `max abs dY <= 1e-10`, `abs dT <= 1e-9` K; at least 1000 cells with `max abs(Y - Y0) > 1e-6`; no host refusal | P (both builds: the state is double) | both builds alike: dY `6.92e-14` (cell 491, CO), dT `7.64e-10` K (cell 890, 0.76 of the gate: thin, reported as it stands); 3448 cells moved, largest `max abs(Y - Y0)` `1.05e-3`, largest `abs(T - T0)` 3.79 K; 429 cells with a different step count (reported) |

### 132.11 The split step as built (CHR-09, `src/chem/source.rs`, `src/species.rs`)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` The equations are §132.4's reactor and
§132.5's split, (132.7)-(132.10); nothing is added to them.

**The species set carries a source.** `Species::use_reaction_sources` gives
each solved species one `[n_cells]` buffer `su`, allocated once (§81), and
`Species::correct_with_density` hands species `i` its own buffer as the
`su` of `ScalarTransport::correct_with_density`, which adds it as
`fvm_su(su, +1)`: `source[P] += V_P su_P`, after the equation's own terms and
before relaxation, where every other source of the solver goes (§18). A set
without reaction sources hands every equation `None`, which is the call it
made before CHR-09, so that path is the same arithmetic by construction and
is held to a hash pinned before the change.

**The split step fills it.** `chem::source::ChemSource::new` maps every
mechanism species by name to a solved index or to the inert remainder of
§19 and refuses, by name, a mechanism species that is not in the set and a
member of the set that is not in the mechanism: the reactor needs the whole
composition. `ChemSource::step(species, T, p, rho, dt)` then, for one flow
step `dt`:

1. packs `Y°` in mechanism order (the inert remainder included) and copies
   `T°`, by device-to-device copies;
2. runs CHR-07b's `integrate_fields` (§132.10) in place, every cell's reactor
   at its `p` and in `double` in both builds (§132.6), with each cell's step
   memory `h` seeded with `opts.h0` and carried from flow step to flow step
   (`RosStats::h_next` out, the next step's first trial step in);
3. writes, per solved species, (132.10) in the currency of the equation it
   enters: `su_k = (Y*_k - Y°_k)/dt` on §19's constant-density equation
   (`d(Y)/dt`), and `su_k = rho (Y*_k - Y°_k)/dt` on §86's mass-weighted one
   (`d(rho Y)/dt`), with `rho` the density `correct_with_density` is handed.
   `Y* - Y°` is formed from the two Scalar values, so it is exact
   (Sterbenz) whenever the step changed `Y_k` by less than a factor of two.

`T*` is kept (`ChemSource::temperature`) for (132.10)'s `Q_chem`, which is
CHR-10b's; CHR-09 does not touch `T`. Refused by name: `dt` not finite or not
above 0; a density on the constant-density set or none on the mass-weighted
one (as §86.5 row 6); a set without reaction sources; `T` or `p` shorter than
the cell count. A cell the reactor refuses carries NaN into its sources and
its status into `ChemSource::refused_cells`, one read-back and so a
diagnostic, not a loop step. The step allocates nothing and reads nothing
back, and it captures (§81.7).

**(133.5) is not built.** §133.5 lists `species_fluxes_sum_to_zero` under
CHR-09, while the plan's CHR-09 row (docs/17 §12.2) names neither the
correction nor its files or test. The correction is a new explicit face flux
in every species equation. That is a numerics addition to species diffusion,
and the diffusivity it corrects is not there yet: §133.4's route (b) is
refused by name (§133.7), and on the Lewis route with one Lewis number for
every species the correction is identically zero. This was decided by
recommendation, and the row moves to the unit that brings species-specific
mixture-averaged diffusivities into the species equation.

| row | measure | tolerance | class | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `species_box_matches_reactor` | a closed adiabatic box with no flow, 2^3 cells cyclic on all three axes and uniform (the plan's one-cell-wide periodic box is the same 0-D problem), stoichiometric H2-air with H, O, OH at 1e-4 moles each, `T0` 1400 K, 1 atm, on §132.8's 15-reaction fixture (placeholder rates); Lie split at `dt = 1e-6` s over 200 steps, `T` fed back from `T*`; every species of the set, solved and inert, against the host `ConstPressureReactor::advance` chained over the same 200 `dt` (each chunk's first trial step the last one's `h_next`), on both species equations | `max abs dY <= 1e-6`; the host must move `max abs dY > 1e-3` | P | host: `T` 1400 -> 1456.270 K, `max abs dY` `2.33e-2`. f64 build: `3.12e-13` (constant density) and `4.59e-13` (mass-weighted), `T*` within `1.7e-9` K. f32 build: solved species `7.04e-7` on both equations; **the inert N2 MISSED**, `1.086e-6` (constant density) and `1.026e-6` (mass-weighted), at step 196 |
| `species_budget_closes_with_chemistry` | (86.5) with the source metered: a closed 4^3 box (walls, a non-solenoidal internal flux, conservative upwind, `rho` varying in space and held in time, non-uniform `T` and `Y`), the mass-weighted set with the split step's sources; per step and per solved species `abs(Δ Σ rho Y V - dt Σ su V - Δ clip) / Σ rho V`, three steps | `1e-12`, tol32 `1e-5` (D-F32-1); the chemistry term above `1e-6` of the mass | R | f64 build `1.23e-16`; f32 build `3.27e-9`; the chemistry term `2.52e-4` of the mass |
| `species_without_chemistry_is_bitwise` | three steps of each species equation with no reaction sources, FNV-1a over every solved field and the inert remainder, against the hash pinned at afd0f30 before `src/species.rs` changed | bitwise | D | f64 `0x1bc5208b67b6041e`, f32 `0x018e7024cfdec719`: both unchanged |
| `chem_source_replays_under_capture` | `ChemSource::step`, `T*` copied back into `T`, then `Species::correct` on a 3^3 box with a flux, captured and replayed | bitwise | D | 1027 nodes (896 kernel, 100 memset, 31 memcpy), 3 replays bitwise over 6 buffers / 162 values (f64 lib test) |

**The f32 miss.** The inert remainder is `1 - Σ` over nine f32 fields, and
each of them is rounded once per step, so the remainder carries their
summed round-off. The test measures that cause: N2's error minus the
negated sum of the solved species' errors is `8.1e-8` on both equations,
while every solved species stays within `7.0e-7`. The miss is the f32
storage of the mass fractions, which §19's construction sends to the inert
species. A cure (f64 mass fractions, or a renormalised set) changes the
species numerics and is the user's decision (docs/17 §5.3.4). Under the
user's rule of 2026-10-14 the test asserts the miss as MISSED, prints its
value and cause, and the unit lands.

No new equation labels.

## 133. Mixture-averaged transport, and the reacting low-Mach constraint

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.`

**Sources.**

* **Day & Bell**, "Numerical simulation of laminar reacting flows with complex
  chemistry", *Combust. Theory Model.* 4 (2000) 535-556, DOI
  10.1088/1364-7830/4/4/309. Crossref agrees. **Read** from the open copy at
  the University of North Texas Digital Library (`digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc740043/`,
  sha256 `70a948e048d324ef2c4f1422013d67f3787795897ef3668898f0db20813664d5`).
  Read: eqs. (1)-(8) and the paragraphs on the species-flux correction (§3,
  around eq. (14)).
* **Gordon & McBride**, NASA RP-1311 (1994), Chapter 5, eqs. (5.1)-(5.7).
  **Read.** Mixture viscosity and frozen conductivity. Their eq. (5.5) is
  Wilke's interaction coefficient.
* **Wilke**, *J. Chem. Phys.* 18 (1950) 517-519, DOI 10.1063/1.1747673.
  Crossref agrees. Closed, not read. Its formula is stated here from RP-1311
  (5.3)/(5.5).
* **McBride, Gordon & Reno**, NASA TM-4513, eq. (10) and Table IV. **Read.**
  Pure-species viscosity and conductivity fits for 155 species, in μP and
  μW/(cm K), on 300-1000-5000 K.
* **The FDS Technical Reference Guide** (McGrattan et al., NIST SP 1018,
  public domain), `Manuals/FDS_Technical_Reference_Guide/Momentum_Chapter.tex`
  at firemodels/fds `e14ec3f`. **Read**: the kinetic-theory `mu_alpha` and
  `D_alpha,beta`. This repository does not carry it; the copy read was fetched.
* **Neufeld, Janzen & Aziz**, *J. Chem. Phys.* 57 (1972) 1100-1102, DOI
  10.1063/1.1678363, and **Mathur, Tondon & Saxena**, *Mol. Phys.* 12 (1967)
  569-579, DOI 10.1080/00268976700100731. Both checked on Crossref, both
  **closed and not read**.
* **Kee, Dixon-Lewis, Warnatz, Coltrin & Miller**, *A Fortran Computer Code
  Package for the Evaluation of Gas-Phase, Multicomponent Transport
  Properties*, Sandia SAND86-8246 (December 1986), OSTI **7157265** (the plan
  had no id). The OSTI record exists, but the report's full text is not on
  OSTI, so it was **not read**. It is the source of the TRAN data format,
  which CHR-08 therefore cannot treat as read (§133.4).
* The low-Mach formulation this extends is §25's: Rehm & Baum, *J. Res. Natl.
  Bur. Stand.* 83 (1978) 297, DOI 10.6028/jres.083.019; Majda & Sethian,
  *Combust. Sci. Technol.* 42 (1985) 185-205, DOI 10.1080/00102208508960376.
  Both DOIs were checked here.

### 133.1 The reacting low-Mach equations

These are Day & Bell eqs. (1)-(6) in this document's notation, with **`omega`
the production rate** of (130.1). Day & Bell's `ω̇_m` is a destruction rate
(their eq. (2) carries `-ω̇_m`), so `W_m omega_m = -ω̇_m`:

```
d(rho Y_m)/dt + div(rho u Y_m) = - div(Γ_m) + W_m omega_m,   Γ_m = - rho D_m grad Y_m   (133.1)
d(rho h)/dt + div(rho u h) = div(λ grad T) - Σ_m div(h_m Γ_m) + dp0/dt         (133.2)
p0 = rho R T Σ_m Y_m / W_m                                                       (133.3)
```

`h = Σ_m Y_m h_m(T)` per unit mass, from (128.7) with `h_m = H_m/W_m`, so heat
release is implicit in `h`. The `dp0/dt` term is §25.2's, which Day & Bell's
open domain does not need. Their (3) has no `dp0/dt`, so it is added here as
§25 has it. Summed over `m`, (133.1) is continuity **only if
`Σ_m Γ_m = 0`** and `Σ_m W_m omega_m = 0`. The second is (130.7). The first
is §133.3.

### 133.2 The divergence constraint, derived

Differentiate (133.3) along a particle path: `-D(ln rho)/Dt = div u`. Expand
`ln rho = ln p0 + ln W - ln R - ln T`. Then replace `DT/Dt` from (133.2)
(written with `cp = Σ Y_m dh_m/dT`) and `DY_m/Dt` from (133.1):

```
div u = (1/(rho cp T)) [ div(λ grad T) - Σ_m Γ_m . grad h_m ]
      + (1/rho) Σ_m (W/W_m) ( - div Γ_m )
      + (1/rho) Σ_m ( W/W_m - h_m/(cp T) ) W_m omega_m
      - (1/(γ p0)) dp0/dt,           γ = cp / (cp - R/W)                         (133.4)
```

**The `dp0/dt` coefficient.** The `ln p0` term gives `-(1/p0) dp0/dt`. The
energy equation's `+dp0/dt` gives `+(1/(rho cp T)) dp0/dt`. Their sum is
`-(1/p0)(1 - R/(W cp)) dp0/dt = -(1/(γ p0)) dp0/dt`, because
`p0/(rho T) = R/W` and `cp - R/W = cv` for an ideal-gas mixture. That is
§25.1's term with the mixture's own `γ`.

**The check against the paper.** With `dp0/dt = 0`, `Γ_m = -rho D_m grad Y_m`
and `W_m omega_m = -ω̇_m`, (133.4) is Day & Bell's eq. (7) term by term.

**The checks against this document.** With one species, `W` constant and no
reactions, (133.4) is §25.1's constraint, and §26.1 says what `Q` must
include. With `Q` from (133.4)'s first line, the sealed-box `p0` evolution of
§25.2 follows by integrating (133.4) over the domain. CHR-11's sealed-box gate
uses a mole-changing, heat-neutral reaction: the `h_m/(cp T)` part of the
third line sums to zero, and `W/W_m` alone drives `dp0/dt`. That gives an analytic `p0(t)`,
"no tolerance excuses" (§25.2).

**Day & Bell's eq. (8)** adds a damping term, proportional to `(p - p0)/Δt`
with a factor `f < 1`, that pulls a fractional-step solution back onto (133.3).
Its exact coefficient is not restated here, because the open copy's text layer
is garbled at that line. It is **named and not
adopted in v1**. §25's loop holds the equation of state by recomputing `rho`
from (133.3), and CHR-11 measures the drift that remains: first order in
`Δt` (§133.10), so the term is not needed for it. If that drift needs
the term, it is a numerics change and goes to the user (docs/17 §5.3.4).

**§25 is amended in place by CHR-11** (§133.10), not here. §25's
"constant W" line points to (133.20), and §25.1 and §25.2 point to (133.21)
and (133.22). This section is the derivation those pointers cite.

### 133.3 The species fluxes must sum to zero

Mixture-averaged `D_m` does not conserve mass: Day & Bell say "numerically,
`Σ_m Γ_m ≠ 0`", and they consider two corrections. The first adjusts the
locally dominant species. It is "not free-stream preserving": a species with
uniform `Y` that takes part in no reaction acquires spurious variation. The
second redistributes the excess "in a mass-weighted" way, and it is free-stream
preserving. **The second is adopted:**

```
Γ_m = - rho D_m grad Y_m  +  Y_m Σ_k rho D_k grad Y_k                            (133.5)
```

`Σ_m Γ_m = 0` holds exactly, because `Σ_m Y_m = 1`. A uniform `Y_m` gets
`Γ_m = Y_m Σ_k(...)`. The divergence of that over the mesh is what the
transport of a passive uniform scalar must reproduce, and §86's mass-weighted
form already does.

**On the mesh**, (133.5) is evaluated per face with face-interpolated `Y_m`,
and its sum over `m` is zero per face up to round-off. §86's species budget
then closes with the correction metered, not hidden. CHR-09 was to prove it;
it did not build (133.5), and §132.11 says why.

### 133.4 Mixture-averaged coefficients

**Pure species.** Each species has `mu_k(T)` and `λ_k(T)`.

* **(a), read.** TM-4513 eq. (10) fits: `ln mu = A ln T + B/T + C/T^2 + D`,
  and the same form for `ln λ`, converted from μP and μW/(cm K) to SI.
* **(b), the plan's route.** Chapman-Enskog with Lennard-Jones parameters, in
  FDS TRG's form:

  ```
  mu_k = 26.69e-7 (W_k T)^(1/2) / (sigma_k^2 Ω_v(T*_k))        [kg/(m s)], W in g/mol, sigma in Å   (133.6)
  D_kj = 2.66e-7 T^(3/2) / ( W_kj^(1/2) sigma_kj^2 Ω_D(T*_kj) ) / (p / 1 atm)   [m^2/s]
  W_kj = 2 (1/W_k + 1/W_j)^-1,   sigma_kj = (sigma_k + sigma_j)/2,   T* = T / (eps/k_B)       (133.7)
  ```

  FDS TRG writes `D` at 1 atm. The `1/p` scaling is kinetic theory's, stated.
  FDS TRG calls `Ω_v` and `Ω_D` "an empirical function of the temperature" and
  does not print one. **The Neufeld, Janzen & Aziz fit is the plan's choice
  and was not read**, so its coefficients are not written here. Route (b)
  needs them transcribed from a read copy, and until then **`D_kj` from (133.7)
  is NAMED and NOT BUILT.**

**The Lennard-Jones and `eps/k_B` data** for route (b) are not GRI's
`transport.dat`, which is not vendored (§129.6). A candidate open source is the
species data in FDS's own public-domain source. CHR-08 checks it. It is not
adopted here, because it was not read.

**Mixture viscosity and frozen conductivity, read (RP-1311 (5.3)-(5.6)):**

```
mu_mix = Σ_i X_i mu_i / ( X_i + Σ_{j≠i} X_j φ_ij )                               (133.8)
λ_mix  = Σ_i X_i λ_i / ( X_i + Σ_{j≠i} X_j ψ_ij )                                (133.9)
φ_ij = (1/4) [ 1 + (mu_i/mu_j)^(1/2) (W_j/W_i)^(1/4) ]^2 ( 2 W_j / (W_i + W_j) )^(1/2)     (133.10)
ψ_ij = φ_ij [ 1 + 2.41 (W_i - W_j)(W_i - 0.142 W_j) / (W_i + W_j)^2 ]              (133.11)
```

RP-1311 writes the sums over all `j` with `φ_ii` implied. (133.10) gives
`φ_ii = 1`, which is why the `j ≠ i` form with the explicit `X_i` is the same
thing. **Mathur, Tondon & Saxena's** average (the plan's choice) was not read.
It is named and not built until it is. (133.9) and (133.11) are the v1
conductivity (decided by recommendation): both are public domain and read, and
CHR-08's air gate (Kadoya 1985, within 5 %) measures them either way.

**Mixture-averaged diffusion coefficient (the plan's §2.2, stated as the
plan states it):**

```
D_m = (1 - Y_m) / Σ_{j≠m} ( X_j / D_mj )                                         (133.12)
```

This is the form Day & Bell use, citing SAND86-8246 (their reference [14]).
Its derivation is in SAND86-8246 and Hirschfelder, Curtiss & Bird, and neither
was read. It is the plan's design and is stated as a model, not derived. It
waits on `D_mj` (route (b)) like everything else in that route.

**The Lewis-number route (read in full, and the one available in v1 without
route (b)):** `λ = mu cp / Pr` and `D_m = λ / (rho cp Le_m)`, with `mu(T)`
from (133.8) on route (a) or from §100's Sutherland curve, and `Pr` and `Le_m`
stated by the case (plan §2.2's "cheaper alternative"). It has no hidden
constant.

### 133.7 The transport as built (CHR-08, `src/chem/transport.rs`, `cuda/chem.cu`, `src/chem/device.rs`)

**The data.** Route (a)'s pure-species fits are TM-4513 Table IV, read from
the report as NASA serves it (`ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19940013151`, sha256
`6b274fb921918f938b01d4525d8a7b7e8dff50b9990a496886db32354e2c4947`, the copy
§128.6 read). Eq. (10) is printed on p. 5 as

```
ln eta, ln lambda, ln eta_ij = A ln T + B/T + C/T^2 + D                       (TM-4513 eq. (10))
```

with `eta` in micropoise and `lambda` in microwatts per centimetre kelvin,
so `mu = 1e-7 e^(...)` Pa s and `lambda = 1e-4 e^(...)` W/(m K). Table III
(p. 74) states the record format: up to three intervals each for `V` and
`C`. The ten species of `table_II.csv` (N2, O2, CH4, CO2, H2O, CO, H2, OH,
O, H) are transcribed from the page images of pp. 78-86 (the text layer is
OCR) into `reference/mcbride-gordon-reno1993/table_IV.csv`, four rows per
species, digit for digit. Every record is "V2C2 GORDON; NASA TM86885, OCT
1984", on 300-1000-5000 K. Two checks were made on the transcription. Each
number was matched against the OCR layer where the OCR is legible, and the
six numbers it garbles were re-read from higher-resolution crops. Each
species' two intervals also meet at 1000 K: the largest jump is 0.80 %
(CH4's conductivity). CO's viscosity rows are printed equal to N2's, and
are kept as printed.

**Design choices (ORIGINAL).**

* **T1, the interval.** The first fit in increasing order with `t_lo <= T
  <= t_hi` is used, so 1000 K takes the lower fit. Below the first fit's
  `t_lo`, down to the **200 K** floor (`TRANSPORT_FLOOR_K`), the first fit
  is used, extrapolated (the paragraph below). A `T` below 200 K or above
  the last fit's `t_hi` is refused by name (species, property, `T`,
  range).
* **T2, the sums.** (133.8) and (133.9) run over the species with `Y_k !=
  0` in index order: `den = X_i`, then `den += X_j φ_ij` (or `ψ_ij`) for
  each present `j != i`, then `acc += X_i q_i / den`. A species with `Y_k =
  0` is not evaluated and its range is not checked, as `cp_mass` does.
  `X` is computed exactly as `ThermoSet::mole_fractions` computes it
  (`transport_mixture_reduces_to_pure_species` holds the two bitwise).
  `ψ_ij` multiplies the viscosity `φ_ij` of (133.10), as RP-1311 (5.6)
  writes it.
* **T3, the Lewis route** is two expressions, `λ = (mu cp)/Pr` and `D_m =
  λ/((ρ cp) Le_m)`, with `Pr` and every `Le_m` refused unless finite and
  above zero. The second also takes route (a)'s `λ`. With route (b) unbuilt,
  it is the only source of `D_m`.
* **T4, route (b)** (`binary_diffusion`, `mixture_diffusivities`) returns
  `Error::Refused`, naming Neufeld, Janzen & Aziz (1972) as not read and
  this section, and pointing to the Lewis route.
* **T5, the device.** Three kernels compute in `ofchem` in both builds:
  `chemMixtureTransport` (the host's `mixture_ty`, choice for choice),
  `chemPrandtlConductivity` and `chemLewisDiffusivity`. `T`, `Y`, `ρ`,
  `cp` and the outputs are `ofscalar`, rounded once. The records go up as
  one flat array of 40 doubles per species: `W`, `n_v`, three viscosity
  fits `(t_lo, t_hi, a, b, c, d)`, `n_c`, three conductivity fits, and a
  pad. The field list is stated in both `device.rs` and `chem.cu`. The
  per-cell statuses keep §132.9 D3's codes 2-4 in the host's order of
  checks, and add **10**, a present species' `T` outside its transport
  range; a refused cell writes NaN. `chem.cu` keeps nvcc's default
  contraction (§132.9 D4). The SASS of every existing chemistry kernel is
  unchanged, and only `chem.cubin` changed.

**The 200 K floor (CHR-08b).** TM-4513 Table IV publishes every fit from
300 K, so CHR-08 refused any cell below 300 K, ambient inlets at 293.15 K
included. The user chose on 2026-10-14 to move the accepted lower end to
200 K, on the host (`TRANSPORT_FLOOR_K`) and on the device
(`CHEM_TRANSPORT_FLOOR_K` in `chemFitPick`) alike. Between 200 and 300 K
the first fit of eq. (10) is evaluated outside its published range: this

### 133.8 A per-cell `cp` in the energy equation's ddt and convection rows (CHR-10a, `src/energy.rs`)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.`

**What it is.** §26 writes the temperature equation with one constant `cp`
and says a `cp(T)` is "a coefficient change, not a structure change". (133.2)
in temperature form, with `cp = Σ_m Y_m dh_m/dT` as §133.2 writes it, puts
the mixture's own `cp` in front of `DT/Dt`. CHR-10a makes `Energy` carry
that `cp` as a field: one value per cell and one per boundary face, set by the
caller (`Energy::set_cp_field`). The producer of the field (NASA-7 (128.7)
through the mixture rule, from `T` and `Y`) is CHR-10b's (§133.9, (133.18)).
CHR-12a lowers its inputs from the case (§137.7) and CHR-12b wires it in the
driver; this unit builds the slot and the two rows
that read it. Without a field nothing changes.

**The two rows.** §26's ddt and convection carry the same weight, so the
field enters both:

```
(rho cp)_c^(l) = rho_c^(l) cp_c,   l = n, n-1, n-2;   under backward, §105.17: (rho* cp)_c = (p0/R_s) cp_c / T*_c   (133.13)
phi_m,f = cp_f rho_f phi_f,   cp_f = w_f cp_P + (1 - w_f) cp_N (internal),   cp_f = cp_b (boundary)            (133.14)
```

*DESIGN.* All three time levels carry the field as last set: the same lag
`rho*` already has under backward (§105.17), and the form in which §26's
discrete `rho cp DT/Dt` (the conservative rows plus §26.1's bounded
correction, now on (133.14)'s flux) stays a temperature equation. `cp_f`
is §25.3's linear interpolation, the convention every face coefficient in
this module uses, and is formed once, when the field is set, not every
outer iteration. A value that is not finite and positive, or a buffer
shorter than the mesh, is refused by name, naming the cell or boundary face.

**What still reads the constant `cp`, stated.** `k_eff`'s turbulent part
`rho cp nu_t/Pr_t` (S26, both `Pr_t` models), §25.1's target divergence
on a gas without a mixture (with one, (133.21) of §133.10 reads the field), and the S29.3 thermal wall function.
The §120.8 Danckwerts inlet reads `phi_m` itself, so it follows (133.14).
`assembly_budget` divides by (133.14)'s own `cp_f` and weighs by the cell's
`cp_c`; its mass diagnostics come from the same pass on `rho_f phi_f`, exact,
because no one number divides a face-varying `phi_m` back to kg/s.

**Gates, measured 2026-10-14 (both builds, `tests/energy_cp_field.rs`).**

| `energy_cp_field_default_bitwise` | SHA-256 of the restart checkpoint of `cases/channelPeriodicFluxWF.jsonc`, `ofgpu-lowmach -iters 20 -restartWrite 20`, against the parent commit 0777b1d's binaries, one pin per build | bitwise | D | equal in both builds |
| `energy_uniform_cp_field_equals_constant` | 16-cell channel, plug flow 0.01 m/s, 310 K in, 10 steps of 2 s, Euler and backward: (a) a uniform field equal to `cp` against the constant path, T and `assembly_budget`'s entries; (b) a uniform `2 cp` with `k` against the constant `cp` with `k/2`, the same equation times two, which holds only if both rows read the field | `1e-12` relative (D-F32-1: `1e-5` in f32) | R | (a) `0` and the budget's entries within `9.7e-15` (f64), `3.0e-6` (f32, its mass rows, formed by another route); (b) `0` in both builds; the `2 cp` run differs from the `cp` run by `1.5e-2` (Euler) and `3.0e-3` (backward), so (b) is not vacuous |
| `energy_cp_field_refuses_by_name` | zero, negative and NaN cells, a negative boundary face, a short buffer | refused by name | D | — |

The two exact zeros are not a promise: the uniform mesh's `w_f = 1/2` makes
`w_f c + (1 - w_f) c = c` exact, and on a graded mesh (133.14)'s `cp_f` may
differ from `c` in its last bit, which the R tolerance allows.

### 133.9 Heat release and species-enthalpy diffusion in the temperature equation (CHR-10b, `src/energy.rs`, `src/chem/source.rs`, `cuda/energy.cu`)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` The equations are Day & Bell's
eqs. (1)-(6) as (133.1)-(133.2) of §133.1 write them, and the split of
(132.10) of §132.5; nothing is added to them.

**The temperature form.** Subtract `Σ_m h_m` times (133.1) from (133.2), use
continuity, and write `h = Σ_m Y_m h_m(T)` with `grad h_m = cp_m grad T`:

```
rho cp DT/Dt = div(λ grad T) - Σ_m Γ_m . grad h_m - Σ_m h_m W_m omega_m + dp0/dt              (133.15)
```

The first line of (133.4) is this equation divided by `rho cp T`, term for
term. §26 already carries `rho cp DT/Dt` (with CHR-10a's `cp` field,
§133.8), `div(λ grad T)` and `dp0/dt`. CHR-10b adds the other two terms, both
as explicit sources on §18's `EnergySources`, so they also enter §25.1's `Q`
and with it the target divergence and the sealed-box `p0`, as §26.1 requires
of every heat source.

**The heat release.** `-Σ_m h_m W_m omega_m` is the split step's: the reactor
(132.7)-(132.8) has already integrated it over `Δt` into `T* - T°`, and
(132.10) hands it to the transport step as `Q_chem = rho cp (T* - T°)/Δt`.
The `rho cp` is the energy equation's own:

```
Q_chem,c = w_c (T*_c - T°_c) / Δt,    w_c = the ddt row's current-level weight                 (133.16)
```

`w` is `rho_c cp_c` (or `rho_c cp` on the constant path), and (133.13)'s
`rho* cp` under backward, refreshed from the gas state exactly as
`Energy::correct` refreshes it (`Energy::heat_release_weight`). *DESIGN.*
With this weight a cell with no flux under Euler, at the first outer
iteration of a step (`rho^n = rho^(n-1)`, `ofgpu-lowmach`'s order: open the
step, then `update_density`), solves `w (T^(n+1) - T°)/Δt = Q_chem` and lands
on `T*` to round-off: the 0-D box is the reactor. Under backward the row is
`w (3/2 T - 2 T° + 1/2 T^(n-1))/Δt` and lands near, not on, `T*`; Lie
splitting is first order in `Δt` either way (§132.5). `T* - T°` is formed
from the two Scalar values (`ChemSource::start_temperature` keeps `T°`),
exact whenever the step changed `T` by less than a factor of two.

**The species-enthalpy diffusion.** §19's inert remainder `N` closes the
fluxes as it closes the mass fractions, `Γ_N = -Σ_k Γ_k` over the solved
species (§133.3's (133.5) is not built, §132.11), so with
`Γ_k = -rho D_k grad Y_k`

```
- Σ_m Γ_m . grad h_m = Σ_{k solved} rho_c D_k (cp_k(T_c) - cp_N(T_c)) (grad Y_k)_c . (grad T)_c   (133.17)
```

per cell, from Gauss gradients of `T` and of each solved `Y_k`. `D_k` is
the species' molecular diffusivity (`SpeciesCoeffs::d`), the laminar flux
of Day & Bell's equations. *DESIGN, decided by recommendation:* the
turbulent part `nu_t/Sc_t` of the species flux is not added, because §26's
turbulent heat flux `rho cp nu_t/Pr_t grad T` is the model of the turbulent
enthalpy transport and adding a second turbulent enthalpy flux would count
it twice. `rho` is the cell density of §25. (133.17) is not a divergence, so
its domain integral is not zero: it moves sensible heat between species of
different `cp`, which the temperature equation sees as a source.

**The mixture `cp`**, the producer §133.8 left open:

```
cp_c = Σ_m Y_m,c cp_m(T_c),   cp_m = (R/W_m)(a1 + a2 T + a3 T^2 + a4 T^3 + a5 T^4)            (133.18)
```

(128.7) with (128.1), the lower set at or below `t_mid` (128.5), on every
cell and every boundary face from that face's `T` and `Y`, into the two
buffers `Energy::set_cp_field` takes. A member with `Y_m = 0` adds exactly
nothing, as `ThermoSet::cp_mass` skips it. The polynomial ranges are not
checked here; a cell outside them is the reactor's refusal (§132.4).

**As built.** `cuda/energy.cu` gains `energyMixtureCpAdd` (one member per
launch), `energyEnthalpyDiffusionAdd` (one solved species per launch) and
`energyRoundAcc`: every sum is formed in `ofacc` (double in both builds,
§118.1) and rounded once to the build's scalar. `chem::source::SpeciesEnthalpy`
holds one 12-value row per member (`R/W`, `t_mid`, the two sets'
`a1..a5`), built by name from the `ThermoSet` and refused by name for a member
it does not carry; `mixture_cp` and `diffusion_source` allocate nothing and
read nothing back. `ChemSource::heat_release(weight, out)` forms (133.16)
and is refused by name before the first step. `EnergySources::use_meters`
gives the registry two opt-in meters, and `register_heat_release` and
`register_enthalpy_diffusion` add into `q` and into their meter;
`EnergyBudget` gains `heat_release_w` and `enthalpy_diffusion_w`, each
`-Σ_c q_meter,c V_c`, two sub-entries of `sources_w` in the same sign. A
registry without meters runs the launches it ran before, and the six
existing kernels of `energy.cubin` keep their SASS (the cubin's three new
functions are its only change).

### 133.10 The mixture molar mass in the equation of state and the molar-change term of the constraint (CHR-11, `src/energy.rs`, `cuda/energy.cu`)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` The equations are Day & Bell's
eqs. (3) and (7) as (133.3) and (133.4) of §133.1-§133.2 state and derive
them; nothing is added to them. What this section adds is how they are
evaluated.

**The mixture.** `GasMixture` names the solved members `k`, in the order
their mass-fraction fields are handed over, and §19's inert remainder `N`,
each with its molar mass. (133.3)'s `Σ_m Y_m/W_m`, with `Y_N = 1 - Σ_k Y_k`
written out, is

```
1/W = 1/W_N + Σ_k Y_k (1/W_k - 1/W_N)                                                          (133.19)
rho^(l) = p0^(l) / ( R T^(l) (1/W)^(l) ),    l = n, n-1, n-2 on the cells, and l = n on the boundary faces   (133.20)
```

`GasState::update_density_mixture` forms both on every level §25's
`update_density` refreshes, each level from its own `T`, `Y` and `p0`.
*DESIGN.* (133.19) equals (133.3)'s sum while `Σ_k Y_k <= 1`, where §19's
clip of `Y_N` at zero is idle (`Species::max_sum_error` measures when it is
not), and it reads the solved members' own old levels, which the inert field
does not keep.

**The constraint.** In (133.4), the first line and the `- h_m/(cp T)` part of
the third are `Q/(rho cp T)`, with `Q` §26.1's registry and conduction (CHR-10b
registers the heat release (133.16) and the enthalpy diffusion (133.17) there).
What is new is `(1/rho) Σ_m (W/W_m) S_m` with `S_m = W_m omega_m - div Γ_m`,
the member's net mass source, and `S_N = -Σ_k S_k` by the closure. By (133.3),
`W/rho = R T/p0` and `1/(rho cp T) = R_s/(cp p0)` exactly, so per cell

```
D_c = Q_c R_s,c / (cp_c p0) + (R T_c / p0) Σ_k (1/W_k - 1/W_N) S_k,c,    R_s,c = R (1/W)_c
(div u)_target,c = D_c - (1/γ_c) (dp0/dt) / p0,    1/γ_c = 1 - R_s,c / cp_c                    (133.21)
```

with `cp_c` CHR-10a's field when one is set and the constant `cp` otherwise,
`dp0/dt` at §25's one-iteration lag. Integrating (133.21) over a sealed domain,
where `∫ div u dV = 0`:

```
dp0/dt = p0 ∫ D dV / ∫ (1/γ) dV     (sealed),     dp0/dt = 0     (open)                         (133.22)
```

With one constant `W` and `γ = cp/(cp - R/W)` this is (25.2)'s
`(γ - 1)/V_dom ∫ Q dV`. On the gate's box (uniform, `Q = 0`, one solved `A`
against the inert `N`, `Σ_m omega_m = S_A/W_A + S_N/W_N`) it is the closed form

```
dp0/dt = γ R T S_A (1/W_A - 1/W_N) = γ R T Σ_m omega_m,     γ = cp / (cp - R (1/W))             (133.23)
```

**As built.** `cuda/energy.cu` gains `energyFillAcc` and `energyAxpyAcc`
((133.19), and the molar sum `Σ_k (1/W_k - 1/W_N) S_k` that
`GasState::set_molar_change` forms from the members' sources in kg/(m3 s)),
`energyMixtureDensity` ((133.20)) and `energyMixtureConstraint` ((133.21) on
every cell, grid-stride, with the per-block sums of `D V` and `V/γ`). Every sum
and quotient is in `ofacc` (double in both builds, §118.1), rounded once to the
build's scalar; `Energy::constraint_integrals` totals the block sums on the
host in block order, and `GasState::advance_p0_mixture` takes one explicit
Euler step of (133.22) in f64 and rounds `p0` once. Because the rate never
passes through a rounded `rho`, class A holds in f32. A gas without a mixture
runs every launch it ran before (the old `energyTargetDivergence`, `update_density`,
`advance_p0`), and on a gas with one `update_density` and `advance_p0` are refused
by name. Under backward, `rho* cp` of (133.13) becomes `(p0/R) cp / ((1/W) T*)`
with the current level's `1/W`, as it takes the `cp` field as last set.

**What is not built, stated.** The `- div Γ_k` half of `S_k` is the caller's:
`set_molar_change` takes the net source, and CHR-12b forms it, (133.24) of
§133.11, from the species equations it solves (the reaction half is CHR-09's (132.10) source, times `rho`
on the constant-density equation). The Mach number of §93.5 and `GasState::rho_at`
still read the constant `R_s`. Day & Bell's damping eq. (8) is not adopted: the
measured drift below is first order in `Δt`.

**Gates, measured 2026-10-15 (both builds, `tests/gas_wmix.rs`).**

| row | measure | tolerance | class | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gas_constant_w_default_bitwise` | a sealed 4^3 walled box without a mixture, `T` 300-330 K, a uniform 1e3 W/m3 heater, three Euler steps of `update_density`, `update_target_divergence`, `correct` and `advance_p0`: SHA-256 of every `rho`, target divergence, `T`, `p0` and `dp0/dt`, against pins captured at the parent commit 41d449a, one per build | bitwise | D | equal in both builds |
| `gas_wmix_sealed_box_p0_closed_form` | a sealed 2^3 walled box, `T` held at 300 K (isothermal: the energy equation not solved), no flow, no heat source, `A` with NO2's `W` and the inert `N = 2 A` (the shape of 2 NO2 -> N2O4, heat-neutral by construction), `S_A = -2 kg/(m3 s)`, `Y_A` in {0.9, 0.6, 0.3}: `dp0/dt` against (133.23) evaluated in f64 from the stored inputs; `p0` one Euler step of it (D); `rho` against (133.20) and, at the new `p0`, the target divergence against its own `D` (R, D-F32-1); seven refusals by name | `1e-12` relative (A); `1e-12`, `1e-5` in f32 (R) | A, D, R | `dp0/dt` `1.15e-16` (f64) and `1.19e-16` (f32); `rho` `2.29e-16` and `4.35e-8`; target divergence `2.05e-16` and `1.76e-8` |
| (diagnostic, same test) | the same box adiabatic, `T` solved (Euler, one outer iteration per step, `ofgpu-lowmach`'s order), `Y_A(t) = 0.9 + S_A t/rho`, to `t = 0.05` s: `p0` against the exact `rho R Z (T_0 - p0_0/(rho cp))/(1 - R Z/cp)`, `Z = 1/W(t)`, and the mass drift `Σ rho V` | printed | — | 10 steps: `p0` error `1.05e-3` of its change, mass drift `5.8e-4`; 20 steps: `5.4e-4`, `2.9e-4`; order `0.96` in both builds |

**The order of a step matters, measured.** The adiabatic leg first ran with
`Y` at the step's new value on its current level and the old value on the
previous one when `T` was solved. Then §26's conservative ddt row
`(rho^n T - rho^(n-1) T°) cp/Δt` saw `rho^n ≠ rho^(n-1)` from `W` alone. `T`
fell 9 K where the exact fall is 1.66 K, and the error did not shrink with
`Δt`. In `ofgpu-lowmach`'s order the species are solved after `T`, so `Y`
holds the step's opening value on both levels and `rho^n = rho^(n-1)` at the
energy solve, as on the constant-`W` path. The numbers above are for that
order. CHR-12b keeps it.

### 133.11 The reacting driver as built (CHR-12b, `src/bin/lowmach.rs`, `src/bin/lowmach_chem/`)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` The equations are Day & Bell's as
§133.1-§133.10 write them and §132's split step; this section adds the
discrete diffusion half of (133.21)'s net source, (133.24), and the order in
which `ofgpu-lowmach` runs them. It is this project's own contract (ORIGINAL).

**What runs.** A JSONC case whose `species`, `chemistry` and `combustion`
blocks lower (§137.7) with `combustion.model laminar` runs as laminar
finite-rate chemistry, Lie split (§132.5): chemistry first, then transport.
`common::load_case_with(path, true)` lets the blocks past §137.7's seam for
this driver only; every other driver keeps the refusal through
`common::load_case`.

**The species set.** Every solved member gets §86's mass-weighted equation,
`d(rho Y)/dt`, with the density of the step. Its diffusivity is the Lewis
route of §133.4, `D_k = lambda/(rho cp Le_k) = nu/(Pr Le_k)`, with this
driver's constant `nu` and `Pr` and `Le_k` from the case (1 by default), and
`Sc_t` the case's. The controls are read by the species' own entry names
(§13.4.1): `solvers` and `relaxation` under `Yi` (relaxation 1 when the case
names none), `grad(Yi)`, and the convection `div(phi,Yi_h)` or `div(phi,Yi)`
when the case names one (two different entries are refused), otherwise §19's
bounded Gauss upwind. The case's `div` `default` is never taken.

**One step, in this order.** `o` marks the step's opening state.

1. Open the step (from the second on): `Simple::begin_time_step`, `T`'s
   levels, `p0`'s levels, and then every solved `Y_k`'s levels
   (`Y^(n-2) <- Y^(n-1) <- Y`). The last rotation is what makes (133.20)'s
   `rho^(n-1)` the opening state's, so `rho^n = rho^(n-1)` at the energy
   solve, as §133.10 requires of the order.
2. `T`'s and every `Y_k`'s `inletOutlet` faces switch on the last flux.
3. `rho` by (133.19)-(133.20) from `T`, `Y_k` and `p0`.
4. `EnergySources::clear`; the mixture `cp` (133.18) into the energy
   equation's `cp` field; the split step (132.10) with every cell's reactor
   at `p0`; the heat release (133.16) and the enthalpy diffusion (133.17)
   registered, ahead of `-heaterPower`, the thermostat and the case's sources.
5. The molar change of (133.21), with each solved member's net source

```
S_k,P = rho_P (Y*_k,P - Y°_k,P)/dt + (1/V_P) Σ_f rho_f D_k |S_f| snGrad(Y°_k)_f          (133.24)
```

   The first term is the split step's own source on the mass-weighted
   equation (§132.11). The second is `-div Gamma_k` with
   `Gamma_k = -rho D_k grad Y_k`: `rho_f` interpolated linearly, the
   uncorrected `snGrad` and `fvc::div` of the face flux (`fv::sn_grad_flux`,
   `fv::fvc_div_surface`). *DESIGN, decided by recommendation:* it carries
   the laminar `D_k` only, as (133.17) does and for the same reason (§133.9).
6. `Energy::update_target_divergence` ((133.21)), `Simple::correct_outer_low_mach`
   and `Energy::correct`.
7. The species equations, on the flux the pressure solve made.
8. Transient: `GasState::advance_p0_mixture` from
   `Energy::constraint_integrals`, (133.22); an open gas keeps `p0`.

A case without the blocks makes the calls it made before CHR-12b, in the same
order: `outer_iteration`'s `None` arm is the old sequence.

**Written.** Every solved `Y_k` with its own boundary types, the inert member
and `HRR` (133.16)'s `Q_chem` in W/m3, both with `calculated` in place of the
value rules and the constraint patches kept. The final cell values of `T`,
`rho`, `HRR` and every member are also held at full precision in the driver's
`RunEnd`, because the written fields carry six digits.

**Refused by name, before a field is set up** (`lowmach_chem::refuse_settings`):
a steady run (the split step integrates over a physical `dt`); EDM, EDC and
PaSR, which lower (§137.7) and are CHR-14's and CHR-15's; Strang splitting;
a `ddt` other than Euler (the box lands on the reactor under Euler, §133.9,
and the species keep one old level); a checkpoint, `-restartFrom`,
`-restartWrite` or an output restart series (the `.mcr` format carries no
mass fractions); a motion block; and a species named like another field the
run writes. The dictionary route keeps §137.7's refusal: a case directory
with chemistry is refused by every driver.

**What is not built, stated.** The dictionary route, Strang, `backward`, a
restart of the mass fractions, the closures of §134, the turbulent part of
(133.24), and §93.5's Mach number with the mixture's own `R_s` (it still
reads the constant one, §133.10).

**Tree against plan.** The plan's row names "a reduced 1-D JL flame".
`cases/mech/jl4.ck` does not exist: its paper is unread and no rate is

box is CHR-09's 2^3 box, cyclic on all three axes. Through the driver that box

flow it makes grows to about 2 m/s in 200 steps (measured). The pair below
therefore runs the box as two cells with adiabatic walls. There the pressure

## 134. Turbulence-chemistry interaction — EDM, EDC and PaSR, selected through `MixingRate`

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Docs/17 §4.3 allocates §134-§137 to
turbulence-chemistry interaction, participating-media radiation, their
coupling and the case blocks of tranche 17's CHEMRAD stream. CHR-00b wrote
these four sections as contracts. No code cites them yet. CHR-14 to CHR-29
implement them, and each of those units amends its own section in place
when it lands.

**What "read" means here** is §128's rule, unchanged. A source marked
**read** was opened and the equation stated from it, with the page or
equation number given. A source marked *not read* had its identifier checked
on Crossref (and its access on OpenAlex). Its text was not available, and
nothing below is stated from it. No coefficient, constant or table entry
below comes from memory. Every number is either printed by a read source, or
computed here from a printed formula, and the computation is shown.

**Sources.**

* **Ertesvåg**, "Analysis of some recently proposed modifications to the Eddy
  Dissipation Concept (EDC)", *Combust. Sci. Technol.* 192 (2020) 1108-1136,
  DOI 10.1080/00102202.2019.1611565. Crossref agrees. **Read** from the
  author's revised manuscript (dated 16 April 2019; NVA labels it the accepted version) in NTNU's archive (`hdl.handle.net/11250/2642182`,
  file `Ertesvag2020.pdf`, sha256
  `8bc1b327408107dd995746cd79fa82c6973bbb4eccaedbc67d7907966a5e83dc`), which
  is the version OpenAlex lists as the open copy. Read: §2 eqs. (1)-(11), §3.1
  eqs. (12)-(20), §5.1-§5.3 eqs. (38)-(41) and Table 1. It is a review by
  Magnussen's successor, and it states the 1981, 1989 and 2005 formulations
  side by side. That is why it is this section's primary source for EDC.
* **Gran & Magnussen**, *Combust. Sci. Technol.* 119 (1996) 191-217, DOI
  10.1080/00102209608951999. Crossref agrees. Closed, *not read*. Its
  formulation is stated from Ertesvåg eq. (18) and §3.1, which quote it.
* **Magnussen**, "The Eddy Dissipation Concept - a bridge between science and
  technology", ECCOMAS Thematic Conference on Computational Combustion, Lisbon,
  21-24 June 2005. It has no DOI. Ertesvåg's reference list says it is
  available at `folk.ntnu.no/ivarse/edc`, which was reached (a redirect) and
  *not read*. Its formulation is stated from Ertesvåg eqs. (19)-(20).
* **Magnussen & Hjertager**, *Symp. (Int.) Combust.* 16 (1977) 719-729, DOI
  10.1016/S0082-0784(77)80366-4. Crossref agrees. Closed, *not read*. The EDM
  form is stated from the FDS Technical Reference Guide, which cites it.
* **The FDS Technical Reference Guide** (McGrattan et al., NIST SP 1018,
  public domain), `Manuals/FDS_Technical_Reference_Guide/Combustion_Chapter.tex`
  at firemodels/fds `e14ec3f29c5b06fd7e3ee35b137c90531cb04fe3`, sha256
  `60d3ee21fb5aee27a67c855533e2e62fd688de1a4541c759c64953d7864a3899`.
  **Read**: "Reaction Time Scale Model", "Time Integration for Mixing and
  Reaction" and "Infinitely Fast Chemistry, Single Reaction", equations
  `eqn_tau_mix`, `mass_prod_rate` and `eq:edc`.
* **Piscopo, De Paepe, Parente & Iavarone**, "Chemical timescale analysis of
  the Partially Stirred Reactor model for a hydrogen-fuelled scramjet",
  *Results in Engineering* 23 (2024) 102834, DOI 10.1016/j.rineng.2024.102834,
  CC BY. Crossref agrees. **Read** from the ULB repository copy
  (`dipot.ulb.ac.be/dspace/bitstream/2013/378950/1/doi_362594.pdf`, sha256
  `ca1904de05aa17c95ec0f462d4595b7e4be23dd0129739b9c1025642b31e83ed`): §2,
  eqs. (2)-(12). It is a **secondary** source for PaSR: its eq. (3) cites
  Chomiak & Karlsson.
* **Chomiak & Karlsson**, "Flame liftoff in diesel sprays", *Symp. (Int.)
  Combust.* 26 (1996) 2557-2564, DOI 10.1016/S0082-0784(96)80088-9. Crossref
  agrees. Closed, *not read*. The plan cited it with no DOI. This is it.
* **Sabelnikov & Fureby**, *Combust. Flame* 160 (2013) 83-96, DOI
  10.1016/j.combustflame.2012.09.008. Crossref agrees. Closed, *not read*.

### 134.1 Where the closure acts, and what selects it

The laminar finite-rate source of (133.1), `W_m omega_m(T, p, Y)` with
`omega` from (130.1), is evaluated at the cell's mean state. Under turbulence
the mean of a nonlinear rate is not the rate of the mean. A closure replaces
`W_m omega_m(T̃, p, Ỹ)` by a mean rate `W_m ω̄_m`, and nothing else in §133
changes. This document writes `Ỹ` for the Favre mean that `Species`
transports (§86). The closure is selected by name and reads its turbulent time
scales from the turbulence model through `MixingRate` (`src/models/coupled.rs`).

| `combustion.model` | needs from `MixingRate` | mechanisms it accepts |
|---|---|---|
| `laminar` (the default) | nothing | any (§129) |
| `EDM` | the rate `ε/k` | one- or two-step global only (§134.2) |
| `EDC` | `k`, `ε` and `ν` | any |
| `PaSR` | `τ_mix` by name (§134.4) | any |

**The `Omega` arm carries no `k`.** `MixingRate::Omega` gives `β* ω`, which is
`ε/k`, and that is all EDM needs. EDC's (134.3) and (134.4), and PaSR's
Kolmogorov and geometric times, need `ε` itself, and `ε = β* k ω`. The
contract, decided by recommendation: the TCI entry points take `MixingRate`
together with an `Option` of the model's `k` field. With the `Omega` arm and no
`k`, EDC and the two `ε` forms of PaSR are refused, naming the missing field.
`MixingRate` itself is not edited. It is a dispatch key in a shared solver
file, and the `k` field already exists in every k-ω model.

**Refusals (§13.4), each naming the combination:**

* EDM, EDC or PaSR with `MixingRate::None` (laminar, Spalart-Allmaras). This
  is the refusal `coupled.rs` already documents.
* EDM or EDC with `MixingRate::Strain` (LES). Both are RANS closures in every
  read source. LES-EDC is named and not built.
* EDM with a mechanism that has more than two reactions, or one whose
  reactions are not global (any third body, falloff or reverse reaction).
* PaSR without a named `tauMix` or `tauChem` (§134.4). It has no default.

### 134.2 EDM — the eddy-dissipation model

FDS states the single-reaction, mixing-controlled rate it attributes to
Magnussen & Hjertager (TRG eq. `eq:edc`):

```
ṁ'''_F = - ρ min( Y_F , Y_A / s ) / τ_mix                                       (134.1)
```

`s` is the mass stoichiometric coefficient of the oxidiser, and `τ_mix` the
mixing time. The RANS form this crate builds sets `1/τ_mix = A ε/k`, and adds
Magnussen & Hjertager's product-limiting third argument `B Y_P/(1 + s)`.
Their constants `A` and `B` are in the 1977 paper, which was **not read**. So
**`A` and `B` have no default: the case states both**, or states `B` absent
(which removes the third argument and gives exactly (134.1)). A case that
omits `A` is refused, naming the parameter and the closed source. The value
moves to a default only when the paper is read.

**More than one global reaction (DESIGN, for BFER's two steps).** Each global
reaction `r` gets its own rate of progress, in kmol/(m3 s), limited by its own
reactants. It uses the stoichiometric weighting of the FDS single-reaction
rule (TRG eq. `eq:stoich_fuel_single`, which divides each `Y_α` by
`ν_α W_α`):

```
q_r = A (ε/k) ρ min( min_{α ∈ R(r)} Ỹ_α / (ν'_αr W_α) ,
                     B Σ_{β ∈ P(r)} Ỹ_β / Σ_{β ∈ P(r)} ν''_βr W_β )             (134.2)
W_m ω̄_m = W_m Σ_r (ν''_mr - ν'_mr) q_r
```

`R(r)` and `P(r)` are the reactants and products of reaction `r`. For one
reaction with fuel `F`, `q_r ν'_F W_F` is the magnitude of (134.1), with
`s = ν'_O W_O / (ν'_F W_F)`. The product term reduces to `B Y_P/(ν'_F W_F (1 + s))` because mass
balance gives `Σ_P ν'' W = ν'_F W_F (1 + s)`. That is Magnussen &
Hjertager's third argument, which this reduction is the check of. Element
conservation holds by construction: (134.2) is a rate of progress multiplied
by a balanced stoichiometric vector (§129.4).

**The analytic limit CHR-14 gates.** Take a closed, well-stirred box with
frozen `k` and `ε`, one global reaction, `B` absent, and a fuel-lean mixture,
so that `Ỹ_F < Ỹ_O/s` holds for all `t`. Then (134.1) is linear in `Ỹ_F`:

```
Ỹ_F(t) = Ỹ_F(0) exp( - A ε t / k )                                              (134.3)
```

### 134.3 EDC — the eddy dissipation concept

All equations in this subsection are Ertesvåg's, in his notation: `*` marks
the fine structures, `o` the surroundings and `~` the mean.

**The cascade constants** (Ertesvåg eqs. (9)-(11)):

```
γ_λ = (3 C_D2 / (4 C_D1^2))^(1/4) (ν ε / k^2)^(1/4) = C_γ Re_T^(-1/4)           (134.4)
τ*  = (C_D2 / 3)^(1/2) (ν / ε)^(1/2)                = C_τ (ν/ε)^(1/2)           (134.5)
```

**`C_γ` and `C_τ` are computed from `C_D1` and `C_D2` in f64, and never
typed in.** With Ertesvåg Table 1's row (a), "original (Magnussen 1981;
Ertesvåg & Magnussen 2000)", `C_D1 = 0.135` and `C_D2 = 0.50`:
`C_γ = (1.5/0.0729)^(1/4) = 2.12981034748758` and
`C_τ = (1/6)^(1/2) = 0.408248290463863`. Table 1 prints 2.130 and 0.4082.

**A correction to the plan.** (The published version was not read, and it may have corrected the sentence below.) Docs/17 and the CHEMRAD plan give
`C_γ = 2.1377` and `C_τ = 0.4083`. Ertesvåg Table 1 lists 2.1377 as row
(a'), "variant of original", with **`C_D1 = 0.134`**:
`(1.5/(4 · 0.134^2))^(1/4) = 2.13775`. The manuscript's own §2.2 sentence
prints "2.1377" beside `C_D1 = 0.135`, and its eq. (9) contradicts that
pairing. `C_τ = 0.4083` is `0.408248` rounded the wrong way. **Decided by
recommendation:** the default is row (a), the one the source calls original. A
case selects (a') by stating `CD1 0.134`. Both are evaluated by (134.4), so
neither is ever a typed `C_γ`.

**The two variants, selected by name and never substituted for each other**
(Ertesvåg §3.1):

| `variant` | fine-structure mass fraction | source as read |
|---|---|---|
| `1989` (used by Gran & Magnussen 1996, and named `1996` in the plan; both spellings are accepted) | `γ* = γ_λ^3` | Ertesvåg eq. (18) |
| `2005` | `γ* = γ_λ^2` | Ertesvåg eqs. (19)-(20) |

`χ`, the reacting fraction, is **1 in both variants in v1**. That is Gran &
Magnussen's choice for detailed chemistry, and the practice Ertesvåg reports
in §3.1. A reactor that does not react contributes nothing anyway. The 2005
`χ` of Ertesvåg eq. (19) needs a global fuel-oxidiser-product split, and it is
named and not built.

**The fine-structure reactor (Ertesvåg eqs. (1), (4), (5), (38)).** This is a
steady perfectly stirred reactor, fed at the **surroundings** state `Y°`, with
residence time `τ*`:

```
Y*_k - Y°_k = τ* R*_k(T*, p, Y*) / ρ*                                           (134.6)
Ỹ_k = γ* χ Y*_k + (1 - γ* χ) Y°_k                                                (134.7)
```

Eliminate `Y°` with (134.7). The fine-structure state then solves an equation
in the mean alone:

```
Y*_k - Ỹ_k = (1 - γ* χ) τ* R*_k(T*, p, Y*) / ρ*                                 (134.8)
```

**Energy (derived, DESIGN in its reading).** The reactor is adiabatic and
isobaric. A steady adiabatic PSR has outflow enthalpy equal to inflow
enthalpy, `h* = h°`, and (134.7) applied to `h` then gives `h* = h̃`. `T*`
therefore solves `h(T*, Y*) = h̃` by (128.7). Ertesvåg does not write this
step. It is the PSR energy balance under the same mass-weighting he writes
for species.

**How (134.8) is solved.** Integrate the transient PSR to steady state. This
is "the species mass balance of the homogeneous reactor (transient PSR)
integrated to steady state, as used by Gran (1994), Gran & Magnussen (1996)"
(Ertesvåg §5.3):

```
dY*_k/dt = R*_k(T*, p, Y*) / ρ*  -  (Y*_k - Ỹ_k) / ((1 - γ* χ) τ*),   Y*(0) = Ỹ  (134.9)
```

It is integrated with §132's Rosenbrock kernel over a pseudo-time span of
`psrSpan` time constants `(1 - γ*χ) τ*`. `psrSpan` defaults to 20 (DESIGN:
`e^-20 = 2.1e-9`, below CHR-15's `1e-8` gate when the chemistry is slower than
the mixing; faster chemistry converges sooner). The residual of (134.8) is
evaluated after the span. A cell whose relative residual exceeds `rtol` is
counted and reported, never hidden.

**Refused by name: the batch-reactor variant.** Integrating
`dY/dt = R/ρ` from the **mean** `Ỹ` over `τ*` (Ertesvåg eqs. (40)-(41)) is
the Ansys Fluent implementation. Ertesvåg §5.2-§5.3 shows it is not EDC: its
inflow is the mean rather than the surroundings, and the low-Reynolds limit
`Re_T > 65` derived from it does not apply to EDC. The CHEMRAD plan's phrase
"integrated as a PSR over tau*" could be read as this variant. The contract
here is (134.9), and `variant "batch"` is refused, with this reason.

**The mean rate (Ertesvåg eqs. (3) and (5)):**

```
W_k ω̄_k = ρ̄ γ* χ (Y*_k - Y°_k) / τ*  =  ρ̄ γ* χ (Y*_k - Ỹ_k) / ((1 - γ* χ) τ*)    (134.10)
```

**The cap.** (134.10) has `1 - γ*χ` in its denominator, and `γ_λ = 1` at
`Re_T = C_γ^4` (20.58 with row (a)). `γ_λ` is capped at `gammaMax`, which
defaults to 0.95 (DESIGN: no read source fixes a value, and Ertesvåg §5.3
states only that the fraction must stay below 1). Every capped cell is
counted in the step's report, so a run cannot cap silently.

**The closed form CHR-15 gates.** Take one first-order irreversible reaction
`R*_F/ρ* = -k_r Y*_F`, with `T*` not entering. (134.8) is then linear:

```
Y*_F = Ỹ_F / (1 + (1 - γ* χ) k_r τ*)                                             (134.11)
W_F ω̄_F = - ρ̄ γ* χ k_r Ỹ_F / (1 + (1 - γ* χ) k_r τ*)
```

**Hand values for `edc_constants_by_variant`** (f64, computed here from
(134.4), (134.5) and (134.11)), with `ν = 1.5e-5 m2/s`, `k = 1 m2/s2`,
`ε = 10 m2/s3`, row (a), `χ = 1`, `k_r = 1000 1/s` and `Ỹ_F = 0.05`:

| quantity | `1989` | `2005` |
|---|---|---|
| `γ_λ` | 0.235702260395516 | 0.235702260395516 |
| `τ*` (s) | 5.0e-4 (exactly `(1/6 · 1.5e-6)^(1/2)`) | 5.0e-4 |
| `γ*` | 0.013094570021973 | 0.055555555555556 (= 1/18) |
| `Y*_F` | 0.033479466405716 | 0.033962264150943 |
| `W_F ω̄_F / ρ̄` (1/s) | -0.4383992171479441 | -1.886792452830188 |

### 134.4 PaSR — the partially stirred reactor

Piscopo et al. eq. (3), citing Chomiak & Karlsson, gives the reacting
fraction from a mixing time and a chemical time:

```
κ = τ_c / (τ_c + τ_m)                                                            (134.12)
```

Their eq. (4) gives the mean rate as `κ ρ̄ (Y* - Y°)/τ*`, with `Y*` from a
reactor integration. **v1 builds the frozen-mean form**, decided by
recommendation:

```
W_k ω̄_k = κ W_k ω_k(T̃, p, Ỹ)                                                    (134.13)
```

This is the reacting fraction applied to the laminar rate at the mean state.
It has the two limits CHR-14 gates: `τ_m → 0` gives `κ → 1`, which is the
laminar rate **bitwise** when `τ_m = 0` is exact; and a linear rate gives
`κ` exactly. The reactor form of eq. (4) is named and not built.

**Mixing times, by name** (Piscopo et al. eqs. (8)-(10)):

| `tauMix` | `τ_m` | reads |
|---|---|---|
| `integral` | `C_mix k/ε` (eq. 8). `C_mix` has no default, because the source says it "must be tuned" | `ε/k` |
| `kolmogorov` | `(ν/ε)^(1/2)` (eq. 9) | `ε`, `ν` |
| `geometric` | `(τ_I τ_K)^(1/2)` with `τ_I = k/ε` (eq. 10) | `k`, `ε`, `ν` |
| `strain` | `1 / \|S\|` (DESIGN, the LES arm of `MixingRate`) | `\|S\|` |

The plan wrote `C_mix sqrt(tau_k tau_int)`. The read source's geometric form
has **no `C_mix`**, and it notes that avoiding the tuned constant is the
reason for the form. The contract follows the source.

**Chemical times, by name** (Piscopo et al. eqs. (5)-(7)). In these,
`ẏ_i = W_i ω_i/ρ` (1/s), and the dormant species with `|ẏ_i| < 1e-8 1/s` are
excluded (their threshold, the unit read as 1/s):

| `tauChem` | `τ_c` |
|---|---|
| `sfr` | `max_i Y_i / \|ẏ_i\|` (eq. 5) |
| `ffr` | `min_i Y_i / \|ẏ_i\|` (eq. 6) |
| `gfr` | `(τ_c^sfr τ_c^ffr)^(1/2)` (eq. 7) |

If every species is dormant, `κ = 1` and the rate is the (negligible)
laminar one. Their eq. (11), Batchelor's species-dependent time, is named and
not built.

### 134.5 What CHR-14 and CHR-15 must make true

The TCI host twins are written in `f64` types, so every row runs unchanged in
both builds and carries one tolerance (docs/17 §5.1.4). The device path
(`cuda/chem.cu`, `ofchem = double`, the chemistry scope of §118, which F32-02 creates in lane S) inherits the same rows.

| row | measure | tolerance | class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edm_box_closed_form` | box `Ỹ_F(t)` against (134.3) at three times | 1e-10 relative | P |
| `edm_two_step_conserves_elements` | (134.2) element production per cell | 1e-14 relative to `Σ \|q_r\|` | A |
| `edm_requires_a_and_b` | a case with no `A` | refused, naming `A` and the closed paper | D |
| `pasr_limit_is_laminar` | `τ_m = 0`: (134.13) against the laminar `omega` | bitwise | D |
| `pasr_linear_kappa_exact` | linear test rate: `κ` of (134.12) | 1e-12 relative | P |
| `tci_refuses_no_mixing_rate` | EDM, EDC, PaSR with `MixingRate::None` | refused, naming the combination | D |
| `edc_constants_by_variant` | the §134.3 hand-value table | 1e-14 relative | P |
| `edc_psr_closed_form` | (134.9) integrated over `psrSpan`, against (134.11) | 1e-8 relative | P |
| `edc_cap_is_counted` | `Re_T < C_γ^4` cells | count equals the cells with `γ_λ > gammaMax` | D |
| `edc_refuses_batch_variant` | `variant "batch"` | refused with §134.3's reason | D |

## 135. The radiative transfer equation, the exact slab, and P1 with Marshak walls

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.`

**Sources.**

* **Siegel & Howell**, *Thermal Radiation Heat Transfer*, Volume III:
  *Radiation Transfer with Absorbing, Emitting, and Scattering Media*, NASA
  SP-164 (1971), NTRS **19710021465**, distribution PUBLIC. A US-Government
  work. **Read** from the NTRS PDF (sha256
  `56375112ebbdaafa38222f9dca1324ca26336fccd4e849ec7574ab58060b3039`), from the
  page images, because the text layer drops every equation. Read: §2.6.2-§2.6.3
  eqs. (2-43)-(2-47) (the plane layer and `E_n`); §3.6.2 eqs. (3-110)-(3-123)
  (the "differential approximation", which is P1, and its wall condition);
  §8.5 eqs. (8-43)-(8-52) (scattering layers). The plan cited Modest's
  textbook for P1 and Marshak. This open, primary-equivalent statement
  replaces it as the read source.
* **The FDS Technical Reference Guide**,
  `Manuals/FDS_Technical_Reference_Guide/Radiation_Chapter.tex` at firemodels/fds
  `e14ec3f29c5b06fd7e3ee35b137c90531cb04fe3`, sha256
  `7e503b92574bc1e28ca2baaae2b138846f5ffbdc51855d5c74b354373c7befeb`. Public
  domain. **Read**: "Radiation Transport Equation" (eq. `RTEbasic`),
  "Radiation Contribution to Energy Equation" (eq. `net_emission`),
  "Spatial Discretization" (eq. `RTEdiscrete2`) and "Boundary Conditions"
  (eq. `RTEbc`).
* **Modest**, *Radiative Heat Transfer*, 3rd ed., Academic Press (2013), DOI
  10.1016/C2010-0-65874-3. A book, *not read*. Cited as the textbook
  statement, as `s2s.rs` already does, and nothing below is taken from it.
* **Heaslet & Warming**, "Radiative transport and wall temperature slip in an
  absorbing planar medium", *Int. J. Heat Mass Transfer* 8 (1965) 979-994, DOI
  **10.1016/0017-9310(65)90083-9**. The plan said the DOI was "to be verified".
  Crossref finds it with a final `9`, not `X`. Closed, and NTRS 19650046628
  holds the reprint record with no file, so it was *not read*. SP-164 §2.6.2
  describes it (four significant figures, radiative equilibrium between
  heated walls, its fig. 2-6). **It is not an isotropic-scattering table at
  `ω = 0.5`**. It is the radiative-equilibrium problem, which is the
  conservative `ω = 1` case. The non-conservative tables are Heaslet &
  Warming, "Radiative source-function predictions for finite and
  semi-infinite non-conservative atmospheres", *Astrophys. Space Sci.* 1
  (1968) 460-498, DOI 10.1007/BF00658770 (Crossref; closed, *not read*;
  NTRS 19680053525 has no file). §135.5 says what this does to CHR-21's gate.

### 135.1 The equation of transfer

FDS eq. `RTEbasic`, grey, with the phase function normalised so that
`(1/4π) ∫ Φ dΩ' = 1`:

```
Ω · ∇I(x, Ω) = - (κ + σ_s) I + κ I_b + (σ_s / 4π) ∫_{4π} Φ(Ω', Ω) I(x, Ω') dΩ'   (135.1)
I_b = σ T^4 / π,      β = κ + σ_s,      ω = σ_s / β                               (135.2)
G = ∫_{4π} I dΩ,      q = ∫_{4π} I Ω dΩ                                           (135.3)
```

In FDS's notation `G` is `U` and `q` is `q_r''`. Two phase functions are
built. `isotropic` is `Φ = 1`. `linearAnisotropic` is `Φ = 1 + A_1 Ω'·Ω`,
which is normalised for any `A_1`, and non-negative only for `|A_1| <= 1`. A
case with `|A_1| > 1` is refused, because the phase function would be negative
for some pair of directions.

**The volumetric source (FDS eq. `net_emission`, grey).** Integrate (135.1)
over all directions. The scattering terms cancel, since
`∫∫ Φ I dΩ' dΩ / 4π = G` for a normalised `Φ`. What remains is:

```
- ∇·q = κ (G - 4 σ T^4)                                                          (135.4)
```

This is the energy the gas gains. §137.1 registers it.

### 135.2 The exact isothermal slab (the reference for CHR-20 and CHR-22)

A non-scattering grey slab of optical thickness `τ = κ L` sits at uniform
`T` between cold black walls. SP-164 eq. (2-47) gives the net flux at the
first wall, with `E_n` from eq. (2-45):

```
E_n(x) = ∫_0^1 μ^(n-2) exp(-x/μ) dμ                                              (135.5)
q(0) = σT_1^4 - 2 [ σT_2^4 E_3(τ) + σ ∫_0^τ T^4(t) E_2(t) dt ]
```

Set `T_1 = T_2 = 0` and `T` uniform. Then `∫_0^τ E_2 = E_3(0) - E_3(τ)` with
`E_3(0) = 1/2` (SP-164 appendix, `dE_n/dx = -E_(n-1)`). The flux into each
wall is:

```
Ψ_exact(τ) = |q_w| / (σ T^4) = 1 - 2 E_3(τ)                                      (135.6)
```

The derivation, as a check: a ray reaching the wall at polar cosine `μ`
carries `I = I_b (1 - e^(-τ/μ))`. Then
`|q_w| = 2π I_b ∫_0^1 (1 - e^(-τ/μ)) μ dμ = π I_b (1 - 2E_3(τ))`, and
`π I_b = σT^4`. The two routes agree.

| `τ` | `1 - 2 E_3(τ)` (f64, `scipy.special.expn`) |
|---|---|
| 0.1 | 0.167417084183 |
| 1 | 0.780616065604 |
| 10 | 0.999992902475 |

For a grey gas `j` of a WSGG set (§136.4) with weight `a_j` and coefficient
`κ_j`, the same slab gives `Σ_j a_j (1 - 2E_3(κ_j L))` by linearity. That sum
is CHR-22's reference.

### 135.3 P1, derived

SP-164 §3.6.2 derives the P1 equation by keeping the first two spherical
harmonics, `I = (G + 3 q·Ω)/(4π)` (its eq. (3-117) in Cartesian form). It
does this for a non-scattering medium in radiative equilibrium. Here the same
step is applied to (135.1) with absorption and scattering.

* **The zeroth moment** is (135.4).
* **The first moment.** Multiply (135.1) by `Ω` and integrate. With the P1
  intensity, `∫ Ω (Ω·∇I) dΩ = (1/3) ∇G`, the emission term integrates to
  zero, and the in-scattering term gives `(σ_s A_1 / 3) q` (because
  `∫ Ω (Ω'·Ω) dΩ = (4π/3) Ω'`). So
  `(1/3) ∇G = -(β - σ_s A_1/3) q`, which is:

```
q = - Γ ∇G,          Γ = 1 / (3β - A_1 σ_s)                                      (135.7)
- ∇·(Γ ∇G) + κ G = 4 κ σ T^4                                                     (135.8)
```

With `σ_s = 0` and `κ = a`, eliminate `G` between (135.4) and (135.7):
`∇G = 4σ∇T^4 - ∇((1/a)∇·q) = -3a q`, which is SP-164 eq. (3-112),
`∂/∂x_k((1/a) Σ_j ∂q_j/∂x_j) - 4σ ∂T^4/∂x_k - 3a q_k = 0`, term by term. The operator `-∇·(Γ∇) + κ` is symmetric positive
definite for `κ > 0`, so P1 is solved on the existing fv assembly and the
PCG/GAMG path (plan §2.5).

### 135.4 The Marshak wall, from SP-164's boundary condition

SP-164 eqs. (3-114)-(3-118): a grey diffuse wall with emissivity `ε` emits
and reflects, `q_o = ε σ T_w^4 + (1 - ε) q_i`. The P1 intensity of (3-117)
integrated over the outgoing hemisphere gives
`q_o = G/4 + q_n/2` (3-118), with `q_n` the net flux in the gas **away from
the wall**. Eliminate `q_i = q_o - q_n`:

```
q_n = 2ε/(2 - ε) (σ T_w^4 - G/4)  =  ε/(2(2 - ε)) (4σT_w^4 - G)                 (135.9)
```

That is SP-164 eq. (3-120) written in `G`. In this document's convention
**`n` is the outward unit normal of the medium** (pointing into the wall),
the convention of every boundary face in this crate. Then `q·n = -q_n`, and
with (135.7) the Robin condition on `G` is:

```
- Γ n·∇G = ε / (2(2 - ε)) (G - 4 σ T_w^4)          (n outward from the medium)   (135.10)
```

**A correction to the plan's sign.** The CHEMRAD plan wrote
`-Gamma n.grad G = eps/(2(2 - eps)) (4 sigma T_w^4 - G)`. That holds for an
**inward** normal. With this crate's outward face normals it is (135.10). A
cold wall (`T_w = 0`) must take energy out of the medium (`q·n > 0`), and
(135.10) gives `q·n = ε G/(2(2 - ε)) > 0`. The plan's sign would make a cold
wall heat the gas.

(135.10) is a §4 triple rewrite on `G` (Robin), which is docs/17 §5.2's first
rule for a new BC. Its names are `MarshakRadiation` (wall `T_w` from the wall's `T`
patch value) and `MarshakRadiationFixedTemperature` (a stated `T_w`). CHR-23
registers both (docs/17 §12.2 correction 5).

### 135.5 The P1 slab closed form (derived; CHR-18's gate)

Take a slab `0 <= x <= L`, isothermal at `T`, with uniform `κ`, `σ_s` and
`A_1`, and walls at `T_w` and `ε` on both sides. By symmetry,
`G = 4σT^4 + C cosh(m (x - L/2))` with `m^2 = κ/Γ`. Apply (135.10) at `x = 0`,
where `n = -x̂` gives `-Γ n·∇G = Γ G'(0)`. With `h = mL/2`,
`a = ε/(2(2 - ε))`, `g = Γ m` and `ΔE = σ(T^4 - T_w^4)`:

```
C = - 4 a ΔE / (a cosh h + g sinh h)
q·n |wall = - g C sinh h
Ψ_P1 = q·n / ΔE = 4 a g tanh h / (a + g tanh h)                                  (135.11)
g = ((1 - ω) / (3 - ω A_1))^(1/2),       h = ((1 - ω)(3 - ω A_1))^(1/2) τ / 2,   τ = β L
```

With `ω = 0` and black walls (`a = 1/2`, `g = 1/√3`, `h = √3 τ/2`), this is
`Ψ_P1 = 4 tanh h / (√3 + 2 tanh h)`. Its thin limit is `2τ`, the same as
(135.6)'s. Its thick limit is `4/(2 + √3) = 1.0718`, where the exact value is
1. **That 7 % is P1's own error, not a discretisation error**, and the plan
reports it rather than gating it.

(135.11) was checked here against a direct numerical solve of the P1
boundary-value problem (135.8) with (135.10) (scipy `solve_bvp`, tolerance
1e-12, a scratchpad probe of this unit and never part of the tree). The two
agree to 12 digits in all seven cases below.

| `ε` | `τ` (`ω = 0`) | `Ψ_P1` (135.11) | `Ψ_exact` (135.6), black only | `Ψ_P1/Ψ_exact - 1` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.1 | 0.181406101221 | 0.167417084183 | +8.36 % |
| 1 | 1 | 0.893523053720 | 0.780616065604 | +14.46 % |
| 1 | 10 | 1.071796739833 | 0.999992902475 | +7.18 % |
| 0.5 | 0.1 | 0.153551010980 | — | — |
| 0.5 | 1 | 0.471883905488 | — | — |
| 0.5 | 10 | 0.517327167876 | — | — |
| 1 | 1, `ω = 0.5`, `A_1 = 0.5` | 0.620331780315 | — | — |

**What CHR-18's gate measures, therefore.** The discrete P1 solution is
compared with (135.11), which is the exact solution of the **same** PDE. The
error is pure discretisation and must show order 2.0 ± 0.1 on two meshes
(§94). The P1-versus-exact difference of the table's last column is printed
and is not a gate row.

| `viewfactor_still_refuses_absorption` | §50.9 unchanged | refused | D |

| `p1_observed_order` | as above, §94's reporting | the same | P |
