## 138. SPMD transports — the `Comm` trait, ThreadComm, and MPI

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` This section is this project's own
contract (ORIGINAL). Its one external input is the MPI Forum's MPI-4.1 report,
read as a specification for what a message envelope, a buffered send, a
collective call and a tag bound mean. No MPI implementation's source was opened.

In an SPMD run every rank owns one part of the mesh and talks to the other
ranks only through a `Comm`. Every operation of a `Comm` moves bytes and does
no arithmetic on them, so a ghost cell still holds its owner's value bit for
bit whatever the transport, and §71-§73's bitwise gates stay valid for SPMD
runs. The collectives stay gathers and never become reductions, per §72.4.

This section defines no equation, so it carries no equation label.

### 138.1 The `Comm` contract and `ThreadComm`

`src/comm.rs` holds the object-safe trait `Comm` and its two constants.
`src/comm/thread.rs` holds `ThreadComm`. Both are host code on `std` alone: no
`Gpu`, no `Scalar`, no `unsafe`, no feature gate, so the default build and
`--features single` compile the same lines and every test of §138.1.5 holds in
both with the same expectations. Under `--features single` the same tests run
through `tests/comm_thread.rs`, which includes `src/comm/tests.rs`, because the
library's own test target does not compile in that build.

| name | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_TAG` | 32767 | the largest tag a caller may use; MPI-4.1 section 10.1.2.1 guarantees that `MPI_TAG_UB` is at least 32767, so a tag this transport accepts is valid on every MPI |
| `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` | 120 s | how long a `ThreadComm` call waits for a message before it fails by name |

The trait has `rank`, `size`, `transport` (a name), `barrier`, `exchange`,
`allgather`, `allgatherv` and `bcast`. Nothing else is in it, and nothing in
the crate calls it yet: the parallel stream's later units build on it.

#### 138.1.1 One code path, two transports

`ThreadComm` is the transport `cargo test` runs on a one-GPU machine with no
MPI: N ranks as N threads of one process, each holding its own handle. MPI is a
later transport behind the same trait (PAR-06, which adds its own subsection
here), so a program written against `Comm` is one code path and the transport
is a choice made where the world is built.

The in-process sequential path of §71-§73 stays as it is. It is the reference
that SPMD runs are compared with bitwise: a program that runs P ranks over a
`Comm` must produce the bytes the one-process, P-part run produces.

#### 138.1.2 Matching, order and progress — the ten rules

| rule | statement | rests on |
|---|---|---|
| R1 World | `rank()` is in `0..size()` and `size() >= 1`. Rank numbers are fixed for the life of the world. `size() == 1` is not a special case: every operation works with the one rank alone | MPI-4.1 section 7.1 |
| R2 Exchange: what each list means | `exchange(tag, sends, recvs)` sends `sends[i].1` to rank `sends[i].0` under `tag`, and fills each `recvs[j].1` with the message from rank `recvs[j].0` under `tag`. A peer may be the calling rank itself, and a message to self is delivered like any other. The order of entries in either list does not change any result | MPI-4.1 section 4.2.3 |
| R3 Exchange: matching | Messages are matched by the envelope `(src, dst, tag)`, and FIFO within one envelope: the k-th message rank a sends to rank b under tag t fills the k-th receive that b posts from a under t. Arrival order across different envelopes is never consulted | MPI-4.1 sections 4.2.3 and 4.5 |
| R4 Exchange: progress | Sends are buffered: the bytes are copied out before the call waits on anything. So `exchange` returns once every entry in `recvs` is filled and never waits for a receiver. With consistent lists there is no deadlock, whatever the peer counts and whatever order the ranks call in | MPI-4.1 section 4.5 |
| R5 Exchange: exact lengths | A received message's length must equal its buffer's length exactly. If it does not, the call fails, naming both lengths | stricter than MPI-4.1 section 4.5 |
| R6 Collectives | Every rank calls the collectives (`barrier`, `allgather`, `allgatherv`, `bcast`) in the same order. `ThreadComm` checks this: each call carries a per-rank collective sequence number, its kind and its parameters (the root for `bcast`, the block length for `allgather` and `bcast`). If any rank's call differs at the same sequence number, every rank fails, naming the sequence number and both differing values | MPI-4.1 section 7.14, checked here |
| R7 Collectives never match point-to-point messages | Collective traffic and `exchange` traffic are separate channels. No tag value, including `MAX_TAG`, can cross them | MPI-4.1 section 7.1 |
| R8 The four collectives | `barrier` returns on any rank only after every rank has entered it. `allgather`: every rank passes `mine` of the same length n and `all` of length `n * size()`; afterwards `all[q*n .. (q+1)*n]` is rank q's `mine`, on every rank. `allgatherv` returns `size()` vectors in rank order, entry q being rank q's `mine`; the lengths may differ, zero is allowed, and every rank receives identical vectors. `bcast`: every rank passes `buf` of the same length and the same `root`; afterwards every `buf` holds root's bytes, and root's own `buf` is unchanged | MPI-4.1 sections 7.3, 7.7 and 7.4 |
| R9 Local argument errors fail before anything is sent | a tag above `MAX_TAG`; a peer `>= size()`; a peer listed twice in `sends`, or twice in `recvs`; `all.len() != mine.len() * size()`; `root >= size()`. The other ranks are not told: if only one rank makes the mistake, the others may wait until their timeout | this contract |
| R10 After any `Err`, the world is spent | No later call on it is specified | this contract |

The contract is stricter than MPI in two places, both on purpose. **Exact
receive lengths (R5):** MPI accepts a message shorter than its receive buffer,
but a halo's length is known on both sides, so a short message is a bug, and it
is refused with both numbers. **Checked collective order (R6):** MPI makes a
mismatched collective sequence the program's error and leaves the outcome
undefined; `ThreadComm` is the test transport, so it turns the mistake into an
`Err` on every rank instead of mixed bytes or a hang.

#### 138.1.3 ThreadComm — buffered mailboxes, collective headers, timeout and abort

One `Mutex` and one `Condvar` guard a shared state of two mailbox maps and an
abort slot. Nothing in `ThreadComm` runs caller code while holding the lock.

* **Buffered sends, envelope-keyed FIFO mailboxes.** `exchange` copies every
  outgoing message into the map `(src, dst, tag) -> FIFO of messages` under the
  lock, wakes the waiters, and only then waits for its own receives, in list
  order. A receive pops the front of its envelope's queue, so a message is
  matched by what it says and never by when it arrived, and a rank that runs
  ahead cannot overtake itself (R3). A message to self goes through the same
  map.
* **A separate collective channel and its per-call header.** Every collective
  call takes the next per-rank sequence number and sends every other rank a
  header (its kind, its root and its block length) together with its bytes, in
  a second map keyed `(src, dst, sequence)`. A rank then reads every other
  rank's message in rank order and checks that header against its own, which
  is the R6 check on every rank: whichever rank looks, it sees the difference.
  Only a `bcast` root sends bytes; its peers send the header alone.
* **The timeout.** A wait for one message ends after the world's timeout,
  `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` = 120 s unless `world_with_timeout` chose another, with an
  `Err` naming the waiting rank, what it waited for (the peer and the tag, or
  the collective's sequence number) and the timeout in milliseconds. A message
  that arrives as the timeout expires is still delivered. A failed collective
  or a bad length does not abort the world: each rank that sees the problem
  fails on its own, and a rank whose call was fine returns `Ok`.
* **The abort.** `ThreadComm::run` catches each rank's panic, marks the world
  aborted naming that rank, and wakes every waiter. From then on every blocked
  or later call on any rank returns `Err` naming the aborted rank, without
  waiting for the timeout, and `run` returns `Err` naming the lowest panicking
  rank with the panic message when the payload is a string. A test that goes
  wrong therefore ends in a named failure, never a hang.
* **`MAX_TAG` = 32767.** MPI-4.1 section 10.1.2.1 requires the tag upper bound
  to be at least 32767 and lets an implementation offer more. Capping tags at
  the guaranteed minimum means a halo plan that works on `ThreadComm` cannot
  hold a tag some MPI refuses.

`world(n)` returns n handles, entry r being rank r; each handle is `Send` and
need not be `Sync`. It refuses `n == 0`, and `world_with_timeout` also refuses
a zero timeout. `run(n, f)` runs `f(&handle_r)` on n scoped threads and returns
the n results in rank order.

#### 138.1.4 Refused by name

Every failure is `Error::Config` and its message starts `comm: `.

| case | the message names |
|---|---|
| `world(0)` | `at least one rank` |
| zero timeout | `timeout` |
| tag above `MAX_TAG` | the tag (`32768`) and `32767` |
| peer out of range | the peer and the size, e.g. `peer 4` and `size 4` |
| peer twice in one list | `peer 1` and `twice` |
| received length differs | the rank, the tag, the received length and the buffer length, e.g. `rank 0`, `tag 2`, `10` and `12` |
| `allgather` wrong `all` length | both numbers (`97` and `96`) |
| `allgather` block lengths differ across ranks | the other rank, and both lengths (`23` and `24`) |
| `bcast` root out of range | `root 3` and `size 3` |
| `bcast` length differs | both lengths (`999` and `1000`) |
| different collective kinds | both kinds, e.g. `bcast` and `allgather`, and `collective #0` |
| different roots | `root` |
| a missing message | the waited-for peer (`rank 0`), the tag (`tag 4`) and the timeout (`200 ms`) |
| an aborted world | the panicking rank and `panicked`, e.g. `rank 2` |

#### 138.1.5 What must hold

Every row is class D: exact bytes and exact counts, nothing is a tolerance. The
payloads are SplitMix64 streams and the digests FNV-1a 64, so each rank can
compute what it should have received.

| test | what it asserts | class |
|---|---|---|
| T0 `the_test_generators_are_the_published_ones` | SplitMix64 from seed 0 gives the published first three outputs, FNV-1a 64 the published digests of `""`, `"a"`, `"foobar"`, and `payload(1,2,0,16)` its pinned bytes | D |
| T1 `allgather_returns_rank_order` | N = 1..8: every rank's `all` is the rank-order concatenation (N = 8: 192 bytes, pinned digest); exact bytes at N = 4; a wrong `all` length and mismatched block lengths are refused on every rank | D |
| T2 `allgatherv_ragged_lengths` | N = 1..8: entry q is rank q's block, every rank's result equals rank 0's; N = 8 lengths `[0,5,3,1,6,4,2,0]`, 21 bytes, pinned digest; N = 1 gives one empty entry | D |
| T3 `exchange_asymmetric_neighbour_lists_never_deadlock` | an uneven graph (rank 0 with no peer, rank 1 with five) under three tags and opposite list orders completes, every buffer is its payload, the N = 6 and N = 8 digests are pinned, under 10 s | D |
| T4 `exchange_is_byte_identity` | N = 1..8 all-to-all of 100000 bytes including to self, byte for byte; pinned digests for tag 7, tag 0 and `MAX_TAG` | D |
| T5 `bcast_from_every_root` | N = 1..8, every root: all buffers equal the root's, the root's own is unchanged, pinned digests; an out-of-range root and a length mismatch are refused on every rank | D |
| T6 `a_thousand_runs_produce_identical_bytes` | 1000 repetitions at N = 1..8 (8000 worlds, 36000 rank threads) of a six-operation program under scheduler jitter give the pinned `D(N)` and byte count every time, under 60 s in the release build | D |
| T7 `refusals_are_named` | the world, tag, peer and received-length refusals of §138.1.4 are each an `Error::Config` starting `comm: ` and naming what that table lists; the sending rank of a length mismatch returns `Ok` | D |
| T8 `collectives_and_point_to_point_never_cross` | ring exchanges (including tag `MAX_TAG` and a repeated tag) interleaved with every collective: no byte crosses between the channels | D |
| T9 `repeated_exchanges_never_overtake` | 200 consecutive exchanges under one tag with the sender running ahead arrive in order | D |
| T10 `mismatched_collectives_are_refused_by_name` | different kinds and different roots fail on every rank, naming both kinds and `collective #0`, or the root | D |
| T11 `a_panicking_rank_aborts_the_world_instead_of_hanging` | a panic before an `allgather` makes `run` return `Err` naming the rank and the panic message in under 5 s with the 120 s timeout | D |
| T12 `a_missing_message_times_out_by_name` | a receive nobody sends fails after at least 200 ms and under 5 s, naming the peer, the tag and `200 ms` | D |
| T13 `barrier_holds_every_rank` | N = 1..8, 50 rounds: no rank passes a barrier before all have entered | D |
| T14 `a_world_knows_its_ranks` | `rank`, `size` and `transport` of every handle, `run` returning results in rank order, and the trait used as `&dyn Comm` | D |

The program of T6 is: three exchange rounds (tags 0, 1, 2) over the uneven
graph, an `allgather` of 24-byte blocks, an `allgatherv` of `5r mod 7`-byte
blocks, and a `bcast` of 64 bytes from root `N-1`. Rank r yields the scheduler
`(rep*7 + r*3 + op) mod 5` times before operation `op`. `D(N)` is the digest of
every rank's received bytes concatenated in rank order.

| N | bytes | `D(N)` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 88 | `0x410f8f0a4284d037` |
| 2 | 234 | `0xb991fe33bbce0ec7` |
| 3 | 618 | `0x54c750f57eb6de7f` |
| 4 | 1270 | `0x1394b8a5e5356558` |
| 5 | 2117 | `0xca7aee5aa3e1b481` |
| 6 | 3132 | `0xf228d3ea2871ed1a` |
| 7 | 4018 | `0xa6096b18ace7f85e` |
| 8 | 4574 | `0xcaa0cded0010ae47` |

The values were computed by an independent Python oracle before the Rust ran.

  The plan row for PAR-01 cites "sections 3-6" for point-to-point and
  collective communication; those are MPI-4.0's chapter numbers. In the 4.1

  4.1 ones.

  *OOPSLA 2014*, DOI 10.1145/2660193.2660195, for the test generator.

### 138.3 The SPMD halo exchange

(§138.2 is reserved for the MPI transport, PAR-06.) ORIGINAL: this project's
own design, with no external source. It defines no equation.

§71.4's exchange has every part in one process and moves the packed cells with
a device-to-device copy. In an SPMD run a rank holds **one** part and cannot
read another rank's memory, so the move goes through the host and a `Comm`.
`src/halo/spmd.rs` holds `SpmdHalo`, built from one `PartMesh` and the number
of ranks. Rank r holds part r. One exchange of one field is five steps:

```
1. pack     sendBuf[k] = psi[sendIndex[k]]        the kernel of §71.4, unchanged
2. D2H      sendBuf -> a page-locked host buffer; then the stream is synchronised
3. Comm     exchange(HALO_TAG, sends, recvs):
              to   nbr[i]: the bytes of host send slice [send_offset[i], send_offset[i+1])
              from nbr[i]: the bytes of host receive slice [recv_offset[i], recv_offset[i+1])
4. H2D      the whole host receive buffer -> psi[n_cells .. n_cells + n_halo], ONE copy
5. sync     the stream is synchronised; on return no copy is pending
```

* **Still no unpack and no arithmetic.** The halo is ordered by (owning part,
  global cell id), so the neighbours' runs, in `nbr` order, are the halo itself:
  the receive buffer is the halo and step 4 is one contiguous copy. Steps 2-4
  are the identity on every byte and step 1 is a gather, so a ghost cell holds
  its owner's value bit for bit, on any transport that keeps §138.1's contract.
* **No handshake.** The lengths come from the plan (§71.4): what r sends to s is
  as long as what s expects from r. Every neighbour is in both lists, an empty
  slice included, so the two sides always post matching envelopes. R5 turns a
  plan that disagrees into a named error instead of mixed bytes.
* **One tag.** `HALO_TAG` = 71. Messages are FIFO within an envelope (R3) and
  every rank runs the same program, so consecutive exchanges of different
  fields under one tag cannot overtake each other.
* **Why two synchronisations.** This crate runs cudarc with event tracking off
  (`Gpu::new`), so a page-locked buffer does not wait for the copy that fills
  it. The copy of step 2 is asynchronous and the host must not read the bytes
  before it ends; the copy of step 4 reads the host buffer asynchronously, and
  the next exchange must not overwrite that buffer before it ends. Both waits
  are explicit. The page-locked buffers come from cudarc's `alloc_pinned`,
  which sets the write-combined flag: cudarc 0.19.9, the version `Cargo.lock`
  pins, offers no other. Write-combined memory is slow for the host to read,
  and the host reads the send buffer once, front to back, in step 3. That
  costs time and changes no byte. `alloc_pinned_with_flags` arrives in cudarc
  0.19.10; the send buffer moves to it when the lock file does, and PAR-16's
  measured exchange latency says how much it matters.
* **Not capturable.** Steps 2-5 are host round trips, so an SPMD exchange
  inside `Gpu::capture` is refused by name (§81.3). A captured region lies
  between two exchanges.
* Four payloads, as §71.4: `Scalar`, `Vec3`, `Tensor` and `Label`. A payload's
  bytes are its in-memory representation; all four are `#[repr(C)]` without
  padding (`types::tests::layout_matches_device`). Each payload has its own
  device send buffer and its own two host buffers, allocated once in `new`; an
  exchange allocates nothing on the device.

**Refused by name.** Every failure is `Error::Config` and its message starts
`halo: `.

| case | the message names |
|---|---|
| `new`: the part's number is not below the rank count | the part and the rank count, e.g. `part 2` and `2 ranks` |
| `new`: a neighbour is not below the rank count | the neighbour and the rank count |
| `new`: the offsets do not fit the neighbour list, or the send list's length is not where its offsets end | the lengths, as §71.4's in-process form does |
| `new`: the send or the receive offsets do not start at 0, or decrease, or the receive offsets do not end at `n_halo` | which list (`send offsets` or `receive offsets`), and `start at 0`, or `decrease` with the two entries, or where they end and the `halo cells` count |
| an exchange inside a capture | `capture` |
| `comm.size()` differs from the rank count given to `new` | both numbers and `ranks` |
| `comm.rank()` is not the part | `rank r` and `part p` |
| a field buffer shorter than `n_cells + n_halo` | the buffer's length, `n_cells`, `n_halo` (as `halo cells`) and the length it `must be` |

The checks run in that order and before anything is launched or sent.

**What must hold.** Class D: bytes. `tests/halo_spmd.rs` runs in both builds;
each rank is a `ThreadComm` thread with its own `Gpu` on device 0.

| test | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| **`an_spmd_halo_is_bit_for_bit_the_in_process_halo`** | **the gate.** Two `blockgen` boxes (`Big` 5×4×3 and 12×10×8), `P = 1..4`, three partitioners (Hilbert, linear, round robin), four payloads: every local cell of every rank, owned and ghost, equals bit for bit the in-process `HaloExchange` result and the owner's value. For `P > 1` every part has a halo, and the number of ghost cells compared is counted and positive |
| `two_spmd_exchanges_back_to_back_do_not_share_bytes` | two different scalar fields exchanged one after the other with no synchronisation in between, `P = 4`, round robin, 12×10×8: each field's ghosts hold that field's owner values |
| `an_spmd_halo_refuses_by_name` | the eight rows of the table above |
| `an_spmd_halo_crosses_a_cut_cyclic_couple` (library, f64 build) | a cyclic 5×4×3 box, `P = 2..4`, three partitioners, `Scalar` and `Tensor`: ghosts equal the owner's values and the in-process result; at least one of the cuts splits a cyclic couple |

**What this does not establish.** The ranks are threads of one process sharing
one device, so nothing here measures an exchange's latency (PAR-16) and nothing
runs over MPI (PAR-06). The first solver that calls `SpmdHalo` is §138.5's
`spmd_pcg`.

### 138.4 The SPMD exact reduction

ORIGINAL: this project's own design, with no external source. It defines no
equation: the limb decomposition is §72.2's, unchanged.

§72's `ExactReduction` holds every part in one process and gathers the per-part
results with a device-to-device copy (§72.4, step 1). In an SPMD run a rank
holds **one** part, so the gather goes through the host and `Comm::allgather`.
`src/exactsum/spmd.rs` holds `SpmdReduction`, built on one rank from a `Comm`
and the number of terms `n` the rank owns. The kernels are §72's own, and so is
the order of the gathered values: slot q of a gathered buffer is rank q's
value, as slot q was part q's.

```
set-up   new(gpu, comm, n):  allgather of the term counts (8 bytes each)

an exact reduction (sum, sum_mag, dot, norm_factor) on every rank:
1. the rank's own maximum of |t|          the stage-one and stage-two kernels of §72, unchanged
2. allgather  8 bytes: that maximum, widened to a double
3. solMaxStage2 over the P gathered maxima -> the global anchor      (§72.3)
4. the rank's own limbs against the global anchor; exCombine over its blocks
5. allgather  40 bytes: the rank's five limb words (i64)
6. exCombine over the P gathered limb sets, then exToScalar          (§72.4)

max_mag:        steps 1-3, and the anchor is the answer
gathered_*:     the rank's own two-stage partial, one allgather of 8 bytes,
                then solSumStage2 over the P gathered partials       (§72.5)
```

* **The collective is still a gather.** Steps 2 and 5 move bytes and do no
  arithmetic. Every combine runs on every rank, on the same P values in the
  same rank order, with the kernel the in-process form uses. So every rank
  holds the same answer, and it is the in-process answer bit for bit: for the
  exact reductions whatever part each rank holds, for `gathered_*` when rank q
  holds what part q held.
* **Two collectives for an exact reduction, one for a maximum or a gathered
  partial.** §72.3 shows why the anchor cannot ride with the limbs: the limbs
  are cut against the anchor, so the anchor must be global first.
  `n_allgathers()` counts the calls a handle has made, the one in `new`
  included.
* **The wire.** A value's bytes are its in-memory representation. The count is
  a `u64`. The maximum and the gathered partial travel as a double in both
  builds (§118.1): the rank's stage two stores a `Scalar`, and the host widens
  it, which is exact because every float is a double. The limbs travel as five
  `i64`: §72.2's four value limbs and the count of non-finite terms.
* **A rank that owns nothing** contributes a zero maximum, zero limbs and a
  zero partial, as an empty part does in §72.
* **The counts are checked once, by every rank alike.** `new` gathers the
  counts first and checks them afterwards, so every rank reaches the same
  refusal and none is left waiting in a collective. `counts()` returns them in
  rank order.
* **Host round trips.** Each collective is one device-to-host copy and one
  host-to-device copy of at most 40 bytes per rank. Both go through pageable
  memory, which the driver completes before the call returns, so there is no
  separate wait as in §138.3. A reduction allocates nothing on the device.
* **Not capturable.** A reduction inside `Gpu::capture` is refused by name
  (§81.3). In one process `ExactReduction` stays the capturable form.

**Refused by name.** Every failure is `Error::Config` and its message starts
`exactsum: `.

| case | the message names |
|---|---|
| `new`: a rank's count does not fit a `Label` | `rank q` and its count, on every rank |
| `new`: the counts sum to more than `EXACT_MAX_TERMS` | the sum and the limit (§72.2), on every rank |
| a reduction inside a capture | `capture` |
| `comm.size()` differs from the rank count seen by `new` | both numbers and `ranks` |
| `comm.rank()` is not the rank `new` ran on | both ranks |
| a buffer shorter than `n` | the buffer's name and length, and `n` |

The last four are checked in that order, before anything is launched or sent.
A short buffer is one rank's fault and the other ranks cannot see it: after
any `Err` the world is spent (R10).

**What must hold.** Class D: bytes. `tests/exactsum_spmd.rs` runs in both
builds; each rank is a `ThreadComm` thread with its own `Gpu` on device 0.

| test | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| **`spmd_exact_reduction_is_the_in_process_one`** | **the gate.** 20,011 terms of full mantissa spread over 100 binades, `P = 1..4`, four dealings (contiguous, round robin, shuffled, and one with an empty part), every rotation of the rank labels (rank r holds part (r + k) mod P): on every rank `sum`, `sum_mag`, `dot`, `norm_factor` and `max_mag` equal the in-process `ExactReduction` by bits, by limbs and by anchor, and equal the one-part answer; `gathered_sum`, `gathered_dot`, `gathered_sum_mag` and `gathered_norm_factor` equal the in-process gathered answer for the same part order. 1,071 answers are compared, and each handle has made 14 allgathers |
| `an_spmd_reduction_counts_a_non_finite_term_on_every_rank` | one NaN and one infinity on different ranks, `P = 3`: `sum` is NaN on every rank and `non_finite_terms` is 2 on every rank |
| `an_spmd_reduction_refuses_by_name` | the six rows of the table above |

**What this does not establish.** Nothing here measures the latency of an
allgather (PAR-16) and nothing runs over MPI (PAR-06). The first solver that
calls `SpmdReduction` is §138.5's `spmd_pcg`.

### 138.5 The SPMD PCG

ORIGINAL: this project's own design, with no external source. It defines no
equation: the recurrence is §73.2's (Hestenes & Stiefel 1952, as §8 cites it),
unchanged.

§73's `dist_pcg` holds every part in one process. In an SPMD run a rank holds
**one** part, so the solve is the same program on every rank with §73's two
cross-part steps moved onto the transports of §138.3 and §138.4.
`src/distsolve/spmd.rs` holds it:

* `DistSystem::split_one(gpu, halo, comm, m, dec, a)` builds the rank's
  one-part system: part `comm.rank()` of `dec`, its mesh and its split matrix
  (§71.6), uploaded. As in `DistSystem::split`, the two constraint arrays reach
  the halo through the exchange, `is_fixed` first and `fixed_value` second, here
  through `SpmdHalo`. `rank_part()` answers `Some(part)` for such a system and
  `None` for one from `split`.
* `SpmdWorkspace::new(gpu, comm, sys, reduce)` allocates the rank's Krylov
  vectors, each `n_cells + n_halo` long, and its `SpmdReduction`. It is a
  collective (§138.4's count allgather), so every rank builds it at the same
  point of the program.
* `spmd_pcg(gpu, sol, comm, psi, sys, halo, w, ctrl)` runs the solve and
  returns §73's `DistPerformance`.

```
the same program on every rank r, on its own part:
  r = b - A psi ;  z = M^-1 r ;  p = z ;  rho = (r,z)
  repeat
      SpmdHalo::scalar(p) ;  q = A p              the one exchange (§73.2, §138.3)
      alpha  = rho / (p,q)                        SpmdReduction (§138.4)
      psi   += alpha p ;  r -= alpha q
      [ sum|r| ; convergence test ; read the flag ; vote ]
      z      = M^-1 r
      rho'   = (r,z) ;  beta = rho'/rho ;  p = z + beta p ;  rho = rho'
```

* **The kernels and their order are `dist_pcg`'s for one part.** Every launch
  on a rank is the launch `dist_pcg` makes for that part, with the same
  arguments and the same launch geometry; the exchange is `SpmdHalo::scalar`
  where `dist_pcg` calls `HaloExchange::scalar`, and each reduction is the
  `SpmdReduction` method where `dist_pcg` calls the `ExactReduction` one. §138.3
  and §138.4 make those two bit for bit the in-process forms, so every rank's
  field is bit for bit `dist_pcg`'s field for its part, and with the exact
  reduction and `Diagonal` or `None` it is the one-part field, hence the serial
  solver's (§73.8).
* **The mean still divides by the whole mesh's cell count** (§73.4), which the
  system carries from the decomposition.
* **Every rank decides alone, and every rank decides alike.** The residual sum
  and the normalisation factor are global values with the same bits on every
  rank, and the convergence test is one kernel on those values, so every rank's
  flag is the same and no rank has to be told to stop. The **flag vote** checks
  this instead of trusting it: after each read of the flag, the ranks allgather
  one byte each (the rank's flag, 0 or 1), and a rank that sees two different
  votes refuses by name. The vote is a collective, so every rank must have it
  switched the same way. It is on by default in a debug build and off in a
  release build (`SpmdWorkspace::set_flag_vote`); `n_flag_votes()` counts the
  votes taken. A solve to a tolerance that stops after `k` iterations with
  `check_interval` 1 takes `k + 1` votes. A `fixed_iters` solve reads no flag
  and takes none.
* **The counts are §73.8's.** At `k` fixed iterations a rank makes `k + 3`
  exchanges and `2k + 5` reductions. With the exact reduction each reduction is
  two allgathers and with the gathered one it is one (§138.4), so the handle
  counts `1 + 2 (2k + 5)` or `1 + (2k + 5)` allgathers, `new`'s included. A
  vote is one more allgather on the `Comm` and is counted by `n_flag_votes()`
  alone.
* **Both reductions.** `DistReduce::Exact` is partition-invariant.
  `DistReduce::Gathered` is `dist_pcg`'s gathered answer when rank q holds part
  q, and is run-invariant only (§72.5).
  `SpmdWorkspace::partition_invariant` answers as
  `DistWorkspace::partition_invariant` does.
* **Preconditioners.** `Diagonal` and `None`, and, once the workspace is
  coloured, the block-local `Dic` and `Dilu` of §138.6. On an uncoloured
  workspace `Dic` and `Dilu` are refused by name.
* **Not capturable.** Every exchange and every collective is a host round trip
  (§138.3, §138.4), so `spmd_pcg` inside `Gpu::capture` is refused by name
  (§81.3).

**Refused by name.** A failure of `split_one`, of `SpmdWorkspace::new` or of
`DistWorkspace::new` is `Error::Config` starting `distsolve: `. A failure of
`spmd_pcg` is `Error::Config` starting `spmd_pcg: `, except the last row,
which is §13.4's `Error::Refused`.

| case | the message names |
|---|---|
| `split_one`: `comm.size()` differs from the decomposition's part count | both numbers and `ranks` |
| `split_one`: the halo plan is not this rank's part, or was built for another rank count | `rank r` and `part p`, or both rank counts |
| `SpmdWorkspace::new`: the system is not from `split_one` | `DistSystem::split_one` |
| `SpmdWorkspace::new`: `comm.rank()` is not the system's part | `rank r` and `part p` |
| `DistWorkspace::new`: the system is from `split_one` | `SpmdWorkspace` |
| `spmd_pcg` inside a capture | `capture` |
| `spmd_pcg`: the system is not from `split_one` | `DistSystem::split_one` |
| `spmd_pcg`: `comm.size()` differs from the rank count the workspace saw | both numbers and `ranks` |
| `spmd_pcg`: `comm.rank()` is not the system's part | `rank r` and `part p` |
| `spmd_pcg`: the workspace was built for another system | the owned and halo cell counts of both |
| `spmd_pcg`: the halo plan's cell counts are not the system's | the owned and halo cell counts of both |
| `spmd_pcg`: a solution buffer shorter than `n_cells + n_halo` | the buffer's length, the length it must have, the owned and the halo cell counts, and `lduAmul` |
| `spmd_pcg`: the flag vote disagrees | `flag` and every rank's vote in rank order, on every rank |
| `spmd_pcg`: `Dic` or `Dilu` on an uncoloured workspace | the setting, the value, `diagonal` and `SpmdWorkspace::colour` |

The `spmd_pcg` rows are checked in that order, the vote excepted, and before
anything is launched or sent. A refusal that only one rank can see leaves the
other ranks waiting in a collective: after any `Err` the world is spent (R10).

**What must hold.** Class D: bytes. Each rank is a `ThreadComm` thread with its
own `Gpu` on device 0.

| test | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| **`an_spmd_pcg_is_the_in_process_pcg`** (library, f64 build) | **the gate.** §73.8's 5×4×3 box, plain and with a cyclic couple, `P = 1..4`, three partitioners (Hilbert, linear, round robin; linear alone at `P = 1`), `Diagonal` and `None`, the exact reduction, solved to `1e-12` with the flag vote on: on every rank every owned cell equals bit for bit `dist_pcg`'s field for that part and the one-part field, and the iteration count, the exchange count, the reduction count, the two residuals' bits and `converged` equal `dist_pcg`'s. Every rank took `n_iterations + 1` votes and none disagreed. 112 rank results and 2,400 cells are compared |
| `an_spmd_pcg_is_the_in_process_pcg_in_both_builds` (`tests/distsolve_spmd.rs`) | the same comparison in both precisions on two `blockgen` boxes (`Big` 5×4×3 and 8×6×5), `Diagonal` and `None`, the exact reduction, and, on the 5×4×3 box with `Diagonal` at `P = 2..4`, the gathered reduction against `dist_pcg`'s gathered answer for the same parts. 139 rank results and 6,540 cells are compared. The solver tolerance is `1e-12` in the f64 build and `1e-5` in the f32 build; it is a solver control and not a gate tolerance, and every comparison is exact |
| `an_spmd_pcg_counts_its_exchanges_and_collectives` | 5 fixed iterations, `P = 3`: every rank makes 8 exchanges, 15 reductions and no vote; the handle counts 31 allgathers with the exact reduction and 16 with the gathered one |
| `an_spmd_flag_vote_names_a_disagreement` | `P = 2`, one rank given a tolerance it meets at once: both ranks are refused with `flag` and both votes |
| `an_spmd_pcg_refuses_by_name` | the other rows of the table above |

**What this does not establish.** The ranks are threads of one process sharing
one device, so nothing here is a speed-up (PAR-16) and nothing runs over MPI
(PAR-06). PBiCGStab and the block-local `Dic`/`Dilu` on a rank are §138.6.
`split_one` still cuts a matrix assembled on the whole mesh, on the host; a
rank that assembles its own part is PAR-10's.

### 138.6 The SPMD PBiCGStab, and the block-local DIC and DILU on a rank

ORIGINAL: this project's own design, with no external source. It defines no
equation. The recurrence is §73's `dist_pbicgstab` (van der Vorst 1992, as §8
cites it), and the factorisation is §21's, applied to one part's own
submatrix as §73.5 describes. Both are unchanged.

§138.5 put `dist_pcg` on a rank. This section does the same for the two things
§138.5 left out. `src/distsolve/spmd.rs` holds them:

* `spmd_pbicgstab(gpu, sol, comm, psi, sys, halo, w, ctrl)` runs
  `dist_pbicgstab` for the rank's one part and returns §73's
  `DistPerformance`. It takes the system, the halo plan and the workspace
  `spmd_pcg` takes.
* `SpmdWorkspace::colour(gpu, sys)` colours the rank's own part, so that `Dic`
  and `Dilu` become available to both solvers. `colours()` gives the colour
  count, and 0 before `colour`.
* `SpmdWorkspace::effective_preconditioner(requested)` answers as
  `DistWorkspace::effective_preconditioner` does (§13.4).
* `spmd_solve(gpu, sol, comm, psi, sys, halo, w, ctrl)` dispatches on
  `ctrl.solver` as `dist_solve` does. `GAMG` is refused by name, with
  `PBiCGStab` as the alternative. (Amended by §141.11: `GAMG` runs `spmd_gamg`, the
  distributed cycle on its own, when a cycle is attached, and is refused by name, with
  `PCG` and `PBiCGStab` named, without one.)

```
the same program on every rank r, on its own part:
  r = b - A psi ;  r0 = r ;  p = 0 ;  v = 0 ;  rho_old = alpha = omega = 1
  repeat
      rho   = (r0,r)                              SpmdReduction (§138.4)
      beta  = (rho/rho_old)(alpha/omega)
      p     = r + beta (p - omega v)
      pHat  = M^-1 p
      SpmdHalo::scalar(pHat) ;  v = A pHat        exchange 1 (§73.2, §138.3)
      alpha = rho / (r0,v)                        SpmdReduction
      s     = r - alpha v
      sHat  = M^-1 s
      SpmdHalo::scalar(sHat) ;  t = A sHat        exchange 2
      omega = (t,s) / (t,t)                       two SpmdReductions
      psi  += alpha pHat + omega sHat ;  r = s - omega t ;  rho_old = rho
      [ sum|r| ; convergence test ; read the flag ; vote ]
```

* **The kernels and their order are `dist_pbicgstab`'s for one part.** The
  rule is §138.5's: every launch on a rank is the launch `dist_pbicgstab`
  makes for that part, with the same arguments and the same launch geometry.
  The exchange is `SpmdHalo::scalar` and each reduction is the `SpmdReduction`
  method of the same name. So every rank's field is bit for bit
  `dist_pbicgstab`'s field for its part. With the exact reduction and
  `Diagonal` or `None` it is also the one-part field, and the ranks stop on
  the one-part iteration (§73.8).
* **`(t,s)` and `(t,t)` stay two reductions**, as in `dist_pbicgstab`
  (§73.8's first row is the proof that this equals the serial solver's fused
  pair).
* **The mean, the flag and the vote are §138.5's.** The mean divides by the
  whole mesh's cell count. Every rank reads its own flag, and the flag vote,
  when it is on, follows each read. A solve that stops after `k` iterations
  with `check_interval` 1 takes `k + 1` votes.
* **The counts are §73.8's.** At `k` fixed iterations a rank makes `2k + 3`
  exchanges and `4k + 4` reductions with PBiCGStab, and `k + 3` and `2k + 5`
  with PCG. The handle counts `1 + 2 (4k + 4)` allgathers with the exact
  reduction and `1 + (4k + 4)` with the gathered one, `new`'s included. A
  preconditioner changes none of these numbers, because no preconditioner
  here exchanges or reduces.
* **Block-local `Dic` and `Dilu`.** `SpmdWorkspace::colour` builds
  `MultiColour::new` on the rank's part mesh, which is what
  `DistWorkspace::colour` builds for that part. The colouring is greedy in the
  part's local cell order, so it is the same colouring. The factorisation and
  the two sweeps then walk the part's own faces only, and a cut face is absent
  from them (§73.5). So a rank's factorisation is bit for bit the in-process
  block-local one for its part, and the solve that uses it is bit for bit
  `dist_pcg`'s or `dist_pbicgstab`'s with the same preconditioner.
* **It is still not partition-invariant.** The preconditioner is a different
  one for every cut (§73.5), so `SpmdWorkspace::partition_invariant` answers
  `false` for `Dic` and `Dilu`, and the answer is not the one-part answer.
* **Every rank must colour alike.** `colour` is local: it sends nothing. A
  world in which only some ranks coloured would refuse on the others, and
  after any `Err` the world is spent (§138.5).
* **Not capturable**, for §138.5's reason: `spmd_pbicgstab` and `spmd_solve`
  inside `Gpu::capture` are refused by name (§81.3).

**Refused by name.** `spmd_pbicgstab` checks §138.5's `spmd_pcg` rows, in the
same order and before anything is launched or sent, and its messages start
`spmd_pbicgstab: `. The flag vote's refusal starts with the name of the solver
that took the vote. The rows that are new or changed:

| case | the message names |
|---|---|
| `SpmdWorkspace::colour`: the system is not from `split_one` | starts `distsolve: `; `DistSystem::split_one` |
| `SpmdWorkspace::colour`: the system's part is not the workspace's rank | starts `distsolve: `; `rank r` and `part p` |
| `SpmdWorkspace::colour`: the system's cell counts are not the workspace's | starts `distsolve: `; the owned and halo cell counts of both |
| `spmd_pcg` or `spmd_pbicgstab`: `Dic` or `Dilu` on an uncoloured workspace | §13.4's `Error::Refused`: the setting, the value, `diagonal` and `SpmdWorkspace::colour` |
| `spmd_solve`: `GAMG` without a cycle (§141.11) | starts `spmd_gamg: `; `solver`, `GAMG`, `SpmdWorkspace::set_gamg` and `PBiCGStab` |

**What must hold.** Class D: bytes and counts. Each rank is a `ThreadComm`
thread with its own `Gpu` on device 0. The solver tolerance is `1e-12` in the
f64 build and `1e-5` in the f32 build; it is a solver control and not a gate
tolerance, and every comparison is exact.

| test | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| **`an_spmd_pbicgstab_is_the_in_process_pbicgstab`** (library, f64 build) | **the gate.** §138.5's gate with `spmd_pbicgstab` against `dist_pbicgstab`: the 5×4×3 box, plain and cyclic, `P = 1..4`, three partitioners, `Diagonal` and `None`, the exact reduction, the flag vote on. Every owned cell equals bit for bit the in-process part's and the one-part field's; the iteration, exchange and reduction counts, both residuals' bits and `converged` equal the in-process solve's; every rank took `n_iterations + 1` votes. 112 rank results and 2,400 cells are compared |
| `an_spmd_block_local_factorisation_is_the_in_process_one` (library, f64 build) | the same boxes and cuts with PCG + `Dic` and PBiCGStab + `Dilu`, both sides coloured: every owned cell, every counter and both residuals' bits equal the in-process block-local solve's, each rank's colour count equals the in-process part's, and `partition_invariant` is `false` on every rank. 112 rank results and 2,400 cells are compared |
| `an_spmd_pbicgstab_is_the_in_process_pbicgstab_in_both_builds` (`tests/distsolve_spmd.rs`) | §138.5's both-builds comparison with PBiCGStab, the gathered leg included. 139 rank results and 6,540 cells are compared |
| `an_spmd_block_local_factorisation_is_the_in_process_one_in_both_builds` | the two `blockgen` boxes, PCG + `Dic` and PBiCGStab + `Dilu`, `P = 1..4`, the exact reduction: the comparison of the library test, in both precisions. 112 rank results and 6,000 cells are compared. On the 8×6×5 box at `P >= 2` with `Dic`, at least one rank's field differs from the one-part `Dic` field, so "not partition-invariant" is measured and not assumed |
| `an_spmd_pbicgstab_counts_its_exchanges_and_collectives` | 5 fixed iterations, `P = 3`. PBiCGStab with `Diagonal` and with `Dilu`: 13 exchanges, 24 reductions, no vote, and 49 allgathers with the exact reduction or 25 with the gathered one. PCG with `Dic`: 8 exchanges, 15 reductions, 31 or 16 allgathers |
| `an_spmd_flag_vote_names_a_disagreement` | extended to both solvers: each message starts with its solver's name |
| `an_spmd_pbicgstab_refuses_by_name` | the `spmd_pcg` rows of §138.5 with the `spmd_pbicgstab: ` prefix, and the three `colour` rows |
| `an_spmd_solve_dispatches_and_refuses_gamg` | 3 fixed iterations in a one-rank world: `spmd_solve` makes 6 exchanges for PCG and 9 for PBiCGStab, and refuses `GAMG` with the setting, the value and `PBiCGStab` |

**What this does not establish.** §138.5's limits hold: threads of one process
on one device, no speed-up, no MPI. The block-local iteration counts on the
shipped meshes are §73.5's and are not re-measured here, because a rank's
solve is the in-process solve bit for bit. No pressure backend runs on a rank
yet (PAR-10b).

### 138.7 Ranks placed on devices

ORIGINAL: this project's own design (docs/17 PAR-05), with no external source.
It defines no numerical equation, only the rule below. `src/comm/placement.rs`
holds the rule and `src/device.rs` opens the device.

**The rule.** Rank `r` of an SPMD world uses device

    device(r) = L[r mod |L|]

where `L` is the list `0, 1, ..., n - 1` over the `n` devices the driver sees,
unless the environment variable `OFGPU_DEVICES` gives the list. Its value is
a comma-separated list of device ordinals. Entries are trimmed, and an ordinal
may appear more than once. So four ranks on one device all use device 0. Four
ranks on two devices use 0, 1, 0, 1. `OFGPU_DEVICES=1` puts every rank on
device 1, and `OFGPU_DEVICES=0,0,1` puts two ranks in three on device 0.

* `Placement::new(device_count, devices: Option<&str>)` builds the list.
  `Placement::from_env(device_count)` reads `OFGPU_DEVICES` (unset means no
  override). `Placement::device_of(rank)` applies the rule. The module is host
  only, so it is tested with faked counts.
* `Gpu::device_count()` is the driver's count. `Gpu::for_rank(&placement,
  rank)` opens `Gpu::new(placement.device_of(rank))`. `Gpu::ordinal()` names
  the device a `Gpu` is on.

**One `Gpu` per rank, event tracking off.** Every rank thread opens its own
`Gpu`. `CudaContext::new` returns a new handle on the device's primary context
each call, with its own event-tracking flag, and `Gpu::new` switches that flag
off before its first allocation and creates one non-blocking stream (§81.3
needs both). So four ranks on device 0 have four handles on one context and
four streams, and nothing orders work across the streams. The safety rule that
makes this correct is on `Gpu`: **a buffer belongs to the `Gpu` that allocated
it, and is passed only to that `Gpu`'s methods and kernels.** The SPMD path
keeps it by construction. Each rank builds its halo, system, workspace and
fields from its own `Gpu`, and every byte that crosses ranks goes through the
`Comm` in host memory (§138.3). `Gpu::owns(&buf)` (the buffer's stream is
this `Gpu`'s) answers the question for any one buffer. CHR-18's fixture broke
the rule once by uploading on one `Gpu` and launching on another, and
compute-sanitizer reported an illegal address. `Gpu::event_tracking()` reads
the flag back.

**Refused by name.** Every message starts `placement: `.

| case | the message names |
|---|---|
| a device count of 0 | `the device count is 0` |
| `OFGPU_DEVICES` set but empty or blank | `OFGPU_DEVICES`, `empty`, and the default `r mod n` |
| an empty entry (`0,,1`) | the entry's position and the value |
| an entry that is not an ordinal (`a`, `-1`, `1.5`) | the position, the entry and `not a device ordinal` |
| an ordinal `>= n` | the position, the ordinal, the count and the range `0..n-1` |
| a value that is not UTF-8 | `OFGPU_DEVICES` |
| `Gpu::for_rank`: a placed device the driver does not have | the rank, the device and the driver's count |

**What must hold.** Class D: bytes and counts, in both builds
(`tests/comm_placement.rs`).

| test | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| **`placement_maps_ranks_to_devices`** | at faked counts 1, 2, 4 and 8, ranks 0..31 go to `r mod n` (128 ranks checked). The overrides `1`, `3,1`, ` 0 , 2 `, `0,0,1` and `7,...,0` cycle as listed. The nine refusal rows each name what they refuse |
| **`four_ranks_on_one_device_run_concurrently`** | a one-device placement puts a `ThreadComm` world of 4 on device 0. On the 5×4×3 and 8×6×5 boxes, with `Diagonal` and `None` and three partitioners (12 worlds), every rank is on ordinal 0 with event tracking off. The four rank streams and the main thread's stream are five distinct streams. Each rank's field is owned by its own `Gpu` and not by the main one. The last rank's solve starts before the first rank's solve ends, so the four solves overlap in time. §138.5's comparison holds bit for bit: every owned cell equals the in-process `dist_pcg` part and the one-part answer, the counters and both residuals' bits are equal, and every rank took `n_iterations + 1` votes. 48 rank results and 1,800 cells are compared |
| `for_rank_refuses_a_device_the_driver_lacks` | a placement built for one device more than the driver sees, with `OFGPU_DEVICES` naming that device: `Gpu::for_rank` refuses it, naming the rank, the device and the driver's count |
| `peer_placement_two_devices` (`#[ignore = "needs 2 GPUs"]`) | ranks 0 and 1 on devices 0 and 1, then swapped by `OFGPU_DEVICES=1,0`, three partitioners: the same comparison against the in-process solve on device 0 (12 rank results). **Written and not run**: this machine has one GPU. The bits match only on two devices of the same architecture (the same SASS) |

**What this does not establish.** No run on two devices has been made, so the
two-device placement is untested. The halo still goes through host memory and
does not use peer-to-peer copies. Running ranks concurrently on one device
gives no speed-up claim: the ranks share one GPU and its context.

### 138.8 The parallel driver `ofgpu-par`

ORIGINAL: this project's own design (docs/17 PAR-07), with no external source.
It defines no equation. `src/bin/par.rs` is the driver and
`tests/par_driver.rs` its test.

```
ofgpu-par <case> [-np 2,3,4] [-comm threads] [-method all] [-sweeps N] [-alpha A] [-quiet]
```

`ofgpu-decompose` (§71.9, §72.9, §73.9) holds every part in one process.
`ofgpu-par` runs the same three gates SPMD, as a decomposed solve will run. One
`ThreadComm` world is built per (rank count, partitioner), and every rank does
all of the following itself:

1. It opens `Gpu::for_rank(&placement, r)`, with
   `Placement::from_env(Gpu::device_count()?)` (§138.7).
2. It computes the partition map with `partition` and rotates it,
   `r -> (r + shift) mod P`, for every `shift` in `0..P`. It builds its own
   `Decomposition::from_map` and holds part `r` only.
3. It runs every gate below at every rotation. Every byte that crosses ranks
   goes through the `Comm` (§138.3, §138.4, §138.5).

The partitioners are Hilbert, linear and round robin (`c mod P`). The matrices,
the fields and the sweep pipeline are `ofgpu-decompose`'s, unchanged, so the two
drivers gate the same systems. The whole-mesh references are computed once, on
the main thread, on rank 0's device.

| gate | what each rank does | passes when |
|---|---|---|
| MAP | it hashes the rotated map with 64-bit FNV-1a, over `P` as a little-endian u64 and then every label's little-endian bytes, and allgathers the 8 bytes | every rank received P equal hashes, equal to the main thread's hash of the same map |
| HALO | (a) it fills a `Scalar`, a `Vec3`, a `Tensor` and a `Label` field from the global cell id, poisons the ghosts, and runs one `SpmdHalo` exchange per payload; (b) it runs §71.8's pipeline: `split_matrix` of the pinned Laplacian, `is_fixed` and `fixed_value` through the exchange, relax, `set_values`, the fold, `1/diag`, then `-sweeps` Jacobi sweeps (default 8), with an exchange before each | (a) every local cell, owned and ghost, holds the value at its global id; (b) every owned cell equals the undecomposed run |
| REDUCTION | `SpmdReduction` `sum` and `dot` of (swept field, `V`) and of §72's adversarial field with `V`, with the halo poisoned | the four values equal the whole mesh's `ExactReduction` |
| KRYLOV | `spmd_solve` with PCG and with PBiCGStab, `Diagonal` and `DistReduce::Exact`, flag vote on, on §73.8's SPD Poisson plus `ddt` | every owned cell equals the whole mesh's `dist_solve` answer, and every rank stopped on the whole mesh's iteration |

Every comparison is `to_bits()` equality. The HALO and Krylov lines report the
number of cells that differ and the worst `|d|`, so `worst == 0` is the pass, and
the REDUCTION line reports how many values moved. The solver
tolerance is a solver control and not a gate tolerance. It is 1e-10 in f64,
`ofgpu-decompose`'s value, and 1e-5 under `--features single`,
`tests/distsolve_spmd.rs`'s value. `rel_tol` is 0 and `max_iter` is 600. If the
whole-mesh reference does not converge, the driver refuses to run, because the
gate would have no reference. The exit status is 0 only when every gate at every
rotation passes. The last line is `ofgpu-par: PASS - ...` or
`ofgpu-par: FAIL - ...`.

**The MPI half waits for PAR-06.** The docs/17 row asks for `-comm threads|mpi`
and for auto-detection of `PMI_RANK`/`PMI_SIZE` under `mpiexec`. The user
deferred the MS-MPI install, so PAR-06 (§138.2, `MpiComm`) is not in the tree.
Until it lands, only `-comm threads` is built. The driver refuses, by name and
before the case is read or a device is opened:

| case | the message names |
|---|---|
| `-comm mpi` | `-comm mpi`, that the MPI transport is `deferred (PAR-06)` and not built, and `-comm threads` |
| `PMI_RANK` or `PMI_SIZE` in the environment, whatever `-comm` says | the variable, `mpiexec`, `deferred (PAR-06)`, and to run one process with `-comm threads`. Under `mpiexec`, every process would otherwise run a whole threads world of its own |
| any other `-comm` | the value and the known transport `threads` |
| `-np` with a 0 or a non-number | the value, and `at least 1` for a 0 |

`-np` above the cell count and an unknown `-method` are refused by value after
the case is read and before a device is opened. An unknown option is refused by
name while the arguments are parsed.

When PAR-06 lands, `-comm mpi` (and the PMI detection) runs `rank_body` once per
process over `MpiComm`. That rank body is unchanged, because each rank already
computes its own map and decomposition. The MAP gate is the check that makes this
safe, since separate processes do not share the map.

**What must hold.** Class D: bytes and counts, in both builds.

| test | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| **the row gate**, `ofgpu-par cases/plume.jsonc -np 2,3,4 -comm threads` | 9 worlds and 27 rotations, all PASS, with `worst == 0` and the whole mesh's iteration count. Measured 2026-10-14 on the RTX 5070 Ti: f64 in 28.7 s wall, with PCG at 125 and PBiCGStab at 79 iterations to 1e-10 at every P, partitioner and rotation; single in 8.9 s, with PCG at 49 and PBiCGStab at 32 iterations to 1e-5. The tree has the tracked `cases/plume.jsonc` (98×42×20 = 82,320 cells). The `cases/plume` that the row names is not a tracked case |
| **`par_threads_gates_pass_on_a_small_plume`** | the same run on `cases/plume.jsonc` at 28×12×5: 27 MAP, HALO, REDUCTION, PCG and PBiCGStab PASS lines each, no FAIL, the verdict `9 worlds, 27 rotations`, and ghost cells compared on every HALO line |
| `par_refuses_mpi_by_name` | `-comm mpi` is refused with the four names above |
| `par_refuses_mpiexec_environment` | `PMI_RANK` and `PMI_SIZE` together with `-comm threads`, then `PMI_SIZE` alone and `PMI_RANK` alone without `-comm` |
| `par_refuses_bad_options` | `-comm tcp`, `-np 2,0`, `-np x`, `-method metis`, and an unknown option |

Each gate was shown able to fail. The supervisor ran a mutated copy, which was
not kept, with four changes: the exchange before each sweep dropped, the exact
`sum` swapped for `gathered_sum`, one rank's Krylov reference perturbed by
1e-6, and the expected map hash taken from the next rotation. At P = 2 and 3,
Hilbert, every one of the 5 rotations failed MAP, HALO and REDUCTION, and both
Krylov lines failed (10 lines).

**What this does not establish.** All ranks are threads of one process on one
device. So nothing here runs over MPI (PAR-06), nothing runs on two devices
(§138.7's ignored test), and no time is a scaling number (PAR-16). The driver
gates the linear algebra of a decomposed solve. It does not yet run a flow
solver decomposed (PAR-10c, §139).

---

## 139. Distributed flow — the flow solver on a part of a cut mesh

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` This section is this project's own
contract (ORIGINAL). It has no external input.

§71 cuts the mesh and §73 solves a linear system across the cut. §138 moves
the bytes between ranks. This section runs the flow solver itself on one part:
first the room the halo needs (§139.1, PAR-09), then the exchanges that fill it
(§139.2, PAR-10a), the Krylov routing (§139.3, PAR-10b) and the decomposed SIMPLE gate (PAR-10c).

This section defines no equation, so it carries no equation label.

### 139.1 Room for the halo (PAR-09)

**What a part is.** §71.4 builds a part as an ordinary `HostMesh`. Its processor
faces are `PatchKind::Cyclic` (§71.5), and their `b_nbr_cell` points past
`n_cells`, into the halo `n_cells .. n_cells + n_halo`. Every kernel that
couples across a cyclic face reads `psi[bNbrCell[f]]` without a check. For
example, `lduAmul` reads `psi[nbr]` and the fixed-cell elimination reads
`isFixed[nbr]` (cuda/ldu.cu). So on a part, every buffer such a read can reach
must be `n_cells + n_halo` long. A shorter buffer is a read out of bounds,
not an error.

**The rule.** `GpuMesh` carries `n_halo` and `n_local() = n_cells + n_halo`.
Every existing constructor sets `n_halo = 0`. `GpuMesh::upload_with_halo(gpu,
m, n_halo)` is the plain upload plus the count. It refuses by name a mesh with
some `b_nbr_cell >= n_cells + n_halo`, and names the face, the cell and the
room. On the laminar SIMPLE + scalar + energy path, every cell buffer is
`n_local` long:
- `f`, `f0` and `f00` of the scalar and vector field constructors (their
  signatures are unchanged);
- `diag`, `source`, `is_fixed` and `fixed_value` of `GpuLduMatrix::new`;
- the cell vectors of `SolverWorkspace::for_mesh`, and under `single` the
  §118.4 `x_hi`, `d` and `b_in`;
- every per-cell buffer of `Simple`, `Momentum`, the energy equation and the
  scalar transport.

Face buffers stay face-sized. The cell-length checks of `src/fv.rs` want
`n_local`. Every launch still runs `n_cells` threads with `nCells = n_cells`,
and every solve still runs over `n_cells` rows. So no kernel writes the halo,
and nothing here fills it: the exchange is PAR-10a's. `SolverWorkspace::new(gpu,
n)` and `GpuMesh::upload` are unchanged. On a whole mesh `n_local = n_cells`,
every allocation has its former length, and the f64 build is unchanged bit for
bit.

**The audit.** `tests/halo_room.rs` (`every_simple_path_buffer_has_room_for_the_halo`)
reads the non-test part of `field.rs`, `fv.rs`, `simple.rs`, `momentum.rs`,
`energy.rs`, `scalar_transport.rs`, `ldu.rs`, `solver.rs` and `mesh.rs`. It
classifies every `.zeros(` site by its argument:
- the argument spells `n_local`: a halo site, and there must be exactly 62;
- the argument names `faces`: face-sized;
- otherwise the site must be on an allow list, with its exact count in that
  file and a reason. The list has 15 kinds and 33 sites: device scalars,
  reduction partials, `one(nbf)`/`one(nif)` face scratch, the CSR `nnz`
  slots, and the energy scratch sized `max(n_local, n_boundary_faces)`.

A new `zeros(n_cells)` on the path fails the audit. To pass, it either spells
`n_local` or joins the list with a reason (the PAR-09 rule of docs/17-completion-plan.md). `compressible/`,
`chem/`, `radiation/` and `dust/` are outside the audit, because their drivers
refuse decomposition by name.

**Measured (2026-10-16, RTX 5070 Ti).** The mesh is an 8 x 8 x 1 lid cavity cut
in two (`Linear`). Each part has 32 cells and a halo of 8, and its processor
faces are left `Cyclic` for U, p and T. The test runs three steady SIMPLE
iterations with PBiCGStab pressure on each part, under `compute-sanitizer
--tool memcheck`:
- uploaded without the room (`GpuMesh::upload`, so `n_halo = 0`): 377 errors,
  all invalid 8-byte global reads;
- uploaded with `upload_with_halo`: 0 errors, in f64 and in `single`.

The halo tail of U and p is still exactly zero after the three iterations, so
no kernel launched over it. A whole mesh gives `n_halo = 0` and
`n_local = n_cells`. A halo one cell short is refused by name. The serial
`ofgpu-validate -sections 1-9,16,57,61` rows were compared before and after:
all 329 rows of the JSON document (276 checks and the skip rows) are
identical (`tools/f64_identity.py rows`).

**What this does not establish.** The halo holds zeros. A part's answer is not
the whole mesh's answer until PAR-10a fills the halo and PAR-10c gates the
decomposed SIMPLE. On a part, `gpu.download` of a field returns `n_local`
values; trimming them to the owned cells for writers and drivers is PAR-14's
job. A host write of `n_cells` values into an `n_local` buffer is refused by
`Gpu::write`'s length check, which is loud and is not a read out of bounds.

### 139.2 The exchange points (PAR-10a)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` This subsection is this project's own
contract (ORIGINAL). It has no external input.

**What a rank holds.** `RankCtx` (`src/distflow.rs`) is what one rank of a
parallel flow solve holds besides its part. A `&dyn Comm`: the transport of
§138, which moves bytes and does no arithmetic on them, so a ghost cell holds
its owner's value bit for bit. A `SpmdHalo`: the rank's half of §71.4's
exchange plan plus §138.3's host round trip, built once, an exchange
allocating nothing. A `SpmdReduction`: the exact cross-part reduction of
§138.4, handed out mutable, because the global norms PAR-10b and PAR-10c
take go through it. And the part number, which `new` pins to the rank
number. `new` refuses BEFORE any collective and any device allocation, so
the refusing rank sends nothing. A peer that did not refuse goes on into
`SpmdReduction::new`'s allgather and waits there until the transport's
timeout: after an `Err` the world is spent (§138.1, R10). The checks are
local, and every rank of a correct program passes them alike:

| call | refusal, `Error::Config`, starting `distflow: ` |
|---|---|
| `comm.rank() != part.part` | names `rank {r}` and `part {p}` |
| `mesh.n_cells != part.mesh.n_cells` | names both counts |
| `mesh.n_halo != part.n_halo` | names both counts and says to upload the part with `GpuMesh::upload_with_halo` |

A fourth refusal is `SpmdHalo`'s own (§138.3): `exchange_field` on a field
whose `f` is shorter than `n_cells + n_halo` is refused by name, before
anything is launched or sent.

**The four exchange calls.** `exchange_field` fills the ghost cells
`n_cells .. n_cells + n_halo` of a scalar field - bit for bit the owning
rank's values - and then runs `field_ops::correct_boundary_conditions`. A
processor face is a `Cyclic` face whose `b_nbr_cell` names a halo cell
(§139.1). Its evaluated value is `w psi_P + (1 - w) psi_ghost`, and the
ghost is the neighbour rank's value: what the whole mesh's internal face
read. `exchange_field_vector` is the same through
`correct_boundary_conditions_vector`. `exchange_gradient` and
`exchange_gradient_tensor` fill the halo of a CELL GRADIENT - of a scalar
through `SpmdHalo::vector`, of a vector through `SpmdHalo::tensor`, nine
components as one struct. The operators that read `grad` at the far cell of
a face read it on ghost cells too, so a gradient is exchanged like a field.
No boundary evaluation follows a gradient exchange: a gradient carries no
boundary state, and the cells it fills are read only.

Every exchange is a host round trip: pack, device-to-host, `Comm`,
host-to-device, two synchronisations. So an exchange inside `Gpu::capture`
is refused by name - `SpmdHalo`'s own row, starting `halo: ` (§81.3,
§138.3). `distflow.rs` launches no kernel of its own. It calls `SpmdHalo`
and `field_ops`, nothing else, and no existing numerics move.

**The gate.** `tests/distflow.rs`, in BOTH builds, P = 2, 3, 4, Hilbert,
Linear and round robin (`c % P`). Two meshes: A, the axis-aligned box
`build_case(Big, 12, 10, 8)`; B, the skewed, non-orthogonal unit cube
`solid::prototype::jittered_block(10, 0.25)`. Two smooth fields of the whole
mesh's cell centres, with `xh = (x - xmin)/(xmax - xmin)` over those centres
and `yh`, `zh` alike:

```text
psi = exp(3 xh + 2 yh + 2.5 zh)
U   = (exp(3 xh + 2 yh + 2.5 zh), exp(-2 xh + 3 yh + 2 zh), exp(2 xh + 2 yh - 3 zh))
```

Each part writes its owned values only, with its halo zero, so an exchange
that did not happen cannot pass. The boundary kinds are the ones the field
constructors seed, on the whole mesh and on the parts alike.

| test | what it holds |
|---|---|
| `a_halo_gradient_equals_the_whole_mesh_gradient` | grad of a smooth psi and U on P = 2..4 parts of an axis-aligned box and of a skewed cube, against the whole mesh: every GHOST cell bit for bit the value its owning rank computed, ghosts compared > 0; on every OWNED cell and component the 4-ulp line is MEASURED and reported (MISSED - see Measured), and the ASSERTED line is the conditioning check `\|a - b\| <= 4 eps S` with `S` below |
| `a_processor_patch_reads_the_owner_value` | after `exchange_field`, every ghost is the whole-mesh value at its global cell bit for bit, and on every face of every processor patch the exchanged `bf` equals a same-mesh reference evaluation whose whole `f`, ghosts included, was written from the host with the whole-mesh values |
| `a_rank_ctx_refuses_by_name` | the refusal table above, plus `SpmdHalo`'s refusal of a halo-less field |

The conditioning check's `S` is the magnitude of that component's
Green-Gauss sum on the WHOLE mesh, computed on the host in f64 from the
whole mesh's geometry and its fields after their
`correct_boundary_conditions`. For grad psi, component `k` of cell `c`:

```text
S = (1/V_c) * sum over the faces f of c of |Sf_k| * |psi_f|
```

For grad U, component `(i, j)` of cell `c` - `i` is the area-vector index,
`j` the U component, and `Tensor.xy` is `i = x`, `j = y`:

```text
S = (1/V_c) * sum over the faces f of c of |Sf_i| * |U_f,j|
```

An internal face `f` counts for BOTH its cells, at
`|psi_f| = max(|psi[owner]|, |psi[neighbour]|)` (each U component the same
way) and `Sf = sf[f]`. A boundary face `b` counts for its one cell
`b_face_cells[b]`, at `|psi_f| = |bf[b]|` of the whole mesh's field and
`Sf = b_sf[b]`; a face whose `bc_kind` is `Empty` counts nothing.

**Measured (2026-10-16, RTX 5070 Ti).** The ghost cells are bit for bit the
owners' values everywhere they were compared: 29 694 ghost cell-payloads in
the gradient gate and 14 847 ghosts and 20 892 processor faces in the
processor-patch gate, f64 and single alike. **MISSED**: the owned-cell
gradients are not within 4 ulp everywhere, in either build. The line is not
loosened and is listed for review (docs/17-review-later.md). The measured
maxima, in ulp (grad psi / grad U):

| mesh, partitioner | P = 2 | P = 3 | P = 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A box, Hilbert | 6 / 13 (f64), 8 / 15 (single) | 10 / 13, 10 / 17 | 9 / 13, 10 / 15 |
| A box, Linear | 5 / 7, 4 / 6 | 10 / 10, 9 / 9 | 7 / 7, 4 / 6 |
| A box, round robin | 19 / 22, 17 / 26 | 19 / 22, 17 / 26 | 19 / 22, 17 / 26 |
| B jittered, Hilbert | 22 / 26, 22 / 46 | 22 / 22, 22 / 25 | 14 / 26, 22 / 46 |
| B jittered, Linear | 15 / 234, 13 / 135 | 19 / 51, 27 / 39 | 18 / 234, 21 / 135 |
| B jittered, round robin | 43 / 131, 39 / 305 | 82 / 244, 52 / 177 | 43 / 151, 64 / 177 |

The f64 global maxima are 82 ulp (grad psi) and 244 ulp (grad U); the single
build's are 64 and 305. Of 211 680 owned-component comparisons per build,
1 808 grad-psi and 7 325 grad-U components sit above 4 ulp in f64, and 2 339
and 9 010 in single - all on cells touching a processor face, and most under
the round robin, which cuts nearly every face. The asserted cause check
holds everywhere, in both builds: the max normalised error
`|a - b| / (eps S)` is 1.034 for grad psi and 1.034 for grad U in f64, and
1.096 and 1.307 in single, against the check's bound of 4 - every owned
component's difference is within 4 eps of the magnitude of its own
Green-Gauss sum on the whole mesh.

**What this does not establish.** The gradient is not bitwise, and the 4-ulp
line does not hold. Two reasons, both structural. A processor face's
contribution is summed in the boundary loop, after the internal faces; on
the whole mesh the same face was internal and was summed in the face loop,
so the order of addition differs. And on the non-owning side of a cut the
face's weight is `weight_from_offsets(b, a)`, not `1 - w`, so the
interpolated face value itself differs in the last bits. Where a cell's
Green-Gauss sum nearly cancels - a smooth field's gradient is small next to
its face fluxes - a few reordered additions show up as many ulps of the
result. The conditioning check is what shows the miss is the order of
rounding and not a wrong value. PAR-13a makes the gradients bitwise. A
part's p and momentum solves go through the SPMD Krylov solvers in §139.3
(PAR-10b). No decomposed SIMPLE is gated here: that is PAR-10c.

### 139.3 The Krylov routing (PAR-10b)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` This subsection is this project's own
contract (ORIGINAL). It has no external input.

**Why.** A part's linear solves still went through the serial `solver::solve`,
whose every residual norm is THIS RANK'S alone: `sum|b - A·psi|` summed over
the part's own cells, `normFactor` divided by the part's cell count. Two
ranks of one SIMPLE iteration would then disagree about whether the equation
converged, and a rank could declare convergence while the world's residual
was far from met. §138.5/§138.6's `spmd_solve` reports the world's norms -
each one a cross-part reduction, the same bits on every rank. This
subsection routes a part's pressure and momentum solves through it.

**The one-part system, part-assembled.** `DistSystem::for_rank(gpu, comm,
dec)` builds part `comm.rank()` of `dec` as ONE part: the mesh uploaded with
`GpuMesh::upload_with_halo` (§139.1), a zero `GpuLduMatrix::new` of that
mesh, `n = [part.mesh.n_cells]`, `n_local = [part.n_local()]`,
`part = Some(rank)`. It refuses (`distsolve: `) a world whose rank count
differs from the decomposition's part count, naming both numbers, before
any upload. `DistSystem::load_matrix(gpu, halo, comm, a)` then copies a
matrix ASSEMBLED ON THE PART into that shell - diag, source, is_fixed and
fixed_value over the owned cells, upper and lower over the internal faces,
internal_coeffs and boundary_coeffs over the boundary faces, one
`memcpy_dtod` each - and fills the halo of `is_fixed` (FIRST) and
`fixed_value` (second) through `halo.label`/`halo.scalar`, exactly as
`split` and `split_one` fill them. Only the two constraint arrays cross the
halo because they are the only matrix state a kernel reads at a halo index
(`lduSetValues` at a coupled face's neighbour); every other array is read
only at owned indices, and the halo slots of `diag` and `source` are never
read - `split_one`'s comment says why - so they stay as they are. The
matrix is assembled on the part, never split from a whole: the flow path
has no whole-mesh matrix to split. `load_matrix` refuses, in order and
BEFORE any copy or exchange: the system is not a one-part `for_rank`
system; `a.n_cells` differs (both counts named); `n_internal_faces` or
`n_boundary_faces` differs (both named); any source buffer is shorter than
what would be copied (the array and both lengths named).

**The three handles.** `SpmdKrylov` holds one rank's `comm`, `SpmdHalo`,
`DistSystem`, `SpmdWorkspace` and `SolverKernels`, plus the colouring flag
and the solve count. One `run` is, in order: refuse GAMG as solver or
preconditioner - a part's flow solve routes PCG and PBiCGStab only, the
distributed cycle of §141.11 not being attached on the flow path; refuse a
mesh that is not the part's and a `psi` shorter than `n_local` (both
counts, `upload_with_halo` named); build the part-local colouring the first
DIC/DILU solve needs (a device pass, once, not a collective);
`load_matrix`; `spmd_solve`; count and remember. The refusals fire BEFORE
anything collective, so every rank given the same input refuses alike and
no rank waits for one that refused (§138.1, R10). `SpmdPressureBackend`
wraps a `SpmdKrylov` as a `PressureBackend` - `name` "SPMD Krylov",
`applicable` always, `setup` refusing a host or uploaded mesh that is not
the part's (both counts and the rank named), `solve` mapping the
distributed record onto `SolverPerformance` - and drops into the seam
`Simple` already takes, `&mut dyn PressureBackend`. `SpmdMomentumRoute`
wraps one as a `ComponentRoute`, the ONE seam in `momentum.rs`'s
`solve_once`: `Momentum` gains `set_route`/`has_route`, `None` (the
default, and every path shipped before) keeping the old `solver::solve`
call launch for launch, and `Simple::set_momentum_route` passes it through
unchanged. Routing only: the SIMPLE loop itself does not change.

**Not capturable.** Each routed solve is a host round trip by construction -
`load_matrix`'s constraint exchange and `spmd_solve`'s per-iteration
exchanges and reductions all leave the device - and `spmd_solve` refuses
inside a CUDA-graph capture by name (§81.3, §138.5). A routed solve fails a
capture rather than silently serialising it. No kernel is launched in
`distflow.rs`.

**Under `single`.** The routed solve is refined (§118.12): the flag vote
counts `n_iterations + 2·outer + 1` reads, and `refined_solution` hands out
the f64 `x_hi`, the answer's precision class A form.

**The gate.** `tests/distflow_krylov.rs`, in BOTH builds, P = 1, 2, 4,
Hilbert, Linear and round robin, two meshes (A, the axis-aligned box
`build_case(Big, 12, 10, 8)`; B, `solid::prototype::jittered_block(10,
0.25)`), solver pairs (PCG, DIC), (PCG, Diagonal), (PBiCGStab, DILU),
tolerance `1e-12` in both builds (a solver control, not a gate), the exact
reduction:

| test | what it holds |
|---|---|
| `a_part_assembled_poisson_reaches_the_serial_answer` | a part-assembled SPD Poisson solved by `SpmdPressureBackend` reaches the whole-mesh `solver::solve` answer: every owned cell `<= 1e-8` rel in BOTH builds (class A - under `single` both sides are the refined f64 solutions, docs/17 §12.3 note 5), every rank converged, `initial_residual`, `final_residual` and `n_iterations` the same bits on every rank - a rank-local serial solve would norm its own cells only, so identical norms everywhere is what shows the route was taken - the flag vote `n_iterations + 2·outer + 1` on every rank, and the parts' owned cells covering the mesh exactly once; the fixture folds every coefficient in f64 and rounds ONCE, because under `single` a float running sum would make the part's operator differ from the whole's by its summation order - the assembly question PAR-13a owns, not this gate's |
| `a_part_momentum_solve_goes_through_the_spmd_route` | the routed momentum predictor on P = 2, 4 (Hilbert, round robin), controls `nu 0.01`, upwind, uncorrected snGrad, no bounded convection, no variable-viscosity stress: every component `n_iterations > 0` and its residual bits and iterations identical on every rank, and the owned U within `1e-8` rel of the whole mesh's in f64, tol32 `1e-5` under `single` (class R, §5.1.4 - the stored field is float); `has_route` false before and true after `set_route` |
| `the_spmd_routes_refuse_by_name` | the refusal table below, all six rows, on every rank of a 2-part cut |

The refusals, all `Error::Config`, checked with `contains`:

| call | message starts | names |
|---|---|---|
| `for_rank`, ranks != parts | `distsolve: ` | both counts |
| `load_matrix`, no one-part system | `distsolve: ` | - |
| `load_matrix`, `n_cells` differs | `distsolve: ` | both counts |
| `load_matrix`, face counts differ | `distsolve: ` | all four counts |
| `load_matrix`, a source buffer short | `distsolve: ` | the array and both lengths |
| `SpmdPressureBackend::new`/`SpmdKrylov::run`, GAMG | `distflow: ` | `GAMG` |
| `SpmdKrylov::run`, mesh/`psi` sizes | `distflow: ` | both counts, `upload_with_halo` |
| `SpmdPressureBackend::setup`, whole-mesh meshes | `distflow: ` | `setup`, both counts, the rank |

**Measured (2026-10-16, RTX 5070 Ti).** The fixture folds every coefficient
in f64 and rounds ONCE (the gate row says why). f64: the gate HOLDS
everywhere - 42 Poisson cases, max rel `1.182e-11` (bound `1e-8`), the same
number run to run because in this build the fixture's arithmetic is the
same as it ever was; every case converged with identical residual bits and
iteration counts on every rank; the routed solves ran 17-59 iterations
against serial references at 18-59; the momentum cases at
`2.654e-13`-`6.408e-13` (bound `1e-8`), 10-14 iterations per component;
the refusal test green. Under `single` the Poisson gate HOLDS on every row
too: 42 cases, max rel `1.595e-11`, the P = 1 rows at `0` to `1.277e-12`,
the routed solves 18-68 iterations against references at 18-68; the
momentum gate holds at max rel `1.364e-7` against its tol32 `1e-5`,
9-12 iterations per component; the refusal test green.

The gate also prints, per case and WITHOUT asserting on it, how many owned
rows' `diag` or `source` differ BITWISE between the part's host fold and
the whole fold's row at the global cell, summed over ranks. Under `single`
that count is 0 on EVERY case: one rounding of an f64 sum makes the part's
float matrix the whole's, bit for bit. In f64 it is 0 at P = 1 and 34-400
on the cuts (worst 400, mesh B round robin) - the two f64 folds still add
in different orders and differ in their last bits, and the single rounding
is what removes those last bits.

**What a float running sum in the fixture gave.** The fixture's first
version summed `diag` and `source` in Scalar - a float running sum under
`single` - so the part's operator differed from the whole's by its
summation order: a part adds a processor face in its boundary loop, after
its internal faces, where the whole adds it inside the internal loop, and
the two solves answered two different float systems. Every P >= 2 row of
every solver pair missed the `1e-8` line by ~2e-7 to ~5e-7; the measured
single-build maxima of that version, kept as the evidence that a part's
float assembly order moves the answer by ~5e-7 - the assembly question
PAR-13a owns, not this gate:

| mesh, partitioner | P = 2 | P = 4 |
|---|---|---|
| A box, Hilbert | `3.507e-7` | `5.338e-7` |
| A box, Linear | `2.459e-7` | `2.792e-7` |
| A box, round robin | `4.003e-7` | `4.371e-7` |
| B jittered, Hilbert | `1.993e-7` | `3.191e-7` |
| B jittered, Linear | `2.693e-7` | `2.677e-7` |
| B jittered, round robin | `3.021e-7` | `2.984e-7` |

In that version every P = 1 row held (`0` to `5.2e-13`), so the route
itself was class A and the miss began exactly at the first cut; and on one
mesh and cut the error was the same to the digits shown on ALL THREE
solver pairs - on mesh B to every printed digit - which says the
difference was NOT the iterate path (a cut-dependent preconditioner would
move the pairs apart) but the MATRIX: each fold converged to the solution
of its own slightly different float system.

**What this does not establish.** No decomposed SIMPLE: the exchange points
and this routing are in place, but `Simple` does not reduce globally or
exchange per outer iteration yet - that is PAR-10c. The part-assembled
matrix is not bitwise the split one (PAR-13a): this gate's fixture now
folds in f64 and rounds once, so its two folds agree bitwise here, but the
library's own float assembly still sums in whatever order the fold walks
the faces - the first version's numbers above are what that cost. GAMG on the flow
path is refused by name, not run. MPI and
multi-GPU are deferred: the gates run `ThreadComm` ranks on one GPU.

---

## 141. Native GAMG and AMGX — aggregation, the Galerkin hierarchy, and the AMGX library

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Docs/17 §4.3 allocates §141 to the GAMG units
(AMG-01 writes §141.1) and to AMX-01. This section is the contract of a native
aggregation multigrid: §141.1 says how a matrix is coarsened; the Galerkin operator,
the smoothers, the coarsest solve and the cycles are later subsections (AMG-02 to
AMG-04a, the K-cycle of §141.6, AMG-04c, and the decomposed levels of §141.10, AMG-07a). Since AMG-04a `solver::solve` runs the cycle (§141.5), since AMG-04b a case asks
for it and its settings (§141.7), and since AMG-05 it is a pressure backend the selector measures
(§141.8). AMX-01 opens AMGX at run time (§141.20), and since AMX-02 AMGX keeps its hierarchy structure
in the time loop and is compared with PBiCGStab and GAMG (§141.21).

Sources: **Notay, Y. (2010), "An aggregation-based algebraic multigrid method",
*Electron. Trans. Numer. Anal.* 37, 123-146** (open full text at
<https://etna.ricam.oeaw.ac.at/vol.37.2010/pp123-146.dir/pp123-146.pdf>, read on
2026-10-11): §2, Algorithm 2.1 (pairwise aggregation) and Algorithm 2.2 (double
pairwise aggregation), and the statement after Algorithm 2.2 that "the coarsening
ratio n/nc is slightly less than 4". **Napov, A. & Notay, Y. (2012), "An algebraic
multigrid method with guaranteed convergence rate", *SIAM J. Sci. Comput.* 34(2)
A1079-A1109, doi:10.1137/100818509** (title, volume and pages checked against Crossref
on 2026-10-11), named by docs/17 for the AMG-01 row; it was not opened, and no
formula below is taken from it. No multigrid code of any licence was read for this
section. In particular OpenFOAM's GAMG and the AGMG code that Notay's paper offers
for download were not opened.
