| `types::tests::no_kernel_unit_carries_a_double_only_literal_outside_its_pair` (library, f64) | the §112.1 scan, `cuda/amg.cu` among the files it reads | D |

**Measured** (supervisor's runs, 2026-10-15; `single` first, f64 in brackets; the f64
numbers are §141.5's and §141.6's, unchanged).

- `POI(64)` GAMG-PCG: 20 iterations in 2 outer steps [24], against a gate of 30.

- §141.5.1 under `single`, for POI 32³ / 64³ / 128³:

  The f64 rows are the table of §141.11.1, unchanged.

### 141.10 Decomposed levels: block-local aggregation, coarse processor faces and coarse halos (AMG-07a)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` `src/amg/dist.rs` holds the decomposed levels, host
code only; `src/halo.rs` gains `LevelHalo`, the exchange plan of one level, from which
`HaloExchange::from_levels` and `SpmdHalo::from_level` build the in-process and the SPMD
exchange (§71.4, §138.3) exactly as `new` builds them from a `PartMesh`, which they now
delegate to. `Aggregation::from_map` (§141.1) builds the members CSR and the fold table of a
given (141.8)-numbered map with the code that ends `aggregate_level`, moved and not changed.
The tests are `tests/amg_dist.rs`, an integration test that runs in both builds (§118).
Nothing in the solve path called this when it landed; the distributed cycle is AMG-07b's
(§141.11), so no existing solve, case or SASS moved. Multi-GPU runs are deferred by the user: every rank is a
`ThreadComm` thread on device 0 (§138.7). Sources: Notay (2010) of §141.1 for the aggregation
and the Galerkin product; the decomposition into blocks is this project's own design, and no
multigrid code of any licence was read for this subsection.

**A decomposed level** is one part's LDU level (§1, §71): owned cells `0..n`, ghosts
`n..n+n_h`, internal faces among owned cells, and boundary faces. A boundary face with
`b_nbr_cell >= n` is a **processor face**: its coefficient enters the operator as
`-boundary_coeffs · psi[b_nbr_cell]`, the sign of (141.2) and of `split_matrix` (§71.6). The
finest level is the part's mesh with its split and folded matrix; a coarse level has only
processor faces.

**Block-local aggregation** (*DESIGN*, docs/17 AMG-07a). Each part runs §141.1 on its own
cells, with every processor face read as uncoupled. A cyclic couple inside the part stays an
edge. So every aggregate lies inside one part, and no aggregate spans a cut, which is a gate.
`σ` of (141.3) is the part's own; §141.1 gives `A` and `-A` the same aggregation, so a part
whose diagonal sum differs in sign from the whole matrix's would only be an indefinite input.

**Keys** (*DESIGN*; they are what makes the parts' sums the serial sums, bit for bit). Every
local cell and every boundary face carries a global key:

```
fine cell c:            key(c)  = global cell id
fine boundary face bf:  key(bf) = (global face slot, -1)   (f, or n_if + bf of the whole mesh)
aggregate I:            key(I)  = min_{c in I} key(c)        (its root)
coarse processor face:  key(I, H) = (min(key I, key H), max(key I, key H))      (141.40)
```

A part's owned cells are ascending in global id (§71.4), so the (141.8) numbering inside a
part is ascending in root, and the union of the parts' aggregations, numbered by root, is
numbered by (141.8) on the whole level. By induction the same holds at every level. The
halo of every level is ordered by (owning part, key), as the fine halo is (§71.4).

**The coarse level of a part.** Its own cells and faces are §141.2 on the part, unchanged: a
`GalerkinPlan` of the block-local aggregation, its sums (141.14)-(141.16), and its list order.
That order is the serial one, because the part's cells, internal faces and inherited boundary
faces are each ascending in their global ids. Its processor faces are new:

```
coarse halo:  the distinct (q, R) over the fine processor faces, q the ghost's owning part,
              R the ghost's aggregate on q (its local id), ascending in (q, R)
send to q:    the distinct own aggregates I joined to q by a fine processor face, ascending
coarse face:  every distinct (I, h_c), I own, h_c a coarse ghost, ascending, with
    a_{I,H} = round( Σ_{bf -> (I, h_c), ascending in key(bf)} -boundary_coeffs[bf] )
    boundary_coeffs_c = -a_{I,H}                                          (141.41)
```

summed in an f64 accumulator (`ofacc`'s width in both builds) and rounded once, as the host
twin of §141.2 sums. IEEE negation is exact, so (141.41) stores the bits the serial sum
produces. A part receives from `q` exactly the aggregates `q` sends, in the same order,
because every cut face is a processor face on both sides (§71.6) and `q`'s local order is
its key order; no extra message settles the plan. The ghost's `R` and root come from the
owner: in one process by a key lookup in the owner's level (`halo_aggregates`), and SPMD by
two label exchanges over the level's own plan (`spmd_halo_aggregates`).

**Why the gathered level is the serial product.** For a coarse face `(I, J)` with `I` on part
`p` and `J` on part `q`, every fine entry in its two slots crosses the cut, so its upper slot
`(A_c)_{IJ}` is exactly the sum `p` forms for `(I, H = J)`, and its lower slot is the one `q`
forms. A fine cut face gives `p` the coefficient `-upper[g]` or `-lower[g]` (§71.6), so
`-boundary_coeffs` is the serial term. The serial list order is internal faces ascending,
then coupled faces ascending (§141.2); a fine key is the face's global slot, internal before
boundary, so the key order is that order. At a coarse level the gathered level has no
boundary faces and its faces are ascending by `(owner, neighbour)` in global numbering, which
is the order of (141.40). The diagonal slots never see a processor face, because no
aggregate spans parts.

**The hierarchy.** `DistHierarchy::build_in_process` and the collective
`DistHierarchy::build_spmd` stop by §141.3's rule on the WHOLE level: at `n_cells_coarsest`
or `max_levels`, dropping a coarsening that does not shrink the whole level. Every part
therefore has the same number of levels. SPMD, the counts travel in one allgather per step,
which is also a vote, so a step refused on one rank is refused on every rank before the next
collective. `gather_level` puts the parts' coarse levels into one `HostLevel`, numbered by
key; AMG-07b uses it for the coarsest level (§141.11).

**Refused by name** (`Error::Config`, every message starts with `amg::dist: `): array
lengths that disagree with the level; a halo plan of another part or cell count; owned keys
not strictly ascending, or a halo group's keys not strictly ascending; a `b_nbr_cell` past the
halo; halo aggregates or roots of the wrong length; an aggregate that arrives with two keys
or out of key order; two processor faces with one key; `gather_level` given a level with a
non-processor boundary face, or with an entry from two places or one side only;
`n_cells_coarsest = 0` or `max_levels = 0`. `Aggregation::from_map` refuses a map not
numbered by (141.8) (`amg::aggregate: `), and a level plan that sends a cell it does not
own is refused by both exchanges (`halo: `).

**Precision.** Every row is class D (docs/17 §5.1.4): bitwise in both builds. The f32
matrices aggregate differently from their f64 parents (§141.1, rounded coefficients), so the
level counts differ between the builds; the gate holds in each.

#### 141.10.1 The gates

The meshes are boxes with every patch a wall: 9×7×5 with (141.18), 8×6×5 cyclic on x, y and
z with (141.18), and 12×10×8 with the folded §2 laplacian. The partitions are Hilbert,
linear, and blocks of three cells dealt round robin; `n_cells_coarsest = 4`.

| test (`tests/amg_dist.rs`) | what | class |
|---|---|---|
| `gathered_coarse_levels_are_the_galerkin_product_of_the_gathered_fine_level` | **the AMG-07a gate.** The three meshes, `P = 2, 3, 4`, the three partitions: the fine level gathered from the parts is the whole matrix bit for bit; then at every level, the union of the block-local aggregations is a (141.8) map in which no aggregate spans parts, and the parts' next level, gathered, is bit for bit `GalerkinPlan(from_map(union), gathered level).coarse_host`. Measured: 95 levels (f64) and 94 (`single`), 5319 and 4761 cross-part coarse faces, 3584 and 3500 of their slots summing three or more sources. Summing the processor sources in reverse key order fails it (checked in f64) | D |
| `one_part_is_the_serial_hierarchy` | `P = 1` on the three meshes: aggregations, plans and levels equal `HostHierarchy::build`'s | D |
| `an_spmd_build_is_the_in_process_build_and_its_coarse_halos_carry_the_owners_value` | the first two meshes, Hilbert, `P = 2, 3, 4`: `build_spmd` on `ThreadComm` ranks (device 0) equals the in-process build; at every level `HaloExchange::from_levels` and `SpmdHalo::from_level` bring every ghost its owner's value `1 + key/2` (3588 ghosts in f64, 3632 in `single`) | D |
| `a_malformed_decomposed_level_is_refused_by_name` | the refusals above | D |

### 141.11 The distributed V-cycle over SPMD ranks, and GAMG on the SPMD path (AMG-07b)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` `src/amg/distcycle.rs` holds `DistGamg`, one rank's
part of the cycle of §141.5 on the decomposed hierarchy of §141.10. `src/distsolve/spmd.rs`
takes it, attached by `SpmdWorkspace::set_gamg`, as `Preconditioner::Gamg` of `spmd_pcg` and
`spmd_pbicgstab` and, through the new `spmd_gamg`, as `LinearSolverKind::Gamg` of
`spmd_solve`, which no longer refuses `GAMG` (§138.6 is amended). `src/amg/smooth.rs` splits
`SmootherSetup::new` into `without_interval` and `set_interval`, the same arithmetic in the
same order, so every serial setup keeps its bits, and gains `GpuSmoother::smooth_with`, a
sweep whose product the caller forms. No kernel and no `.cu` file changes. The tests are
`tests/amg_dist_cycle.rs`, an integration test in both builds (§118). Multi-GPU runs are
deferred by the user: every rank is a `ThreadComm` thread with its own `Gpu` on device 0
(§138.7). Sources: Saad (2003) §13.4.3 Algorithm 13.3 and Notay (2010) eq. (2.1), as in
§141.5, and Saad's Algorithm 6.15 (Lanczos), as in §141.3. The decomposition of the cycle
over the parts, the redundant coarsest solve and the rank-ordered sums are this project's own
design; no multigrid code of any licence was read for this subsection.

**Tree vs plan.** docs/17's AMG-07b row asks that `dist_solve` stop refusing GAMG. Since
PAR-04a/b the solve a rank runs is `spmd_solve` (§138.5, §138.6), and `dist_solve` holds
every part in one process as the bitwise reference of those gates. The cycle is a collective
over one part per rank, so the SPMD path takes GAMG; the in-process `dist_solve` and
`DistWorkspace` keep a refusal that names the SPMD route (*DESIGN*, taken by recommendation:
a second, lockstep copy of the cycle for the in-process form would add no gate of the row).

**The level product.** Level `l` of rank `r` is a `DistLevel` of §141.10. After the level's
halo is filled by its own `SpmdHalo::from_level` (§138.3), its product is the row of
`lduAmul` (§70):

```
(A_l x)_c = d_c x_c + Σ_{f: o(f) = c} u_f x_{n(f)} + Σ_{f: n(f) = c} l_f x_{o(f)}
            - Σ_{bf: c(bf) = c, b_nbr(bf) >= 0} bc_bf x_{b_nbr(bf)}                  (141.42)
```

On level 0 the coupled boundary faces are the part's cyclic couples and its processor faces,
and `ldu_ops::amul` runs on the part's mesh. On a coarse level they are the processor faces
of (141.41), and the same kernel runs on the level's own merged row map: per cell its internal
faces in ascending face id, then its processor faces in ascending face id.

**The smoothers.** Each part runs §141.3's smoother on its own rows: the diagonal and, as
off-diagonal entries, its faces and its coupled boundary faces of (141.42), whose columns may
be ghosts. The smoothing diagonal `m` of (141.3.3)/(141.3.4) is therefore the whole matrix's
row value. `σ` is the part's own. When every part's setup succeeds, every row has
`σ a_cc > 0` with one sign, so all parts' `σ` agree, and an allgather checks it. The global
quantities are taken over the whole level:

```
g = max_r g_r                                Gershgorin's bound of (141.3.7)
θ = §141.3's Lanczos on the whole level, with
    v_c = frac((key_c + 1) s) - 1/2          the start by GLOBAL key (§141.10)
    (a, b) = Σ_{r = 0 .. P-1} (a, b)_r       each rank's f64 partial, allgathered and
                                             added from 0 in rank order
    S v = σ |D|^-1/2 A_l |D|^-1/2 v          (141.42) in f64, after an f64 halo exchange   (141.43)
```

Every rank therefore holds the same bits of `θ`, `g` and the coefficients of (141.3.5). On
level 0 the keys are the global cell ids, so the start vector is the serial one, permuted.

**The coarsest level** (*DESIGN*, docs/17 AMG-07b: "coarsest level allgatherv'd and solved
redundantly"). At setup every rank allgathervs its coarsest `DistLevel`. `gather_level`
(§141.10) puts them into one `HostLevel` numbered by key, and every rank factors it as
`Gamg::new` factors its coarsest level, `CoarseSetup::general` (§141.4, (141.5.4)). Every
cycle then runs

```
b[gid(key_c)] = b_L[c] of every rank (one allgatherv);   x = C(b) on every rank;
x_L[c] = x[gid(key_c)]                                                                (141.44)
```

where `gid(k)` is the rank of `k` among the whole coarsest level's keys. Every rank solves the
same bits with the same kernel, so every rank's copy of `x` is the same.

**The cycle** is (141.5.1) with (141.42) for every `A_l`, the smoothers above, the part-local
`GpuGalerkin` of the block-local aggregation for `P_l` and `P_l^T` (no aggregate spans a cut,
so the transfers send nothing), and (141.44) for `C`. Only the V-cycle is built, and a
hierarchy without a coarse level is refused, because such a system belongs on one rank. PCG
takes the cycle only with `n_pre = n_post`, as `solve_pcg` does. `spmd_gamg` is
`solve_gamg` (§141.5) on SPMD: one iteration is one cycle, and the residual of §8.4 is tested
every `check_interval` iterations with `spmd_pcg`'s norm factor, reductions and flag vote. The
exchanges of the cycle's products are counted in `DistPerformance::n_exchanges`.

**Not partition-invariant** (§73.5's pattern). A cut changes the block-local aggregation and
so the whole hierarchy. `SpmdWorkspace::partition_invariant(Gamg)` and
`DistWorkspace::partition_invariant(Gamg)` are `false`, and the answer moves under a cut,
which a gate shows. The gates hold the answer against the serial GAMG, not bits.

**Refused by name.** `DistGamg::new` (`amg::distcycle: `, voted on every rank): a hierarchy
without a coarse level, `n_pre + n_post = 0`, a part given to another rank, a part with no
cell on some level, parts whose `σ` differ, and a coarsest level `CoarseSetup` refuses (for
example more than `MAX_DENSE_CELLS` cells). `DistGamg::cycle`: a CUDA-graph capture, a handle
of another rank or world, an operator or field of another shape. `SpmdWorkspace::set_gamg`:
a cycle of another rank, world or part shape (`distsolve: `). `Preconditioner::Gamg` without
a cycle: §13.4's `Error::Refused`, naming `SpmdWorkspace::set_gamg`. `spmd_gamg` without a
cycle: `spmd_gamg: solver GAMG was requested`, naming `set_gamg`, `PCG` and `PBiCGStab`.
`spmd_pcg` with `n_pre != n_post`. In one process, `dist_solve` with `GAMG` and
`DistWorkspace::effective_preconditioner(Gamg)` name the SPMD route.

**Precision.** The answer gate is class R (docs/17 §5.1.4): `1e-8` relative to the serial
answer. The iteration gate is a count. As AMG-07b landed, the SPMD solves under `single` were
float solves without §118.4's refinement, so they ran at the solver tolerance `1e-5` of the
SPMD gates of §138.5 against `tol32 = 1e-5`. At `1e-6` the stationary float cycle stalled at
its floor (a true residual of `4.3e-6` after 500 cycles on POI 32³), while the refined serial
solve converged in 42 cycles. That is a property of the unrefined float solve, not of the
cycle. F32-07 then refined `spmd_pcg` and `spmd_pbicgstab` (§118.12), and AMG-06a refined
`spmd_gamg` (§141.9). Since AMG-06a both numbers are the f64 ones in both builds: the solver
tolerance is `1e-11`, and the gate `1e-8` on the double answers.

#### 141.11.1 The gates

POI is the §2 laplacian negated (`σ = +1`), walls folded as Dirichlet zero, cyclic couples as
`boundary_coeffs`, and `b = 1 + (c mod 7)/7`. The config is the default (Chebyshev degree 2,
V(2,2), `n_cells_coarsest = 64`), and the solver tolerance is `1e-11` in both builds (it was
`1e-5` under `single` before AMG-06a), from zero.

| `the_distributed_cycle_moves_the_answer_under_a_cut_and_says_so` | POI 16×12×10, `P = 2, 4`, Hilbert and linear: `partition_invariant(Gamg)` is `false` on every rank and in one process, every cut is within the answer gate of the serial GAMG-PCG, and the answers of the cuts differ in their bits (6 of 6 pairs, both builds) | R, D |

### 141.12 The f32 GAMG preconditioner of an f64 solve (AMG-06b)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` An f64 solve can take its GAMG preconditioner in single
precision: `Gamg::new_with_precision(.., GamgPrecision::Single, ..)` builds the solve's own host
hierarchy (§141.3) and coarsest setup (§141.4) exactly as `Gamg::new` does, and then holds them on the
device in `f32` instead of `Scalar`. A case asks for it with the GAMG key `precision single` (§141.7;
the default is `native`), read by the dictionary route; the pressure backends of §141.7 and §141.8
pass it to the build. The JSONC `gamg` block does not carry the key yet, so it refuses `precision` by
name as an unknown field (`io/case_json.rs` was another lane's file in this wave). It is opt-in: no default moves, and a case that does not write the key keeps
its hierarchy, its counts and its answers bit for bit. Under `--features single` the hierarchy is
already float, both values build the native one, and the key changes nothing (the gates hold this
bitwise). The unit is AMG-06b.

Sources: **Kronbichler & Ljungkvist, "Multigrid for Matrix-Free High-Order Finite Element Computations
on Graphics Processors", *ACM Trans. Parallel Comput.* 6(1) (2019)**, DOI `10.1145/3322813`, the
reference docs/17 names: the design idea only, a multigrid V-cycle run in single precision as the
preconditioner of a conjugate gradient iterated in double. No equation of this section is taken from
it, and its code was not read. The cycle is §141.5's (Saad 2003 §13.4.3, the author's open copy). The
roundings are IEEE-754 round-to-nearest conversions.

**What the f32 copy holds** (*DESIGN*, `src/amg/single.rs`). The aggregation and every level are the
solve's own, built in f64 in the f64 build, so the f32 copy coarsens level for level as the f64
hierarchy does. That is unlike the `single` build, where the aggregation itself reads float strengths
(§141.9).
- Each coarse level's `diag`, `upper` and `lower`, each smoother's diagonal `m` and its Chebyshev
  coefficients `c1`, `c2` are rounded once to `f32` from their f64 setups.
- The per-level cycle vectors are `f32`.
- The coarsest factor and its work vector stay in `Acc` (f64), as under `single` (§141.4); only the
  solve's `x` and `b` are float.
- The transfers keep the aggregate lists of (141.11)-(141.13). The Galerkin slot lists of (141.17) are
  not uploaded, because the levels come from the host and no device Galerkin product runs.
- Level 0's operator is `A32 = fl32(A)` taken entrywise inside the product (`amgFineAmulFloat`), from
  the solve's own matrix and the mesh's row map, so no copy of the fine matrix is stored.

The V-cycle on the copy is `cuda/amg.cu` compiled a second time with `-DOFGPU_SINGLE`
(`kernels::AMG_F32`, build.rs's `F32_TWIN_UNITS`); under `single` that constant names `AMG` itself.
Four kernels cross the precisions, from the native module: `amgToFloat`, `amgAddFloat`,
`amgFineAmulFloat` and `amgFineResidualFloat`. Each is one thread per cell and only launches, so the
copy captures into a CUDA graph (§81; `single_cycle_replays_under_capture`).

**The equations.** `M32` is the V-cycle (141.5.1) from zero on the float levels, its level-0 operator
`A32`. The preconditioner application is

```
z = fl64( M32( fl32(r) ) )                                              (141.45)
```

where `fl32` rounds each entry to nearest and `fl64` widens it exactly. One stationary cycle from the
caller's `x` (`Gamg::vcycle`, `Gamg::cycle`, and so `LinearSolverKind::Gamg`) is

```
x <- x + fl64( M32( fl32(b - A x) ) )                                  (141.46)
```

with `b - A x` formed in the solve's precision in `lduAmul`'s order (`amgFineResidualFloat`). For a
linear cycle, (141.46) is one step of the same stationary method as (141.5.1), written in correction
form. Its residual is the solve's, so the f32 levels do not floor the stationary solve. In exact
arithmetic `M32` would be `M`; the copy changes the preconditioner by its float rounding only, and PCG
and PBiCGStab iterate in the solve's precision around it. The memory measure is

```
rho = B(single) / B(native),  B = sum over every DevBuf a Gamg holds of len * sizeof(element)   (141.47)
```

`Gamg::device_bytes` sums the levels, transfers, row maps, smoothers, the coarsest factor and its work
vector, the per-level cycle vectors and any K-cycle buffers. It reports them split into the
precision-chosen arrays (`float`), the `Acc` ones and the `Label` ones. Level 0's matrix is the solve's
and is counted in neither.

**What is refused.** The K-cycle (§141.6) on the f32 copy: `set_cycle(K)` is refused naming `K-cycle`,
`precision single` and this section, and the Gamg keeps its V-cycle. The distributed GAMG of §141.11
has no f32 copy; `DistGamg` is unchanged.

**Measured gate interpretation** (TAKEN by recommendation). The row's "the hierarchy's memory" is read
as (141.47) over every byte, integers included. That is the strictest reading. The float-only ratio is
reported beside it.

#### 141.12.1 The gates

`POI(n)` of (141.5.5), default `GamgConfig`, from zero, `relTol 0`. "Iterations" is
`SolverPerformance::n_iterations`. All rows run in both builds.

| test (`tests/amg_single.rs` unless marked) | what | class |
|---|---|---|
| `an_f32_gamg_preconditions_an_f64_pcg_on_poisson_128` | **the AMG-06b gate.** PCG/GAMG at tol `1e-10` on `POI(128)`, native and `precision single`. f64 build: both converge; the copy has the native level sizes; it takes `<= 1.15x` the all-f64 iterations; its answer's §8.4 residual, on the host in f64, is `<= 1e-10`; and `rho <= 0.55` by (141.47). Under `single` the two are one: equal counts, equal bytes, bitwise answers | P, R, count |
| `the_gamg_precision_key_reaches_the_solve` | the §13.4.1 pair: fvSolution texts that differ in the one line `precision single;`, read by `read_solver_controls` and solved through `PbicgstabBackend` on `POI(16)` at `1e-8` under `PCG`/`GAMG` and the `GAMG` solver. The key lands bare, in the `preconditioner { }` sub-dictionary and under `solver GAMG`; `precision native` is the default text's controls. f64: the answers differ in their bits and all converge. `single`: bitwise one. `precision half` is refused naming `solvers/p/precision`, `half`, `native`, `single` and this section | P, D |
| `the_single_cycle_refusals_are_named` | the K-cycle on the copy is refused by name, and the cycle stays V (f64); under `single` it is set | D |

| `amg::single::tests::single_cycle_replays_under_capture` (library) | (141.45) and two cycles of (141.46) on `POI(8)`, with one coarse level and with more, captured and replayed bitwise (§81, the registry row of `src/amg/single.rs`) | D |

**Measured** (supervisor's runs, 2026-10-15; f64 build, then `single` in brackets).

- `POI(128)` PCG/GAMG at `1e-10`:
  - The levels are 2097152, 524306, 131244, 32879, 8227, 2059, 516, 129, 33 in both precisions
    [2097152, 524288, ..., 32].
  - Native: 45 iterations, single: 45, a ratio of 1.000 against a gate of 1.15 [39 and 39].
  - The §8.4 residuals of the answers are 1.502986e-12 native and 1.502995e-12 single. The two
    answers differ by 9.13e-14 relative [9.521613e-13 for both, bitwise equal].
  - Device bytes: native 449.65 MiB (206.52 float, 0.0045 acc, 243.13 label); single 207.68 MiB
    (103.26 float, 0.0045 acc, 104.42 label).
  - `rho = 0.4619` by (141.47), against a gate of 0.55. The float-and-acc-only ratio is 0.5000
    [275.15 MiB both, `rho = 1`].
- `POI(16)` pair: PCG/GAMG 10 iterations native and 10 single, 4096 of 4096 entries differing in
  their bits; the GAMG solver 31 and 31, 3681 of 4096 differing [9 and 9, 28 and 28, 0 differing].
- `POI(32)` `solver GAMG` at `1e-10`: 85 cycles in both precisions, §8.4 residual 4.689e-12 [70
  and 70, 5.619e-12].

The f32 copy holds under half the bytes because it drops the Galerkin slot lists and the duplicated
coarse addressing as well as halving every float array. Its iteration count equals the native one
here: the preconditioner's float rounding, about `2^-24` relative, is far below the V-cycle's own
contraction, as the cited design expects.

### 141.20 AMGX by dynamic load (AMX-01)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` §141.2 to §141.19 are left for the GAMG units
(AMG-02 onward) and AMX-02. This subsection says how the AMGX pressure backend of
`src/pressure/amgx.rs` reaches the library. Before AMX-01 the `amgx` Cargo feature
linked `amgxsh` at build time (`build.rs` emitted `cargo:rustc-link-lib=dylib=amgxsh`), so
`--features amgx` did not even build on a machine without an AMGX import library. Now
the library is opened at run time and the feature builds anywhere. No solve changes:
the configuration string, the CSR export of §48.2, the mode constants and the calls
in the solve are the same, so the f64 build is untouched and the feature-off build is
bit-for-bit what it was.

Sources: **NVIDIA AMGX** (BSD-3-Clause, <https://github.com/NVIDIA/AMGX>), release 2.5.0,
its public C API `include/amgx_c.h` (the functions already bound in
`src/pressure/amgx.rs`; this unit changes only how they are reached), and **Naumov, M.
et al. (2015), "AmgX: a library for GPU accelerated algebraic multigrid and
preconditioned iterative methods", *SIAM J. Sci. Comput.* 37(5) S602-S626,
doi:10.1137/140980260**, the paper docs/17 names for AMGX. **libloading** (ISC, already a
dependency through cudarc's `dynamic-loading`, NOTICE) opens the library. No AMGX source
is vendored or reproduced.

**The file.** `amgxsh.dll` on Windows and `libamgxsh.so` elsewhere: the shared build,
which is the only AMGX build that exports the C API.

**The search** (*DESIGN*). An explicit setting is used alone, so a typo never loads a
different copy of the library from somewhere else:

```
AMGX_DLL set and non-empty:  [ AMGX_DLL ]                                (141.20)
else AMGX_DIR set and non-empty, D = AMGX_DIR:
    [ D/<file>, D/bin/<file>, D/lib/<file>, D/build/<file>, D/build/Release/<file> ]
else:  [ <file> ]   (the bare name, so the system loader searches PATH)
```

The candidates are tried in order, and the first that opens is used. The library is
opened once per process, on the first query, and stays open. A library that opens but
lacks one of the bound entry points is refused, naming the entry point and the file.

**Availability.** With the feature off, the backend is listed and unavailable with the
reason "feature 'amgx' not enabled" (unchanged). With the feature on and no library,
it is listed and unavailable with the reason "AMGX library not loaded: tried <every
candidate>; set AMGX_DLL to the library file or AMGX_DIR to its directory", followed by
the loader's last error. `setup` returns the same reason as an error. The selector of
§8.3 therefore prints why AMGX was not a candidate, which is the file's original rule.

**`OFGPU_REQUIRE_AMGX`** (*DESIGN*). The value `1`, and only `1`, makes absence a
failure. A device test that needs AMGX then fails with "OFGPU_REQUIRE_AMGX=1 but
<reason>" instead of passing vacuously. Without it, such a test prints "AMGX not
loaded, skipped: <reason>" and passes, the convention of a machine without a card.

**The copy back** (a bug found by this unit's gate). `AMGX_vector_download` into a device pointer is a
device-to-device `cudaMemcpy`, which the CUDA runtime documents as not synchronising with the host, and AMGX
issues it on the runtime's legacy default stream. The crate's `Gpu` runs on a non-blocking stream, which does not
wait for the legacy one. The backend returned as soon as the call did, so the caller's next read of `p` raced the
copy: on the plume matrix AMGX converged in 22 iterations (residual 1.653e2 to 7.746e-11) and the field read back
was all zeros, `rel = 1.000`. `solve` now synchronises the whole context after the AMGX calls and returns only
then. Before AMX-01 the feature could not be linked on this machine (there is no import library), so the gate
had not been run against the crate's non-blocking stream.

**The modes** (`amgx_config.h`'s mode encoding, unchanged): `dDDI = 0x2001 = 8193` in the
f64 build and `dFFI = 0x2111 = 8465` under `single` (device memory, double or float
vectors and matrix, 32-bit indices).

**The recipe.** `tools/amgx/build.cmd` records how the DLL is built from the 2.5.0
sources with CUDA 13.3 for `sm_120`: CMake with Ninja, `CMAKE_NO_MPI`, C++17, and the
`--pre-include thrust/tuple.h` that CUDA 13's CCCL 3.x needs, because without it about 30
translation units of AMGX 2.5.0 do not compile. The DLL must contain SASS for the card
it runs on: an `sm_89`-only build fails on `sm_120` at `AMGX_matrix_create` with
`rc = 6` (THRUST_FAILURE). The recipe is written and not re-run in this unit (docs/17
A18). The gate below used the existing 2.5.0 build, `amgxsh.dll` of 135,625,728 bytes,
MD5 `67ba838e20c3ed60fd738632b3e8ef68`.

#### 141.20.1 The gates

| test | gate | class (docs/17 §5.1.4) |
|---|---|---|
| `pressure::amgx::tests::the_search_order_is_amgx_dll_then_amgx_dir_then_path` | (141.20) on fixed inputs, no environment read | D |
| `pressure::amgx::tests::only_the_value_1_requires_amgx` | `1` requires; `0`, `true`, the empty string and unset do not | D |
| `pressure::amgx::tests::require_turns_absence_into_an_error` | absent and required is an error naming `OFGPU_REQUIRE_AMGX=1` and the reason; absent and not required is a skip | D |
| `pressure::amgx::tests::a_missing_library_is_unavailable_with_the_paths_it_tried` (feature on) | a candidate that does not exist gives the "AMGX library not loaded" reason and names that path | D |
| `cargo build --release --features amgx`, and `--features "amgx single"`, with no AMGX on the machine | both compile | D |
| `pressure::tests::amgx_agrees_with_pbicgstab` (feature on, `OFGPU_REQUIRE_AMGX=1`, the 2.5.0 DLL) | AMGX and the PBiCGStab reference agree to `1e-8` relative on the 40×30×20 box | R |

Measured on 2026-10-11 (RTX 5070 Ti, the DLL above, deterministic over five runs): the plume gate gives

converged), so both rows pass; the dFFI row passes with a margin of 1.16x.

### 141.21 AMGX in the time loop: the kept structure, and the three-way comparison (AMX-02)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` This is the subsection after §141.20, and AMX-02 is the second AMGX unit.
§141.20 left the backend calling `AMGX_solver_setup` on every solve. That call rebuilds the whole classical-AMG
hierarchy from the new matrix. Before this unit it was most of AMGX's time on the plume matrix, and nobody had
measured it inside a time loop. Now the backend keeps the hierarchy's structure from one solve to the next and
re-sets up only what depends on the coefficients. `ofgpu-buoyant` runs AMGX in the time loop and prints what the
set-ups cost. The comparison below puts AMGX beside PBiCGStab and the native GAMG of §141.8.

Sources: **Naumov, M. et al. (2015), "AmgX: a library for GPU accelerated algebraic multigrid and preconditioned
iterative methods", *SIAM J. Sci. Comput.* 37(5) S602-S626, doi:10.1137/140980260** (title, journal, volume, issue
and pages checked against Crossref on 2026-10-15). It gives the split of AMGX into a set-up phase and a solve
phase. **NVIDIA AMGX 2.5.0** (BSD-3-Clause, <https://github.com/NVIDIA/AMGX>). Its reference manual
(`doc/AMGX_Reference.pdf`, `AMGX_solver_setup`) says "anytime the matrix changes AMGX solver setup must be called
again". The manual does not document the two things this unit uses, so the following files were read to learn what
they mean: `include/amgx_c.h` declares `AMGX_solver_resetup(AMGX_solver_handle, AMGX_matrix_handle)`, in its
"C-API deprecated" block; `src/core.cu` registers `structure_reuse_levels` as "controls reuse of AMG hierarchy,
0 - everything rebuilds, 1 - reuse coloring on the finest level, 2 - reuse coloring on the next level, etc.",
default 0; `src/amg_solver.cu` (`setup`, `resetup`) and `src/amg.cu` (the level loop) say what the parameter does in
each call. These files were read for meaning only. No AMGX code is reproduced here.

**The hierarchy, solve by solve.** The matrix `A_0` of one session (one `setup` of the backend) changes from solve
to solve. Its pattern is the CSR of §48.2, and it does not change:

```
first solve of a session:      full set-up; the levels {A_l}, prolongations P_l and restrictions R_l      (141.21a)
                               are built from A_0, as AMGX_solver_setup does
later solve, reuse on:         P_l and R_l kept;  A_{l+1} = R_l A_l P_l,  l = 0 .. L-2, from the new A_0;  (141.21b)
                               the smoothers and the coarsest solve redone from the new A_l
later solve, reuse off:        full set-up again, as (141.21a)                                          (141.21c)
```

(141.21b) is a Galerkin coarse operator on a kept coarsening, which is what §141.8's re-gather does for the native
GAMG. Each level's operator is the Galerkin product of the new matrix, so the cycle preconditions the new `A_0` and
not the old one, and PCG is still run to AMGX's own tolerance (`1e-12` relative to the initial residual, §141.20's
configuration). What can change is the iteration count, because the kept coarsening was built for the first
matrix's strength of connection. Measured here, it did not change: 20 iterations with and without reuse (below).

**The calls** (*DESIGN*). With reuse on, the session's configuration is `DEFAULT_CONFIG` plus
`amg:structure_reuse_levels=-1` (`REUSE_KEY`, in the AMG preconditioner's scope `amg`). Every solve after the
session's first then calls `AMGX_solver_resetup`, and in that call `-1` keeps every level's structure. With reuse
off, the key is absent (AMGX's default 0) and every solve calls `AMGX_solver_setup`, which is §141.20's
behaviour. The key is never paired with `AMGX_solver_setup`. With `-1`, that call returns at once on a matrix it
has set up before (`amg_solver.cu`), so the hierarchy, values included, would stay the first matrix's for the
whole run. That would be a frozen preconditioner, not a re-set-up. `AMGX_solver_resetup` is the 23rd bound entry
point. A library that lacks it is refused by §141.20's rule, and the 2.5.0 DLL exports it.

**The switch** (*DESIGN*). Reuse is on by default. `OFGPU_AMGX_REUSE=0`, and only the value `0`, turns it off
(`reuse_from`, the rule of §141.20's `OFGPU_REQUIRE_AMGX` turned around). `AmgxBackend::with_reuse` sets it in
code. It exists so that the saving can be measured against the full set-up. It is not a tuning knob.

**The timing.** A solve's set-up time runs from the matrix upload (`AMGX_matrix_upload_all` on the first solve,
`AMGX_matrix_replace_coefficients` after it) to the end of the set-up call. The CUDA context is synchronised on
each side, because AMGX works on the legacy default stream (§141.20). `setup_secs` reports it for the decision
table's set-up column (§141.8), and `run_summary` gives `ofgpu-buoyant`'s end-of-run line: the full set-ups and
the re-set-ups, with the mean of each. The vector uploads, the solve and the copy back come after the set-up, so
the order of the calls changed, but AMGX's answer does not depend on it.

## 142. Gate 95-A diagnosis and the GMRES outer loop

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Docs/17 §4.3 allocates §142 to VAL-10 (§142.1, the diagnosis) and VAL-11
(§142.2, the GMRES outer loop). §109.7 measured Gate 95-A and found it holding at 2.5:1 and missing at 5:1 and
10:1, without saying whether the miss is the outer loop's or the discretisation's. §142.1 answers that by solving
for the discrete fixed point of §109.6's block map directly, so that the loop's answer and the discretisation's
answer can be read apart. No solver numerics change.

### 142.1 The exact discrete fixed point of the block map

**What is solved.** In linear elasticity the block matrix `A` of (109.1)-(109.2) depends on the mesh and the
material only, and once the boundary values are closed the source of (109.3)-(109.5) is affine in the cell
displacement. So the residual of (109.6) at the closed state is affine,

```text
  ub*(u) = the boundary values at which one more boundary pass of §95.2 changes nothing
  R(u)   = A u - source(u, ub*(u)) = B u + R(0),     B e_k = R(e_k) - R(0)                  (142.1)
  u*     = the solution of  B u* = -R(0)                                                     (142.2)
```

with `e_k` the unit vector of flat unknown `k = 3c + i` (109.8). The loop of §109.6 carries `ub` from one
application to the next, with three boundary passes each. At its fixed point `ub` is a fixed point of three passes,
and therefore of one, so `u*` of (142.2) is the loop's own fixed point and not that of some other map. `ub*` is
found by repeating single passes until the boundary values move by no more than `1e-14` of the field's magnitude.
From a zero start this took 93 passes on every mesh below; a cap of 2000 refuses by name. The columns of `B` come
from the device's own `correct_boundary`, `BlockOperator::assemble` and `residual`, so `B` is the operator the
loop iterates, kernel for kernel. The factorisation is dense, in `f64`, with partial pivoting (`P B = L U`). The
1-norm condition number is estimated by Hager's method (W. W. Hager, *SIAM J. Sci. Stat. Comput.* 5 (1984)
311-316, DOI `10.1137/0905023`; in the LAPACK xLACON form of N. J. Higham, *ACM TOMS* 14 (1988) 381-396, DOI
`10.1145/50063.214386`), with at most five steps:

```text
  x = (1/N, ..., 1/N);  repeat:  y = B^-1 x,  xi = sign(y),  z = B^-T xi,  j = argmax |z_j|;
  stop when |z_j| <= z.x (after the first step), else x = e_j;   cond1 ~ ||B||_1 ||y||_1      (142.3)
```

A fixed point **exists** when the factorisation finds no zero pivot, `cond1 < 1e15`, and the device's residual of
(109.6), evaluated at `u*` with its boundary closed, satisfies

```text
  max_c |R_c(u*)| <= 1e-12 scale,     scale = max_c ||diag[c]||_F max_c |u*_c|                  (142.4)
```

The probe is `solid::coupled::tests::gate_95a_probe_the_exact_fixed_point_of_the_block_map`. It is `#[ignore]`
and `#[cfg(not(feature = "single"))]`, because its subject is the f64 discrete fixed point. It runs Gate 95-A's
beams (§109.6: plane strain, `E = 200` GPa, `nu = 0.3`, `P = 1e5`, `2c = 0.2`, cubic cells, one cell through the
thickness) at 2.5:1 on `n_y = 4, 8, 16`, at 5:1 on `n_y = 4, 8, 16` (N = 3840 at most), and at 10:1 on
`n_y = 4, 8`. It asserts (142.4) on every mesh. On every 2.5:1 mesh it also asserts that §109.6's own loop
(Anderson of depth five, three boundary passes) converges and that its answer equals `u*` to `1e-9` relative
(`max |u_loop - u*| / max |u*|`). For that comparison the loop runs to 12 decades with the block solve at
(109.11) `1e-14`. The coder's first probe run, with the block solve at Gate 95-A's `1e-12`, put the loop's answer
`3.6e-9` from `u*` on `n_y = 8`. That gap is the inner solve's floor, not a property of the loop, and it is six
decades below the discretisation error. The whole probe takes 32 s. Its two dense-algebra tests
(`dense_lu_solves_both_ways_and_hager_estimates_the_inverse_norm`,

reach. The condition estimate grows with slenderness and refinement, from 9.5e3 to 7.8e6, which is still about
nine decades short of `1/eps`. Gate 95-A's shortfall therefore has two separate causes:

1. **The loop.** "Converges on every mesh" fails at 5:1 and 10:1 on `n_y = 4` only. The discrete solution exists
   there (`e_u` 8.3e-3 and 1.4e-3), and the Anderson loop around the block map diverges from it (5:1) or stalls at
   `q_obs = 0.992` (10:1). This half belongs to the loop, and it is what VAL-11's GMRES outer iteration is for.
   Where the loop does converge, it lands on `u*`: to 1e-11 on 2.5:1, and to §109.7's printed digits on the 5:1 and
   10:1 meshes it converged on.
2. **The discretisation.** The displacement order is short of 1.9 at the exact fixed point itself: 1.135 at 5:1
   between `n_y = 8` and 16, and 0.032 at 10:1 between 4 and 8. No outer iteration can change either number. The
   orders are not monotone (5:1 gives 3.85 and then 1.14; the 5:1 tip error passes near zero at `n_y = 8`), and
   the same scheme gives 2.5-2.8 on the 2.5:1 beam. So the slender beams are read before their asymptotic range,
   and the stress order (1.45-1.49 everywhere, against a bar of 0.9) is not the problem. This half is VAL-12's
   fourth mesh (`n_y = 32`, D-VAL-6). Whether the order then settles near 2, or near 1 (the D-VAL-7 trigger for
   VAL-13's implicit tangential stencil, §109.4), is VAL-12's measurement. Two levels cannot settle it.

What this subsection does not do: it changes no gate, no tolerance and no default. Gate 95-A's rows in
`ofgpu-validate` are unchanged. It does not run 10:1 at `n_y = 16`, because N = 7680 is over the probe's dense
budget; that row is §109.7's converged loop. It is not an f32 measurement. In the single build the probe does not
exist. The two dense-algebra tests sit in the library test crate, which does not compile in the single build at
present (pre-existing f32 errors in other modules' tests); they use no `Scalar` and would hold there unchanged.


### 142.2 GMRES on the block map's state, and Gate 95-A per loop

**Sources.** Y. Saad and M. H. Schultz, "GMRES: a generalized minimal residual algorithm for solving
nonsymmetric linear systems", *SIAM J. Sci. Stat. Comput.* 7 (1986) 856-869, DOI `10.1137/0907058`: the
Arnoldi basis by modified Gram-Schmidt, the least-squares problem by Givens rotations, the restart. H. F. Walker
and P. Ni, *SIAM J. Numer. Anal.* 49 (2011) 1715-1735, DOI `10.1137/10078356X`: on a linear map, Anderson
acceleration that drops no column is essentially GMRES, so §109.6's Anderson of depth five is a truncated
relative of what this subsection runs. No GPL-licensed source was consulted. No solver numerics change: the
block map, its kernels, the block solve and every default are §109's.

**The state and the map.** §142.1 found that the loop carries two things from one application to the next:
the cell displacement `u` and the boundary values `ub` its three boundary passes start from. GMRES iterates
both. With `n_c` cells and `n_bf` boundary faces the state is the `3 (n_c + n_bf)` numbers

```text
  x = (u, ub),    Phi(x) = (F(u; ub), ub'(u; ub))                                            (142.5)
```

where one application writes `x` into `d.u.f` and `d.u.bf`, runs `apply_block` (three boundary passes, the
assembly, one block solve from `x = u`) and reads back the solve's answer and the boundary values the passes
left. In linear elasticity `Phi` is affine, `Phi(x) = J x + c`, and its fixed point is §142.1's `u*` with its
closed boundary. The fixed-point residual `r(x) = Phi(x) - x = c - (I - J) x` is the residual of the linear
system `(I - J) x = c`, and GMRES solves that system with no operator except `Phi`:

```text
  (I - J) v = v - (Phi(x0 + s v) - Phi(x0)) / s,     s = max(||x0||_2, ||r(x0)||_2)          (142.6)
```

for a unit vector `v`. `Phi` is affine, so (142.6) holds for any `s`; `s` the size of the state keeps the block
solve's own relative error relative in every difference. One cycle of GMRES(`m`) from `x0`:

```text
  g0 = Phi(x0);  r0 = g0 - x0;  beta = ||r0||;  v_1 = r0 / beta;  g = (beta, 0, ..., 0)
  for j = 1..m:  w = (I - J) v_j by (142.6)                      one application of Phi
                 h_ij = w . v_i,  w -= h_ij v_i   (i = 1..j, modified Gram-Schmidt)
                 h_(j+1)j = ||w||;  the earlier rotations on column j, then its own:
                 (c_j, s_j) = (h_jj, h_(j+1)j) / hypot(h_jj, h_(j+1)j);  g_(j+1) = -s_j g_j;  g_j = c_j g_j
                 stop the cycle if |g_(j+1)| <= target or h_(j+1)j <= eps beta;  v_(j+1) = w / h_(j+1)j
  x = x0 + V y,  H y = g on the j columns (back substitution)                              (142.7)
```

The dot products, `H`, `g` and `y` are `f64` whatever the crate's `Scalar` is; the state vectors are `Vec3`
in `Scalar`. The code is `solid::outer::gmres_fixed_point` (host) and `solid::coupled::solve` with
`Relaxation::Gmres(m)` (the device application). The segregated loop refuses `Gmres` by name.

**What is counted, what stops it, what is accepted.** One outer iteration is one application of `Phi`: a
cycle's opening application and each Arnoldi step count alike, and `maxOuter` caps their sum. The stop reads only
the TRUE residual `||r(x)||_2` over the whole state, at a cycle's opening application: converged when it is at
most `10^-decades` of the first one. The least-squares estimate `|g_(j+1)|` only ends a cycle early. Convergence
accepts `Phi(x)`, as the Anderson loop accepts `F(u)`, and the loop ends with the same closing boundary
correction. A true residual that is not finite or grows a million-fold over the first is `Error::Diverged`, named.
`norms` holds the true norm at each opening application and the estimate at each Arnoldi step, so (109.13)'s
`q_obs` is read over both. `omegas` stays empty. The stop is therefore not Anderson's: Anderson reads the `u` part
of the residual of the lagged map, and GMRES reads the whole state's, which is never smaller.

**The case knob.** `mechanics.solver.outer` is `"anderson"` (the default, §95.3's Anderson of depth five) or
`"gmres"` (GMRES(50), `solid::outer::GMRES_RESTART`). Any other name is refused listing both, and `"gmres"`
without `coupled: true` is refused (96.3 row 23). The banner and the summary name the loop. Pair 12 of §96.4 turns
it.

**Measured** (2026-10-15, RTX 5070 Ti, f64; the GPU shared with two other lanes).

- On the host, an affine map on six unknowns whose Picard iteration diverges (eigenvalues 2, -1.5, 0.5, 3, 0.9,
  -0.2): GMRES(50) takes 8 applications (one to open, six Arnoldi steps, one to check) and lands on
  `(I - M)^-1 c` to 2.9e-16 (`gmres_finds_the_fixed_point_of_an_affine_map_picard_cannot`).
- **The gate.** From rest on the `6^3` free-expansion block, with the block solve at (109.11) `1e-12`, GMRES(50)
  reaches eight decades (8.06) in **16** outer iterations and 283 BiCGStab iterations, within 3.5e-9 of
  `alpha dT x`. The bar is 20. Anderson(5) on the same problem takes 15 and 223
  (`gmres_reaches_eight_decades_on_the_free_expansion_block_in_twenty`).
- Two GMRES runs capped at six applications leave `u`, `ub` and the norm history equal bit for bit
  (`gmres_runs_of_a_fixed_count_are_bitwise_identical`). The device work of one outer iteration, one
  `apply_block` with a fixed-iteration block solve (4 iterations), captures into a CUDA graph of 128 nodes
  (121 kernels, 7 memsets) and replays bitwise three times over 4 buffers and 2592 values, per §81.7
  (`the_gmres_matvec_replays_bitwise`).
- Pair 12 on the bar of §96.4: Anderson 18 outer iterations, GMRES 16, `max|du|` 3.824e-13 against
  `max|u_a|` 5.480e-5.

At the reference, `p_u` on 16 -> 32 is **1.416** at 5:1 and **1.745** at 10:1. Anderson's eight decades of the
lagged `u` residual leave up to 1.6e-5 of iteration error on the 10:1 beams, which is ten per cent of `e_u` there,
and that error is what put §109.7's 10:1 order at 1.896, 0.004 short of the bar. The fixed point's own order is
1.745. GMRES's eight decades of the whole state's residual stay within 1e-6.

**The attribution, after GMRES.** §142.1 split Gate 95-A's shortfall in two. The loop's half is closed: GMRES(50)
converges on every mesh of both slender beams, and "converges on every mesh" holds at 5:1 and 10:1 on this loop.
The discretisation's half is not: at the fixed point the displacement order on the finest pair is 1.416 at 5:1
and 1.745 at 10:1, both short of 1.9, and no outer iteration can move either. Gate 95-A on the GMRES loop is
therefore **MISSED** at 5:1 and 10:1 on `p_u` alone, asserted and printed as such by `ofgpu-validate`; the
stress order (1.45-1.47) and the finest tip (within 0.017 %) hold on every beam. Both orders still rise with
refinement (5:1 from 1.135 to 1.416, 10:1 from 1.318 to 1.745), so the D-VAL-7 trigger still does not fire.
Whether they settle near 2 past `n_y = 32` is the open question; it is the D-VAL-7 question of §109.7 asked again
with the iteration error removed, and the measurement that answers it is a fifth mesh (`n_y = 64`, 40 960 cells
at 10:1) or §109.4's implicit tangential stencil (VAL-13), neither of which this unit builds.

What this subsection does not do: no bar, tolerance, mesh or default moved. `outer: "anderson"` and every
caller that does not ask for GMRES run the code they ran, and Gate 95-A's Anderson rows print the same digits.
The single build compiles the GMRES path; it is not measured there. Three of the new tests (the host affine
map, the gate, pair 12) hold bounds below f32 round-off and carry §112.3's attribute; the fixed-count and replay
tests are bitwise in either build, and the probe is f64 only.

## 143. The 1-D RANS oracle and Wilcox 2006

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Docs/17 §4.3 allocates §143 to VAL-20 (§143.1, the oracle), VAL-21
(§143.2, Wilcox 2006 and the measured TG0 bands) and VAL-22a. The oracle is `src/vv/rans1d.rs`: host only, `f64`
whatever the crate's `Scalar` is, no `Gpu`, no kernel, no capture row, and no solver numerics change. It replaces
the independent one-dimensional discretisation that §114 measured with and that was written outside the tree.

### 143.1 The fully developed pipe on TG0's radial cell set

**Sources.** Menter, Kuntz & Langtry 2003 and Menter 1994 for kOmegaSST, as §6.3 tabulates them; the wall-cell
treatment of §6.4 as `wallfunctions.rs` implements it; Wilcox's 1988 k-omega as the NASA Turbulence Modeling
Resource states it, <https://tmbwg.github.io/turbmodels/wilcox.html> (read 2026-10-11; US-government
documentation, not source), citing Wilcox, *AIAA J.* 26(11) (1988) 1299-1310, DOI `10.2514/3.10041` (cited, not
read); Launder & Sharma 1974 as §33.1 states it; Spalart-Allmaras SA-noft2 as §56.1-§56.3 state it, from the TMR
page <https://tmbwg.github.io/turbmodels/spalart.html> and ICCFD7-1902; Tucker 1998 for the wall distance (§6.6);
Celik et al. 2008 for the extrapolation (§94, `vv::observed_order`). The pipe metrics are `tools/cad/post.py`'s
`pipe_block` definitions, this tree's own.

**Geometry (143.1).** TG0's mesh (§114.1, `tools/cad/pipe_mesh.py`) is a wedge of angle `theta = 5 deg` cut from a
pipe of radius `R = 0.025 m`. The vertices lie at radii `r_i` in the two planes at `+-theta/2`, so a cell's
section normal to `x` is the trapezoid with corners `(r cos(theta/2), +-r sin(theta/2))`, and its wall face is the
flat chord at distance `rho_w = R cos(theta/2)` from the axis. In the bisector coordinate `rho = r cos(theta/2)`,
with `t = tan(theta/2)` and periodic length `L`, a cell between faces `rho_a < rho_b` has

```
A_f = 2 L t rho_f                 radial face area
V   = L t (rho_b^2 - rho_a^2)     volume
c   = (2/3)(rho_b^3 - rho_a^3)/(rho_b^2 - rho_a^2)     centroid                            (143.1)
```

which is exactly a polar finite-volume cell of a pipe of radius `rho_w`. The common factor `2 L t` cancels from
every balance below, so the oracle carries `A_f = rho_f` and `V = (rho_b^2 - rho_a^2)/2`.

**The cell set (143.2).** `n` cells graded geometrically to the wall: `q` solves `h1 (q^n - 1)/(q - 1) = R` by 200
bisection steps on `(1, 4)` (`wedge_mesh.solve_q`), and the vertex radii counted from the wall are
`r_i = R (1 - (q^i - 1)/(q^n - 1))`, `i = 0..n` (`r_0 = R`, `r_n = 0` exactly). TG0's level `l` has
`n = 40 * 2^l` and `h1 = (R / 2358) 2^-l`: L0 is 40 cells, L1 80, and §114.3's 160/320/640 are levels 2/3/4.

**The discrete operators (143.3).** Internal face `f` between the inner cell `P` and the outer cell `N`:
weight `w_f = (c_N - rho_f)/(c_N - c_P)`, face value `phi_f = w_f phi_P + (1 - w_f) phi_N`, distance
`delta_f = c_N - c_P`. The wall face: `delta_w = rho_w - c_P` (this is `b_y`). The axis face has zero area. Gauss
gradient of a cell field with wall-face value `phi_w`:

```
grad(phi)_P = 2 [phi_b rho_b - phi_a rho_a - phi_P (rho_b - rho_a)] / (rho_b^2 - rho_a^2)                       (143.4)
```

(the wedge faces contribute the `-phi_P (rho_b - rho_a)` term). Diffusion of `phi` through face `f`:
`Gamma_f A_f (phi_N - phi_P)/delta_f`, with `Gamma_f = w_f Gamma_P + (1 - w_f) Gamma_N` for a cell diffusivity
`Gamma = nu + sigma nu_t` (`turbGammaInternalCell`), and `nu` alone on the wall face, where `nu_t` is
`fixedValue 0`.

**Momentum (143.5).** With the body force `g = 2 u_tau,in^2 / R`, `u_tau,in = Re_tau nu / R`, `nu = 1.516e-5 m^2/s`
(`turb_integral.pipe_drive`), each cell satisfies `sum_f (nu + nu_t)_f A_f (U_N - U_P)/delta_f + g V_P = 0`,
`U = 0` on the wall face. Summed over the cells inside face `f` it telescopes to the exact statement

```
-(nu + nu_t)_f (U_N - U_P)/delta_f = g rho_f / 2     at every face, the wall face included                       (143.6)
```

so the measured `u_tau^2 = nu U_P/delta_w` equals `g rho_w / 2` to round-off for every model. This is why
`u_tau = 0.349538` in every row of §114 although the case was driven at `u_tau,in = 0.349705`:
`sqrt(cos(2.5 deg)) = 0.999524`.

**kOmegaSST (143.7).** §6.3's equations with this tree's choices: `S = |dU/drho|`, `P = G/nu_t = (dU/drho)^2`,
`nu_t = a1 k / max(a1 omega, b1 F2 S)`, `G = nu_t P`, k production `min(G, c1 beta* k omega)`, omega production
`blend(gamma) P`, the cross-diffusion `2 (1 - F1) sigma_w2 grad k . grad omega / omega`, blended `sigma` per cell
and interpolated as `Gamma` above; `F1`, `F2` and `CD_kw+ = max(CD_kw, 1e-10)` exactly as `sstBlending`, with `y`
Tucker's distance from the same operators (`laplacian(phi) = -1`, `phi_w = 0`, then
`y = -|grad phi| + sqrt(|grad phi|^2 + 2 phi)`). The wall-adjacent cell is pinned, as `wfOmegaWallCell` pins it:

```
omega_P = sqrt(omega_log^2 + omega_vis^2),  omega_log = sqrt(k_P)/(C_mu^1/4 kappa delta_w),
omega_vis = 6 nu/(beta_1 delta_w^2),  kappa = 0.41, C_mu = 0.09, beta_1 = 0.075                                  (143.8)
```

and its `G` is §6.4's blended wall production `e^{1/Gamma} nu |U_P/delta_w| C_mu^1/4 sqrt(k_P)/(kappa delta_w)`,
`Gamma = -0.01 y+^4/(1 + 5 y+)`, `y+ = C_mu^1/4 delta_w sqrt(k_P)/nu`, which is zero to round-off at TG0's
`y+ < 0.1`. `k = 0` on the wall face; omega's wall face is zero-gradient (its only reader is the pinned cell).

**k-omega 1988 (143.9).** `nu_t = k/omega`, `Dk/Dt = div((nu + sigma_k nu_t) grad k) + G - beta* k omega`,
`Domega/Dt = div((nu + sigma_w nu_t) grad omega) + gamma P - beta omega^2`, with the TMR page's constants
`sigma_k = sigma_w = 0.5`, `beta* = 0.09`, `beta = 3/40`, `gamma = 5/9`, and the wall cell of (143.8). §6.2's
`beta = 0.072` (the later editions', which `KOmegaCoeffs` carries) is a named alternative constructor, not the
default: the oracle's model is the one its name says.

**Launder-Sharma (143.10).** §33.1 as written, `k = epsilon~ = 0` on the wall face, `D = 2 nu |grad sqrt(k)|^2`
with (143.4) and `sqrt(k)_w = 0`, and `E = 2 nu nu_t |grad grad U|^2` with
`|grad grad U|^2 = (dg/drho)^2 + (g/rho)^2`, `g = dU/drho` from (143.4), `dg/drho` from (143.4) with the
zero-gradient wall value `g_w = g_P`, and `g/rho` the hoop curvature of the axisymmetric field.

**SA-noft2 (143.11).** (56.1)-(56.6) with `c_t3 = 0`, (56.9) for `Stil`, `Omega = |dU/drho|`, `r = 10` where
`Stil <= 0`, `nu~ = 0` on the wall face, face diffusivity `(nu + nu~_f)/sigma`, `d` Tucker's distance by default
(the solver's choice); the exact `rho_w - c` is selectable for every model.

**The iteration (143.12).** One Picard sweep solves each equation's tridiagonal system exactly (Thomas): the
transported turbulence fields first, under-relaxed `phi <- phi + alpha (phi* - phi)`, then `nu_t`, then `U` from
(143.5) unrelaxed. Sinks are implicit with the previous iterate, productions explicit, a source of either sign is
split by sign. The sweep stops when the largest relative change of `U` and of each transported field is under
`1e-11`; `alpha` is 0.7 for both k-omega models, 0.5 for Launder-Sharma and 0.1 for SA, which oscillates at 0.3.
Under-relaxation does not move the converged answer.

**Metrics (143.13)**, `post.py`'s: `U_b = sum U V / sum V`; `u_tau = sqrt(nu U_P/delta_w)` in the wall cell;
`f = 8 (u_tau/U_b)^2`; `U_axis = U_0 - (U_1 - U_0) c_0^2/(c_1^2 - c_0^2)`, the even fit through the two innermost
centroids; defect `(U_axis - U_b)/u_tau`; and `nu_t,axis/(u_tau R)` with `R = 0.025 m`.

### 143.2 Wilcox 2006 k-omega in the oracle, and the five models' TG0 bands measured

**Sources.** Wilcox's 2006 k-omega as the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource states it,
<https://tmbwg.github.io/turbmodels/wilcox.html>, section "Wilcox (2006) k-omega" (read 2026-10-11, equations and
constants read from the rendered equation images; US-government documentation, not source), citing Wilcox,
"Formulation of the k-omega Turbulence Model Revisited", *AIAA J.* 46(11) (2008) 2823-2838, DOI `10.2514/1.36541`
(cited, not read: paywalled), and Wilcox, *Turbulence Modeling for CFD*, 3rd ed., DCW Industries (2006) (cited, not
read). The band references are those of `tools/cad/turb_integral.py`, from Schlichting's lecture series, NACA TM 1218
(1949): Prandtl's smooth-pipe law (its eq 16.26), Blasius (16.4), the log law `u+ = 2.5 ln y+ + 5.5` (16.14) and
Nikuradse's core defect 4.07 (16.22). The page's HTML alt text writes `chi_omega` with `Omega_ij Omega_ij`; the
rendered image, used here, has `Omega_ij Omega_jk`.

**The model (143.15)**, incompressible, `nu_t = k / omega_hat`:

```
Dk/Dt = P - beta* omega k + div[(nu + sigma_k k/omega) grad k]
Dw/Dt = gamma (omega/k) P - beta omega^2 + div[(nu + sigma_w k/omega) grad omega] + (sigma_d/omega) grad k . grad omega
omega_hat = max(omega, C_lim sqrt(2 Sbar_ij Sbar_ij / beta*)),   P = nu_t 2 S_ij S_ij
beta = beta_0 f_beta,  f_beta = (1 + 85 chi)/(1 + 100 chi),  chi = |Omega_ij Omega_jk Shat_ki| / (beta* omega)^3
Shat_ki = S_ki - (1/2)(du_m/dx_m) delta_ki,   sigma_d = 0 if grad k . grad omega <= 0, else 1/8
sigma_k 0.6, sigma_w 0.5, beta* 0.09, gamma 13/25, C_lim 7/8, beta_0 0.0708                                     (143.15)
```

with the page's identity `gamma = beta_0/beta* - sigma_w kappa^2/sqrt(beta*)` at `kappa = 0.40`. The diffusivities
carry `k/omega`, not `nu_t`. No production limiter (the page's "Wilcox2006", not "-klim"); in incompressible flow
the "m", "s" and "e" variants coincide.

**In the pipe (143.16).** `2 S_ij S_ij = (dU/drho)^2`, so `omega_hat = max(omega, C_lim |dU/drho| / sqrt(beta*))` and
`gamma (omega/k) P = gamma (omega/omega_hat)(dU/drho)^2`, the form the oracle evaluates (no division by `k`). A
unidirectional shear has `Omega Omega` diagonal and `S` off-diagonal in the same axes, so every product in `chi`
holds an exact zero and `f_beta = 1` bitwise. The cross-diffusion is a non-negative source, explicit; it is non-zero
in 33 of L1_lo's 80 cells at Re_tau 576.69 and 44 at 2358, and the stress limiter is inactive in every cell of the
converged L1 pipe at both. The sweep is (143.12)'s, `alpha = 0.7`, `nu_t` rebuilt from the new `k`, `omega` and the
sweep's `dU/drho`. The wall-adjacent cell is (143.8) unchanged: its `omega_vis = 6 nu/(beta_1 delta_w^2)` keeps
`beta_1 = 0.075`, the wall function's own constant (`WallFunctionCoeffs::beta1`, `wallfunctions.rs`), not the
model's `beta_0`, as for the other two k-omega models, because that is what a device run of this model would use.

**The band metrics (143.17)**, `post.py`'s `pipe_block` on the oracle's pipe of radius `rho_w`:
`Re_D = U_b 2 rho_w / nu`; the measured `Re_tau = u_tau rho_w / nu`; f against Prandtl,
`(2.0 log10(2 sqrt(8) Re_tau,in) - 0.8)^-2`, at the case's INPUT Re_tau; f against Blasius `0.3164 Re_D^-1/4` at
the measured Re_D; the log-law deviation `max |U/u_tau - (2.5 ln y+ + 5.5)|` over the cells with
`30 <= y+ <= 0.2 Re_tau`, `y+ = (rho_w - c) u_tau / nu`; the defect against 4.07. TG0's bands (§114.1): Prandtl and
Blasius within 5 %, log law within 1.0, defect within 10 %. `D = 2 rho_w` (not `2R`, not `post.py`'s
area-equivalent diameter) is the one that reproduces §114.3's Blasius column at both Re_tau.

**The gates (143.18)**, added to `tests/rans1d.rs`, both builds, the same assertions:

| test | what | class |
|------|------|-------|

| `wilcox2006_cross_diffusion_is_zero_unless_grad_k_dot_grad_omega_is_positive` | `+0.0` bits for a negative, an orthogonal and a cancelling dot; 0.1875 and 2.0 exactly; on the solved L1_lo pipe `+0.0` in every cell with `gk gw <= 0`, positive elsewhere, both sets non-empty | D |
| `wilcox2006_f_beta_is_one_for_simple_shear` | `f_beta` bits `== 1.0` for three shears (one tilted); `[[1,2,0],[1,0,3],[0,1,0]]` at omega 10 gives 85729/100729 within 1e-15 | D, A |
| `wilcox2006_pipe_matches_the_supervisor_oracle` | L1, Re_tau 576.69: U_b 6.089861407, f 0.0263551108, defect 3.857669312, `nu_t,axis/(u_tau R)` 0.09696406419; Re_tau 2358: U_b 30.73986073, f 0.01729333019, defect 3.590450099; 1e-6 rel | P |
| `tg0_bands_reproduce_spec_lit_114` | (143.17) on SST against §114's own band numbers, below | P |

**What the table says for D-VAL-5** (docs/17 §11 item 3: Wilcox 2006 on the device only if the oracle closes the
TG0 bands). Wilcox 2006 closes Prandtl and Blasius at both Re_tau, and the defect at 576.69, but not the log-law
band at either (1.134 and 1.179 against 1.0) and not the defect at 2358 (-11.8 %). So the oracle does not close
TG0 with Wilcox 2006, and the trigger the plan states does not fire. No model closes all four bands at both Re_tau:
SA-noft2 closes all four at 2358 and misses only Blasius at 576.69. The log-law band's reference is Nikuradse's
`kappa 0.40, B 5.5`, while the three k-omega models produce a log layer of `kappa` about 0.41 (SST, 1988) or 0.40 (2006,
by its gamma); a band missed by 0.13 to 0.37 in u+ is partly the reference line's intercept. That is a reading, not
a measurement of the intercept.

**Not claimed.** The oracle discretises each model's equations on TG0's cells; its table is the models' answer on
that cell set with a pinned wall-cell omega, not a device run and not validation of the solver. Wilcox 2006 exists
only in the oracle: there is no device kernel, case keyword or registry row (VAL-22a-c, conditional on D-VAL-5).

### 143.5 Gate 131-P: TG0's turbulent pipe on the true wedge, kOmegaSST, replayed (VAL-23)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Docs/17 VAL-23. 짠143.3 and 짠143.4 were allocated to VAL-22a and VAL-22c,
which are not built because D-VAL-5 did not fire (짠143.2), so this unit records kOmegaSST only and there is no
`kOmega2006` case keyword. No new equation: the metrics are (143.13) and the bands (143.17), evaluated by
`vv::rans1d` itself.

**The rig.** TG0's pipe (짠114.1) on 짠119.0's wedge: `R = 0.025 m`, `theta = 5 deg`, periodic length `L = 0.1 m`
in 4 axial cells, `nu = 1.516e-5 m^2/s`, `x` the radius, `z` the axis, `zmin`/`zmax` a cyclic pair. The wedge is
the tangent one, so its radial faces are the planes `x = r_i` and its wall is at `x = R`: (143.1) with
`theta_deg = 0` (`rho = r`) is the same cell set, and `rans1d::PipeMesh` is built from the device's own graded
nodes. The drive is (143.5)'s `g_z = 2 u_tau,in^2 / R`, `u_tau,in = Re_tau nu / R`: 9.78347667 m/s^2 at
`Re_tau = 576.69`, 163.567108 at 2358. TG0's wall (`U = 0`, `k` and `nu_t` fixedValue 0, `omega`
`omegaWallFunction`, `T` fixedValue), TG0's numerics (SIMPLE, relaxation 0.7 on `U`, `k`, `omega`, `T` and 0.3
on `p`, `bounded Gauss linearUpwind grad(U)`, `bounded Gauss upwind` for `k` and `omega`), and 짠114.5's O1: the
`k`/`omega` PBiCGStab `tolerance 1e-12`, `relTol 0.01`. The start state is `U_z = U_b` of Prandtl's law and TG0's
own `k`, `omega` (`case_writer.py` `turb_refs`, `I = 1 %`, `l = 3 mm`). Levels `l = 0, 1, 2`: `n = 40 2^l`
radial cells, the wall cell `(R/2358) 2^-l` (143.2), `mesh.grading.x.expansion = q^-(n-1)` = 0.00306719135840698,
0.00297925479726894, 0.00293619304606138. `cases/pipeTurb576.jsonc` and `cases/pipeTurb2358.jsonc` are level 1;
levels 0 and 2 are copies with only `cells` and `expansion` edited.

**Found on the way: a cyclic patch inherits a wall function from the catch-all rule.** A JSONC case needs a
catch-all patch rule for its cyclic pair (`cases/README.md`), and every catch-all rule in the shipped cases is
`"kind": "wall"`. With `turbulence.wallTreatment` at its default, that rule's `k`, `omega` (or `epsilon`) and
`nut` are completed to `kqRWallFunction`, `omegaWallFunction` and `nutkWallFunction` on the cyclic patches as well
(짠29.1, route b). The solver's boundary kind there is still `Cyclic` (`field_setup::topology_override`), but its
wall-cell set is read from the field's patch TYPE names (`field_setup::faces_where`, through
`WallFaces::from_case`), which does not consult the patch kind, so every cell next to a cyclic face is pinned as a
wall cell. Measured at `Re_tau = 576.69` with the catch-all naming only `U`, `p` and `T`: on level 0, after one
iteration, `omega` in the cells next to the cyclic faces is 27.97 (the log-branch pin at
half an axial cell from the "wall") where the two interior stations carry 34 to 46 across the core; on level 1 from rest, after 8000
iterations, the four axial stations differ by up to 0.4425 m/s in `U_z` (6.7 % of `U_axis`), `|U_x|` reaches 5.08e-3 m/s, and
`U_b = 5.55938`, `f = 0.0315835`, +22.5 % against Prandtl, against 6.02305 and +4.44 % with the workaround below.
`cases/channelPeriodicWF.jsonc` (k-epsilon, standard wall functions, the same catch-all) shows it too: after one
iteration its wall-row `epsilon` is 0.508872 in the two end cells and 0.545202 in the six interior ones. The
pipe cases name `k` zeroGradient, `omega` zeroGradient and `nut` calculated in their catch-all, which gives the
cyclic faces no wall-function type; then the stations agree to the written digit (spread 0) and `|U_x|` falls to
3.4e-9 m/s. The cure, `faces_where` skipping a patch whose `topology_override` is not `None`, moves the results of
every shipped JSONC case with a cyclic pair and a turbulence model, so it is not made here; it is a REVIEW-LATER
item.

**Measured: the plan's 8000 iterations do not reach the fixed point.** On level 1 at 576.69 from rest (TG0's
start) `U_b` at 8000 is 6.023051, 6.8e-4 below the oracle's 6.027151 on the same cells, with `U_axis` still moving
8.1e-4 of itself per 1000 iterations; from `U_b` it is 6.030511, 5.6e-4 above. From `U_b` the excess falls by a
factor of about 5.5 per 2000 iterations on level 1 and about 0.80 per 1000 on level 2: the SIMPLE pseudo-time step of
a core cell scales with its size squared, so each level takes about four times the iterations of the last. The
records therefore run 12 000 (level 0), 24 000 (level 1) and 80 000 (level 2, two 40 000-iteration legs through
`-restartWrite`/`-restartFrom`, which continues the count) iterations at 576.69, and 16 000, 32 000 and 80 000
at 2358. Nothing else changed: the case, its numerics and the solver are as above.

**The recorder.** Each run writes every 1000 iterations. The ignored test `record_pipe` of `ofgpu-validate`
(`OFGPU_PIPE_CASE`, `OFGPU_PIPE_META`) lowers the run's case, checks that cell `i + n k` has the oracle's centre
`i` to `1e-12 R`, reads `U` and `nut` of the last two writes (ASCII at six digits), averages the four axial
stations, and puts the profile into a `rans1d::Solution` for `rans1d::metrics` and `rans1d::tg0_bands`. It records
`change` (the largest change of a cell's `U_z` between the last two writes, over `U_axis`) and `spread` (the largest
difference of a cell's `U_z` from its station mean, over `U_axis`). The records are constants of
`src/bin/validate_gates/pipe.rs`, replayed by `ofgpu-validate`'s section 69.

**The rows.** Per `Re_tau`, on the finest level (`n = 160`), the four band errors of (143.17): `E_P = f/f_P - 1`
at the input `Re_tau`, `E_B = f/f_B(Re_D) - 1`, the log-law deviation in `u+`, and `E_D = defect/4.07 - 1`; `u_val`
is `|U_fine|` of 짠94's study of the same error over the three levels at `h = R/n`; 짠110.1's rule (`band_110`)
reads Inside as a passing row, Undecided as OPEN and Outside as MISSES (Nikuradse's measured pipes, via
Schlichting). Each f64 record is held to the 짠143.1 oracle on the same cells: `U_b` and `f` within `1e-4`
relative (class P; 짠114.2 measured 1e-5 once omega converges, and six written digits give 5e-7). Class R: the
single build's finest record lands in the f64 band of each of the four rows.

**The price** (2026-10-15, the one RTX 5070 Ti shared with two other lanes' work): level 1, 8000 iterations,
100.7 s with the card to itself and 265.8 s beside another run; an iteration costs 11.8 to 28 ms on levels 1 and 2, as
much by what else the card runs as by the level.
The six f64 records took 4273 s of card time and the two single ones 2863 s; with the pricing and the
diagnosis runs above (about 1160 s) the unit used about 2.3 h of the 3 h it was given.

**The records** (2026-10-15, `ofgpu-lowmach` built at f9bcb4a, unchanged by this unit), with the oracle (143.1) on the
same cells beside them:
