## 158. The one-domain vent, the compressible coupling, and the REMBE gate

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Written by DST-00 as the contract of DST-09, DST-10 and
DST-11 (lane S, W4). The labels (158.1)-(158.4) are D.57-D.60. Vented vessels run on
`ofgpu-compressible` (§122-§127): a vent at 0.6 bar overpressure drives a near-sonic jet, and
choking starts near Δp/p ≈ 0.89 (INSIGHTS (c), docs/17 DD1).

### 158.1 The one-domain membrane

**[the design of this section; the physical rule from H22 §2-§3.6: the foil ruptures at the
static activation pressure p_stat = 0.1 bar ± 15 %]**

```
  M: an internal face set of the one mesh, selected by geometry; its state s ∈ {closed, open}
  closed: every face of M is a wall on both sides (zero mass, normal-momentum and energy flux;
          slip or no-slip as the case states)
  opens at the first step n with   p‾_in(M) − p‾_out(M) ≥ p_stat ,  p‾ the area-weighted face-neighbour pressure
  open:   the faces of M are ordinary interior faces from step n + 1 on (irreversible)             (158.1)
```

The mesh holds the outside domain from t = 0 (docs/17 DD9). H22 instead stopped the closed run at
0.1 bar and mapped it onto a second mesh; a mesh-to-mesh map does not conserve mass and energy
exactly, must re-seed the turbulence, the time levels and the flame clock, and needs its own code
path. One domain has none of these problems. The outside gas is quiescent ambient air during
the closed stage, and nothing in it changes until the membrane opens. A membrane burst is a
Riemann problem, so a 1-D tube with an opening membrane must reproduce Sod's shock tube (CMP-07's
exact solution, §127).

The `vent { faces: plane + centre + radius | a face set, pStat }` block selects M. The opening
step, its time and its Δp are reported. **Not modelled, named:** membrane inertia and an opening
time, partial or petal opening, and the boundary-condition names that describe active baffles.
BC-01's catalogue (§120) registers `activePressureForceBaffleVelocity` and `activeBaffleVelocity`
as refused by name, with a message naming the vent block.

### 158.2 The planar deflagration jump conditions

**[derived from the 1-D conservation laws at low Mach number (Rankine-Hugoniot)]** A flame
leaving a closed end, the burned gas at rest, moving at S_L relative to the fresh gas. In the
lab frame the flame moves at `V_f = u_u + S_L`. Mass through it: `ρ_u (V_f − u_u) = ρ_b V_f`.
Momentum: `p_u + ρ_u (V_f − u_u)² = p_b + ρ_b V_f²`.

```
  mass:      ρ_u S_L = ρ_b (u_u + S_L)            =>   u_u = (σ − 1) S_L
  momentum:  p_u + ρ_u S_L² = p_b + ρ_b (σ S_L)²  =>   p_u − p_b = ρ_u S_L² (σ − 1)                (158.2)
```

(ρ_b σ² S_L² = ρ_u σ S_L², so `p_u − p_b = ρ_u S_L² (σ − 1)`.)

### 158.3 The acoustic precursor

**[linear acoustics, as CMP-20 uses it, c = (γ R T)^{1/2}]** The fresh gas set moving at u_u by
the flame is a piston:

```
  Δp_wave = ρ_u c_u u_u = ρ_u c_u (σ − 1) S_L                                                      (158.3)
```

### 158.4 The heat release in the compressible energy equation

**[derived as (152.12), on §125's c_p T + K form]**

```
  ∂(ρ(h_s + K))/∂t + ∇·(ρ u (h_s + K)) − ∂p/∂t = ∇·(α_eff ∇h_s) + q̇ ,     q̇ = Δh_c ω̇_c                (158.4)
```

with a constant c_p per pseudo-species (CMP-14's `hConst` per component), h_s the sensible
enthalpy, Δh_c the formation-enthalpy difference of U and B, and R_mix(c~) from (152.8). The
compressible AICC identity uses the same constant-c_p thermo ((152.11) evaluated with hConst),
not the NASA-7 value. ρ_u(p) of (155.10) is local.

f64 and f32 rows, ≤ 6 min per build. As built (§158.8), the closed membrane is the wall pair of a
split mesh, so there is no face mask and no kernel change; the rows below hold as written:

* `dust::vent::tests::sod_through_membrane`: the same run against the exact Riemann solution

* `dust::vent::tests::opens_at_first_step_over_p_stat`: a chamber pressurised at a constant

### 158.7 Gate DST-REMBE (DST-11)

The REMBE 11.5 m³ vented explosion as one domain: the vessel plus a 15.5 × 5 × 6.355 m outside
box, half by symmetry, in `ofgpu-compressible`. Formula thermo, extended FSC (154.7) with
t_flacc = 0.15 s, SST, p_stat = 0.1 bar on the 0.5 m² vent, and pressure probes P1/P2. A case
generator builds the geometry from a stated parameter file and meshes it with
`ofgpu-automesher`. **Reference:** key J.3 (`huang2022-rembe-p-vented`).

**NAMED and NOT RUN until the vessel geometry is obtained:** H22 publishes no dimensions
(§151.7 item 9; docs/17 §11 item 9). Then, as an R-run (docs/17 §11 item 10):

* the peak overpressure within **± 10 %** of 0.60 bar, at a time within ± 0.015 s of 0.31 s;
* the stage-(iii) rise rate (0.20 → 0.28 s) within ± 15 % of 4.55 bar/s (the key gives 4.56);
* the rupture within ± 0.01 s of 0.10 s.

The bands are H22's own model deviation (+4 %, −0.01 s) plus the reading uncertainty.
t_flacc is H22's tuned value, used as published.

**The REDUCED smoke run**, ≤ 10 min in both builds, on a PLACEHOLDER 11.5 m³ cylinder (L/D = 2),
labelled and never compared: finite fields, the membrane opens exactly once, a pressure peak
exists (D), and the mass budget closes to 1e−10 relative (A). `src/bin/validate_gates/dst_rembe.rs`,
`src/dust/gatemesh.rs` (the vessel and box STL), `cases/dust/rembeVented.jsonc`, and
`reference/huang2022-rembe/geometry.json` once obtained.

### 158.8 The vent as built (DST-09)

`src/dust/vent.rs` (the library), `src/compressible/mod.rs` (one setter,
`Compressible::set_steps_taken`), `src/io/case_json.rs` (the JSONC `vent` block),
`src/bin/common/mod.rs` (`load_case_vented`), `src/bin/compressible.rs` (the driver),
`src/field/catalogue.rs` and `src/field.rs` (the two refused names, §120), and the tests
`tests/shared/dust_vent_cases.rs`, run as `dust::vent::tests` and, in both builds, as
`tests/dust_vent.rs`. No kernel was added or changed; f64 results of every existing path are
unchanged.

**The design, and why the tree differs from §158.5's file list.** §158.5 names a face-mask hook
and a masked face flux in `cuda/compressible.cu`. A mask cannot give the gate's bitwise wall:
every operator the compressible solver applies (`fv`'s Green-Gauss gradients, the Laplacians,
the convection weights, Rhie-Chow, the retarded density, the energy flux) gathers a cell's
interior faces in one loop with ONE face value, while a wall face supplies each side's own
boundary value in the boundary loop. A masked interior face would need per-side wall values in
every one of those kernels. Instead the closed membrane IS a wall pair of a second mesh, and
(158.1) is met without touching a kernel:

* **The split mesh.** `split_raw` takes the case's raw mesh (the merged mesh) and M: the internal
  faces not in M keep their order, every original boundary face keeps its place, and M's faces
  are appended twice, as the wall patch `ventIn` (each face as seen from its in-side cell) and
  the wall patch `ventOut` (as seen from its out-side cell). A face whose new owner is the merged
  neighbour is reversed, keeping its first vertex: `[v0, v1, ..., vk-1] -> [v0, vk-1, ..., v1]`.
  The cells, their order and the points are the merged mesh's, and the merged boundary arrays
  are a PREFIX of the split ones, so every patch's `start` and every rule's face range is the
  same on both meshes.
* **Closed:** the run steps on the split mesh, the membrane patches carrying `U` `noSlip` (or
  `slip`, `vent.wall`) and `p`, `T` `zeroGradient`: zero mass flux through M, hence zero
  normal-momentum and energy flux, by the wall condition itself.
* **The trigger (158.1).** `p‾_in` and `p‾_out` are the area-weighted means of the gauge `p` of
  the cells on either side of M's faces (the face-neighbour pressure), `p‾ = Σ a_f p_f / Σ a_f`,
  both sums in f64 in M's face order, from f64 face areas of the raw points; the datum cancels in
  `Δp = p‾_in − p‾_out`. The cells are gathered on the device by `presGather` and the sums are
  formed on the host. The check runs on the initial state (n = 0) and after every step n; the
  first n with `Δp ≥ p_stat` opens the membrane, irreversibly, and step n + 1 is the first on the
  merged mesh.
* **The opening (`open_onto`).** A state and a solver are built on the merged mesh from the
  case's own lowering. Opened on the initial state, the merged solver is initialised and nothing
  is carried: the membrane never existed, so the run is the run without one bit for bit. Opened
  after step n ≥ 1, the closed state is carried by host round trip: every cell array of `U`, `p`,
  `T`, `rho`, `psi`, `mu`, `kappa` (the current and both old levels) bit for bit, the first
  `n_b` entries of each boundary array (`bf`, `fr`, `ref_value`, `ref_grad`), and `mdot` through
  the face map, M's faces starting at exactly 0; the solver is initialised on the carried fields,
  the carried values are restored (initialise re-seeds `mdot` and the old levels), and the step
  count and both ddt clocks are handed over, so step n + 1 advances them as an uninterrupted run
  would. The cells are the same cells holding the same values, so the opening itself moves no
  mass, momentum or energy.

**The block.** JSONC only (an OpenFOAM case has no route to it):
`vent { normal: [x, y, z], pStat, centre: [x, y, z], radius }` (the disc route) or
`vent { normal, pStat, faces: [ids] }` (the face-set route, internal face ids of the case's mesh),
with an optional `wall` (`noSlip`, the default, or `slip`). `normal` points from the inside to the
outside and is normalised in f64. The disc selects every internal face whose area vector is
parallel to `normal` (`|S·n|/|S| ≥ 1 − 1e-6`), whose vertex-average centre lies within
`1e-6 L` of the plane through `centre` (L the bounding-box diagonal of the points) and within
`radius` of `centre` in the plane. A face's owner is on the inside when `S·n > 0`. Refused by
name, each with its key and `(SPEC-LIT §158.8)`: a zero or non-finite `normal`; a negative or
non-finite `pStat`; `radius` without `centre` and the reverse; a non-positive `radius`; both
routes or neither; an empty or out-of-range or repeated `faces` list; a listed face edge-on to
`normal`; an M that selects no face; `wall` other than the two words; a mesh that already has a
patch or a field entry named `ventIn`/`ventOut`; a vent beside `mesh.wedge` or `mesh.sector`; a
steady run (no opening time); and every driver but `ofgpu-compressible` (`refuse_vent`).
`ofgpu-compressible` prints M (faces, area, `pStat`, the wall), the opening (step, time, `Δp`,
`p‾_in`, `p‾_out`) or, at the end of a run in which it stayed closed, the last `Δp`; it writes
the case's own mesh in both phases (the prefix makes each patch's slice the same).

**Not modelled** (as §158.1 names): membrane inertia, an opening time, partial or petal opening.
`activeBaffleVelocity` and `activePressureForceBaffleVelocity` are refused by name, their notes
naming the `vent` block (§120).

**The tests** (Sod's tube is §127.2's problem in dimensional air, `p_L = 1e5` Pa, `rho_L = 1`
kg/m³, inviscid, van Leer on `U`, `T` and the retarded density, Euler, PBiCGStab with DILU at
`1e-12`, acoustic CFL 0.5, one cell across with `symmetry` sides and walls at the ends, run to
`t = 0.2`; the coupling is PIMPLE with 5 outer iterations, 2 correctors and `alpha_p = 1`, an
input the gate row does not fix; CMP-19 (lane G) measured the same tube without a membrane under
PISO missing the bars and under this PIMPLE meeting them). Measured in both builds:

| test | row | f64 | f32 (`single`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `closed_membrane_is_a_wall` | 200 cells, a Sod problem in each chamber, 176 steps: `mdot` on both membrane patches `== 0` after every step, and U, p, T, rho and every `mdot` bitwise against a hand-built mesh with a wall pair there (D) | holds; the reflected shock moved `p` of the in-side cell by 96713.6 Pa | holds; 96055.1 Pa |

### 158.9 The compressible coupling as built (DST-10)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` The specification was informed by a review of
FSCDustFoam (Huang & Lipatnikov, GPL) and no code was copied. Equations from §152-§156 and
§158.1-§158.4 only; the three relations below are derived here.

`src/compressible/thermo.rs` (`DustHConst`, `MixKernels`), `src/compressible/energy.rs` (the
mixture mode), `src/compressible/mod.rs` (`Compressible::attach_dust`), `src/dust/source.rs`
(`CompressibleDust`), three kernels appended to `cuda/compressible.cu` (`cmpGasStateMix`,
`cmpScaleCp`, `cmpDustRhoURatio`), `src/io/case_dust.rs` and `src/bin/common/mod.rs` (the case
reaches the driver), `src/bin/compressible.rs` (the driver), and the tests
`tests/shared/compressible_dust_cases.rs`, run as `compressible::tests::dust` and, in both builds,
as `tests/compressible_dust.rs`. No existing kernel changed; without a dust coupling every line of
the solver runs as before (`no_dust_no_change`, a hash pinned before the unit).

**[derived] The constant-c_p pair.** §158.4 asks for one constant c_p per pseudo-species. The
formula gas of §152.4 is NASA-7, so the pair is fitted to keep its isobaric burned state:

```
  cp_U = c_p,U(T_u) ,   cp_B = (h_B(T_b) − h_B(T_u)) / (T_b − T_u) ,   T_b of (152.10)
  h_X(T) = a_X + cp_X T ,   a_X = h_X(T_u) − cp_X T_u                                           (158.5)
```

so `h_B(T_b) = h_U(T_u)` holds for the pair as for the NASA-7 gas. The prescribed mode is already
constant-c_p and the pair reproduces it (`dust_hconst_matches_gas`: the AICC ratio and T_b to 0 in
f64). REMBE at T_u = 273 K: cp_U 1039.1, cp_B 1218.21 J/(kg K), Δh_c = a_U − a_B 1.8841e6 J/kg,
T_b 1779.51 K, hConst AICC T_v 2238.74 K and P_max/p_0 8.859252 (the NASA-7 value of §152.6 is
8.6006; the compressible rows compare with the hConst value, as §158.4 states).

**[derived from (158.4)] The energy equation in energy units.** With h_s = cp(c~) T (a 0 K
datum) the total enthalpy is `h_s + (1 − c~) a_U + c~ a_B`; subtracting (a_B − a_U) times (155.3)
from the enthalpy equation leaves (158.4) with `q̇ = Δh_c ω̇_c`, `Δh_c = a_U − a_B`, and Le = 1
((157.6), Γ = κ + D_t with the LOCAL κ = k/(ρ c_p) of the gas's own transport law) splits the
diffusion of h_s:

```
  d(ρ cp(c~) T)/dt + ∇·(ṁ cp(c~_f) T_f) − ∇·(λ ∇T)
        = dp/dt − [d(ρK)/dt + ∇·(ṁ K)] + ∇·(τ·u) + ρ g·u + Δh_c ω̇_c + ∇·(ρ Γ T (cp_B − cp_U) ∇c~)
  λ = ρ Γ cp(c~) = k + ρ cp(c~) D_t                                                               (158.6)
```

`RhoEnergy::enable_mixture` assembles exactly the old matrix with three substitutions: the time
term's weights are `ρ cp(c~)` at the three levels (c~'s own levels), the convection runs on the
face flux `ṁ cp(c~_f)` (c~_f linear; the weights of T are still formed on ṁ), and nothing is
divided by c_p (every `rcp` is 1). The last two terms enter as one cell source in W/m3 through
`fvm_su`; the divergence is the Gauss sum of `ρ_f Γ_f T_f (cp_B − cp_U) |S_f| snGrad c~`. In a
sealed box (158.6) telescopes: `ρ cv(c~) T` changes by Δh_c times the burned mass, which is
(152.11) for the pair:

```
  T_v = (a_U − a_B + cv_U T_0) / cv_B ,   cv_X = cp_X − R0/W_X ,   P_max/p_0 = T_v W_U / (T_0 W_B)   (158.7)
```

**The gas law and ρ_u(p).** `psi = 1/(r(c~) T)`, `r(c~) = R0/W_U + c~ (R0/W_B − R0/W_U)`
((152.8)-(152.9)) on the cells and the boundary faces, in the order `cmpGasState` uses, so c~ = 0
gives its bits. (155.10) is local: the propagation term reads `ρ_u0 U_t'` with
`U_t' = U_t ((p + p_op)/p_init)^{1/γ_u}` formed per cell in double (one scalar ρ_u reaches the
DST-04 kernel, so the pressure factor rides the speed); the measured flame-Courant number reads the
same pair.

**The loop.** `Compressible::step` with a coupling attached: the c~ old level once per step; in
every outer iteration `mu_eff = mu + ρ ν_t` for the momentum predictor (with a turbulence model),
then before the energy solve the closures at the step's end time, U_t', the ignition bracket, Γ,
one solve of (155.3) on the solver's own mass flux ṁ and density levels, ω̇_c, and the energy
equation's mixture state and λ; the energy solve; the mixture gas law wherever the solver formed
psi and rho; and at step 7 the ρ-weighted SST of §156 (`correct_rho` on ṁ with `ρ_f` linear and
the volume flux ṁ/ρ_f, ν the fresh gas's μ(T_u)/ρ_u0), frozen before 2 t_0 as §157.7's D6.
Refused by name: a steady or localEuler run, a ddt other than Euler, any §126 rule (the mixture
gas law forms each boundary face from its own c~, which a rewritten face has none of), a
prescribed U_t law with α or β ≠ 0, and a mixture state asked of an equation with a local step.

**The case and the driver.** `physics.compressible` beside the dust blocks now lowers (§157.7's
refusal is lifted); the compressible presets `farfield` and `supersonicInlet` stay refused.
`ofgpu-compressible`'s loader lets the dust case through and `ofgpu-lowmach`'s refuses it when it
also states the gas (`physics.compressible`, the gas would be ignored). The driver accepts
`kOmegaSST` only beside a dust block (its refusal otherwise names §158.6), builds the coupling on
the case's `c`, `k`, `omega`, `nut` and `dust.sst` with `p_init = pOperating + initial.p`
(refused when `initial.p` is not uniform) and `k_mol = κ(T_u)`, prints one `dust (SPEC-LIT
§158.6)` line with the pair's values, refuses a predicted Co_f above `maxFlameCourant` and prints
the measured one and the c~ bounds count at every report, and writes `c`, `Ut` (U_t'), `Cof`
(per cell) and `HRR` (q̇) beside the five fields, with `Mach` from the mixture (`a² = γ(c~) r(c~) T`,
`γ = cp/(cp − r)`). A vent beside a dust block is refused: the hand-over of c~ and the closures
on opening is DST-11's.

**Gates, measured 2026-10-17** (`tests/compressible_dust.rs` and the lib module, both builds;
`ofgpu-compressible` bin tests f64).

| row | measure | tolerance | class | f64 | single |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `no_dust_no_change` | viscous Sod tube, 100 cells, 40 steps, FNV-1a 64 of every state array | the pin taken on 8b13cb2 | D | 0xac0f1e9c5966b505 holds | 0x534040adc523b30a holds |
| `dust_hconst_matches_gas` | the pair against the prescribed gas and the REMBE T_b; (158.7) against its definition | 1e-12 | A | 0, 2.6e-16 | same (host f64) |

The tube run's burning rate dM_c/dt is 0.31130 (single 0.31162) against ρ_u0 S_L 0.31232 kg/(m² s);
its mass is conserved to the last printed digit in f64 (3.3e-7 relative in single). c~ leaves
[0, 1] by at most 8e-5 in single and by less than 5e-7 in f64 on the burned side of the brush, where
the explicit propagation term of (155.3) lifts it: 7716 and 16677 cell-steps are counted, and the
tube rows record them instead of failing. The six tests take 110 s in f64 and 154 s in single on
the shared card.

**The recorded misses.** (i) *The box's order in Δt.* (158.6) telescopes, so the box has no
first-order time error to measure: its error is the outer loop's lag (the energy equation reads
dp/dt from the previous outer iteration's p). Measured: e = 6.783e-4 and 6.811e-4 at 5 outer
iterations, and 4.2e-9 and 2.7e-9 at 20 (T_end 2238.7401 K against T_v 2238.7401 K). The row's
0.5 % holds at 5; the ratio says nothing about the order. Under single the box also drifts in mass
(8.3e-5 relative, the f32 density levels), which moves e by 5e-5 between the two steps. (ii) *The momentum jump.*
The predicted p_u − p_b is 0.41 Pa, so the 2 % bar is 0.008 Pa; the measured difference of the
two zone means is +0.466 Pa (f64) and +0.598 Pa (single), while p varies by about ±10 Pa cell to
cell inside the flame brush and by about 1 Pa along P on the ~550 Pa plateau. The relation is
below the pressure noise of the run: the zone means move by tenths of a pascal with the outer
iterations (−0.52 Pa at 20, +0.47 Pa at 10), and on the zone that reached into the spread front
they differed by −23.5 Pa. The cure (a quieter pressure field across the brush, or a much longer
quasi-steady run) is not an input of the gate row and is not built.
**Inputs, measured before they were fixed.** The tube runs 10 outer iterations: at 3 the
expansion is 9 % short (u_u 1.20 m/s on the plateau, dp 509 Pa) because the c~ and energy
updates of an outer iteration precede its pressure correction; 10 and 20 agree (dp 540.3 and
540.1 Pa on the zone that reached into the front). c~ is convected with van Leer, as T; upwind
gave the same u_u at 3 outer iterations. The acoustic front spreads over about 0.2 m by 1.5 ms,
so P ends at 0.25 m and the run asserts the front's 50 % point has passed 0.45 m.

**Decisions (TAKEN, by recommendation).** D1: the constant-c_p pair (158.5) keeps the NASA-7 T_b
of each case. D2: h_s = cp(c~) T on a 0 K datum and the energy equation in energy units (158.6),
conservative, so the sealed box telescopes to (158.7). D3: Le = 1 on the gas's own local κ, as
§157.7's D1. D4: the local ρ_u(p) rides U_t' (no change to DST-04's kernel). D5: kOmegaSST only
beside a dust block; ν of the SST is μ(T_u)/ρ_u0; frozen before 2 t_0. D6: a dust case with a §126
rule, a vent, or a non-Euler ddt is refused (DST-11 joins the vent). D7: `Mach` of a dust case is
the mixture's.

Labels: (158.5)-(158.7).

## 159. Phase B — reacting parcels, char, the cloud, two-way coupling, particle radiation, and its gates

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` Written by DST-00 as the contract of DST-12 and DST-13
(lane M, W3) and DST-14 to DST-18 (lane S, W4-W5). The labels (159.1)-(159.8) are D.61-D.68.
Equations from ISL22 unless stated. Phase B covers what the equivalent gas cannot: coarse
particles, low-volatile dusts, non-uniform or settling clouds, near-limit mixtures (INSIGHTS
(l)). Positions and the walk stay f64, as F32-12 made them.

### 159.1 The parcel and its energy

A parcel carries moisture, volatile, char and ash masses, staged in that order: moisture leaves
first (§76's evaporation, ISL22 eq. (14)), then volatiles (159.4), then char (159.5); ash is
inert. ISL22 eq. (13):

```
  m_p C_p dT_p/dt = π d_p k_g Nu (T_∞ − T_p) + (dm_p/dt) ΔH + π d_p² ε_0 σ_SB (θ_R⁴ − T_p⁴)          (159.1)
```

m_p, C_p, T_p, d_p: the particle's mass, specific heat, temperature and diameter; k_g the gas
conductivity; T_∞ the cell gas temperature; ε_0 the emissivity; σ_SB the Stefan-Boltzmann
constant; θ_R the radiation temperature (159.7); ΔH the latent heat of evaporation, of
devolatilisation, or the heat of the surface reaction, by stage. ISL22's values: evaporation
2.25 MJ/kg, devolatilisation 100 kJ/kg (endothermic), C oxidation 32.9 MJ/kg.

The Nusselt and Sherwood numbers (Ranz-Marshall; ISL22 ref. 102; §76.1-§76.2 already cite Ranz &
Marshall 1952):

```
  Nu = 2 + 0.6 Re_p^{1/2} Pr^{1/3} ,     Sh = 2 + 0.6 Re_p^{1/2} Sc^{1/3}                              (159.2)
```

The blowing correction (Bird), ISL22 eq. (15):

```
  Nu* = Nu β / (e^β − 1) ,      β = − C_p,vap ṁ_p / (π d_p k_g Nu)                                      (159.3)
```

**[derived] Its limits.** `β/(e^β − 1) = 1 − β/2 + β²/12 − …`, so it tends to 1 as β → 0;
evaluated by its definition it cancels catastrophically there, and the host and the device use
the series below |β| = 1e−3 (DST-12's `bird_limits`). At β = 1 it is `1/(e − 1) =
0.5819767068693265`.

### 159.2 Devolatilisation and char

Single first-order devolatilisation (SFOM), ISL22 eqs. (16)-(17), with the moisture already gone:

```
  −dm_p/dt = k(T_p) ( m_p − (1 − f_VM0) m_p0 ) ,      k(T) = A exp(−E_a/(R0 T))                      (159.4)
```

f_VM0 is the initial volatile mass fraction and m_p0 the initial particle mass (after drying).
**No open source gives corn starch's (A, E_a)** (§151.8); a case states them, and DST-16 (iii) is
NAMED and NOT RUN until open kinetics are found.

The char surface reaction, kinetic-diffusion limited, ISL22 eqs. (20)-(23) (Baum & Street 1971,
not open):

```
  C(s) + O2 -> CO2
  dm_p/dt = − π d_p² p_O R_diff R_kin / (R_diff + R_kin)
  R_diff = C_0 [ 0.5 (T_g + T_p) ]^{3/4} / d_p ,      R_kin = A exp(−E_a/(R0 T_g))                     (159.5)
```

p_O is the oxidiser partial pressure and C_0 the mass-diffusion constant. ISL22 writes T_g in
R_kin, as printed. **Heat retention:** the ΔH term of (159.1) is multiplied by h_s = 0.3 during
the surface reaction (ISL22 refs. 59, 127); the rest, `(1 − h_s)`, goes to the gas. The O2
taken and the CO2 given are accumulated per parcel.

### 159.3 The closed forms of the Phase B gates

**[derived from (159.1)-(159.5)]**

```
  isothermal devolatilisation:  m_p(t) − (1 − f_VM0) m_p0 = f_VM0 m_p0 exp(−k t)
  lumped heat-up (Re -> 0, Nu = 2, no reaction, no radiation, m_p constant):
        T_p(t) = T_∞ + (T_p0 − T_∞) exp(−t/τ_T) ,    τ_T = m_p C_p / (2 π d_p k_g)
  diffusion-limited char (R_kin -> ∞), constant T, p_O and ρ_p, m_p = ρ_p π d³/6:
        d(d²)/dt = −4 p_O C_0 T_m^{3/4} / ρ_p    =>   d²(t) = d_0² − (4 p_O C_0 T_m^{3/4}/ρ_p) t
  kinetic-limited char (R_diff -> ∞):   d(d)/dt = −2 p_O R_kin / ρ_p      (linear shrinking)          (159.6)
```

with `T_m = 0.5 (T_g + T_p)`. The devolatilisation form integrates (159.4) at constant T. The
heat-up form integrates (159.1) with Nu = 2 and no other term. For the char, `dm/dt = (ρ_p π d²/2)
dd/dt` at constant ρ_p (a shrinking particle of constant density, the stated assumption of the
gate); with R_kin → ∞ the harmonic combination is R_diff, so `(ρ_p π d²/2) dd/dt = −π d p_O C_0
T_m^{3/4}`, i.e. `d·dd/dt = −2 p_O C_0 T_m^{3/4}/ρ_p`; with R_diff → ∞ it is R_kin, so
`(ρ_p π d²/2) dd/dt = −π d² p_O R_kin`.

### 159.4 Particle radiation and two-way coupling

**[derived from (159.1)'s radiation term and §135's P1 incident radiation G]**

```
  θ_R⁴ = G / (4 σ_SB)
  a_p = Σ_parcels n_p ε_0 π d_p² / 4 / V_cell             (added to P1's absorption coefficient)
  S_rad = Σ n_p π d_p² ε_0 σ_SB (θ_R⁴ − T_p⁴)           (per cell; removed from G's equation)          (159.7)
```

**[derived]** An optically thin isothermal cloud at T_p in a cold black enclosure emits
`Σ n_p π d_p² ε_0 σ_SB T_p⁴ = 4 a_p σ_SB T_p⁴ V`.

Two-way coupling [§68 (momentum, energy), §77 (vapour mass and enthalpy), CHR-26]:

```
  per step:  the mass, momentum and energy the parcels give = what the gas gains, to round-off;
             the volatile mass enters a named gas species (the volatile pseudo-species);
             char oxidation takes O2 from and gives CO2 to the species equations                        (159.8)
```

The volatile pseudo-species takes its formula from the dust's volatile matter and its NASA-7 data
as in (152.8). It burns with an authored one-step `volatile + O2` reaction on the CHEMRAD
finite-rate path (CHR-03/09; docs/17 DD11), `cases/mech/volatile1.ck`.

### 159.7 What DST-12 landed

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` `src/dust/particle.rs` (the module `dust::particle`:
`ParticleInputs`/`ParticleProps`, `ParticleState`, `GasAtParcel`, `Exchange` and the host twin
`step`), the kernel `dustParticleStep` in the new `cuda/dustparticle.cu` with its launcher
`particle_step` (`ParticleKernels`) in `src/dust/device.rs`, and `dustparticle.cu` in build.rs's
`KERNEL_UNITS` and, as the fifth unit, `FMAD_OFF_UNITS`. The tests are written once in
`tests/shared/dust_particle_cases.rs` and included as the lib tests `dust::particle::tests` and
by `tests/dust_particle.rs` in the default and the `single` build. The launcher is gated under
capture by `dust_particle_step_replays_under_capture` in `src/dust/device.rs`. Nothing outside
`dust/` calls it yet: DST-14 to DST-18 (lane S) seed the cloud, deposit the accumulators and
couple the radiation. Positions and the walk are not touched.

**The step.** One call advances one particle of each parcel by Δt in a gas frozen over the step
(the cell's T_g, water vapour Y_w, ρ_g and incident radiation G, and the parcel's |u_p − u|;
μ, k_g and c_p,g are constants, as §76's `GasState` holds them). d_p is held fixed through drying
and devolatilisation (the swelling or shrinking of a devolatilising particle is not modelled);
DST-13's char stage shrinks it at constant ρ_p as (159.6) states. C_p is one value for the whole
particle and m_p = m_w + m_v + m_c + m_a. The step is at most eight segments, taken in stage order:

1. **Moisture**, while m_w > 0. Below the boiling point T_b(p) (the root of Hyland-Wexler's
   (S54.3) at p_amb; 373.124 K at 1 atm) the loss rate is (76.1)'s Ranz-Marshall rung,
   `ṁ = π d ρ_f D_f Sh (Y_s − Y_g)`, with §76.4's film (the 1/3 rule, ρ_f = ρ_g T_g/T_f,
   D_f = D_ref (T_f/T_ref)^2.072 p_boil/p_amb), Watson's h_v(T_p) and §76.5's Y_s; it is
   floored at 0, because a dust particle does not take water up. ΔH of (159.1) is h_v(T_p). The
   segment ends when the moisture is gone (m_w is set to exactly 0), when T_p reaches T_b, or at
   the end of the step. A particle at T_b whose net heat at T_b,
   `Q_b = π d k_g Nu f_B (T_g − T_b) + π d² ε_0 (G/4 − σ_SB T_b⁴)`, is positive boils as in (76.9):
   T_p is held at T_b and `ṁ = Q_b/h_v`. **[derived]** The boiling branch closes Bird's factor
   by its convective part: with `ṁ = π d k_g Nu f(β) (T_g − T_b)/h_v` and β of (159.3),
   `β = B f(β)` with `B = c_p,v (T_g − T_b)/h_v`, so `e^β − 1 = B`, `β = ln(1 + B)` and
   `f_B = ln(1 + B)/B`, the Spalding factor §76.9's branch already uses; no iteration is needed.
2. **Volatiles**, once m_w = 0 and while m_v > 0, for the rest of the step: (159.4) at the
   frozen T_p, `Δm_v = m_v (1 − e^{−kΔt})` exactly (as `−expm1`). The stage ends when what is
   left is at most `1e−6` of the parcel's remaining mass; the remnant leaves in that step, with
   its ΔH. ṁ in (159.3) and the source of (159.1) are the segment's mean `Δm_v/Δt`.
3. **Char and ash**: inert in DST-12, heated and radiating only; DST-13 adds (159.5).

**[derived] The segment integrator.** Over a segment of length t the rates are frozen at its
start: the conductance `a = π d k_g Nu f(β)`, the source `s = −ṁ ΔH`, and the radiation
linearised about T_0, `rad(T) ≈ rad_0 − b (T − T_0)` with `rad_0 = π d² ε_0 (G/4 − σ_SB T_0⁴)`
and `b = 4 π d² ε_0 σ_SB T_0³`. (159.1) is then linear in T and is integrated exactly:

```
  num = a (T_g − T_0) + rad_0 + s ,   λ = a + b ,   x = λ t/(m C)
  T(t) = T_0 + num (t/(m C)) φ1(x)
  Q_conv = a [ (T_g − T_0) t − num t² g2(x)/(m C) ] ,    Q_rad = rad_0 t − b num t² g2(x)/(m C)
  φ1(x) = (1 − e^{−x})/x ,   g2(x) = (x − 1 + e^{−x})/x²                                       (159.9)
```

so that `m C (T(t) − T_0) = Q_conv + Q_rad + s t` identically. φ1 and g2 are their series
`Σ (−x)^j/(j+1)!` and `Σ (−x)^j/(j+2)!` below x = 1 (stopped at a term below 1e−17 of the sum,
at most 30 terms) and their closed forms above, where g2's cancellation costs at most a factor
2.7; both are finite at λ = 0. The sub-cooled segment ends at T_b at
`t_hit = −ln(1 − r) m C/λ`, `r = λ (T_b − T_0)/num`, when num > 0 and r < 1. For an ash particle
at rest with no radiation this is the heat-up form of (159.6) to round-off in one segment per
step.

**The accumulators.** Each parcel carries six `Acc` (f64 in both builds) sums the kernel adds to
and the caller zeroes: the water and the volatile mass given, each times the end-of-step T_p as
the state stores it (77.5), `Q_conv` (the heat the gas gave by convection; the gas loses it) and
`Q_rad` (the net radiation absorbed; DST-17 takes it from G's equation). As §77.4 says, the
latent and devolatilisation heats are inside `Q_conv` and are not a second sink.

**The device.** One thread per parcel; every intermediate is double in both builds and each state
word is rounded once at its store, the DST-03 rule. The unit is compiled with `-fmad=false`, so
the kernel rounds every product as the host twin does, and what is left between them is the last
bit of exp, expm1, log, log1p, pow and cbrt. The host twin is f64 in both builds; its one contact
with the build's precision is the stored end-of-step T_p of (77.5).

**Measured** (RTX 5070 Ti, tests/dust_particle.rs). Isothermal devolatilisation over k t = 3 in
40 steps: host 5.1e−16, device 3.9e−16 in f64 and 1.5e−7 under `single` (bar 1e−10; 1e−5 under
`single` by D-F32-1). Heat-up over 3 τ_T in 40 steps: host 2.5e−16 of |T_0 − T_g| with the
convective heat equal to `m C ΔT` exactly; device 2.5e−16, and 1.6e−7 under `single`. Bird: the
factor is within 1.4e−15 of `1 − β/2 + β²/12` for |β| ≤ 1e−3 and exactly `1/(e − 1)` at β = 1.
Stage order: the 100 µm parcel passes moisture, volatiles and char once each, in order, on the
host and the device. **Device against host**, one 2 ms step of 4096 random parcels in 1024 cells
(555 end their moisture inside the step, 320 boil): the ulps are counted at each word's operand
scale - a mass at the mass it came from, T_p at itself, `m T` at `m_in T_out`, a heat at the
step's integrand `(a_0 |ΔT| + ε_0 π d² (G/4 + σ_SB T⁴)) Δt` - because a mass left when a stage ends
inside the step is a difference, and its own ulps count the cancellation, not the arithmetic. The
3838 parcels that do not reach T_b in the step are within 3 ulp in f64 and 3 ulp under `single`
(bar 4). **The 258 parcels that reach T_b in the step are MISSED in f64 at 6 ulp** (m_w and its
accumulator; 3 ulp under `single`): t_hit moves by `1/(1 − r)` times any change in r, so as
T_eq approaches T_b from above the crossing time, and with it the split of the drying between
the two rates, is ill-conditioned in the model itself, and a 1-ulp difference in a transcendental
becomes a few ulp of the moisture. The row reports the miss and asserts the crossing parcels stay
within 16 × 4 ulp, far below what a branch taken differently would give.

### 159.8 What DST-13 landed

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` `src/dust/char.rs` (the module `dust::char`:
`CharInputs`/`CharProps`, the rates `diff_coef`, `r_kin` and `rate` of (159.5), the shrinkage
`shrink` of (159.10) and the segment `burn`), the char stage of `dustParticleStep` in
`cuda/dustparticle.cu` (the device function `dustpCharBurn`) and of the host twin
`dust::particle::step`, and the launcher `particle_step` with the char's fields. The tests are
written once in `tests/shared/dust_char_cases.rs` and included as the lib tests `dust::char::tests`
and by `tests/dust_char.rs` in the default and the `single` build. Nothing outside `dust/` calls
the char stage yet: DST-14 to DST-18 (lane S) state it in the case, take p_O2 from the cell and
deposit the accumulators.

**The inputs and the interface.** `ParticleInputs` gains `char_rate: CharInputs { c0, a, e_a,
h_c, h_s }`: C_0 (kg/(m s Pa K^0.75)), A (kg/(m² s Pa)) and E_a (J/mol) of (159.5), the heat
released per kilogram of carbon burnt h_c (J/kg; ISL22's 32.9 MJ/kg), and h_s in [0, 1].
`CharInputs::inert()` (all zero) leaves the char inert, as DST-12 did; each of C_0, A, E_a below 0,
a non-finite h_c and an h_s outside [0, 1] is refused by name. `GasAtParcel` gains the cell's O2
partial pressure p_O2 (Pa); no char burns where p_O2 ≤ 0. On the device `ParticleGasDev` gains the
cell field `p_o2`, and the kernel now writes m_c and d_p.

**[derived] The char segment.** Once m_w = m_v = 0 the particle is char and ash; while m_c > 0 and
p_O2 > 0 it burns. Over a segment T_p, T_g and p_O2 are frozen at its start, so are
`C' = R_diff d = C_0 T_m^{3/4}` and R_kin, and the particle shrinks at constant density
`ρ_p = 6 m/(π d³)` (m = m_c + m_a, the density at the segment's start). Then
`(ρ_p π d²/2) dd/dt = −π d² p_O2 C' R_kin/(C' + R_kin d)`, i.e. `(C' + R_kin d) dd = −K dt` with
`K = 2 p_O2 C' R_kin/ρ_p`, whose integral is `C' Δ + R_kin (d_0 Δ − Δ²/2) = K t` for
`Δ = d_0 − d`. Its root that starts at Δ = 0, in the form that does not cancel:

```
  Δ(t) = 2 K t / ( B + sqrt(B² − 2 R_kin K t) ) ,    B = C' + R_kin d_0                          (159.10)
```

With R_kin → ∞ it is `d_0 − sqrt(d_0² − 4 p_O2 C' t/ρ_p)`, the d² law of (159.6); with C' → ∞ it
is `2 p_O2 R_kin t/ρ_p`, the linear shrinking. The char is gone when m = m_a, at
`d_end = d_0 (m_a/m_0)^{1/3}`, after `t_out = (d_0 − d_end) (C' + R_kin (d_0 + d_end)/2)/K`
(the integral at Δ = d_0 − d_end, where the root is still real). A segment that reaches t_out
ends there with m_c = 0 exactly and d = d_end (0 for a particle with no ash), and the step goes
on with the ash; otherwise it takes the rest of the step, and the char burnt is
`Δm = m_0 Δ (d_0² + d_0 d + d²)/d_0³` (that is `m_0 (1 − (d/d_0)³)` without the cancellation). The
new char mass is rounded to `Scalar` where it is stored, `m_c' = round(m_c − Δm)`, the carbon given
is the difference of the two stored words `m_c − m_c'`, and the diameter follows the stored mass,
`d = d_0 ((m_c' + m_a)/m_0)^{1/3}`, so mass and diameter keep one density and the carbon ledger
telescopes in both builds. A remnant whose t_out is not positive (a char too small to move the
diameter) leaves at once, its retained heat added to T_p as `h_s Δm h_c/(m C)`.

**The heat.** The reaction releases `Q = Δm h_c`. (159.1)'s source in the segment integrator
(159.9) is `s = h_s Q/t` (the h_s of §159.2), so `m C (T(t) − T_0) = Q_conv + Q_rad + h_s Q`; the
rest, `(1 − h_s) Q`, is the gas's, accumulated as `q_char`. Bird's factor (159.3) is not applied in
the char stage (f = 1): §159.1 states it for a vapour leaving the particle, and the net Stefan flux
of `C + O2 → CO2` is the carbon alone; this is a choice made here.

**The elements.** `C(s) + O2 → CO2` by mass, with the IUPAC conventional atomic weights
`W_C = 12.011` and `W_O = 15.999` g/mol:

```
  m_O2 = Δm W_O2/W_C ,   m_CO2 = Δm W_CO2/W_C ,   W_O2 = 2 W_O ,   W_CO2 = W_C + W_O2              (159.11)
```

so that carbon plus oxygen is the CO2 by construction.

**The accumulators.** Five more `Acc` per parcel, eleven in all: the carbon burnt Δm, the O2
taken, the CO2 given, the carbon times the stored end-of-step T_p (as (77.5) for the vapours), and
`q_char`. As for drying and devolatilisation, the particle's share h_s Q is inside the segment's
heats and is not a second source.

**The stop on a particle with no mass.** A parcel whose mass is all moisture, all volatile, or
all char without ash loses all of it inside a step; DST-12's loop then took another segment with
m C = 0 and returned NaN for T_p and the heats (`vanished_particle_stays_finite` failed so before
the fix). The loop now stops when the mass is 0, on the host and the device; no DST-12 row moves.

**The device.** As in §159.7: double intermediates, `-fmad=false`, each state word rounded once at
its store, and the char mass rounded where the char segment ends, as the host twin does. The
twin's contact with the build's precision is therefore the stored T_p of (77.5) and the stored char
mass, so its closed-form char rows are class R as the device's are.

**Measured** (RTX 5070 Ti, tests/dust_char.rs). Diffusion-limited (R_kin = 1e12, E_a = 0; C' /
(R_kin d) below 1e−16), a pure-char 50 µm particle at 1500 K, 40 steps to 90 % burnout: d² within
1.5e−15 of the d² law on the host and 3.9e−16 on the device in f64, 2.6e−7 and 3.1e−7 under
`single` (bar 1e−8; 1e−5 under `single` by D-F32-1). Kinetic-limited (C_0 = 1e6, A = 1, E_a = 80
kJ/mol): d within 2.9e−16 (host) and 8.8e−16 (device) of the line in f64, 3.6e−8 and 2.8e−7 under
`single` (bar 1e−10, R). The harmonic combination is within 1/ratio of each limit and 2.2e−16 at a
ratio of 1e16, (159.10) within 1.4e−16 d_0 of both closed forms there, and within 2.5e−16 of its own
integral at finite rates (bar 1e−12 and 1e−13). Element balance, an 80 µm parcel with 30 % ash and
a 30 µm pure-char parcel to burnout in 24 steps: the carbon given equals the char lost exactly,
and O2, CO2 = C + O2 and the elements carried back by the CO2 are within 5.2e−16 in both builds,
host and device (bar 1e−14). Retention, one step at h_s = 0.3: the gas's share is
`(1 − h_s)(Δm h_c)` bit for bit, and the particle's share is within 2.9e−16 of `h_s Δm h_c` (host)
and 9.5e−8 on the device under `single` (bar 1e−12, R); h_s = 1 gives the gas 0 and h_s = 0 keeps a
particle at T_g bit for bit. **Device against host**, one 5 ms step of 4096 random dry parcels in
1024 cells (332 burn out with ash left, 11 with nothing left, 3241 partly, 512 do not burn): m_c,
d, T_p (at the scale `T + h_s h_c m_c/(m C)`, the retained heat of the char), the carbon given and
the two heats (at DST-12's integrand plus `h_s m_c h_c`) are within 4 ulp in both builds (worst 4,
on Q_conv/Q_rad in f64 and Q_rad under `single`), and the O2, the CO2, the carbon times T_p and the
gas's heat are the products of the carbon given bit for bit, on the device as on the host. DST-12's
six rows print what they printed before.

### 159.9 The cloud as built (DST-14)

`No GPL-licensed source was consulted.` DST-14 states a reacting dust cloud in a case and lowers
it, on the host only; DST-15 runs it. Files: `src/dust/seeding.rs` (new), `src/io/case_dust.rs`,
`src/io/case_parcels.rs`, `src/io/case_json.rs`, `docs/schema/case-1.json` and
`tests/shared/case_dust_cases.rs`. The specification was informed by a review of FSCDustFoam
(Huang & Lipatnikov, GPL) and no code was copied; the equations below are (147.1), the open
DLMF and the derivation given here.

**The block.** JSONC `dust.cloud`, and on the dictionary route of §137.2 the sub-dictionary
`dustCloud` of `constant/cloudProperties`. The dictionary is turned into the same JSON object and
read by the same `deny_unknown_fields` deserialiser, so the two routes cannot drift; a file that
states only `dustCloud` has no `parcels` block.

```
  cloud {
    concentration C        kg/m3, > 0                                         required
    diameter d             m, > 0                  exactly one of the two
    rosinRammler { d, n }  m, > 0 ; n > 0          (d is d̄ = X of (147.1), n is its q)
    parcelsPerCell K       integer >= 1                                       default 1
    composition { moisture, volatile, char, ash }  each in [0, 1], sum within 1e-9 of 1, required
    rhoP, cpP              kg/m3, J/(kg K), > 0                               required
    emissivity             in [0, 1]                                          required
    devolatilisation { A >= 0 1/s, Ea >= 0 J/mol, dH finite J/kg }      required iff volatile > 0
    char { C0 >= 0, A >= 0, Ea >= 0, hs in [0, 1], hc >= 0 J/kg }        only with char > 0
  }
```

`char` absent with char > 0 is an inert char (`CharInputs::inert`, as DST-12 left it), and `hc`
absent is ISL22's 32.9 MJ/kg (§159.1); both are decisions taken by recommendation, since the plan
row lists no `hc` and `CharInputs` needs one. The composition is divided by its own sum, so the
stated fractions move by at most 1e-9 relative and the four stage masses of each particle add to
its mass to round-off. The particles start at rest at the case's `initial.T`. The gas side of
`ParticleInputs` (μ, k_g, c_p,g, the volatile's c_p and the drying pressure) is not the cloud's:
`LoweredCloud::particle_inputs` takes it from the caller, which in DST-15 is the gas.

**Refusals** (§13.4; each names its key). A cloud beside `combustion.model` FSC or TFC
(`dust.cloud`): Phase B burns the volatile on the finite-rate path (§159.4), and Phase A's
equivalent gas would count the same fuel twice. A Phase A key (`dust.thermo`, `phi`, `cp`, `Wu`,
`Wb`, `Tb`, `SL`, `sst`) beside a cloud. Both or neither of `diameter` and `rosinRammler`. Every
value outside its range above. `devolatilisation` without volatile, or volatile without it.
`char` with no char. `initial.T` absent. An unknown key: the deserialiser names it. Every driver
refuses a case that states a cloud through `LoweredCase::refuse_parcels` until DST-15 wires
`ofgpu-lowmach`, and `io::case::read_case_controls` already refuses a case directory that holds
`constant/cloudProperties`. A Phase A case (no cloud) now states `dust.thermo` as before; the key
became optional in the schema only so that a cloud can stand without it, and its absence beside
FSC/TFC is refused by name.

**The seeding.** The plan row says the cloud lowers "to CHR-25's injectors". The tree's injector
(§66.8) is a nozzle that emits per event, and a uniform cloud at t = 0 is `Parcels::seed`'s
`SeedParcel` (§66), so the lowering targets that instead: the tree wins. Each cell c of volume
V_c and centroid x_c receives K parcels at x_c, band j = 1..K, in cell-major order:

```
  a = 1 + 1/n ,   X_j = −ln(1 − j/K)   (X_0 = 0, X_K = ∞)
  d_j = K d̄ [ γ(a, X_j) − γ(a, X_{j−1}) ]                                                     (159.12)
  (1/K) Σ_j d_j = d̄ Γ(1 + 1/n)                                                               (159.13)
  M_cj = C V_c / K ,   m_j = ρ_p π d_j³ / 6 ,   n_p,cj = M_cj / m_j                              (159.14)
```

A monodisperse cloud has d_j = d for every j.

**[derived]** (159.12) is band j's mass-weighted mean diameter. With (147.1)'s volume (mass)
fraction Q(d) = 1 − exp(−(d/d̄)^n) and x = (d/d̄)^n, d = d̄ x^{1/n} and dQ = e^{−x} dx. Band j holds
the quantiles (j−1)/K to j/K, i.e. x from X_{j−1} to X_j, mass fraction 1/K, so its mean is
K d̄ ∫ x^{1/n} e^{−x} dx over that interval, which is K d̄ [γ(a, X_j) − γ(a, X_{j−1})]. Summed over
the K equal-mass bands it telescopes to d̄ γ(a, ∞) = d̄ Γ(a) for ANY K, the Rosin-Rammler
mass-weighted mean (159.13); K = 1 gives the one parcel that mean. The seeded mass per volume,
Σ n_p m / Σ V_c, is C by (159.14).

γ(a, x) and Γ(a, x) are the lower and upper incomplete gamma functions (DLMF §8.2,
https://dlmf.nist.gov/8.2, open), evaluated in f64 for a > 1:

```
  γ(a, x) = x^a e^{−x} Σ_{k≥0} x^k / ( a (a+1) ⋯ (a+k) ) ,                 x < a + 1
  Γ(a, x) = x^a e^{−x} / ( b_0 + a_1/( b_1 + a_2/( b_2 + ⋯ ) ) ) ,          x ≥ a + 1
            b_k = x + 2k + 1 − a ,   a_k = −k (k − a)
  Γ(a) = γ(a, a + 1) + Γ(a, a + 1)                                                            (159.15)
```

The series is DLMF (8.7.1) with Γ(a)/Γ(a+k+1) written as the product. The fraction is the even
contraction of DLMF (8.9.2) [derived], evaluated by the modified Lentz algorithm (Lentz, Appl.
Opt. 15 (1976) 668-671; Thompson & Barnett, J. Comput. Phys. 64 (1986) 490-509). x^a e^{−x} is
`exp(a ln x − x)`. Each band takes the form that does not cancel: γ differences when both ends
are below a + 1, Γ(a, ·) differences when both are at or above it (Γ(a, ∞) = 0), and
`(Γ(a) − γ(a, X_{j−1})) − Γ(a, X_j)` across the switch. A supervisor oracle of the same formulas
gives Γ(1 + 1/n) within 9.6e−16 relative for n from 0.3 to 10 and (159.13) within 6.2e−16 for
K = 1, 7, 64 and 1000.

**Precision.** Every number above is f64 in both builds; `CloudParcel::seed_parcel` rounds the
position, diameter, temperature and n_p to `Scalar` once, at the handoff. The gates are class A
in both builds, and `tests/case_dust.rs` runs the same cases under `single`.

**Gates** (`io::case_dust::tests`, and `tests/case_dust.rs` under `single`):

* `cloud_lowers` (D): a JSONC case stating every cloud key at a non-default value lowers to those
  values, `particle_inputs` maps each onto `ParticleInputs`, the defaults are K = 1, inert char
  and hc = 32.9e6, and the dictionary route gives the same `JsonDustCloud` and the same lowering.
* `cloud_mass_is_exact` (A): on 1000 cells of unequal volume, monodisperse and Rosin-Rammler with
  K = 1, 4 and 16, Σ n_p m / Σ V equals C to 1e−12 relative, and each particle's four stage masses
  add to ρ_p π d³/6 to 1e−14.
* `rosin_rammler_moments` (A): Γ(1 + 1/n) for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 2.5 within 1e−14 of its known value;
  γ(2, x) and γ(3, x) within 1e−14 Γ(a) of their closed forms on both sides of a + 1; band
  diameters within 1e−12 of the oracle's; and the seeded set's mass-weighted mean diameter within
  1e−10 of d̄ Γ(1 + 1/n) for each n with K = 1, 7 and 64.
* `cloud_refusals` (D): each refusal above names its key.
* `the_shipped_schema_is_the_generated_one`: the regenerated schema.

**Measured** (host only, 2026-10-17; the f64 build and `single` print the same digits, since every
number is f64). The seeded set's mass-weighted mean diameter is within 9.9e−15 of d̄ Γ(1 + 1/n) at
worst (n = 4, K = 64), 5.4e−16 at best (n = 1, K = 1), against the bar of 1e−10; the error grows
with K only through the f64 sum over 1000 K parcels. The seeded mass per volume holds its 1e−12 bar
on all five clouds, each particle's stage masses their 1e−14 bar, Γ(1 + 1/n) its 1e−14 bar against
the known values, γ(2, x) and γ(3, x) theirs against the closed forms, and the K = 7 bands match the
oracle to 1e−12. Tests: 4 new in `io::case_dust::tests` (f64) and the same 4 in
`tests/case_dust.rs` (14 in that file, both builds); `io::case_parcels` and the schema test pass
unchanged in count.
